title: Ropa vieja (Cuban shredded beef)
description: Tender shredded beef in a juicy tomato and bell pepper sofrito.
steps: Place the beef flank in a pot and cover with the water; add one cut-up onion, one bay leaf and salt. Bring to a gentle simmer and skim off the foam.
Cover and cook for 90 to 120 minutes, until the meat pulls apart with a fork; add hot water if the meat is no longer covered.
Remove the meat, reserve 300 ml of the cooking liquid and shred the beef when cool enough to handle. Discard any hard fat and tough fibers.
Cut the remaining onion and the bell peppers into strips. Sauté in the oil for 8 minutes; add the chopped garlic, cumin and oregano and cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in the tomatoes, wine and remaining bay leaf. Cook for 8 minutes, add the meat and reserved cooking liquid, then simmer gently for another 20 minutes.
Adjust the salt and pepper, remove the bay leaf and serve once the sauce coats the beef without being watery.
tips: Cut the flank into large pieces before simmering to keep the strands long.
Cooking time depends on how tough the meat is; check that it is tender before shredding.

title: Vaca frita (Crispy shredded beef)
description: Shredded beef browned in a skillet with garlic, onion and citrus.
steps: Gently simmer the beef flank with the water, one cut-up onion, bay leaf and salt for 90 to 110 minutes, until it can be shredded.
Drain, remove the bay leaf and shred the meat. Mix with the crushed garlic, sour orange juice, cumin and pepper; refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Drain the meat again and pat it lightly dry with paper towels. Cut the remaining onion into thin strips.
Heat half the oil in a wide skillet and brown the onion for 6 minutes. Transfer to a clean plate.
Add the remaining oil and cook the beef in two batches. Leave it undisturbed for 3 minutes before turning; fry until the edges are browned and crisp.
Return the onion to the skillet, stir for one minute and serve immediately to keep the beef crisp.
tips: An overcrowded skillet steams the meat in its juices and makes browning difficult.

title: Havana-style picadillo (Ground beef with olives)
description: Ground beef with olives, raisins and a Cuban-style tomato sauce.
steps: Chop the onion, bell pepper and garlic. Drain the olives and slice them into rounds.
Sauté the onion and bell pepper in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin and oregano and stir for half a minute.
Add the beef and break it up with a spoon as it cooks for 8 minutes; no large clumps should remain.
Stir in the tomatoes, water, bay leaf, olives and raisins. Partially cover and cook over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Check that the meat reaches 71 °C, remove the bay leaf and adjust the salt at the end, since the olives add plenty.
tips: For a less sweet flavor, omit the raisins without changing the other ingredients.

title: Mojo roast pork shoulder
description: Slow-roasted pork shoulder with sour orange, garlic and oregano.
steps: Crush the garlic with salt, cumin and oregano. Mix with the sour orange juice, oil and pepper.
Make shallow cuts in the shoulder and rub it with the marinade. Cover and refrigerate for 12 hours.
Preheat the oven to 170 °C. Arrange the sliced onion in a roasting dish, set the pork on top and add the marinade and water.
Cover the dish tightly and roast for about 3 hours, checking that there is still liquid in the bottom; add a little hot water if needed.
Uncover and roast for another 45 to 60 minutes, until browned and tender when pierced; for shredding, the center usually needs to reach about 90–95 °C.
Let rest for 15 minutes. Boil the pan juices in a small saucepan for 5 minutes and serve alongside the meat.
tips: The target temperature is for a tender shoulder that falls apart; pork loin requires a different cooking time.
If using a bone-in joint, allow more time and measure the temperature without touching the bone.

title: Fried pork chunks with onion mojo
description: Pork cubes simmered until tender, then browned and served with onion mojo.
steps: Reserve 30 ml of sour orange juice and one garlic clove for the mojo. Marinate the pork with the remaining juice, crushed garlic, cumin, oregano and salt; refrigerate for one hour.
Place the meat and its marinade in a pot with the water. Cover and simmer gently for about 50 minutes, until tender.
Uncover and let the water evaporate. Remove the pork chunks, pat them lightly dry and clean the pot if any bits are stuck to the bottom.
Heat four tablespoons of oil and brown the pork in batches for 8 to 10 minutes, turning carefully.
In another skillet, sauté the reserved onion and garlic in the remaining oil for 5 minutes. Add the reserved juice, boil for one minute and pour over the meat.
tips: Do not pour cold liquids into the frying oil; prepare the mojo separately.

title: Boliche (Chorizo-stuffed beef roast)
description: Beef eye of round stuffed with chorizo and braised in a vegetable sauce.
steps: Working on a stable cutting board, use a long knife to make a channel through the center of the beef. Insert the chorizo and tie the roast with kitchen twine.
Season with salt and pepper and brown the meat on all sides in a pot with the oil; allow 10 minutes.
Remove the meat and sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper and garlic for 8 minutes. Stir in the tomatoes, wine, oregano and bay leaf.
Return the stuffed roast to the pot and add the stock. Cover and cook at a very gentle simmer for 2 and a half to 3 hours, turning the roast every 45 minutes.
Check that the meat is tender and that the center of the filling is thoroughly hot, at least 74 °C. Remove the meat and let rest for 10 minutes.
Remove the twine and bay leaf. Blend the sauce if you prefer it smooth, reduce for a few minutes and serve the sliced roast with the sauce.
tips: Use ready-to-eat cured chorizo and check its label for allergens.

title: Cuban-Style Beef Stew
description: Oxtail slowly braised with red wine and a touch of heat.

ingredients.name: oxtail
ingredients.note: cut into pieces by the butcher

steps: Pat the oxtail pieces dry, season with salt and pepper and brown in the oil in batches; set aside on a plate.
Sauté the chopped onion and bell pepper in the same pot for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin and oregano and cook for one minute.
Pour in the wine and gently scrape the bottom. Add the tomatoes, bay leaf, hot sauce and water.
Return the oxtail to the pot, cover and maintain a very gentle simmer for about 3 hours, until the meat almost falls off the bone.
Check every 40 minutes that the pot is not drying out and add hot water if needed. At the end, skim off surface fat and remove the bay leaf.
Uncover, reduce the sauce for 10 minutes and adjust the salt and heat before serving.
tips: Start with a little hot sauce and let each person add more to their own plate.

title: Bistec de palomilla (Cuban thin-cut steak)
description: Thin beef steak with sautéed onion, garlic and lemon.
steps: Mix the crushed garlic, lemon juice, salt and pepper and rub over the steaks. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Cut the onions into strips. Sauté in one tablespoon of oil for 7 minutes and set aside.
Drain off the marinade and pat the meat lightly dry. Heat the remaining oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook the steaks in batches for approximately 1 to 2 minutes per side, adjusting for thickness, until they reach 63 °C; let rest for 3 minutes.
Top with the onion, sprinkle with parsley and serve with the resting juices.
tips: To check the temperature of a thin steak, insert the thermometer sideways toward the center.

title: Breaded beef steak
description: Beef steak coated in breadcrumbs and fried until golden.

ingredients.name: oil
ingredients.note: for frying; not all of it is consumed

steps: Marinate the meat with crushed garlic, lemon juice, salt and pepper. Refrigerate for 20 minutes, then drain.
Place the flour, beaten eggs and breadcrumbs in three separate dishes.
Coat each steak in flour, shake off the excess, dip in egg and press into the breadcrumbs until both sides are covered.
Heat a layer of oil to about 170 °C. Fry each steak for 3 to 4 minutes per side, without crowding the pan or burning the coating.
Check that the center reaches 63 °C, let rest for 3 minutes on a rack and serve hot.
tips: If the outside browns too quickly, lower the heat so the center can reach the required temperature.

title: Cuban beef and potato stew
description: Beef stew with potatoes that soak up a thick sofrito sauce.
steps: Cut the beef into 3 cm cubes, pat dry and season with salt and pepper. Brown in the oil in batches and set aside.
Chop the onion, bell pepper and garlic; sauté the first two for 6 minutes, then add the garlic and cumin for half a minute.
Add the tomatoes, beef, water and bay leaf. Cover and simmer gently for 75 minutes, or until the beef begins to soften.
Peel the potatoes and cut into evenly sized pieces. Add to the stew and cook for another 20 to 25 minutes, until both the beef and potatoes are tender.
Remove the bay leaf and reduce uncovered if there is too much liquid. Adjust the salt and serve.
tips: Stir gently toward the end so the potatoes do not fall apart.

title: Pork fricassee
description: Pork stewed with potatoes, olives and a wine-scented sofrito.
steps: Marinate the pork pieces with sour orange juice, half the garlic, oregano and salt; refrigerate for one hour.
Drain and brown the pork in the oil for 8 minutes. Remove it and sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper and remaining garlic.
Add the tomatoes and wine and boil for 3 minutes. Return the meat, add the water and cover.
Simmer gently for 55 minutes, keeping an eye on the liquid. Peel the potatoes and cut into large cubes.
Add the potatoes and olives; cook for another 25 minutes, until everything is tender. Adjust the salt and serve with the sauce.
tips: If the pork is still tough, hold back the potatoes and cook the meat longer first.

title: Pork chops with onions
description: Skillet-browned pork chops finished with plenty of onion.
steps: Rub the chops with crushed garlic, sour orange juice, oregano, salt and pepper. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Pat them lightly dry and brown in a skillet with the oil for 3 minutes on each side. Transfer to a plate.
Cut the onions into strips and cook in the same skillet for 7 minutes, stirring.
Add the water, place the chops over the onion and cover. Cook over low heat for 5 to 8 minutes, until the center reaches 63 °C.
Let the chops rest for 3 minutes before serving with the onion and pan juices.
tips: Thickness affects the final cooking time; measure close to the bone without touching it.

title: Orange-roasted pork loin
description: Pork loin roasted with orange juice and served with a quick pan-juice sauce.
steps: Mix the juices, crushed garlic, oil, oregano, salt and pepper. Rub over the pork loin and refrigerate for one hour.
Heat the oven to 180 °C. Cover the bottom of a roasting dish with sliced onion, add the water and place the loin and its marinade on top.
Roast for 50 to 65 minutes, basting once with the pan liquid. Check that the center reaches 63 °C.
Remove the meat and let rest for 10 minutes. Transfer the juices and onion to a saucepan and boil for 5 minutes.
Blend or strain the sauce, adjust the seasoning and serve over thin slices of pork loin.
tips: Do not use the cooking time for pork shoulder when roasting loin: this cut is lean and dries out if overcooked.

title: Stovetop braised pork ribs
description: Pork ribs cooked in their sauce until tender and lightly browned.
steps: Season the ribs with salt and cumin. Brown in the oil for 10 minutes, turning for even color.
Add the chopped onion and bell pepper and cook for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and stir for half a minute.
Stir in the tomatoes, juice, bay leaf and water. Cover and simmer gently for about 75 minutes, until the ribs are tender.
Check every half hour that there is liquid in the pot; add small amounts of hot water if needed.
Uncover, remove the bay leaf and thicken the sauce for 10 minutes, turning the ribs to coat them.
tips: Skim off any fat that rises to the surface before reducing the sauce.

title: Cuban-style meatballs
description: Beef meatballs simmered in tomato sauce with bell pepper and olives.
steps: Mix the beef with the egg, breadcrumbs, one grated garlic clove, cumin, salt and pepper. Shape into about 16 evenly sized meatballs.
Lightly brown the meatballs in a pot with the oil, working in two batches, then set aside.
Chop the onion, bell pepper and remaining garlic. Sauté in the pot for 6 minutes, then add the tomatoes, water and oregano.
Return the meatballs, add the olives and cover. Simmer gently for 20 to 25 minutes, shaking the pot without breaking the meatballs.
Check that the center of a meatball reaches 71 °C and adjust the sauce before serving.
tips: Damp hands make it easier to shape the meatballs without adding more breadcrumbs.

title: Pulpeta (Cuban stuffed meatloaf)
description: A ground-meat roll with hard-boiled eggs in the center and tomato sauce.

ingredients.name: egg
ingredients.note: 3 hard-boiled and 1 raw to bind the mixture

steps: Cook three eggs in boiling water for 10 to 11 minutes, cool, peel and set aside. Mix the meats with the raw egg, breadcrumbs, two grated garlic cloves, salt and pepper.
Spread the mixture into a thick rectangle on parchment paper. Line up the boiled eggs in the center and wrap the meat around them to form a tightly sealed cylinder.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Sauté the chopped onion and bell pepper in the oil for 7 minutes; add the remaining garlic, tomatoes, water and oregano and simmer for 5 minutes.
Pour the sauce into a baking dish and place the meatloaf in it without the paper. Bake for 45 to 55 minutes, covering loosely if it browns too much.
Check that the central area of the meat and filling reaches 74 °C. Let rest for 10 minutes before slicing and serving with the sauce.
tips: Press the seams together firmly so the roll holds its shape while cooking.

title: Beef liver with onions
description: Thoroughly cooked liver strips with soft onion and a splash of vinegar.
steps: Pat the liver dry and cut into even strips one centimeter wide. Slice the onions into half-moons and chop the garlic.
Cook the onions in two tablespoons of oil over medium heat for 9 minutes; add the garlic for the last minute, then set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the skillet and sauté the liver in batches for 4 to 5 minutes, turning to cook evenly.
Return the onion and add the water, vinegar, cumin, salt and pepper. Cover for 3 to 4 minutes, until the liver is completely cooked.
Check that the thickest strips reach 74 °C and serve immediately with the small amount of sauce.
tips: Avoid prolonged cooking after the liver reaches the required temperature, so it does not become tough.

title: Cuban stovetop pot roast
description: A beef roast browned and slowly braised over a bed of onions.
steps: Rub the beef with crushed garlic, oregano, salt and pepper. Brown in a heavy pot with the oil for 10 minutes.
Remove the meat; add the onion strips and carrot rounds and sauté for 7 minutes.
Pour in the sour orange juice and stock, scrape the bottom and add the bay leaf. Return the meat to the pot.
Cover and cook at a very gentle simmer for about 2 and a half hours, turning several times, until a fork slides in without resistance.
Let the meat rest for 10 minutes. Remove the bay leaf, reduce the juices if needed and slice the beef against the grain to serve.
tips: Choose a cut for braising with some connective tissue, rather than a lean steak cut.

title: Roast pork with pineapple
description: Pork shoulder pieces roasted with pineapple, bell pepper and a citrus marinade.
steps: Mix the pork with crushed garlic, sour orange juice, cumin, oil, salt and pepper. Refrigerate for one hour.
Heat the oven to 180 °C. Place the chopped onion and bell pepper in a roasting dish, then add the pork, its marinade and the water.
Cover with aluminum foil and roast for 70 minutes. Check that the meat is beginning to become tender.
Add the pineapple, stir it through the juices and roast uncovered for another 25 to 30 minutes, until the pork is browned and tender.
Let rest for 5 minutes, adjust the salt in the juices and serve, dividing the pineapple among the plates.
tips: Adding the pineapple at the end helps it hold its shape instead of falling apart during roasting.

title: Tasajo with sofrito (Salt-cured shredded beef)
description: Salt-cured beef, soaked and shredded, with bell peppers and tomatoes.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: plus extra for soaking out the salt

steps: Rinse the tasajo and cover generously with cold water. Soak out the salt for 24 hours in the refrigerator, changing the water at least four times; follow the label if it calls for longer.
Drain and gently simmer in fresh water for 90 to 120 minutes, until tender. Taste a small cooked piece; if it is still very salty, change the water and continue cooking.
Remove fat and tough fibers and shred the meat. Reserve 200 ml of the cooking water only if it is not salty.
Sauté the sliced onion and bell peppers in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, oregano, cumin and tomatoes and cook for another 8 minutes.
Add the tasajo and 200 ml of the reserved liquid or fresh water. Cook for 15 to 20 minutes, until the sofrito clings to the strands of beef.
tips: Do not add salt at the start; the saltiness of tasajo varies by product.

title: Aporreado de res (Tender beef in tomato sauce)
description: Cooked beef, gently pounded and simmered in a mild tomato sauce.
steps: Cover the beef with the water and add one cut-up onion and salt. Simmer gently for about 100 minutes, until tender.
Reserve 250 ml of the cooking liquid. Gently pound the cooked meat with a clean mallet and pull it into short shreds.
Chop the remaining onion and the bell pepper; sauté in the oil for 7 minutes, then add the chopped garlic.
Add the tomatoes, paprika, oregano and reserved cooking liquid. Simmer gently for 10 minutes to make an evenly blended sauce.
Stir in the meat and cook for another 20 minutes, stirring so it absorbs the flavor. Adjust the salt and pepper and serve with plenty of sauce.
tips: Unlike a dry sauté, this version keeps a generous amount of sauce.

title: Goat chilindrón (Tomato and pepper stew)
description: Tender goat in a red sauce of bell peppers, tomatoes and wine.
steps: Marinate the goat with sour orange juice, three garlic cloves, cumin, salt and pepper. Refrigerate for four hours.
Drain and pat lightly dry. Brown the meat in the oil in batches and set aside.
Sauté the chopped onion, bell peppers and remaining garlic for 8 minutes. Add the wine and cook for 3 minutes, scraping up the browned juices.
Add the tomatoes, water, oregano, bay leaf and meat. Cover and cook at a very gentle simmer for 2 and a half to 3 hours, until the meat comes away from the bone.
Check the liquid during cooking. At the end, remove the bay leaf, reduce the sauce uncovered and adjust the seasoning.
tips: The age and cut of the goat can greatly affect cooking time; judge by tenderness as well as the clock.

title: Beef tongue in Cuban-style sauce
description: Tender beef tongue, sliced and finished in a sofrito sauce.
steps: Place the tongue in a pot with enough water, one cut-up onion, one bay leaf and salt. Simmer gently for 2 and a half to 3 hours.
When a knife slides in easily, remove the tongue and let it cool just enough to handle. Peel off the thick outer skin while it is still warm.
Reserve 300 ml of the cooking liquid and slice the tongue one centimeter thick, trimming away the tough part at the base.
Sauté the chopped remaining onion, bell pepper and garlic in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the tomatoes, oregano, remaining bay leaf and cooking liquid; cook for 10 minutes.
Place the tongue slices and olives in the sauce. Cook over low heat for 20 minutes, remove the bay leaf and adjust the salt.
tips: The skin is easier to remove while the tongue is warm; use tongs and take care not to burn yourself with the steam.

title: Rabbit fricassee
description: Rabbit pieces stewed with potatoes, tomatoes and olives.
steps: Marinate the rabbit with the juice, two garlic cloves, oregano and salt. Refrigerate for two hours.
Drain and brown the pieces in a pot with the oil. Remove them and sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper and remaining garlic.
Add the tomatoes and wine and boil for 3 minutes. Return the rabbit and add the water, then cover and simmer gently for 50 minutes.
Peel the potatoes, cut into pieces and add with the olives. Cook for another 25 to 30 minutes, until the potatoes and rabbit are tender.
Check that the thickest part reaches 71 °C, adjust the salt and reduce the sauce for a few minutes if needed.
tips: Buy rabbit from an approved supplier, already cut into pieces, to avoid bone splinters from cutting it at home.

title: Pork loin stuffed with ham and prunes
description: Butterflied pork loin, stuffed and roasted for a savory and sweet contrast.
steps: Lay the butterflied loin flat and season with crushed garlic, oregano, salt and pepper. Spread the ham and prunes over it, leaving the edges clear.
Roll up from the long side and tie firmly with kitchen twine. Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Arrange sliced onion in a roasting dish, set the loin on top and add the juices, oil and water.
Cover and roast for 45 minutes. Uncover and continue for another 20 to 30 minutes, until the center of the filling reaches 74 °C.
Let rest for 10 minutes, remove all the twine and serve in slices with the boiled pan juices.
tips: The filling changes the temperature needed for cooking; measure in the center of the roll.

title: Chicken fricassee
description: Chicken stewed with potatoes and olives in a tomato and wine sauce.
steps: Marinate the chicken with sour orange juice, two garlic cloves, cumin and salt. Cover and refrigerate for one hour.
Drain the chicken and brown in a pot with the oil for 8 minutes. Remove it and sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper and remaining garlic.
Add the tomatoes, wine, water and oregano; return the chicken and simmer gently, covered, for 20 minutes.
Peel the potatoes, cut into 3 cm cubes and add with the olives. Cook for another 25 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Check that the chicken reaches 74 °C close to the bone without touching it. Reduce uncovered for a few minutes if you prefer a thicker sauce and adjust the salt.
tips: Do not add the potatoes at the start, so they keep their shape.

title: Mojo roast chicken
description: Whole chicken roasted with garlic, oregano and citrus.
steps: Pat the chicken dry with paper towels without washing it. Mix the crushed garlic, sour orange juice, oil, oregano, cumin, salt and pepper.
Rub the chicken on the outside and under the breast skin without tearing it. Cover and refrigerate for four hours.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Place the onion in a roasting dish with the water and set the chicken on top, breast side up.
Roast for 85 to 100 minutes, basting once with the juices; cover the breast loosely if it browns too much.
Check for 74 °C in the thickest parts of the breast and thigh without touching bone. Let rest for 10 minutes before carving.
tips: A larger chicken takes longer; use the thermometer to decide when to remove it from the oven.

title: Griddled chicken cutlets
description: Thin, juicy chicken breast with sautéed onion and lemon.
steps: If the cutlets are thick, slice them horizontally. Marinate with garlic, lemon juice, oregano, salt and pepper and refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Cut the onion into strips and sauté in one tablespoon of oil for 6 minutes. Set aside.
Drain the chicken and pat it lightly dry. Heat the remaining oil on a griddle or in a skillet.
Cook for 3 to 5 minutes per side, depending on thickness, until the centers of the cutlets reach 74 °C.
Spoon the onion over the chicken and serve immediately with the pan juices.
tips: Even thickness helps all the cutlets cook at the same rate.

title: Chicken vaca frita (Crispy shredded chicken)
description: Shredded chicken with crisp edges and lemony onion.
steps: Cook the chicken in the water with one cut-up onion, bay leaf and salt for about 20 minutes, until it reaches 74 °C.
Drain and shred. Mix with the crushed garlic, sour orange juice and cumin and refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Cut the other onion into strips and sauté in one tablespoon of oil until lightly browned; set aside.
Drain the shredded chicken and spread it in the skillet with the remaining oil. Cook in batches, letting it brown before moving it.
Once crisp edges appear, add the onion and heat everything to 74 °C. Adjust the salt and serve.
tips: You can use chicken cooked the previous day if it has been kept properly refrigerated; reheat it thoroughly.

title: Cuban-style fried chicken
description: Boneless chicken thighs marinated in citrus and fried without breading.

ingredients.name: oil
ingredients.note: for frying; not all of it is consumed

steps: Cut each thigh into two or three evenly sized pieces. Mix with the crushed garlic, juice, cumin, oregano, salt and pepper.
Cover and refrigerate for two hours. Drain thoroughly and pat the surface dry with paper towels to limit splattering.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to approximately 170 °C, keeping the pot no more than half full.
Fry the chicken in batches for 8 to 12 minutes, turning so it browns evenly; the center must reach 74 °C.
Use tongs to transfer the chicken to a rack or paper towels. Let the oil return to temperature between batches and serve hot.
tips: The cooking time is for boneless thighs; do not substitute bone-in pieces without increasing the cooking time.

title: Cuban-style barbecue chicken
description: Stovetop chicken in a homemade butter, soy sauce and lemon sauce.
steps: Marinate the chicken with sour orange juice, crushed garlic and pepper; refrigerate for 30 minutes. Do not add salt yet.
Melt the butter over medium heat in a pot. Drain the chicken and brown for 3 minutes per side without burning the butter.
Add the chopped onion and sauté for 4 minutes. Mix the soy sauce, lemon juice and water and pour around the chicken.
Cover and simmer gently for 25 to 30 minutes, turning halfway through, until the chicken reaches 74 °C.
Uncover for 5 minutes to thicken the sauce slightly. Taste before deciding whether it needs salt and serve with the juices.
tips: This stovetop version does not use a grill; the name reflects its use in Cuban home cooking.

title: Beer-braised chicken
description: Browned chicken braised with pale lager and onions.
steps: Pat the chicken dry and season with cumin, salt and pepper. Brown in the oil for 8 minutes and set aside.
Sauté the onions and bell pepper, cut into strips, for 7 minutes. Add the chopped garlic and tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the beer and bay leaf and return the chicken. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat.
Cover and cook for 30 minutes; then uncover for 5 to 10 minutes to reduce the sauce and check that the chicken reaches 74 °C.
Remove the bay leaf, adjust the seasoning and serve with the onion and bell pepper.
tips: If you prefer to avoid alcohol, replace the beer with the same amount of stock; this also changes the flavor.

title: Chicken and okra stew
description: Chicken stew with tender okra and tomato sauce.
steps: Pat the chicken dry, season with salt and cumin and brown in two tablespoons of oil; set aside.
Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper and garlic for 7 minutes. Add the tomatoes, water and oregano and return the chicken.
Cover and simmer gently for 25 minutes. Meanwhile, wash the okra, dry it thoroughly and trim only the tough ends.
Sauté the okra in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, then add to the stew with the lemon juice. Cook for another 15 minutes without stirring too much.
Check that the chicken reaches 74 °C and the okra is tender. Adjust the salt and serve with the sauce.
tips: Drying the okra and cooking it whole helps control its slippery texture.

title: Chicken breasts stuffed with ham and cheese
description: Chicken breasts opened, stuffed and baked with a garlic and lemon marinade.
steps: Cut a pocket into the side of each breast without separating the halves. Season inside and out with garlic, lemon juice, oregano, salt and pepper.
Divide the ham and cheese among the pockets and secure with toothpicks, counting how many you use.
Brown the breasts for 2 minutes per side in a skillet with the oil. Preheat the oven to 190 °C.
Place in a baking dish with the water and bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the center of the filling reaches 74 °C.
Let rest for 5 minutes and remove every toothpick before serving with the pan juices.
tips: Do not overfill the pockets: this helps keep the cheese inside and allows the chicken to cook evenly.

title: Breaded chicken cutlets
description: Chicken cutlets with a light breadcrumb coating.

ingredients.name: oil
ingredients.note: for frying; not all of it is consumed

steps: Marinate the cutlets with crushed garlic, lemon juice, salt and pepper and refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Prepare three dishes with flour, beaten eggs and breadcrumbs. Drain the chicken and coat each cutlet in that order.
Heat a layer of oil to about 170 °C. Add only a few cutlets at a time so the temperature does not drop too far.
Fry for 4 to 5 minutes per side, depending on thickness, until the center reaches 74 °C and the coating is golden.
Drain on a rack and serve immediately; do not cover the cutlets, as steam softens the breading.
tips: If the cutlets are more than one centimeter thick, slice them horizontally before breading.

title: Chicken meatballs in Cuban-style sauce
description: Tender ground-chicken meatballs in a tomato and bell pepper sauce.
steps: Mix the chicken, egg, breadcrumbs, one grated garlic clove, parsley and salt. Shape into 16 meatballs with damp hands.
Chop the onion, bell pepper and remaining garlic. Sauté in the oil for 7 minutes, until the onion becomes translucent.
Add the tomatoes, water and oregano and bring to a gentle simmer. Arrange the meatballs in a single layer.
Cover and cook for 20 minutes, turning carefully halfway through; check that the centers of the largest meatballs reach 74 °C.
Uncover for a few minutes if the sauce is too thin and adjust the salt before serving.
tips: Keep the simmer gentle so the meatballs do not break apart.

title: Cuban-style turkey picadillo
description: Ground turkey with olives and tomato sofrito for an everyday meal.
steps: Chop the onion, bell pepper and garlic. Heat the oil and sauté the onion and bell pepper for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin and oregano. Stir in the turkey and break it up with a spoon as it cooks for 8 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, water, sliced olives and raisins. Stir and partially cover.
Cook over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring to prevent sticking; check that it reaches 74 °C.
Adjust the salt and let rest off the heat for a few minutes so the sauce settles before serving.
tips: Turkey is lean: keep a little sauce so the picadillo does not become dry.

title: Mojo-roasted turkey breast
description: Turkey breast roasted with garlic and citrus, ready to carve into slices.
steps: Crush the garlic, salt, oregano and cumin and mix with the juice, oil and pepper.
Rub the breast all over and refrigerate, covered, for four hours. Preheat the oven to 175 °C.
Cover the bottom of a roasting dish with onion strips, add the water and set the turkey breast and its marinade on top.
Roast for 80 to 100 minutes, covering loosely if it browns too soon, until the center reaches 74 °C.
Let rest for 10 minutes before slicing against the grain. Boil the pan juices for 5 minutes and serve them separately.
tips: A bone-in breast needs a different cooking time; this recipe is designed for a boneless breast.

title: Cuban-style chicken with garden vegetables
description: Chicken stewed with carrots, peas and small potatoes.
steps: Season the chicken with salt and brown in the oil for 8 minutes; set aside.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic, add the tomatoes, water, bay leaf and oregano, then return the chicken.
Cover and cook for 20 minutes. Peel the potatoes and carrot and cut into similarly sized pieces.
Add the potatoes and carrot and simmer for 20 minutes; add the peas during the last 5 minutes.
Check that the chicken reaches 74 °C and the vegetables are tender. Remove the bay leaf and adjust the salt.
tips: Peas need little cooking and keep their color better when added at the end.

title: Chicken with peanut and sofrito sauce
description: A home-style chicken dish in a creamy roasted-peanut and tomato sauce.
steps: Blend the peanuts with 200 ml of the water until creamy. Cut the chicken into 3 cm pieces and season with salt and cumin.
Brown the chicken in the oil for 7 minutes. Remove it and sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper and garlic for 6 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the peanut cream and remaining water and mix well.
Return the chicken, partially cover and simmer very gently for 20 minutes, stirring the bottom to prevent sticking; check that it reaches 74 °C.
Add the lemon juice, adjust the salt and thin with a little water if the sauce is too thick.
tips: Use roasted peanuts without added sugar; this is a home-style variation, not a dish with a specific regional name.

title: Sautéed chicken with pineapple and peppers
description: Chicken pieces with browned pineapple, bell peppers and a light citrus sauce.
steps: Cut the chicken and pineapple into 2 cm cubes. Cut the onion and bell peppers into squares and chop the garlic.
Brown the pineapple in one tablespoon of oil for 3 minutes and remove. Add another tablespoon and sauté the chicken in batches for 6 to 8 minutes.
Cook the onion and bell peppers in the remaining oil for 5 minutes; add the garlic for the last minute.
Return the chicken and pineapple, add the orange and lemon juices and simmer gently for 3 minutes; check that the chicken reaches 74 °C.
Dissolve the cornstarch in the cold water and stir it in. Cook for one minute, stirring, then adjust the salt and serve.
tips: Leave the vegetables slightly firm to contrast with the pineapple and chicken.

title: Chicken stew with sweet corn
description: Chicken in a sofrito sauce with corn kernels and pumpkin.
steps: Season the chicken with salt and cumin and brown in a pot with the oil; set aside.
Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper and garlic for 7 minutes. Add the tomatoes, oregano and water.
Return the chicken and simmer gently, covered, for 25 minutes. Cut the pumpkin into 3 cm cubes.
Add the pumpkin and corn and cook for another 15 to 20 minutes, until the pumpkin is tender and the chicken reaches 74 °C.
Remove a few pumpkin cubes, mash them and return them to the stew if you want to thicken it. Adjust the salt before serving.
tips: You can add frozen corn directly; if using canned corn, drain it and add during the last 5 minutes.

title: Stovetop orange chicken
description: Chicken thighs in an orange, onion and garlic sauce.
steps: Pat the chicken dry and season with salt, pepper and oregano. Brown in the oil for 4 minutes per side and remove.
Sauté the sliced onion for 6 minutes. Add the chopped garlic and stir for half a minute.
Pour in the juices and water and return the chicken to the pot. Cover and lower the heat once it begins to boil.
Cook for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until the centers of the pieces reach 74 °C.
Uncover and reduce the sauce for 5 minutes. Adjust the salt and serve with the onion.
tips: Taste the oranges before cooking; if they are very sweet, the lemon balances the sauce.

title: Cuban-style garlic chicken
description: Small chicken pieces browned with plenty of garlic and dry wine.
steps: Cut the chicken into 3 cm pieces and season with salt, pepper and oregano. Peel the garlic cloves and lightly crush them.
Heat the oil over medium heat, brown the garlic for 2 minutes and remove before it burns.
Brown the chicken in batches for about 8 minutes. Return all the chicken to the skillet with the garlic.
Add the wine and water and cook, covered, for 15 to 20 minutes, until the center of the chicken reaches 74 °C.
Uncover, add the lemon juice and parsley and reduce for 3 minutes. Serve with the softened garlic and juices.
tips: The garlic should be light golden; burnt garlic makes the entire sauce bitter.

title: Cuban-style braised hen
description: Stewing hen slowly cooked in sofrito until the meat is tender.
steps: Marinate the hen with sour orange juice, three crushed garlic cloves, cumin and salt; refrigerate for one hour.
Drain the pieces and brown in a pot with the oil. Remove them and sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper and remaining garlic.
Add the tomatoes, water, oregano and bay leaf and return the hen. Cover and maintain a gentle simmer for about 2 and a half hours.
Check the liquid every 40 minutes and add hot water if needed. Continue until the hen is tender and has exceeded 74 °C.
Uncover and reduce the sauce for 10 to 15 minutes; remove the bay leaf and adjust the salt before serving.
tips: A stewing hen usually needs much longer than a young chicken; do not use the same cooking time for both.

title: Enchilado de camarones (Cuban shrimp in tomato sauce)
description: Shrimp in a Cuban-style sauce of tomatoes, bell pepper and dry wine.
steps: Keep the shrimp refrigerated while you prepare the sauce. Chop the onion, bell pepper and garlic.
Sauté the onion and bell pepper in the oil for 7 minutes; add the garlic and cook for half a minute.
Add the tomatoes, wine, water, bay leaf, oregano and hot sauce. Simmer gently for 12 minutes to thicken.
Add the shrimp in a single layer and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, turning, until all the flesh is opaque and pearly.
Remove the bay leaf, adjust the salt and serve immediately with plenty of sauce.
tips: The hot sauce is optional and is best added a little at a time.

title: Lobster in Cuban-style tomato sauce
description: Lobster meat gently cooked in a red sofrito sauce.
steps: Cut the lobster into medallions about 3 cm thick and keep chilled. Chop the onion, bell peppers and garlic.
Sauté the onion and bell peppers in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and paprika and stir without letting them burn.
Add the tomatoes, wine, water, bay leaf and hot sauce. Simmer gently for 15 minutes, until the tomatoes lose their raw flavor.
Add the lobster and cook for 6 to 9 minutes, depending on thickness, until the center is white and opaque.
Remove the bay leaf and adjust the salt. Serve immediately, avoiding further boiling once the lobster is cooked.
tips: The listed quantity is for cleaned meat, not the weight of lobster tails with their shells.

title: Fish escabeche (Fish in a vinegar marinade)
description: Cooked fish topped with onion, carrot and a mild vinegar marinade.
steps: Pat the fish dry and salt lightly. Cook in a skillet with two tablespoons of oil for about 3 to 4 minutes per side, until it reaches 63 °C.
Place the portions in a clean, shallow container. Slice the onion and carrot thinly.
Heat the remaining oil and sauté the onion, carrot and sliced garlic for 7 minutes. Add the vinegar, water, bay leaf, pepper and a pinch of salt.
Boil the marinade for 6 minutes and pour over the fish. Let the strongest steam subside, then refrigerate rather than leaving it out for hours.
Refrigerate for at least two hours to blend the flavors. Remove the bay leaf and serve cold with the vegetables.
tips: This is a refrigerated dish, not a preserve for storage at room temperature.

title: Oven-roasted snapper with mojo
description: Whole snapper roasted on onions with garlic and sour orange.

ingredients.name: whole cleaned snapper
ingredients.note: 2 fish weighing about 800 g each, gutted and scaled

steps: Pat the snappers dry and make two shallow cuts on each side. Mix the garlic, juice, oil, oregano, salt and pepper.
Rub the fish inside and out and refrigerate for 15 minutes. Preheat the oven to 190 °C.
Arrange the sliced onion in a roasting dish, add the water and set the snappers and their marinade on top.
Roast for 30 to 40 minutes, depending on thickness, until the flesh beside the backbone reaches 63 °C without the thermometer touching the bone.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve in portions, carefully removing the backbone and small bones.
tips: Ask the fishmonger to clean the fish; check the portions for bones again when serving.

title: Breaded fish fillets
description: Fish fillets with a crisp breadcrumb coating and a hint of lemon.

ingredients.name: oil
ingredients.note: for frying; not all of it is consumed

steps: Check that no bones remain. Season the fish with garlic, lemon juice, salt and pepper and refrigerate for 10 minutes.
Drain well and prepare three dishes with flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs.
Coat each fillet first in flour, then egg and finally breadcrumbs, pressing gently.
Fry in a layer of oil at about 170 °C for 3 to 4 minutes per side; check that the center reaches 63 °C.
Drain on a rack and serve immediately, without stacking the fillets, to keep them crisp.
tips: Very thin fillets cook more quickly; remove each one as soon as it is ready.

title: Fish in Cuban-style sauce
description: Fish fillets simmered in a tomato and bell pepper sauce.
steps: Cut the onion and bell peppers into strips and chop the garlic. Check the fish for bones and season with salt and pepper.
Sauté the onion and bell peppers in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and oregano and cook for half a minute.
Add the tomatoes and water and cook for 12 minutes, until the sauce is slightly thickened.
Arrange the fish in a single layer, cover and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until it reaches 63 °C, shaking the pot gently without breaking the fillets.
Add the lemon juice, adjust the salt in the sauce and serve with a wide spatula.
tips: Use a wide pot so the portions do not overlap.

title: Aporreado de bacalao (Flaked salt cod in sofrito)
description: Salt cod, soaked and flaked, with onion, bell pepper and tomatoes.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: plus extra for soaking out the salt

steps: Cover the cod with cold water and soak out the salt in the refrigerator for 24 hours, changing the water several times; adjust the time according to the label and the thickness.
Drain and simmer gently in fresh water for about 5 minutes, until it reaches 63 °C. Reserve 150 ml of the liquid only if it is not too salty.
Carefully remove the skin and bones and break the cod into small flakes.
Sauté the chopped onion and bell pepper in the oil for 8 minutes; add the garlic, tomatoes and oregano and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the cod and 150 ml of the reserved liquid or fresh water. Cook for 8 minutes, sprinkle with parsley and taste before adding salt.
tips: Flaked salt cod takes less time to soak than a thick loin; do not use the same soaking time for both products.

title: Cuban-style salt cod with potatoes
description: Soaked salt cod and potatoes in a thick tomato sauce.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: plus extra for soaking out the salt

steps: Soak the cod loins, covered with water, in the refrigerator for about 36 hours, changing the water every 8 hours; follow the package instructions if they call for longer.
Peel the potatoes and cut into thick slices. Chop the onion, bell pepper and garlic and sauté in the oil for 8 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, water, bay leaf and potatoes. Cover and simmer gently for 20 to 25 minutes, until the potatoes are almost tender.
Place the drained cod and olives on top. Cover and cook for 8 to 12 minutes, until the fish reaches 63 °C.
Remove the bay leaf, check for bones and taste the sauce before deciding whether it needs salt.
tips: If the potatoes absorb a lot of liquid, add hot water before adding the fish.

title: Garlic shrimp
description: Shrimp quickly sautéed with garlic, oil and lemon.
steps: Pat the shrimp dry with paper towels and keep chilled until cooking. Slice the garlic thinly.
Heat the oil over medium heat and cook the garlic for 1 to 2 minutes, until fragrant without darkening.
Add the shrimp in a single layer; cook for 2 minutes on one side, then turn with tongs.
Cook for another 1 to 3 minutes, until the centers are opaque and pearly. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove from the heat, stir in the lemon juice and parsley and serve with the flavored oil.
tips: If the skillet is small, cook in two batches so the shrimp do not boil in their own liquid.

title: Shrimp in coconut milk
description: Shrimp cooked in a mild coconut, tomato and bell pepper sauce.
steps: Chop the onion, bell pepper and garlic. Pat the shrimp dry and keep refrigerated while you prepare the sauce.
Sauté the onion and bell pepper in the oil for 7 minutes; add the garlic and cumin for half a minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes. Pour in the coconut milk and simmer very gently for 7 minutes.
Add the shrimp and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, until completely opaque and pearly.
Remove from the heat, stir in the lemon juice and cilantro and adjust the salt. Serve without boiling the shrimp any longer.
tips: Use unsweetened coconut milk for cooking; sweet coconut cream for drinks changes the result.

title: Crab in Cuban-style tomato sauce
description: Crab meat in a Cuban-style tomato and bell pepper sauce.
steps: Check the crab meat with clean fingers and remove any shell fragments. Keep chilled.
Sauté the chopped onion and bell pepper in the oil for 7 minutes; add the garlic and stir for one minute.
Add the tomatoes, wine, water, bay leaf and hot sauce. Simmer gently for 15 minutes, until the sauce thickens.
Add the crab and stir carefully to keep the pieces intact. Heat for 5 to 7 minutes, until it reaches 74 °C.
Remove the bay leaf, add the parsley and taste before adding salt; the crab may already be salted.
tips: This recipe starts with cooked crab meat, not live or raw crabs.

title: Spanish mackerel steaks with mojo
description: Pan-browned fish steaks with a quick garlic and onion mojo.
steps: Check for bones and pat the fish steaks dry. Season with salt, pepper and oregano and refrigerate for 10 minutes.
Heat two tablespoons of oil and cook the fish for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until it reaches 63 °C. Transfer to a serving dish.
Sauté the onion strips and sliced garlic in the remaining oil for 6 minutes.
Add the sour orange juice and water and boil for 2 minutes, gently scraping the bottom of the skillet.
Pour the hot mojo over the fish and serve, letting diners know the steaks still contain the central bone.
tips: You can use another firm fish cut into steaks of the same thickness, checking that it is properly cooked.

title: Fish pisto (Flaked fish with tomato and peppers)
description: Flaked fish folded into a tomato and bell pepper sofrito.
steps: Cook the fish in barely simmering water with a pinch of salt for 5 to 8 minutes, until it reaches 63 °C.
Drain, reserve 100 ml of the cooking liquid and flake the fish, removing every bone you find.
Sauté the chopped onion and bell peppers in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, tomatoes and oregano and cook for another 10 minutes.
Add the fish and reserved cooking liquid and cook for 5 minutes, stirring gently to distribute the flakes.
Add the lemon juice, adjust the salt and serve with some sauce, without reducing it until dry.
tips: Flake the fish after cooking so it is easier to spot the bones.

title: Fresh sardines with tomatoes
description: Cleaned sardines cooked in a tomato, garlic and onion sauce.
steps: Check that the sardines are clean and remove any visible bones. Keep refrigerated.
Sauté the chopped onion in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for half a minute.
Add the tomatoes, water, vinegar, bay leaf and oregano. Simmer gently for 15 minutes and season.
Lay the butterflied sardines over the sauce, cover and cook for 7 to 10 minutes, until they reach 63 °C.
Remove the bay leaf and serve with a wide spatula to keep the sardines intact.
tips: Ask the fishmonger to butterfly the sardines and remove the backbones; still check for small bones.

title: Squid in its ink
description: Squid slowly stewed in a dark sauce of squid ink and sofrito.
steps: Cut the squid bodies into rings and halve any large tentacles. Chop the onions and garlic.
Sauté the onion in the oil for 10 minutes over medium-low heat. Add the garlic and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the squid and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in the wine and boil for another 2 minutes.
Dissolve the ink in the water and add with the bay leaf. Cover and simmer gently for 30 to 40 minutes, until the squid is tender and thoroughly cooked.
Uncover for the last few minutes if the sauce needs thickening. Remove the bay leaf and taste before adding salt, since the ink may already contain it.
tips: Use commercially packaged squid ink stored according to its label, and avoid staining porous surfaces.

title: Squid stew with bell peppers
description: Tender squid rings in a tomato and bell pepper sauce.
steps: Cut the squid into wide rings. Slice the onion and bell peppers into strips and chop the garlic.
Sauté the vegetables in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and paprika and stir briefly.
Add the squid and cook for 3 minutes. Stir in the wine, tomatoes, water and bay leaf.
Cover and maintain a gentle simmer for 35 to 40 minutes, until the squid is tender; add a little water if the sauce dries out.
Remove the bay leaf, adjust the salt and reduce the sauce uncovered for a few minutes before serving.
tips: Squid becomes tough during the middle stage of cooking; continue simmering gently until it becomes tender again.

title: Octopus and potato stew
description: Octopus cooked until tender, then finished with potatoes and sofrito.
steps: Bring the water to a boil with one cut-up onion. Add the cleaned octopus and simmer gently for 45 to 60 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Reserve 600 ml of the cooking liquid and cut the octopus into pieces. Peel the potatoes and cut into large cubes.
Sauté the chopped remaining onion, bell pepper and garlic in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the paprika, tomatoes and bay leaf and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes and reserved cooking liquid and cook, covered, for about 25 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Add the octopus and cook for another 8 minutes to blend the flavors and heat thoroughly. Remove the bay leaf and adjust the salt at the end.
tips: Octopus shrinks considerably during cooking; the listed weight is for the cleaned raw product.

title: Tuna with onions and sour orange
description: Thoroughly cooked tuna served with onion and a quick citrus sauce.
steps: Pat the tuna dry and season with salt, pepper and oregano. Cut the onion into strips and slice the garlic.
Sauté the onion in two tablespoons of oil for 8 minutes; add the garlic, juice and water and boil for 2 minutes. Set aside.
Heat the remaining oil and cook the tuna for 3 to 4 minutes per side, adjusting for thickness.
Return the onion and juices and cook briefly until the center of the fish reaches 63 °C.
Serve immediately, covered with the onion, to help keep the tuna moist.
tips: This recipe calls for fully cooked tuna, without a raw or partly raw center.

title: Fish with okra
description: White fish and okra in a light Cuban-style sauce.
steps: Wash and dry the okra; trim only the tough ends. Cut the fish into large portions and check for bones.
Sauté the chopped onion and bell pepper in two tablespoons of oil for 7 minutes; add the garlic, tomatoes, water and oregano.
Cook the sauce for 10 minutes. Meanwhile, sauté the okra in the remaining oil for 4 minutes.
Add the okra and lemon juice to the sauce and cook for 5 minutes. Arrange the fish in the pot, cover and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until it reaches 63 °C.
Adjust the salt and serve, handling gently to keep the portions intact and preserve the okra's texture.
tips: Choose a firm-fleshed fish that will hold together while cooking in the sauce.

title: Griddled lobster with garlic and lemon
description: Split lobster tails cooked on a griddle with garlic butter.
steps: Split the tails lengthwise with sturdy kitchen shears and remove the intestinal tract. Pat the meat dry and season lightly.
Melt the butter gently with the chopped garlic for 2 minutes; remove from the heat and mix in the lemon juice and parsley.
Heat a griddle over medium-high heat and brush with oil. Place the tails flesh side down for 3 minutes.
Turn the tails shell side down, brush with some of the butter and cook, covered, for another 6 to 9 minutes, until the flesh is white and opaque all the way to the center.
Serve immediately with the remaining butter in a clean dish; use a clean spoon so it is not contaminated by the raw meat.
tips: Large tails may need more time; check doneness in the thickest part.

title: Fluffy white rice
description: A simple staple of the Cuban table, with separate grains and a hint of garlic.
steps: Rinse the rice in a strainer until the water runs almost clear, then drain well.
Heat the oil in a saucepan with a lid. Crush the garlic, gently brown it for one minute, then remove it.
Add the rice, stir for one minute, then pour in the water and add the salt. Bring to a boil.
Once boiling, cover and turn the heat down to its lowest setting. Cook for 18 to 20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Turn off the heat, leave covered for ten minutes, then fluff the grains with a fork before serving.
tips: Always use the same variety of rice; some types need a little more water.

title: Eastern Cuban congrí with red beans
description: Rice cooked in red bean broth with sofrito and small pieces of bacon.
steps: Rinse and drain the rice. Finely chop the bell pepper and garlic; set the cooked beans aside without crushing them.
Brown the bacon in the oil for five minutes. Add the onion and bell pepper and sauté for another five minutes.
Stir in the garlic, cumin and oregano for thirty seconds. Add the rice and cook, stirring, for one minute.
Pour in the measured broth, then add the beans, bay leaf and salt. Once boiling, cover and cook on the lowest heat for about twenty minutes.
Check that the liquid has been absorbed. Turn off the heat, leave covered for ten minutes, remove the bay leaf and stir gently.
tips: Red beans distinguish this version from black bean rice; family names for the dishes vary.
If the broth is already salted, reduce the added salt.

title: Moros y cristianos — black beans and rice
description: Rice and black beans finish cooking together so the grains absorb the dark bean broth.
steps: Wash and drain the rice. Chop the onion, bell pepper and garlic; measure the beans and their broth separately.
Sauté the onion and bell pepper in the oil over medium heat for six minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin, oregano and bay leaf. Stir for half a minute, then add the rice and cook, stirring, for another minute.
Add the broth, beans and salt. Bring to a boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat for approximately twenty minutes.
Turn off the heat when the rice is tender. Let stand for ten minutes, remove the bay leaf, then drizzle in the vinegar as you fluff the grains.
tips: For a deep color, use the beans' cooking broth rather than plain water.

title: Cuban-style yellow rice
description: Golden rice with a mild sofrito, perfect alongside meat, fish or vegetables.
steps: Wash and drain the rice. Finely dice the onion and bell pepper and chop the garlic.
Heat the oil and sauté the onion and bell pepper for five minutes, until softened.
Add the garlic, turmeric and cumin. Stir in the rice to distribute the color evenly.
Pour in the hot stock, add the salt and stir in the peas. Once boiling, cover and cook on the lowest heat for twenty minutes.
Let stand off the heat for ten minutes, then fluff with a fork without crushing the peas.
tips: Stock may already contain salt; taste it before seasoning.

title: Cuban chicken and rice
description: Browned chicken, yellow rice and sofrito cook together in a family-sized pot.
steps: Pat the chicken dry, season with half the salt and brown it in the oil for eight minutes, turning it. Set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the chopped onion and bell pepper for five minutes; add the garlic, cumin and oregano.
Add the tomatoes and cook for four minutes. Return the chicken to the pot, pour in the stock and simmer for twenty minutes.
Add the rinsed rice, turmeric, peas and remaining salt. Spread everything evenly without piling up the chicken.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat for twenty minutes, until the rice absorbs the stock and the thickest part of the chicken reaches 74 °C.
Turn off the heat, arrange the roasted bell pepper on top and leave covered for ten minutes before serving.
tips: Use a wide pot; a layer of rice that is too deep will cook unevenly.

title: Arroz imperial — layered chicken and rice bake
description: Layers of yellow rice, shredded chicken, mayonnaise and cheese, baked until golden for sharing.
steps: Cook the rice in the stock with the turmeric and salt: bring to a boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat for about twenty minutes.
Sauté the chopped onion and bell pepper in the oil for six minutes. Add the garlic and tomatoes and reduce for eight minutes.
Stir in the shredded chicken and peas and cook for five minutes. The filling should be moist without loose liquid.
Heat the oven to 190 °C. Spread half the rice in a baking dish measuring about 23 × 33 cm and spread over half the mayonnaise.
Cover with the chicken, some of the cheese and the remaining rice. Spread over the rest of the mayonnaise and finish with the remaining cheese.
Bake for about twenty minutes, until the center reaches 74 °C and the cheese is golden. Let stand for ten minutes before cutting.
tips: Fluff the rice with a fork before assembling the layers; do not pack it down too firmly.

title: Arroz con pollo a la chorrera — brothy chicken and rice
description: A creamy, brothy version of chicken and rice, finished with beer and bell peppers.
steps: Pat the chicken dry, season it and brown it on all sides in the oil for eight minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper and garlic; add the tomatoes, cumin and turmeric and cook down for five minutes.
Return the chicken, add the stock and simmer for twenty-five minutes, until almost tender.
Add the rice and beer. Cook over medium-low heat for twenty to twenty-five minutes, stirring gently several times.
Add the peas during the last five minutes. Check that the chicken reaches 74 °C and that some creamy broth remains.
Arrange the roasted bell pepper on top, let stand for five minutes and serve in deep bowls; the rice will continue absorbing liquid.
tips: For an alcohol-free version, replace all the beer with stock; cooking does not guarantee that all the alcohol will evaporate.

title: Mojo pork and rice
description: Rice with diced pork and a sofrito scented with orange and garlic.
steps: Mix the pork with the citrus juices, crushed garlic, cumin and half a teaspoon of salt. Refrigerate for twenty minutes.
Drain the meat, reserving the marinade. Brown it in batches in the oil, then add the chopped onion and bell pepper.
Pour in the reserved marinade and 250 ml of the stock, add the oregano and simmer, covered, for about twenty-five minutes, until tender.
Briefly remove the meat and measure the liquid in the pot; add stock or water to make 700 ml.
Return the meat and liquid to the pot and add the washed rice and remaining salt. Once boiling, cover and cook on the lowest heat for twenty minutes.
Leave covered for ten minutes. The pork should be fully cooked and tender; fluff the grains before serving.
tips: Boil the marinade with the meat; do not use it uncooked as a sauce.

title: Rice with pork ribs
description: Tender ribs and yellow rice that absorbs their flavorful cooking broth.
steps: Season the ribs with half the salt and brown them in the oil for ten minutes, turning them.
Add the diced onion and bell pepper; cook for five minutes, then add the garlic, cumin and tomatoes.
Add the bay leaf and 500 ml of stock. Cover and simmer gently for forty minutes, until the ribs are tender.
Measure the remaining liquid and top up with stock to make 700 ml. Return it to the pot with the ribs.
Add the washed rice, turmeric and remaining salt. Bring to a boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat for twenty minutes, until the liquid is absorbed.
Turn off the heat, let stand for ten minutes and remove the bay leaf. Serve, dividing the ribs evenly.
tips: If the ribs are still tough, cook them longer before adding the rice.

title: Shrimp and rice
description: Rice with a tomato sofrito, with shrimp added near the end to keep them tender.
steps: Pat the shrimp dry and keep them refrigerated while preparing the sofrito. Rinse and drain the rice.
Cook the chopped onion and bell pepper in the oil for five minutes; add the garlic and cumin, followed by the tomatoes.
Reduce the tomatoes for four minutes. Add the rice, stock and salt and bring to a boil.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat for fifteen minutes. Arrange the shrimp over the rice and cover again.
Cook for five to seven minutes, until the shrimp are opaque and the rice is tender. Let stand for five minutes.
Finish with the parsley and lemon juice, stirring gently to avoid breaking up the shrimp.
tips: Do not cook the shrimp for the entire rice cooking time, or they will become tough.

title: Cuban-style fish and rice
description: Yellow rice with pieces of white fish and bell pepper, gently cooked in one pot.
steps: Cut the fish into pieces about four centimeters across and refrigerate. Wash and drain the rice.
Sauté the chopped onion and bell pepper in the oil for five minutes. Add the garlic and tomatoes and cook for another four minutes.
Add the rice, turmeric, stock and half the salt. Bring to a boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat for twelve minutes.
Season the fish with the remaining salt and place it on top of the rice. Cover and cook for eight to ten minutes.
Check that the fish reaches 63 °C and flakes easily; the rice should have absorbed the stock.
Let stand for five minutes, drizzle with lemon juice and serve, lifting the fish with a wide spatula.
tips: Choose thick fillets so they hold together while the rice finishes cooking.

title: Squid and rice
description: Tender squid in tomato sofrito with rice that absorbs the flavorful broth.
steps: Pat the squid thoroughly dry. Chop the onion, bell pepper and garlic and wash the rice to remove excess starch.
Sauté the onion and bell pepper in the oil for six minutes. Add the garlic and paprika, immediately followed by the tomatoes.
Add the squid, bay leaf and 250 ml of stock. Cover and simmer gently for thirty minutes, until tender.
Briefly set the squid aside while measuring the liquid in the pot; top it up with stock to make 600 ml.
Return everything to the pot, add the rice and salt and bring to a boil. Cover and cook on the lowest heat for twenty minutes.
Let stand off the heat for ten minutes, remove the bay leaf and serve without excessive stirring.
tips: If the squid is still resistant when pierced, wait until it is tender before adding the rice.

title: Cuban fried rice
description: Rice stir-fried with ham, egg, vegetables and soy sauce, inspired by Chinese-Cuban cooking.
steps: Separate the cold rice grains. Finely chop the carrot, ham and scallions and beat the eggs with the salt.
Heat one tablespoon of oil in a wide skillet. Cook a thin omelet on both sides, remove it and cut it into strips.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the carrot for three minutes; add the garlic, ham and peas and cook for another three minutes.
Add the rice in batches and stir-fry for five minutes, breaking up clumps with a spatula without crushing the grains.
Pour the soy sauce around the hot edge, add the omelet strips and scallions and stir until everything is piping hot, at least 74 °C.
tips: Refrigerate cooked rice promptly; never leave it at room temperature overnight.

title: Rice with sweet corn
description: Yellow rice with corn kernels and bell pepper for a mild, flavorful side dish.
steps: Rinse and drain the rice. Finely chop the onion, garlic and bell pepper.
Sauté the onion and bell pepper in the oil for five minutes, stirring so they do not brown too much.
Add the garlic and turmeric, stir briefly, then add the rice and corn.
Pour in the stock, add the salt and bring to a boil. Cover and cook on the lowest heat for about twenty minutes.
Remove from the heat, let stand for ten minutes and fluff with a fork to distribute the corn.
tips: If using canned corn, drain it before weighing.

title: Vegetable rice with sofrito
description: A home-style combination of rice, carrot, green beans and peas with Cuban seasoning.
steps: Finely dice the carrot and cut the green beans into two-centimeter pieces. Chop the onion, bell pepper and garlic.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper and carrot in the oil for five minutes, then add the garlic and cumin.
Add the washed rice and green beans. Stir for one minute before pouring in the hot stock.
Add the peas and salt. Once boiling, cover and cook on the lowest heat for twenty minutes, until the vegetables and rice are tender.
Let stand for ten minutes, then stir from the edges toward the center to avoid crushing the vegetables.
tips: Small carrot cubes will cook in the same time as the rice.

title: Rice with chorizo and bell pepper
description: Simple rice with cooked chorizo, bell pepper and reduced tomatoes.
steps: Rinse and drain the rice. Slice the chorizo, chop the onion and bell pepper and mince the garlic.
Heat the oil and brown the chorizo for two minutes to flavor the pot.
Add the onion and bell pepper and sauté for five minutes. Add the garlic and tomatoes and cook for three minutes.
Add the rice, stock, bay leaf and salt. Bring to a boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat for about twenty minutes.
Leave covered for ten minutes, remove the bay leaf and serve, distributing the chorizo slices evenly.
tips: The amount of salt depends on the chorizo and stock; start with a little.

title: Rice with ham and peas
description: Everyday rice with cooked ham and peas, easy to share around the family table.
steps: Dice the ham and chop the onion and garlic. Rinse the rice and drain well.
Sauté the onion in the oil for four minutes; add the garlic and ham and cook, stirring, for two minutes.
Add the rice, peas and stock. Season cautiously because the ham already adds salt.
Cover as soon as it boils and cook on the lowest heat for twenty minutes, until the rice is tender with no loose liquid.
Let stand for ten minutes, add the roasted bell pepper strips and fluff with a fork.
tips: Brown rice needs a different water ratio and more cooking time; do not substitute it directly.

title: Rice with black-eyed peas
description: Home-style rice with cooked black-eyed peas, sofrito and bay leaf.
steps: Rinse the rice. Drain the black-eyed peas gently so they keep their shape, and chop the vegetables.
Sauté the onion and bell pepper in the oil for six minutes. Add the garlic and cumin and cook for thirty seconds.
Stir in the rice for one minute. Add the hot stock, black-eyed peas, bay leaf and salt.
Once boiling, cover and cook on the lowest heat for twenty minutes without stirring.
Turn off the heat and let stand for ten minutes. Remove the bay leaf and stir gently before serving.
tips: Start with fully cooked black-eyed peas: the rice cooking time is not long enough to soften dried legumes.

title: Pumpkin and garlic rice
description: Small pumpkin cubes bring color and softness to this home-style rice dish.
steps: Peel the pumpkin and cut it into even cubes. Rinse the rice and chop the onion and garlic.
Heat the oil and cook the onion for four minutes. Add the garlic and cumin without letting them burn.
Add the pumpkin and rice and stir for one minute to coat them with the sofrito.
Pour in the stock and add the salt. Bring to a boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat for about twenty minutes.
Let stand for ten minutes and sprinkle with parsley. Fold gently with broad strokes to keep some pumpkin cubes intact.
tips: Firm pumpkin holds its shape better; very ripe pumpkin will partly blend into the rice.

title: Rice with okra
description: Rice with okra and tomatoes, with its distinctive texture and a touch of lemon.
steps: Wash the okra and dry it thoroughly. Trim only the tough tips and cut it into thick rounds.
Sauté the chopped onion and bell pepper in the oil for five minutes. Add the garlic, cumin and tomatoes and reduce for four minutes.
Add the okra and lemon juice and sauté for two minutes, stirring gently.
Add the rinsed rice, stock and salt. Once boiling, cover and cook on the lowest heat for about twenty minutes.
Let stand for ten minutes without uncovering, then serve. A slightly slippery texture is a natural characteristic of okra.
tips: Choose small, flexible pods; very large ones can be fibrous.

title: House-style black beans
description: Black beans thickened with some of their own beans and a garlic and pepper sofrito.
steps: Sort and wash the beans. Cover generously with water and soak for eight hours in the refrigerator; discard the soaking water.
Place them in a pot with the cooking water and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then simmer for sixty to ninety minutes, until tender.
Chop the onion, bell pepper and garlic. Sauté the onion and bell pepper in the oil for six minutes, then add the garlic, cumin and oregano.
Add the sofrito to the pot. Mash a ladleful of beans with a little broth and return it to the pot to thicken the mixture.
Add the salt and cook over low heat for another fifteen minutes. Adjust the consistency with hot water if necessary.
Remove the bay leaf, add the vinegar at the end and serve with a slightly thickened broth.
tips: Older beans take longer to cook; judge by their texture and keep enough water in the pot throughout cooking.

title: Red beans with pumpkin
description: A creamy red bean and pumpkin stew with sofrito and Cuban seasoning.
steps: Sort and wash the beans. Soak them, covered with water, for eight hours in the refrigerator, then drain and rinse.
Cover with the cooking water and boil vigorously for thirty minutes. Reduce the heat, add the bay leaf and cook until tender.
Meanwhile, sauté the chopped onion and bell pepper in the oil for six minutes; add the garlic, cumin, paprika and tomatoes.
Once the beans are tender, add the sofrito, diced pumpkin and salt. Simmer gently for twenty minutes.
Mash some of the pumpkin cubes against the side of the pot and stir to thicken the broth.
Remove the bay leaf and check that all the beans are tender. Serve hot, adding more water if you prefer a lighter stew.
tips: Do not cook dried red beans only at a low temperature; the initial vigorous boil is important.

title: Chickpea stew with chorizo
description: Chickpeas, potatoes and chorizo in a sofrito broth, finished with a gentle simmer.
steps: Sort the chickpeas and soak them in plenty of water for twelve hours in the refrigerator. Drain and rinse.
Bring the cooking water to a boil, add the chickpeas and bay leaf and simmer gently for ninety to one hundred and twenty minutes, until tender.
Slice the chorizo and sauté it in the oil. Add the chopped onion and bell pepper and cook for six minutes.
Add the garlic and paprika, immediately followed by the tomatoes, and reduce for five minutes. Transfer everything to the pot of chickpeas.
Add the peeled, diced potatoes and salt. Cook for another twenty minutes, until the potatoes break apart when pressed.
Mash a few chickpeas to thicken the broth, remove the bay leaf and skim off any excess surface fat before serving.
tips: Do not substitute fresh, raw chorizo without adjusting its cooking time; this recipe uses cured chorizo.

title: Split pea stew
description: Dried split peas with pumpkin and ham, cooked until thick and comforting.
steps: Sort and rinse the split peas until the water runs clear. They do not need soaking for this recipe.
Sauté the chopped onion and bell pepper in the oil for six minutes; add the garlic, cumin and diced ham.
Add the split peas, water and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, skim off the foam and reduce the heat.
Cook, partially covered, for forty minutes, stirring along the bottom regularly to prevent sticking.
Add the diced pumpkin and salt. Cook for another twenty to thirty minutes, until the split peas break down and the pumpkin is tender.
Remove the bay leaf. Add hot water if the stew has become too thick and serve freshly cooked.
tips: This stew thickens considerably as it stands; add a little water when reheating.

title: Cuban-style lentils with potatoes
description: Lentils with sofrito, carrot and potatoes for an everyday Cuban-inspired stew.
steps: Sort and rinse the lentils. Peel the potatoes and carrot and cut them into small cubes.
Sauté the chopped onion and bell pepper in the oil for five minutes. Add the garlic, cumin and tomatoes and cook for three minutes.
Add the lentils, water and bay leaf. Bring to a boil and cook over medium-low heat for fifteen minutes.
Add the potatoes, carrot and salt. Continue cooking for about twenty minutes, until the lentils and potatoes are tender.
Remove the bay leaf, mash a few potato pieces and stir to give the broth body. Serve hot.
tips: Cooking time varies with the type of lentil; add hot water if the pot dries out before they are tender.

title: Ajiaco — Cuban meat and root vegetable stew
description: A stew of meats, corn and root vegetables, thickened with some of the cooked vegetables.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: plus water to boil the cassava separately

steps: Cut the meats into three-centimeter cubes. Sauté the chopped onion and bell pepper in the oil; add the garlic, cumin and tomatoes.
Add the beef and pork, cover with the measured water and simmer gently for about sixty minutes, skimming off foam.
In a separate pot, boil the peeled, cut cassava in plenty of water until tender; drain, discard the cooking water and remove the fibrous core.
Add the chicken, malanga root and peeled plantain pieces to the broth. Cook for twenty minutes.
Add the corn rounds, boniato sweet potato, pumpkin and salt. Cook for about twenty-five minutes, until all the root vegetables are tender; check that the chicken reaches 74 °C.
Add the cooked cassava. Mash a little pumpkin and boniato to thicken the stew, add the lemon juice and simmer for another five minutes.
Serve in deep bowls, distributing the meats and vegetables evenly, and remove any bones or fibers you find.
tips: Add the ingredients in stages: the pumpkin goes in later so it does not break down completely.

title: Cuban-style Galician broth
description: White beans, potatoes, cabbage and cured meat in a home-style version of this Galician soup.
steps: Peel and dice the potatoes. Wash the cabbage and cut it into strips; chop the onion and garlic.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil for five minutes. Add the sliced chorizo and diced ham and stir for two minutes.
Pour in the water, add the potatoes and bay leaf and simmer gently for fifteen minutes.
Add the cooked beans and cabbage. Cook for another twenty minutes, until the potatoes and cabbage are tender.
Taste before adding the salt; mash some beans to give the broth body and remove the bay leaf.
tips: This version uses cabbage; Galician broth has many family variations, including versions with turnip greens.

title: Chicken noodle soup
description: Chicken broth with fine noodles, potato and carrot for a comforting homemade soup.
steps: Place the chicken, halved onion, garlic and celery in a pot with the water. Bring to a boil and skim off the foam.
Reduce the heat and cook for forty minutes, until the chicken reaches 74 °C and is tender.
Remove the chicken and discard the skin and bones. Strain the broth to remove any small bones, then return it to the pot.
Add the peeled, diced potatoes and carrots and the salt; simmer gently for fifteen minutes.
Add the noodles and shredded chicken. Cook for the time specified for the noodles, usually five to eight minutes.
Add the lemon juice at the end and serve immediately so the pasta does not absorb all the broth.
tips: If storing the soup, keep the noodles separate from the broth for the best texture.

title: Creamy malanga soup
description: Thoroughly cooked malanga root blended with milk for a smooth, delicately flavored soup.
steps: Peel, wash and dice the malanga. Do not taste malanga raw.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for four minutes without browning.
Add the malanga, water and salt. Simmer gently for about twenty-five minutes, until every piece is very tender.
Remove the pot from the heat and blend with an immersion blender, keeping the blade submerged to prevent splashing.
Stir in the milk, butter and pepper. Heat gently for five minutes and adjust the consistency with a little water if necessary.
tips: Malanga thickens as it cools; serve the soup hot and loose enough to pour.

title: Cuban-style pumpkin soup
description: Pumpkin, onion and cumin in a dairy-free creamy soup, finished with lemon.
steps: Cut the peeled pumpkin and potato into cubes of about two centimeters. Chop the onion and garlic.
Soften the onion in the oil for five minutes. Add the garlic and cumin and stir for half a minute.
Add the pumpkin, potato, stock and salt. Partially cover and simmer gently for twenty minutes.
Check that both vegetables mash easily with a fork. Remove from the heat and blend with an immersion blender.
Return to low heat for two minutes, add the lemon juice and thin with hot water if the soup is too thick.
tips: The potato helps thicken the soup without cream.

title: Green plantain soup
description: Green plantain and sofrito become a thick soup, finished with garlic and lemon.
steps: Trim the ends of the plantains, slit the skin lengthwise and peel. Cut into one-centimeter rounds.
Sauté the chopped onion and bell pepper in the oil for six minutes. Add the garlic and cumin.
Add the plantains, stock and salt. Bring to a boil and cook over medium-low heat for about twenty-five minutes.
Once tender, crush some of the rounds with a masher or blend briefly with an immersion blender.
Simmer for two more minutes, add the lemon juice and serve with some rounds left whole for texture.
tips: Use green cooking plantains, not sweet bananas.

title: White bean and Swiss chard stew
description: Cooked white beans with Swiss chard, tomatoes and potatoes in a home-style stew.
steps: Wash the chard thoroughly. Separate the stems and leaves and chop them separately; peel and cut the potatoes.
Sauté the chopped onion in the oil for five minutes. Add the garlic, paprika and tomatoes and cook for four minutes.
Add the water, potatoes and chard stems. Simmer gently for fifteen minutes.
Add the cooked beans, chard leaves and salt. Cook for another ten minutes, until everything is tender.
Mash a ladleful of beans and potatoes, return it to the broth and stir. Serve with a slightly thickened broth.
tips: Using cooked beans shortens the preparation time; do not substitute dried beans directly.

title: Stewed black-eyed peas
description: Black-eyed peas with sofrito, pumpkin and oregano, served with white rice or as a stew.
steps: Sort and wash the black-eyed peas. Soak in plenty of water for eight hours in the refrigerator, then drain and rinse.
Place them in a pot with the cooking water and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for forty to sixty minutes.
Sauté the chopped onion and bell pepper in the oil for six minutes. Add the garlic, oregano and tomatoes and reduce for four minutes.
When the peas are almost tender, add the sofrito, diced pumpkin and salt; cook for twenty more minutes.
Remove the bay leaf and stir slowly. Mash a little pumpkin if you would like a thicker broth.
