tips: Keep the peas covered with liquid as they soften, adding hot water whenever necessary.

title: Vegetable soup with sofrito
description: A light soup of everyday vegetables with tomatoes, garlic and a hint of cumin.
steps: Peel the potato, carrot and pumpkin and cut them into small cubes. Wash and chop the cabbage and green beans.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for five minutes. Add the cumin and tomatoes and cook for three minutes.
Pour in the water, add the potatoes, carrots and salt and bring to a boil. Cook for ten minutes.
Add the pumpkin, cabbage and green beans and cook for another fifteen minutes, until all the vegetables are tender.
Taste the broth, adjust the salt if necessary and serve with the vegetables in pieces, without blending.
tips: Cut firmer vegetables into smaller pieces than the pumpkin so they cook evenly.

title: Fish soup with root vegetables
description: White fish in a broth with tomatoes, potato and boniato sweet potato, finished with lemon.
steps: Check the fish for bones and cut it into four-centimeter pieces. Peel the potato and boniato and dice them.
Sauté the chopped onion and bell pepper in the oil for five minutes. Add the garlic and tomatoes and cook for four minutes.
Pour in the stock and add the potato, boniato and salt. Simmer gently for fifteen minutes, until almost tender.
Add the fish and cook for six to eight minutes without vigorous stirring, until it reaches 63 °C and flakes easily.
Finish with parsley and lemon juice. Serve by lifting the pieces carefully with a ladle so they stay intact.
tips: Add the fish at the end so it keeps its shape and does not dry out.

title: Creamy sweet corn soup
description: A savory corn soup with milk and a mild sofrito, intended to be served hot.
steps: Set aside four tablespoons of corn. Finely chop the onion and garlic.
Melt the butter and soften the onion and garlic over medium-low heat for five minutes without browning.
Add the remaining corn and the water. Simmer gently for fifteen minutes, until the kernels are tender.
Remove from the heat and blend with an immersion blender. For a smoother soup, pass it through a strainer, pressing with a spoon.
Return to the pot and add the milk, reserved corn, salt and pepper. Cook for five minutes without boiling vigorously, then serve.
tips: No sugar is added: this is a savory soup, distinct from sweet corn pudding, or majarete.

title: Beef broth with root vegetables
description: Beef broth with corn, malanga root and pumpkin, slowly cooked until the meat is tender.
steps: Place the beef in a pot with the water, quartered onion, garlic, bell pepper and bay leaf. Bring to a boil and skim off the foam.
Reduce the heat and cook, partially covered, for about one hundred and twenty minutes, until the meat comes away from the bone easily.
Remove the meat, discard bones and cartilage and strain the broth. Add hot water if it has reduced too much.
Return the meat and broth to the pot; add the potatoes, malanga and corn pieces. Cook for fifteen minutes.
Add the pumpkin and salt and cook for another fifteen minutes, until all the root vegetables are tender.
Finish with lemon juice and serve, distributing the meat, corn and root vegetables evenly. Check that no bone fragments remain.
tips: Judge when to add the root vegetables by the tenderness of the meat, rather than the clock alone.

title: Tomato and rice soup
description: Tomatoes, rice and a simple sofrito in a homemade soup with Cuban seasoning.
steps: Chop the onion, bell pepper and garlic. Rinse and drain the rice.
Sauté the onion and bell pepper in the oil for six minutes. Add the garlic and cumin and stir for half a minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook over medium heat for eight minutes, stirring to prevent sticking.
Add the stock, rice and salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for eighteen to twenty minutes, until the rice is tender.
Serve without blending; if the rice has absorbed too much broth, add hot water and simmer again for one minute.
tips: Do not automatically add sugar; the sofrito and cooking time soften the tomatoes' flavor.

title: Boniato and roasted garlic soup
description: White boniato sweet potato and roasted garlic in a silky homemade soup.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Cut the top off the head of garlic, drizzle with one teaspoon of oil and wrap in parchment paper and foil.
Bake the garlic for thirty-five minutes, until the cloves are soft. Let cool enough to handle.
Meanwhile, sauté the chopped onion in the remaining oil. Add the diced boniato, stock and salt and cook for twenty-five minutes.
Squeeze the roasted garlic pulp into the pot, remove from the heat and blend with an immersion blender.
Add the lemon juice and pepper, heat for two minutes and thin with hot water to make a smooth, pourable soup.
tips: Roasted garlic tastes milder than raw garlic; add the pulp, not the skin.

title: Garlic soup with egg
description: Homemade garlic, bread and egg soup with a simple paprika seasoning.
steps: Peel and slice the garlic. Cut the bread into thin slices, then into spoon-sized pieces.
Heat the oil over medium-low heat and gently brown the garlic, watching carefully so it does not darken too much.
Add the bread and stir for two minutes. Remove from the heat, stir in the paprika and immediately pour in the stock.
Simmer gently for ten minutes and season. Crack each egg into a cup and slide it into a separate space in the soup.
Cover and cook for six to eight minutes, until both whites and yolks are firm. Serve one egg and some broth with bread in each bowl.
tips: Paprika burns quickly; pour in the stock as soon as you add it.

title: Cassava with mojo sauce
description: Tender cassava covered with garlic, onion and citrus mojo sauce.
steps: Trim the ends of the cassava, completely remove the outer skin and pink layer, and cut the flesh into pieces about five centimeters long.
Wash the pieces and boil them in the water with one teaspoon of salt for thirty to forty minutes, until completely tender.
Drain and discard the cooking water. Remove the tough central fiber from each piece and place the cassava in a serving dish.
Heat the oil over low heat with the crushed garlic and sliced onion; cook for four minutes without burning the garlic.
Remove from the heat, let the sizzling subside, then carefully add the citrus juices, oregano and remaining salt.
Pour the mojo over the cassava, let stand for five minutes and serve hot.
tips: Use commercially sold sweet cassava intended for food; do not use bitter varieties or eat cassava raw.

title: Fried cassava sticks
description: Cassava boiled and then fried for a golden exterior and soft center.

ingredients.name: oil for frying
ingredients.note: amount needed for cooking; not all will be consumed

steps: Peel the cassava completely, removing the pink layer, and cut it into medium-sized pieces. Wash thoroughly.
Boil in the water with half a teaspoon of salt for about thirty minutes, until tender but still holding its shape.
Drain, discard the cooking water and remove the central fiber. Let cool and dry for fifteen minutes before cutting into thick sticks.
Heat the oil to 175 °C in a deep pot, filling it no more than halfway. Fry in batches for four to six minutes.
Drain on paper towels, season with the remaining salt and add a few drops of lemon juice when serving.
tips: The cassava should be thoroughly dry before going into the oil to reduce splattering.

title: Tostones or chatinos — twice-fried plantains
description: Green plantains fried twice and flattened to create crisp edges.
steps: Trim the ends, slit each peel lengthwise and peel the plantains. Cut into rounds about three centimeters thick.
Heat the oil to 160 °C in a deep pot. Fry the rounds in batches for four to five minutes, until softened without much browning.
Remove and drain. Flatten each round between two flat surfaces into a disc approximately one centimeter thick.
Raise the oil temperature to 180 °C and fry the discs again for about two minutes per side, until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels, sprinkle with salt and serve immediately to preserve their texture.
tips: Do not wet the plantains between frying stages: water in hot oil causes splattering.

title: Fried ripe plantains
description: Slices of very ripe plantain, fried until the edges caramelize.
steps: Peel the plantains and cut them diagonally into slices about one and a half centimeters thick.
Heat a one-centimeter layer of oil in a wide skillet over medium heat; it should sizzle without smoking.
Arrange the slices with space between them. Cook on the first side for three to four minutes.
Turn with a spatula and brown the other side for two to three minutes, lowering the heat if the edges darken too quickly.
Drain briefly, add a pinch of salt and serve warm as a side dish.
tips: Partially ripe plantains are firmer and less sweet; use very ripe ones for this recipe.

title: Fufú — mashed plantains with pork cracklings
description: Green plantains mashed with garlic and pork cracklings for a rustic side dish.
steps: Peel and cut the plantains into pieces. Boil in the water with half a teaspoon of salt for twenty to twenty-five minutes.
While they soften, sauté the chopped onion in the oil for four minutes. Add the crushed garlic and cook for one minute without burning it.
Reserve one cup of cooking water and drain the plantains. Mash them while still hot with a potato masher.
Stir in the sofrito, chopped pork cracklings and lemon juice. Gradually add reserved cooking water until the mixture is moist but holds its shape.
Taste, add the remaining salt only if needed and serve immediately, leaving the texture slightly coarse.
tips: Pork cracklings already contain salt; take this into account when seasoning.

title: Garlic-roasted boniato wedges
description: Boniato sweet potato wedges oven-roasted with garlic, oregano and a touch of lemon.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel the boniato and cut it into wedges about two centimeters thick; pat the surface dry with paper towels.
Toss the wedges with the oil, salt and oregano. Arrange in a single layer with space between them.
Roast for twenty-five minutes, turn over and add the chopped garlic mixed with the lemon juice.
Roast for another ten to fifteen minutes, until the centers are tender and the edges are golden.
tips: Add the garlic near the end so it does not burn during the long roasting time.

title: Boiled malanga with garlic and oil
description: Fully cooked malanga root finished with a warm garlic and lemon dressing.
steps: Peel and wash the malanga and cut into evenly sized pieces. Do not taste it raw.
Cover with the water and add half a teaspoon of salt. Bring to a boil and simmer gently for twenty-five to thirty minutes.
Check that a fork passes easily through every piece. Drain and transfer to a serving dish.
Heat the oil with the chopped garlic over low heat for one minute without letting it brown too much; remove from the heat.
Add the lemon juice, parsley and remaining salt to the warm oil, stir and spoon over the hot malanga.
tips: If the pieces are large, continue cooking until no hard center remains.

title: Pumpkin with mild mojo sauce
description: Steamed pumpkin dressed with a light garlic and citrus mojo sauce.
steps: Cut the pumpkin into pieces about four centimeters across, removing all seeds and fibers.
Heat the water in a pot fitted with a steamer. Place the pumpkin in the steamer, cover and cook for fifteen to twenty minutes.
Check with a knife that the pumpkin is tender but still holds its shape; transfer to a serving dish.
Heat the oil with the crushed garlic over low heat for one minute. Remove from the heat and add the citrus juices and oregano once warm rather than hot.
Season the pumpkin with salt, spoon the mojo over it and serve, handling the pieces as little as possible.
tips: Steaming prevents the pumpkin from absorbing excess water and helps it hold its shape when dressed.

title: Avocado and onion salad
description: Thick avocado slices with thinly sliced onion and a simple lemon and oil dressing.
steps: Wash the outside of the avocados before cutting them open. Slice the onion very thinly.
Mix the onion with one tablespoon of the lemon juice and let stand for ten minutes while preparing the rest.
Halve the avocados, remove the pits with a spoon and cut the flesh into thick slices.
Whisk the remaining lemon juice with the oil, salt and pepper. Arrange the avocado in a serving dish without piling it up.
Scatter the onion and dressing over the avocado and serve immediately to preserve its color.
tips: Very soft avocado will break apart when tossed; spoon the dressing over the top instead.

title: Tomato and cucumber salad
description: Tomatoes, cucumber and onion in a fresh everyday salad.
steps: Wash the tomatoes and cucumber under running water and pat dry. Peel the cucumber if the skin is tough.
Cut the tomatoes into wedges and the cucumber into half-centimeter half-moons. Thinly slice the onion.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, salt and oregano in a cup until the dressing is combined.
Place the vegetables in a large bowl and add the dressing just before serving.
Toss with two spoons, lifting from the bottom to keep the tomato wedges intact.
tips: Salt draws water out of vegetables; add the dressing at the end so the salad does not become watery.

title: Cabbage salad with lemon
description: Finely shredded cabbage with carrot and a lemon dressing, without mayonnaise.
steps: Remove any damaged outer cabbage leaves, wash the cabbage and cut into very fine strips.
Peel and grate the carrot. Thinly slice the onion and mix it with the cabbage.
Add the salt and gently massage the cabbage for one minute without crushing it.
Whisk the lemon juice, oil and cumin and pour over the salad. Fold in the grated carrot.
Refrigerate for fifteen minutes, toss again and drain off any excess liquid before serving.
tips: A short resting time softens the cabbage while keeping it crisp.

title: Beet and onion salad
description: Sliced cooked beets with onion, vinegar and oil.
steps: Wash the beets without peeling them and leave a short section of stem attached to reduce color loss.
Cover with water and boil for forty to fifty minutes, until a knife slides in without resistance.
Drain, let cool enough to handle and remove the skins. Cut into slices or cubes.
Mix the vinegar, oil and salt; add the sliced onion and the beets while they are still warm.
Transfer to a shallow container, refrigerate for thirty minutes and add parsley before serving.
tips: You can use plain, precooked beets; if so, skip the boiling step.

title: Cuban potato salad
description: Potatoes, carrot, egg and peas bound with mayonnaise for a creamy salad.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for boiling, plus water for the eggs

steps: Peel the potatoes and carrots and cut into cubes about two centimeters across. Cook in water with half a teaspoon of salt for fifteen to twenty minutes.
Add the peas during the last three minutes. Drain well and spread on a shallow tray to release the steam.
Boil the eggs in a separate pot for eleven minutes; cool under cold water, peel and cut into pieces.
Once the vegetables are no longer hot, mix with the egg, onion, mayonnaise, lemon juice and remaining salt.
Cover and refrigerate for one hour before serving. Keep the salad refrigerated until ready to bring it to the table.
tips: Do not leave the salad at room temperature for more than two hours, or one hour in very hot conditions.

title: Meat-free okra stew
description: Okra with tomatoes, garlic and green plantain in a home-style stew.
steps: Wash and dry the okra, trim the tough tips and cut into thick pieces. Peel the plantain and cut into rounds.
Sauté the chopped onion and bell pepper in the oil for five minutes. Add the garlic, cumin and tomatoes and cook for five minutes.
Add the water, plantain and salt and simmer gently for ten minutes to begin softening the plantain.
Add the okra and lemon juice. Cover and cook for fifteen to twenty minutes, shaking the pot instead of stirring vigorously.
Check that both vegetables are tender. Uncover for a few minutes if there is too much liquid, then serve with the sauce.
tips: Okra naturally thickens the sauce slightly; lemon adds a contrasting flavor.

title: Green beans with sofrito
description: Tender green beans finished in tomatoes, garlic and onion.
steps: Wash the green beans, trim the ends and cut into four-centimeter pieces.
Boil in the water with half a teaspoon of salt for eight to ten minutes, until tender but firm; drain.
Sauté the chopped onion in the oil for five minutes. Add the garlic and cumin and stir for half a minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for seven minutes, until the sauce thickens.
Add the green beans and remaining salt. Stir and cook for three minutes to coat the beans with the sauce.
tips: If the beans are very thin, shorten the initial boiling time and finish cooking them in the tomatoes.

title: Ham croquettes
description: Small croquettes of ham and thick béchamel, with a thin, crisp coating.
steps: Melt the butter and cook the onion over low heat for five minutes. Add the 90 g of flour and stir for two minutes.
Gradually pour in the milk, whisking to remove lumps. Cook for five minutes until the béchamel is very thick.
Add the ham, nutmeg and salt. Cook for another five minutes, stirring until the mixture pulls away from the bottom of the pan.
Spread in a shallow container, let the steam escape for a few minutes, then cover and refrigerate for two hours, until firm.
Shape into twenty-four small cylinders. Coat with flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs on all sides; refrigerate for thirty minutes.
Heat the oil to 175 °C and fry in small batches for three to four minutes, turning to brown evenly.
Drain on paper towels and let stand for a couple of minutes before serving; the filling should be thoroughly hot.
tips: Makes about twenty-four croquettes, three per serving.
Chilling the mixture is part of the recipe: if it is soft, the croquettes will split in the oil.
During frying, the center should reach 74 °C to reheat the refrigerated filling.

title: Chicken croquettes
description: Shredded cooked chicken in a creamy mixture, breaded in small portions.
steps: Finely chop the cooked chicken. Melt the butter and sauté the chopped onion and garlic for five minutes.
Add the 100 g of flour and stir for two minutes. Gradually add the milk and stock, whisking constantly.
Add the chicken, parsley and salt. Cook over low heat for eight to ten minutes, until the mixture pulls away from the pan.
Spread in a shallow dish, let it stop steaming, then cover and refrigerate for two hours to firm up.
Shape into twenty-four croquettes and coat with flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs. Refrigerate for another thirty minutes.
Fry in batches at 175 °C for about four minutes, until golden and thoroughly heated inside.
Drain and serve three croquettes per portion. Cut open one from the first batch to check that the center is hot.
tips: Use cooked chicken that has been kept refrigerated and reheat the centers of the croquettes to 74 °C.

title: Picadillo-stuffed potato balls
description: Potato balls with a center of ground beef, olives and sofrito.
steps: Peel and cut the potatoes into pieces, then boil in the water with half a teaspoon of salt for about twenty minutes. Drain thoroughly and mash without adding milk.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper and garlic in one tablespoon of oil. Add the meat, cumin and remaining salt, breaking up the meat with a spoon.
Add the tomatoes and olives; cook for ten minutes, until the filling is almost dry and the meat reaches 71 °C.
Spread the mashed potatoes and filling in separate shallow containers and refrigerate for thirty minutes, until easy to handle.
Divide the mashed potatoes into twelve portions. Flatten each one, place a tablespoon of picadillo in the center and close without leaving cracks.
Coat with flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs, then refrigerate for thirty minutes. Fry in batches at 175 °C for four to five minutes.
Drain once golden; the centers should be thoroughly hot. Serve two balls per portion.
tips: Potatoes that are too wet will split during frying; drain and dry them thoroughly before mashing.
If the filling was already chilled, check that the center reaches 74 °C by the end of frying.

title: Malanga fritters
description: Small grated malanga fritters with garlic and parsley, golden outside and cooked through inside.
steps: Peel, wash and finely grate the malanga. Chop the garlic and parsley; do not taste raw malanga.
Mix the malanga, eggs, flour, garlic, parsley and salt into a thick batter that holds its shape on a spoon.
Heat the oil to about 170 °C in a deep pot. Line a tray with absorbent paper.
Drop in small spoonfuls without crowding and flatten them slightly. Fry for four to six minutes, turning halfway through.
Cut open the first fritter: the center should be fully cooked, with no wet, raw batter. Adjust the size or cooking time for the next batches.
Drain and serve hot. Makes approximately eighteen small fritters.
tips: Large fritters may still contain raw malanga inside even when the outside looks golden.

title: Fresh corn fritters
description: Spoonfuls of fresh corn batter with onion and garlic, fried until golden.
steps: Blend most of the corn with the eggs, leaving some kernels whole for texture.
Finely chop the onion and crush the garlic. Mix them with the blended corn and reserved kernels.
Stir in the flour, baking powder and salt. The mixture should fall from a spoon as a thick batter, not as a liquid.
Heat the oil to 170 °C and drop in small, well-spaced spoonfuls; fry for three to five minutes, turning them.
Check that the center of the first fritter is set. Drain each batch on paper towels and serve freshly cooked.
tips: If using canned corn, drain it thoroughly so it does not thin the batter.

title: Cuban tamales in corn husks
description: Fresh corn dough with pork and sofrito, wrapped in husks and cooked until firm.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for soaking the husks and cooking; add more if needed

steps: Soak the husks in hot water for twenty minutes, wash and drain. Blend the corn with 150 ml of the stock to make a paste.
Brown the pork in the oil for five minutes. Add the chopped onion, bell pepper and garlic and cook for another five minutes.
Add the tomatoes, cumin, salt and remaining 200 ml of stock. Cover and cook for twenty-five minutes, until the pork is tender.
Add the blended corn and fine cornmeal. Stir over low heat for eight minutes, until the dough is thick, moist and moldable.
Divide the dough into twelve portions on doubled husks. Fold in the sides and ends and tie with strips of husk or kitchen twine.
Place the parcels in a pot with enough boiling water to cover them. Simmer gently for fifty to sixty minutes, topping up with hot water if the level drops.
Remove one tamal, let cool for five minutes and check that it releases from the husk and holds its shape. Serve two per portion.
tips: Use regular fine cornmeal; precooked cornmeal absorbs liquid differently and requires adjustments.
The husks are wrappers and should be removed before eating.

title: Tamal en cazuela — corn and pork stew
description: Creamy corn with pork pieces and sofrito, cooked directly in a pot.
steps: Blend the corn with 400 ml of the stock until thick. Keep the cornmeal separate.
Brown the pork in the oil for eight minutes. Add the chopped onion, bell pepper and garlic and sauté for five minutes.
Add the tomatoes, cumin, oregano, salt and 300 ml of stock. Cover and cook for twenty-five minutes, until the pork is tender.
Stir in the blended corn. Mix the cornmeal into the remaining 200 ml of stock and add it while stirring.
Cook over low heat for thirty to thirty-five minutes, stirring along the bottom frequently to prevent sticking.
The mixture should be thick and creamy, with no raw cornmeal taste. Add hot water if it is too firm.
Let stand for five minutes and serve in deep bowls, distributing the pork pieces evenly.
tips: Fresh corn varies in moisture; adjust the consistency at the end by adding liquid a little at a time.

title: Pressed Cuban sandwich
description: Cuban bread with roast pork, ham, cheese, pickles and mustard, toasted on a griddle.
steps: Split the bread lengthwise without fully separating the halves and spread the mustard inside.
Heat the pork and ham with the water in a covered skillet until thoroughly hot; if using leftovers, heat to 74 °C.
Divide the cheese, pork, ham and well-drained pickles among the rolls. Close and spread a thin layer of butter on the outside.
Heat a griddle or skillet over medium-low heat. Place the sandwiches on it and press down with another clean, heavy skillet.
Toast for three to four minutes per side, until the bread is crisp and the cheese has melted. Cut diagonally and serve.
tips: This version uses pork and ham; some Cuban diaspora variations also include salami.

title: Cuban medianoche sandwich
description: Pork, ham, cheese and pickles on a soft, slightly sweet roll.

ingredients.name: medianoche rolls
ingredients.note: soft egg rolls, about 100 g each

steps: Split the rolls in half and spread mustard evenly inside.
Heat the pork and ham in a covered skillet with two tablespoons of water; if using refrigerated leftovers, check that they reach 74 °C.
Divide the meats, cheese and drained pickles among the rolls. Close and spread a little butter on the outside.
Press in a skillet over medium-low heat for two to three minutes per side, taking care not to burn the sweet bread.
Once the cheese has melted and the surface is golden, remove, cut and serve immediately.
tips: Medianoche bread usually contains egg and may contain milk; check the label.

title: Roast pork and onion sandwich
description: Hot roast pork with onion and citrus mojo inside toasted bread.
steps: Thinly slice the onion and chop the garlic. Split the rolls lengthwise.
Heat the oil and sauté the onion for four minutes; add the garlic and oregano and stir for one minute.
Add the pork, citrus juices and salt. Cover and heat for about five minutes; refrigerated leftover pork should reach 74 °C.
Uncover for one minute to reduce excess juices. Divide the pork and onion among the rolls.
Toast the closed sandwiches on a griddle for two minutes per side, pressing lightly, and serve hot.
tips: The filling should be juicy without so much liquid that it soaks the bread.

title: Cuban steak sandwich
description: Thin steak with onion, potato sticks and tomato inside toasted Cuban bread.
steps: Gently pound the steaks between sheets of parchment paper to even out their thickness. Season with crushed garlic, lemon juice, salt and cumin.
Wash and dry the tomato and lettuce. Slice the tomato into rounds and the onion into strips.
Heat one tablespoon of oil and sauté the onion for six minutes, until softened. Set aside.
Add the remaining oil and cook the steaks in batches for approximately two minutes per side; bring them to 63 °C and let rest for three minutes.
Split and toast the bread. Add the steak, onion, tomato, lettuce and potato sticks, then close without crushing the vegetables too much.
tips: Add the potato sticks at the end so they stay crisp.

title: Frita cubana — Cuban burger
description: A garlic and paprika-seasoned burger topped with potato sticks and onion.
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into very thin strips. Rinse, drain and dry completely before frying.
Heat the oil to 175 °C and fry the potato sticks in batches until golden and crisp; drain and set aside.
Mix the meat with the crushed garlic, paprika, cumin, half the onion, grated, and the salt. Shape into four thin patties.
Heat the griddle with one tablespoon of oil and cook the burgers for about four minutes per side, until the centers reach 71 °C.
Toast the buns, spread with ketchup and add the meat. Top with the remaining onion, chopped, and a mound of potato sticks just before serving.
tips: Internal temperature is more reliable than color for checking that ground meat is cooked.

title: Cuban buttered toast
description: Cuban bread split, buttered and pressed until crisp on the outside.
steps: Cut the loaf into four portions and split each one lengthwise.
Spread a thin layer of butter on the inside faces and close the bread again.
Heat a griddle or wide skillet over medium-low heat. Arrange the portions without crowding.
Press with a clean, heavy skillet and toast for three to four minutes per side, until the surface is golden.
Remove, cut each portion into strips or diagonally and serve immediately while still crisp.
tips: Day-old bread works well if it is not excessively dry.

title: Mariquitas — plantain chips
description: Very thin slices of green plantain fried until light and crisp.
steps: Peel the green plantains by making a lengthwise cut through the skin and removing it in sections.
Cut very thin slices using a mandoline with a hand guard, or a sharp knife on a stable cutting board.
Heat the oil to about 175 °C in a deep pot. Separate the slices so they do not stick together when added.
Fry in small batches for two to three minutes, moving them with a slotted spoon until golden and the bubbling subsides.
Drain on paper towels, season while hot and let cool in a single layer before serving.
tips: Even slicing matters: thick slices stay soft, while very thin ones burn more quickly.

title: Havana-style baked eggs
description: Eggs baked over an onion, bell pepper and tomato sofrito.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Grease four small ovenproof dishes with the butter.
Sauté the chopped onion and bell pepper in the oil for six minutes. Add the garlic and cumin and stir for half a minute.
Add the tomatoes and salt and cook for eight minutes, until the sofrito is thick. Divide among the dishes.
Make two wells in each portion of sofrito and place an egg in each, cracking them into a cup first.
Bake for twelve to sixteen minutes, until both whites and yolks are firm. Sprinkle with parsley and serve carefully, as the dishes will be very hot.
tips: Cooking time depends on the depth of the dishes; check the centers, not just the edges.

title: Guava pastries (pastelitos de guayaba)
description: Golden puff pastries with the guava filling of a classic Cuban afternoon snack.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Keep the puff pastry cold until you cut it.
Roll each sheet out to about 24 × 32 cm and cut it into 12 equal rectangles; you will have 24 pieces for 12 pastries.
Divide the guava paste among 12 bases, leaving a 1 cm border. Moisten the edges, cover with the remaining pieces and press gently.
Beat the egg with the water. Brush the tops, sprinkle with sugar and cut a small steam vent in each pastry.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes, until the layers have risen and are golden on the bottom as well. Let cool for 15 minutes before eating.
tips: Hot guava filling can burn; wait until the center has cooled to warm.
If the puff pastry softens while you work, chill it for 10 minutes.

title: Guava and cheese pastries
description: Guava and cream cheese wrapped in crisp, flaky layers.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Line a baking sheet and cut the cold puff pastry into 24 squares about 8 cm wide.
Cut the guava paste into 12 thin portions and divide the cream cheese into 12 small mounds; do not mix the two fillings.
Place guava and cheese in the center of 12 squares. Keep the edges clean and moisten them lightly.
Cover with the remaining squares, seal with your fingers and make two small cuts on top. Brush with the beaten egg and water.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden. Let rest for 15 minutes and serve; refrigerate any leftover cheese-filled pastries.
tips: Keep the filling centered so the cheese does not leak out.

title: Cream cheese pastries
description: Puff pastries filled with lightly sweetened cream cheese.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Cut the puff pastry into 20 equal rectangles.
Mix the cream cheese with the sugar, vanilla and zest until smooth.
Divide the filling among 10 rectangles, leaving a 1 cm border. Lightly moisten that border with water.
Cover with the other rectangles, seal the edges and cut a slit on top. Brush with beaten egg without soaking the cut sides.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes, until the pastry is fully cooked. Let cool for 20 minutes and refrigerate any leftovers.
tips: Do not overbeat the cheese: a firm filling makes the pastries easier to seal.

title: Coconut pastries
description: Puff pastry triangles filled with sweet coconut cooked until thick.
steps: Put the coconut, sugar, water and cinnamon in a saucepan. Cook for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring, until almost no free liquid remains.
Remove the cinnamon and spread the filling on a plate to cool completely, about 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200 °C. Cut the puff pastry into 12 squares and place a portion of coconut in the center of each.
Moisten the edges, fold each square into a triangle and seal with a fork. Brush with beaten egg and pierce the top.
Bake for 23 to 25 minutes on parchment paper. Wait until the filling has cooled to warm before serving.
tips: A wet filling softens the base; reduce it before filling the pastries.

title: Baked guava turnovers
description: Sweet shortcrust half-moons with a guava center.
steps: Mix the flour with the sugar and salt. Rub in the diced butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add the water gradually, just until a dough comes together. Flatten into a disk, cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Roll out to 3 mm thick and cut out 12 disks about 11 cm wide. Gather the scraps without overworking them.
Place 20 g of guava paste on each disk. Moisten the edge, fold into a half-moon and seal with a fork.
Brush with egg and bake at 190 °C for 23 to 25 minutes, until golden. Let cool for 10 minutes.
tips: Handle the dough as little as possible so it stays tender rather than elastic.

title: Sweet potato and cinnamon turnovers
description: Baked homemade pastry filled with cinnamon-scented Cuban sweet potato.
steps: Boil the sweet potato in enough water to cover for 20 to 25 minutes, until tender. Drain very well and mash.
Cook the mash with the sugar, cinnamon and zest for 5 minutes, stirring; spread on a plate and let cool.
Rub together the flour, salt and butter until crumbly. Add the water gradually, bring the dough together and chill for 30 minutes.
Roll out to 3 mm thick and cut out 12 disks measuring 11 cm. Divide the filling among them, fold over and press the edges with a fork.
Brush with beaten egg. Bake at 190 °C for 22 to 25 minutes, until the bases and edges are golden.
tips: Do not add milk to the mash: it should be firm so it does not make the pastry soggy.

title: Vanilla sponge cake (panetela)
description: A light whisked-egg sponge cake to serve with coffee or fill with your favorite spread.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Grease a 20 cm round pan and line its base with parchment paper.
Beat the eggs with the sugar for 8 to 10 minutes, until greatly increased in volume and the mixture falls in a visible ribbon.
Add the vanilla. Sift the flour and salt over the mixture in three batches, folding gently to combine.
Pour into the pan and smooth the top without tapping it. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes; do not open the oven during the first 20 minutes.
Check that a skewer comes out without raw batter. Rest for 10 minutes in the pan and another 20 on a wire rack before slicing.
tips: Its volume depends on thorough whisking and keeping the air in when folding in the flour.

title: Alcohol-free syrup-soaked sponge cake
description: Sponge cake squares moistened with citrus and vanilla syrup.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 120 g for the sponge cake and 100 g for the syrup

steps: Line a 20 cm square pan and preheat the oven to 175 °C. Beat the eggs with 120 g of sugar until tripled in volume.
Fold in 5 ml of vanilla and the flour sifted with the salt. Pour into the pan.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes and test with a skewer. Let cool to warm and cut into nine squares without removing them from the pan.
Boil the water with the remaining 100 g of sugar and the lemon peel for 5 minutes. Remove the peel and add the remaining vanilla.
Pour the warm syrup over the cake in several additions, allowing it to absorb. Once it is no longer hot, cover and refrigerate for the remainder of the 2-hour resting time.
tips: The Spanish name refers to the syrup soak; this version contains no rum.

title: Guava sponge roll (brazo gitano)
description: A thin sheet of sponge cake rolled around a smooth guava filling.
steps: Line a 30 × 40 cm baking sheet and heat the oven to 180 °C. Beat the eggs with the sugar for 8 minutes to make a stable foam.
Fold in the vanilla and sifted flour. Spread in an even layer and bake for 10 to 12 minutes, without letting it dry out.
Turn the hot sponge onto another sheet of parchment sprinkled with half the powdered sugar. Remove the baking paper and roll up with the clean paper.
Warm the guava paste with the water over low heat until spreadable. Let both the filling and the rolled sponge cool.
Carefully unroll, spread with the guava filling, leaving 2 cm clear at the end, and roll up again. Rest for 30 minutes and dust with the remaining sugar.
tips: Rolling the sponge while it is still warm helps prevent cracks.

title: Cuban marquesitas
description: Guava-filled sponge cake rectangles topped with cooked meringue.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 120 g for the sponge cake, 40 g for the syrup, 100 g for the meringue

steps: Beat the eggs with 120 g of sugar until the mixture forms a thick ribbon. Fold in the vanilla and sifted flour with a spatula.
Spread into a lined 25 × 30 cm pan. Bake at 175 °C for 20 to 25 minutes and cool on a wire rack.
Boil the water with 40 g of sugar for 3 minutes and let cool to warm. Cut the sponge into two equal sheets and brush both with the syrup.
Spread guava over one sheet, place the other on top and cut into 12 rectangles.
For the topping, combine the pasteurized egg whites, 100 g of sugar and the lemon juice in a bowl over a water bath, without touching the water. Stir until it reaches 71 °C.
Remove the bowl and beat until stiff peaks form and the meringue has cooled. Cover each marquesita with meringue and refrigerate until serving.
tips: This is the Cuban sponge cake marquesita, which is different from the Mexican crepe.
Use a thermometer for the meringue; syrup alone does not guarantee that the egg whites reach the required temperature.

title: Torticas de Morón (lime shortbread cookies)
description: Pale, crumbly cookies scented with lime zest.
steps: Mix the softened lard with the powdered sugar until smooth; there is no need to beat in much air.
Add the zest and salt. Add the sifted flour in two batches and mix by hand into a firm dough.
Shape into a log about 5 cm in diameter, wrap and refrigerate for 30 minutes to make slicing easier.
Cut into 20 rounds about 1 cm thick. Space them apart on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake at 170 °C for 15 to 18 minutes: they should cook through while staying pale on top. Leave on the baking sheet for 10 minutes before moving them.
tips: The cookies are delicate while hot.
You can use vegetable shortening; do not replace the fat with the same quantity of liquid oil.

title: Butter cookies for coffee
description: Simple butter and vanilla cookies with lightly golden edges.
steps: Beat the softened butter with the sugar for 3 minutes. Add the egg and vanilla.
Add the flour and salt, mixing just until no dry patches remain.
Shape into a disk, cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Roll out between two sheets of parchment to 5 mm thick.
Cut out about 24 cookies and transfer to a baking sheet, leaving 2 cm between them. Gather and reroll the scraps only once.
Bake at 175 °C for 12 to 15 minutes, until the edges begin to color. Cool for 10 minutes before transferring to a wire rack.
tips: If the cutters stick, dust them lightly with flour.

title: Señoritas (custard puff pastry slices)
description: Crisp puff pastry layers alternating with vanilla pastry cream.
steps: Cut the puff pastry into three rectangles about 12 × 30 cm. Prick them and bake between two parchment-lined baking sheets at 190 °C for 18 minutes.
Remove the top sheet and bake for another 7 minutes until golden. Cool the pastry sheets on a wire rack.
Whisk the egg yolks with the sugar, cornstarch and 100 ml of milk. Heat the remaining 400 ml and gradually pour it into the mixture.
Return to the saucepan; cook, stirring, until it comes to a gentle boil, then cook for 1 minute. Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla and butter.
Transfer the cream to a shallow container, cover its surface and refrigerate once it stops steaming. Cool completely before assembling.
Layer pastry, half the cream, pastry, the remaining cream and the final pastry sheet. Chill for 30 minutes, cut into eight portions with a serrated knife and dust with powdered sugar.
tips: Use gentle sawing motions when cutting so you do not crush the layers.

title: Capuchinos in small molds
description: Egg-yolk sponge bites soaked in syrup, adapted for home baking pans.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 40 g for the dough and 300 g for the syrup

steps: Grease 12 small muffin wells of about 50 ml each. Heat the oven to 180 °C.
Beat the egg yolks, egg white and 40 g of sugar for 12 to 15 minutes, until the foam is very thick and pale.
Sift in the cornstarch and fold gently to combine. Divide the mixture among the wells, filling each three-quarters full.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until set and a skewer comes out clean. Cool for 10 minutes, unmold and arrange in a deep dish.
Boil the water with 300 g of sugar, the cinnamon and lemon peel for 10 minutes. Remove the aromatics and add the vanilla.
Pour the warm syrup over the capuchinos. Once they are no longer hot, refrigerate for at least 2 hours to let them soak.
tips: The traditional shape uses cones; this version uses small molds without changing the type of batter.

title: Cuban celebration cake with meringue
description: A celebration cake with guava filling and a cooked meringue frosting.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 180 g for the sponge cake, 60 g for the syrup, 140 g for the topping

steps: Line the bases of two 20 cm round pans. Beat the eggs with 180 g of sugar for 10 minutes and add 5 ml of vanilla.
Fold in the sifted flour with a spatula. Divide between the pans and bake at 175 °C for 22 to 27 minutes; cool completely.
Boil the water and 60 g of sugar for 3 minutes. Add the remaining vanilla and let cool to warm; moisten both sponge cakes with this syrup.
Place one sponge on a plate, spread with guava and cover with the other.
Combine the pasteurized egg whites, 140 g of sugar and the lemon juice over a water bath. Stir until the mixture reaches 71 °C; then beat away from the heat until the meringue is stiff and cool.
Cover and decorate the cake with the meringue. Refrigerate until serving and wipe the knife clean between slices.
tips: Do not double the batter in the same pan: use more pans to preserve the layer thickness and baking time.

title: Homemade pan de gloria (spiced sweet rolls)
description: Spiced sweet rolls finished with honey and sugar.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 50 g for the dough and 20 g for finishing

steps: Mix the flour, 50 g of sugar, yeast, cinnamon and nutmeg. Add the evaporated milk, water, vanilla, oil and salt.
Knead for 10 to 12 minutes until elastic. If the dough is sticky, let it rest for 5 minutes before continuing to knead.
Cover and let rise for 60 to 90 minutes, until almost doubled in volume.
Divide into 12 portions, shape into rolls and place on a baking sheet with a little space between them. Let rise for another 40 to 50 minutes.
Bake at 180 °C for 22 to 25 minutes, until golden. Transfer to a wire rack.
Brush the hot rolls with honey and sprinkle with the remaining 20 g of sugar. Let cool to warm before serving.
tips: This home version leaves out malt powder.
Rising times depend on the temperature; watch for the increase in volume.

title: Homemade Cuban bread
description: Two thin-crusted loaves with a soft crumb for toast and small sandwiches.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast and sugar. Add the water and salt; knead until the dough is evenly combined.
Add the lard and knead for 8 to 10 minutes, until the dough stretches without tearing immediately.
Cover and let rest for 60 to 75 minutes, until almost doubled in volume. Press down to release excess gas.
Divide in two and shape into loaves about 35 cm long. Place on parchment paper and let rise for 40 minutes.
Score lengthwise with a sharp blade. Bake at 220 °C for 10 minutes, then reduce to 200 °C and bake for another 12 to 15 minutes, until golden.
Transfer to a wire rack and wait 20 minutes before cutting so the crumb can finish setting.
tips: This is a direct-dough adaptation for a home oven, without a preferment or palm leaf.

title: Medianoche rolls
description: Soft, slightly sweet rolls enriched with egg.

ingredients.name: Egg
ingredients.note: 2 for the dough and 1 for brushing

steps: Combine the flour, yeast and sugar. Add the milk, two eggs and salt; mix until no loose flour remains.
Knead for 5 minutes, add the softened butter and continue for another 10 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let rise for 75 to 90 minutes. Divide the dough into eight portions of equal weight.
Shape into oval rolls about 15 cm long and space them apart on a baking sheet. Let rise for another 45 to 60 minutes.
Brush with the remaining beaten egg. Bake at 180 °C for 18 to 22 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
Cool on a wire rack before slicing; their tender crumb is suited to medianoche sandwiches.
tips: The milk should feel lukewarm, never hot, so it does not harm the yeast.

title: Orange muffins
description: Snack-time muffins made with orange juice and zest.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line 12 muffin wells with paper liners.
Beat the eggs with the sugar for 2 minutes. Add the oil, orange juice and zest.
In a separate bowl, mix the flour, baking powder and salt. Fold into the wet ingredients with a spatula without overmixing.
Divide the batter among the wells, filling them no more than three-quarters full.
Bake for 18 to 22 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Rest for 5 minutes in the pan and 10 on a wire rack.
tips: Grate only the colored part of the peel, which adds aroma without as much bitterness.

title: Gaceñiga raisin loaf cake
description: A rectangular cake with a firm yet tender crumb dotted with raisins.
steps: Grease and line a 23 × 10 cm loaf pan. Heat the oven to 170 °C and reserve a tablespoon of the flour for the raisins.
Beat the softened butter with the sugar for 4 minutes. Add the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Mix the remaining flour, baking powder and salt. Add to the creamed mixture alternately with the milk, without overbeating.
Toss the raisins with the reserved flour and fold them in. Pour the batter into the pan and smooth the surface.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes, checking the center with a skewer. Leave in the pan for 15 minutes, then cool on a wire rack.
tips: If the top darkens before the center is cooked, cover it with foil.

title: Baked coconut bites (coquitos)
description: Small coconut mounds with golden outsides and tender centers.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Mix the egg whites with the sugar and salt using a fork; just loosen their texture without whipping them.
Add the coconut and vanilla. Let rest for 10 minutes so the coconut absorbs the moisture.
Using two teaspoons, form 18 compact mounds with space between them. Press lightly so they hold their shape.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until the tips and bottoms are golden. Wait 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack.
tips: Fresh coconut has a different moisture content; this formula uses dry unsweetened shredded coconut.

title: Mini meringues (merenguitos)
description: Small, dry and crisp meringues to serve with coffee.
steps: Combine the egg whites, sugar and lemon juice in a heatproof bowl. Set it over a gentle water bath without letting it touch the water.
Stir until the sugar dissolves and the mixture reaches 71 °C. Remove from the bath and beat until the meringue is glossy and stiff.
Add the vanilla. Using a piping bag or spoons, form 30 mounds about 3 cm wide on a lined baking sheet.
Bake at 100 °C for 80 to 90 minutes, until they release from the paper without a sticky center.
Turn off the oven and leave them inside for 30 minutes with the door slightly open. Cool completely before storing in an airtight container.
tips: Humidity softens the meringues; store them only once they are cold.

title: Coconut tartlets
description: Shortcrust pastry shells filled with coconut and vanilla.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 50 g for the dough and 90 g for the filling

ingredients.name: Egg
ingredients.note: 1 for the dough and 1 for the filling

steps: Rub together the flour, salt, 50 g of sugar and butter until crumbly. Add one egg, bring the dough together and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Heat the milk with the remaining sugar; add the coconut and cook for 5 minutes, stirring. Set aside and let cool to warm.
Roll the dough out to 3 mm thick and line 12 tartlet molds measuring 7 cm. Prick the bases and bake at 180 °C for 10 minutes.
Stir the second egg and vanilla into the cooled coconut mixture. Divide the filling among the shells without filling them to the rim.
Bake for another 18 to 20 minutes, until the filling is set and the edges are golden. Cool before unmolding.
tips: Small muffin wells also work if you line them only halfway up the sides.

title: Guava tartlets
description: Crisp pastry shells with thick guava filling and strips of pastry on top.
steps: Mix the flour, powdered sugar and salt. Rub in the diced butter with your fingertips, then add the egg and bring the dough together.
Wrap and chill for 30 minutes. Meanwhile, heat the guava paste with the water until it forms a thick cream and let cool to warm.
Roll the dough out to 3 mm thick and line 12 molds about 7 cm wide. Reserve the scraps for decoration.
Fill each shell with guava, leaving space below the rim. Cut strips from the scraps and place two crossed strips over each tartlet.
Bake at 180 °C for 23 to 25 minutes, until the edges are golden. Leave in the molds for 10 minutes before removing.
tips: Guava paste softens with a little water; a runny filling will overflow as it boils.

title: Guava bars (masas reales)
description: Sweet pastry bars with a layer of guava between two tender crusts.
steps: Line a 20 cm square pan and preheat the oven to 180 °C. Beat the butter and sugar until creamy.
Add the egg and milk. In a separate bowl, mix the flour, baking powder and salt; incorporate them to form a soft dough.
Divide the dough into two parts, one slightly larger than the other. Refrigerate both for 20 minutes to make them easier to handle.
Spread the larger portion over the bottom of the pan. Cover with thin slices of guava paste, leaving a half-centimeter border.
Roll the remaining dough between two sheets of parchment, place it on top and join the edges. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
Let cool for at least 30 minutes before removing from the pan and cutting into 12 bars.
tips: Cutting while very hot makes the guava spill out and the pastry break.

title: Mini puff pastry palmiers
description: Small puff pastries caramelized on both sides.
steps: Mix the sugar and cinnamon. Sprinkle half over the work surface and place the cold puff pastry on top.
Sprinkle the rest on top and roll gently to press it in, keeping a rectangle about 25 × 35 cm.
Fold both long sides toward the center, then repeat the fold. Bring the two halves together and chill for 20 minutes.
Cut the entire roll into about 35 slices, each 1 cm thick, and space them apart on parchment paper. Bake at 200 °C for 10 minutes, using several baking sheets if needed.
Turn them over with a spatula and bake for another 6 to 8 minutes until caramelized. After 5 minutes, transfer to a wire rack.
tips: Caramel can burn; use a spatula and let it cool before touching the pastries.

title: Vanilla cream horns
description: Puff pastry cones filled with chilled vanilla pastry cream.
steps: Mix the egg yolks, sugar, cornstarch and 80 ml of milk. Heat the remaining milk and add it gradually while whisking.
Return to the saucepan and cook, stirring, until it boils gently; cook for 1 minute. Add the vanilla, cover the surface directly and chill in a shallow container.
Grease ten oven-safe metal cone molds. Cut the puff pastry into 2 cm strips and wrap them around the molds, overlapping the edges.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 200 °C for 22 to 25 minutes. Let cool for 10 minutes before removing the molds.
Once the pastry and cream are cold, fill with a piping bag. Dust with powdered sugar and refrigerate until serving.
tips: Use oven-safe molds, never improvised paper or plastic cones.
Fill close to serving time to keep the pastry crisp.

title: Homemade Tatianoff chocolate cake
description: A layered cocoa sponge cake with chocolate buttercream.

ingredients.name: Pure cocoa powder
ingredients.note: 25 g for the sponge cake and 35 g for the cream

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 120 g for the sponge cake and 50 g for the syrup

steps: Line two 20 cm pans and heat the oven to 175 °C. Beat the eggs and 120 g of sugar until thick and foamy.
Fold in the flour and 25 g of sifted cocoa. Divide between the pans and bake for 18 to 22 minutes.
Cool the sponges completely. Boil 100 ml of water with 50 g of sugar for 3 minutes and add 5 ml of vanilla; let cool to warm.
Beat the softened butter for 3 minutes. Add the sifted powdered sugar and 35 g of cocoa, followed by the milk and remaining vanilla, to make a spreadable cream.
Keep the two sponge cakes whole to make two layers. Brush the first with some of the syrup and spread with about one-third of the buttercream.
Place the second sponge on top, moisten lightly with syrup and cover the sides and top with the remaining buttercream. Refrigerate for 60 minutes before slicing.
Take the portions out of the refrigerator about 15 minutes before serving so the buttercream softens.
tips: This adaptation uses buttercream without raw egg.

title: Baked anise rings
description: Small anise-flavored ring cookies to serve with coffee and milk.
steps: Beat the egg with the sugar. Add the oil, milk and lightly crushed anise seeds.
Mix the flour, baking powder and salt. Add to the wet ingredients to form a soft dough and let rest for 10 minutes.
Divide into 20 portions. Shape into short ropes, join the ends and leave a wide hole in the center.
Place on a parchment-lined baking sheet and bake at 180 °C for 18 to 20 minutes, until the bottoms are lightly golden.
Leave on the sheet for 5 minutes, then cool on a wire rack before storing.
tips: Do not add too much flour when shaping: it makes the cookies hard.

title: Homemade cusubé cassava cookies
description: Delicate cassava starch cookies with a touch of anise.

ingredients.name: Cassava starch
ingredients.note: sweet cassava starch, not whole-root cassava flour

steps: Beat the softened butter with the powdered sugar. Add the egg and ground or crushed anise.
Add the cassava starch and salt. Bring together with your hands; if crumbly, add water a teaspoon at a time.
Cover the dough and let rest for 15 minutes. Shape into 24 equal balls and flatten lightly with a fork.
Space apart on a lined baking sheet and bake at 165 °C for 15 to 18 minutes, until firm and pale.
Wait 15 minutes before moving them, as they break easily while hot. Finish cooling on a wire rack.
tips: Do not substitute grated cassava for cassava starch in this recipe.

title: Milk flan
description: Creamy condensed-milk flan with a layer of caramel.
steps: Heat the sugar with the water until the caramel is amber. Carefully pour into a 20 cm mold and tilt to coat the bottom.
Mix the eggs without making them foamy; add the condensed milk, evaporated milk, whole milk and vanilla. Strain into the caramel-lined mold.
Cover with foil and place inside a baking dish. Add hot water to the dish until it reaches halfway up the mold.
Bake at 170 °C for 55 to 65 minutes. The center should reach at least 71 °C and be set with a slight wobble.
Remove from the water bath, let cool for about 30 minutes and refrigerate for at least 4 hours. Loosen the edges and turn out onto a rimmed plate.
tips: Do not whisk vigorously: air creates holes in the flan.

title: Coconut flan
description: Flan made with coconut milk and the gentle texture of shredded coconut.
steps: Make a caramel with the sugar and water; coat the bottom of a 20 cm mold and let it harden.
Mix the eggs with both milks and the vanilla without incorporating much air. Add the shredded coconut.
Pour into the mold, cover with foil and place in a dish with hot water reaching halfway up the mold.
Bake at 170 °C for 60 to 70 minutes, until set and at least 71 °C in the center.
Remove from the water bath, let cool for 30 minutes and refrigerate for at least 4 hours. Unmold when cold.
tips: Stir the coconut milk before measuring to mix in its fat.

title: Pumpkin flan
description: Cooked pumpkin blended into a milk flan with caramel.
steps: Before measuring the pumpkin, steam it until tender and drain it. Blend to a purée without large fibers.
Heat the sugar with the water and pour the amber caramel into a 22 cm mold.
Mix the purée with both milks, the eggs, vanilla and cinnamon. Pour over the caramel.
Cover and bake in a water bath at 170 °C for 65 to 75 minutes; the center should be set and reach at least 71 °C.
Remove from the bath and let cool for about 30 minutes, then refrigerate for 4 hours. Carefully unmold when thoroughly cold.
tips: The stated weight is for cooked pumpkin; a watery purée changes the texture.

title: Rice pudding with cinnamon
description: Sweet rice pudding slowly cooked with milk, lemon and cinnamon.
steps: Rinse the rice once and put it in a saucepan with the water, cinnamon stick, lemon peel and salt.
Cook over low heat for 12 to 15 minutes, until most of the water has been absorbed.
Add the hot milk in two batches and cook for 30 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent sticking.
When the rice is tender, add the sugar and cook for another 8 to 10 minutes. Remove the lemon peel and cinnamon stick.
Divide among six bowls and sprinkle with cinnamon. Serve warm or refrigerate in shallow containers once it stops steaming.
tips: Take it off the heat a little looser than you prefer: it thickens as it cools.

title: Fresh corn pudding (majarete)
description: A fresh corn pudding with milk, cinnamon and lemon peel.
steps: Blend the corn with 550 ml of milk for 2 minutes. Pass through a fine strainer, pressing to extract the liquid.
Dissolve the cornstarch in the remaining 100 ml of cold milk. Add it to the strained liquid along with the sugar, salt, cinnamon and lemon peel.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened and gently bubbling.
Cook for another 3 minutes to thoroughly cook the starch and corn. Remove the cinnamon stick and lemon peel.
Divide among bowls, let the initial heat subside and refrigerate for at least 2 hours. Serve with ground cinnamon.
tips: This version includes a little cornstarch because the starch content of fresh corn varies.

title: Creamy sweet potato pudding (boniatillo)
description: Sweet Cuban sweet potato purée with a light cinnamon and lemon syrup.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.note: for the syrup, plus water for boiling

steps: Cut the sweet potato into pieces and boil, covered with water, for 20 to 25 minutes, until it falls apart when pierced.
Drain and mash while hot, removing any tough fibers. For a fine texture, pass through a sieve.
Boil the 200 ml of water with the sugar, cinnamon and lemon peel for 5 minutes. Remove the aromatics.
Gradually add the syrup to the purée, then add the salt. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy.
Divide among bowls and let cool to warm. Refrigerate if serving later.
tips: You can serve it with white cheese on the side.

title: Sweet coconut in syrup
description: Grated coconut simmered in a cinnamon-scented syrup.
steps: Check that the grated coconut contains no shell fragments. Set aside in a bowl.
Put the water, sugar, cinnamon, lemon peel and salt in a saucepan; bring to a gentle boil.
Add the coconut and cook over low heat for 25 to 35 minutes, stirring occasionally.
When the coconut is tender and the syrup is light but slightly thickened, remove the cinnamon and lemon peel; do not let it dry out.
Let cool to warm and transfer to a clean container. Keep refrigerated and serve small portions with their syrup.
tips: Fresh coconut gives a different texture from the dried coconut used for baking.

title: Guava shells in syrup (casquitos)
description: Tender guava halves in syrup, prepared for short-term refrigerated storage.
steps: Wash the guavas, peel them thinly and cut in half. Scoop out the seeds with a teaspoon without breaking the walls.
Place the guava shells in a wide saucepan with the water and simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Add the sugar and cinnamon. Simmer over low heat for 20 to 30 minutes, moving the pan rather than stirring vigorously.
When the shells are tender and the liquid is syrupy, add the lemon juice and turn off the heat.
Cool in a shallow container and refrigerate. Serve the guava shells with a little of their syrup.
tips: This is a refrigerated dessert; the recipe is not a canning procedure for storage at room temperature.

title: Papaya in syrup
description: Firm papaya pieces slowly cooked in cinnamon syrup.

ingredients.name: Peeled green or partly ripe papaya

steps: Cut the papaya into strips or 3 cm cubes. Rinse and boil in a pot with enough water to cover for 10 minutes.
Drain and discard this first cooking water. Place the fruit in a clean saucepan with the 800 ml of water specified in the recipe.
Add the sugar and cinnamon. Cook uncovered over low heat for 45 to 55 minutes, until the fruit is tender and slightly translucent.
Add the lemon juice during the last 5 minutes. If the liquid reduces before the fruit softens, add a little hot water.
Let cool to warm and refrigerate in a clean container. Serve cold with some of the syrup.
tips: Very ripe papaya falls apart; choose a firm fruit.

title: Sweet milk curds (dulce de leche cortada)
description: Soft curds made by adding lemon to fresh milk, then simmering them in syrup.
steps: Heat the fresh milk in a heavy-bottomed saucepan until very hot, without allowing it to boil over.
Add the lemon juice, stir just once and let rest for 5 minutes so the curds and whey separate.
Add the sugar, cinnamon and lemon peel. Cook at a very gentle simmer for 50 to 65 minutes.
Stir occasionally with a wide spoon without breaking up the curds. Remove from the heat when the whey has reduced to a clear syrup.
Remove the cinnamon and lemon peel, add the vanilla and transfer to a shallow container. Cool and keep refrigerated.
tips: Use fresh milk in good condition; curdle it with lemon, never use spoiled milk.

title: Vanilla custard (natilla)
description: A milk and egg-yolk custard with vanilla and a light dusting of cinnamon.
steps: Reserve 150 ml of cold milk. Heat the remaining milk with the lemon peel until it starts to steam.
Whisk the egg yolks with the sugar, cornstarch and reserved milk until smooth.
Remove the lemon peel and gradually add the hot milk to the egg yolks while stirring.
Return to the saucepan and cook over medium-low heat, stirring, until it comes to a gentle boil. Cook for 1 minute and add the vanilla.
Divide among six bowls, sprinkle with cinnamon and let the initial heat subside. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving cold.
tips: Stir into the corners of the saucepan as well to prevent the custard from sticking.

title: Cassava fritters in syrup (buñuelos)
description: Figure-eight cassava fritters served with cinnamon syrup.

ingredients.name: Peeled sweet cassava
ingredients.note: fresh or frozen, commercially sold for food

ingredients.name: Oil for frying
ingredients.note: amount needed for the pan; not all will be consumed

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.note: for the syrup, plus water for boiling

steps: Boil the cassava in plenty of water for 25 to 30 minutes, until completely tender. Discard the water, remove the central fibers and mash.
Let cool for 20 minutes. Add the egg, salt, crushed anise and the flour gradually until the dough can be shaped.
Divide into eight parts. Form thick ropes and shape into figures of eight, firmly joining the ends.
Boil 300 ml of water with the sugar, cinnamon and lemon peel for 10 minutes. Set aside and remove the aromatics.
Heat the oil to 170 °C. Fry the fritters in batches for 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked in the center.
Drain on paper towels and serve with syrup poured over them, keeping them from piling up while hot.
tips: Prepare the dough with fully cooked cassava, never grated raw root.

title: Bread pudding with raisins
description: Day-old bread transformed into a milk and raisin pudding.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 100 g for the pudding and 80 g for the caramel

steps: Cut the bread into cubes and soak in the milk for 15 minutes. Mash with a fork, retaining some texture.
Make caramel with 80 g of sugar and the water. Pour into a 20 cm mold with a capacity of at least 1.5 liters.
Beat the eggs, 100 g of sugar, vanilla and cinnamon. Mix with the bread and add the raisins.
Pour into the mold and bake in a water bath at 175 °C for 45 to 55 minutes, until set; check that the center reaches at least 71 °C.
Let cool for 30 minutes and refrigerate for 2 hours. Unmold when cold or serve directly from the mold.
tips: Use bread that is in good condition and has no mold.

title: Cuban torrejas (syrup-soaked French toast)
description: Bread slices dipped in milk and egg, fried until golden and finished with syrup.
steps: Boil the water with the sugar, cinnamon and lemon peel for 10 minutes. Remove the aromatics and reserve the syrup.
Heat the milk with the vanilla until lukewarm. Beat the eggs separately in a shallow dish.
Dip each slice in the milk for a few seconds on each side; it should be moist without falling apart. Then coat with egg.
Heat a thin layer of oil and fry the slices in batches over medium heat, about 3 minutes per side, until the egg is cooked.
Drain on paper towels, arrange in a serving dish and pour over some of the syrup. Let rest for 10 minutes before serving.
tips: If the bread is very soft, shorten the soaking time.

title: Soft peanut turrón
description: Firm bars of ground roasted peanuts bound with syrup.
steps: Pulse the peanuts into a coarse meal without turning them into peanut butter.
Line a small pan about 15 × 15 cm with parchment paper.
Heat the sugar, water and honey until the syrup reaches 115 °C; use a thermometer and avoid stirring once it boils.
Remove from the heat and immediately stir in the peanuts, vanilla and salt with a heatproof spatula.
Pour into the pan and press down with another sheet of parchment on top, without touching the hot mixture. Let cool for 90 minutes and cut into 12 bars.
tips: Finely grinding the peanuts helps the turrón hold together, but they should not become an oily paste.

title: Candied peanuts
description: Peanuts coated in a crisp, toasted sugar crust.
steps: Line a baking sheet with parchment paper and have a heatproof spatula ready.
Put the peanuts, sugar and water in a wide skillet. Cook over medium heat, stirring, until the liquid reduces.
Keep stirring when the sugar turns dry and sandy; this is a normal stage of the process.
Lower the heat slightly and keep stirring until some of the sugar melts again and coats the peanuts. Add the vanilla and salt.
Spread over the baking sheet and separate the peanuts with two forks. Cool completely for 30 minutes before storing.
tips: Do not use your hands to separate the peanuts while the sugar is hot.

title: Sweet egg-yolk bites (yemitas)
description: Small balls of cooked egg yolk and sugar with soft centers.
steps: Boil the water with the sugar and lemon peel for 5 minutes. Remove the peel and let the syrup cool to warm.
Pass the egg yolks through a strainer and gradually add the syrup, stirring so they do not set suddenly.
Cook the mixture in a saucepan over very low heat, stirring continuously, until it forms a thick paste and reaches at least 71 °C.
Add the vanilla, spread in a shallow container and cool. Refrigerate for about 90 minutes, until it can be shaped.
Lightly coat your hands with powdered sugar, shape 12 small balls and roll them in the sugar. Refrigerate until serving.
tips: A silicone spatula helps you stir across the entire bottom without leaving hot spots.

title: Tocinillo del cielo (egg-yolk custard)
description: A small egg-yolk and syrup custard made without milk.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 200 g for the syrup and 80 g for the caramel

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.note: 200 ml for the syrup and 40 ml for the caramel

steps: Cook 80 g of sugar with 40 ml of water until amber and coat a 16 cm mold with the caramel.
Boil the remaining 200 g of sugar with the remaining 200 ml of water for 5 minutes. Let cool to warm so it does not cook the yolks when mixed.
Mix the egg yolks, whole egg and vanilla without making them foamy. Add the warm syrup in a thin stream and strain into the mold.
Cover and bake in a water bath at 160 °C for 30 to 40 minutes, until set and at least 71 °C in the center.
Remove from the bath and let cool for 30 minutes. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours before unmolding and cutting into small portions.
tips: The syrup should be warm, not freshly boiled, when combined with the yolks.

title: Grapefruit shells in syrup
description: The white grapefruit rind softened and sweetened after some of its bitterness is removed.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.note: for the syrup, plus more for soaking and boiling

steps: Wash the grapefruits and use a peeler to remove only the outer yellow layer. Cut into quarters and remove the flesh, keeping the thick white rind.
Soak the shells in water in the refrigerator for 8 hours, changing the water twice.
Boil in fresh water for 15 minutes and discard the water. Repeat twice, until tender and moderately bitter.
Make a syrup with one liter of water, the sugar and cinnamon. Add the drained shells and cook over low heat for 35 to 45 minutes.
Add the lemon juice at the end, remove the cinnamon and let cool to warm. Refrigerate the shells covered with their syrup.
tips: Not all of the bitterness will necessarily disappear; it is part of this dessert’s character.

title: Homemade mango jam
description: Ripe mango cooked down into a thick, spreadable preserve.
steps: Cut the mango into small cubes and remove any coarse fibers.
Put the mango, sugar, lemon juice and water in a heavy-bottomed saucepan. Let rest for 10 minutes to release the juices.
Cook over medium heat until boiling, then lower the heat. Stir during the 25 to 35 minutes of cooking to prevent sticking.
Mash the pieces with a fork or carefully blend away from the heat. A spoon drawn across the bottom should leave a briefly visible trail.
Transfer to a clean container, let cool to warm and refrigerate. Use to fill bread or serve with cheese.
tips: This is not a sterilized shelf-stable preserve: keep it refrigerated.

title: Sweet ripe plantains
description: Ripe plantains cooked in a light caramel and cinnamon sauce.
steps: Cut the plantain into pieces about 5 cm long. Melt the butter in a wide skillet.
Brown the plantain pieces for 2 minutes on each side and transfer to a plate.
Add the sugar to the skillet with 30 ml of the water. Heat until a light caramel forms.
Carefully add the remaining water and cinnamon. Return the plantains and cook, covered, over low heat for 15 minutes.
Uncover, add the lemon juice and reduce the sauce for 3 to 5 minutes. Let cool for 15 minutes before serving.
tips: Adding water to caramel can release steam; use a deep pan and keep your hand clear.

title: Sweet cornmeal pudding
description: A thick cornmeal pudding with milk and cinnamon, served warm.

ingredients.name: Fine cornmeal
ingredients.note: not cornstarch or nixtamalized corn dough

steps: Mix the cornmeal with the cold water until smooth.
Heat the milk with the cinnamon, lemon peel and salt in a heavy-bottomed saucepan.
Pour in the cornmeal mixture in a thin stream while stirring. Cook over low heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the sugar and cook for another 5 minutes. If it thickens before the grains are cooked, add a little hot water.
Remove the cinnamon and lemon peel, divide among bowls and serve warm. Refrigerate leftovers once the initial heat subsides.
tips: Fine cornmeal cooks faster than coarse polenta; check the grind listed on the package.

title: Homemade vanilla custard ice cream
description: Vanilla ice cream with a cooked base of milk, cream and egg yolks.
steps: Heat the milk with half the cream and the salt. Whisk the egg yolks with the sugar in a separate bowl.
Pour some of the hot milk over the yolks, stirring, then return everything to the saucepan.
Cook over low heat to 82 °C, stirring without allowing it to boil; the custard should coat the back of a spoon.
Strain, then add the vanilla and remaining cream. Cool the container in an ice-water bath, then refrigerate for 4 hours.
Freeze in a wide container. During the first 2 hours, stir vigorously every 30 minutes; then freeze for another 4 hours.
Let stand at room temperature for 5 to 10 minutes before serving so it can be scooped.
tips: If using an ice cream maker, churn the cold base according to the appliance instructions.

title: Pineapple ice pops (durofríos)
description: Water-based frozen treats made with ripe pineapple in small molds.
steps: Remove the pineapple peel, eyes and tough core. Weigh 400 g of flesh and cut it into cubes.
Dissolve the sugar in 100 ml of the water, stirring until no visible crystals remain.
Blend the pineapple with the remaining water, sugar water and lemon juice. Strain if you prefer a texture without fibers.
Divide among eight freezer-safe molds, leaving room for expansion.
Freeze for at least 6 hours. To unmold, briefly wet the outside of the mold with water without submerging the contents.
tips: Use food-safe molds; if using small cups, make sure they are rated for freezing.

title: Brown sugar coconut balls (coquitos prietos)
description: Coconut and brown sugar cooked into a firm mixture and shaped into small balls.
steps: Put the brown sugar, water, lemon peel and salt in a saucepan. Boil for 5 minutes and remove the peel.
Add the coconut and cinnamon. Cook over medium-low heat for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring constantly toward the end.
The mixture is ready when it comes together and a spatula drawn through it exposes the bottom; no loose syrup should remain.
Spread in a dish and wait until warm enough to touch without burning. Use two spoons to divide into 12 portions.
Shape into balls with barely damp hands and let cool for 30 minutes on parchment paper.
tips: Do not try to shape the balls while the sugar is still hot.

title: Cuban coffee with sugar foam (espumita)
description: Strong moka-pot coffee mixed with a whipped sugar foam.

ingredients.name: Ground coffee for a moka pot
Water
ingredients.note: or the amount specified for your coffee maker, without exceeding the valve level

steps: Fill the reservoir of a small moka pot according to its marking, always below the valve.
Put the coffee in the filter without tamping it. Close the moka pot and heat over medium-low heat according to its instructions.
Put the sugar in a small heatproof jug. Collect the first two teaspoons of coffee that emerge and add them to the sugar.
Beat with a teaspoon until pale and foamy. Let the coffee finish brewing and remove the moka pot from the heat.
Gradually add the coffee to the sugar foam, stir gently and divide among four small cups.
tips: Adjust the water and coffee quantities to the size of the moka pot; do not block its valve.

title: Coffee with milk (café con leche)
description: Hot milk and strong coffee for breakfast or an afternoon snack.
steps: Make 100 ml of strong coffee using your usual coffee maker.
Heat the milk in a saucepan over medium heat, stirring to prevent a film from forming on the bottom.
Remove before it boils over; if you like it foamy, briefly use a milk frother.
Divide the coffee between two large cups and add the hot milk.
Sweeten to taste, stir and serve immediately.
tips: For a stronger drink, reduce the proportion of milk rather than boiling the coffee.

title: Mamey sapote milkshake
description: A thick milkshake made with ripe mamey sapote and cold milk.
steps: Open the mamey, remove the seed and scoop out the ripe flesh with a spoon.
Weigh the pulp and place it in the blender with the cold milk.
Blend for 30 to 45 seconds, until no pieces remain.
Add the sugar if needed, then the ice. Blend again until smooth.
Pour into two glasses and serve immediately to keep its thick texture.
tips: Unsweetened frozen pulp also works; in that case, you can leave out the ice.

title: Soursop milkshake
description: Seedless soursop blended with milk into a smooth, aromatic drink.
steps: Separate the soursop flesh and carefully remove every black seed before blending.
Check the pulp with clean fingers to make sure no seeds or skin remain.
Blend the pulp with the milk for 45 seconds, until the fibers are incorporated.
Add sugar according to the sweetness of the fruit, then the ice; blend briefly again.
Serve in two chilled glasses immediately after preparing.
tips: If buying frozen pulp, choose a seedless product and check its label.

title: Papaya milkshake
description: Ripe papaya blended with milk and a touch of vanilla.
steps: Wash the outside of the fruit, cut it open and remove the skin and seeds. Weigh 300 g of flesh.
Cut the flesh into cubes and place it in the blender.
Add the cold milk and vanilla. Blend for 30 seconds, until no pieces remain.
Taste and add sugar if needed; add the ice and blend for a few more seconds.
Pour into two glasses and enjoy freshly made.
tips: Very ripe papaya usually needs less sugar.

title: Guava juice
description: Ripe guava blended and strained into a refreshing fruit drink.
steps: Wash the guavas and remove the ends and any damaged areas. Cut into quarters.
Blend with 400 ml of water using short pulses to release the pulp without crushing the seeds excessively.
Pass the mixture through a fine strainer, pressing the pulp with a spoon. Discard the trapped seeds.
Add the remaining water, lemon juice and sugar; stir until dissolved.
Divide the ice among four glasses and pour in the juice. Stir before serving again because the pulp settles.
tips: For a thicker drink, reserve some of the water and adjust at the end.

title: Tamarind cooler
description: A sweet-tart drink made with tamarind pulp and water.

ingredients.name: Shelled tamarind
ingredients.note: with seeds; or 120 g of pure seedless pulp

steps: Check that no hard shell remains on the tamarind. Bring 400 ml of the water to a boil and remove from the heat.
Add the tamarind and soak for 15 minutes. Once cool enough to handle, loosen the pulp with a spoon.
Press through a strainer and discard the seeds and fibers; do not grind them in the blender.
