Dissolve the sugar in the still-warm liquid and add the remaining 600 ml of water. Chill in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Serve in four glasses with ice and stir the jug before each serving.
tips: Commercial concentrated paste can be much more acidic; this recipe uses fruit or pure pulp.

title: Homemade hot chocolate
description: Lightly thickened hot chocolate with milk and cinnamon.
steps: Mix the cocoa, sugar and cornstarch with 100 ml of cold milk to make a smooth paste.
Heat the remaining 500 ml of milk with the cinnamon and salt in a saucepan.
Gradually add the cocoa paste, whisking to combine.
Cook over low heat for 3 to 4 minutes after it begins bubbling, stirring constantly.
Remove the cinnamon, add the vanilla and pour into three cups, letting it cool slightly before drinking.
tips: Pure cocoa powder is not the same as a presweetened instant chocolate mix.

title: Lemonade with spearmint
description: Refreshing alcohol-free lemonade with spearmint.
steps: Wash the lemons and spearmint leaves. Squeeze the lemons and strain out the seeds.
Dissolve the sugar in 150 ml of the water, stirring for 1 to 2 minutes.
Gently press the spearmint leaves between your hands to release their aroma without crushing them.
Combine the juice, sugar water and remaining water in a jug. Add the leaves and let rest for 5 minutes.
Divide the ice among four glasses and pour in the lemonade; remove the leaves if you prefer a completely smooth drink.
tips: Do not crush the spearmint excessively, as this can add bitterness.

title: Puffed wheat milkshake
description: A creamy puffed wheat cereal milkshake with milk and vanilla.
steps: Check that the cereal is ready-to-eat puffed wheat, not raw wheat or flour.
Put the wheat in the blender with the milk and let soak for 2 minutes.
Add the condensed milk and vanilla. Blend for 45 to 60 seconds, until the cereal is thoroughly ground.
Add the ice and blend briefly again. Adjust the texture with a little more milk if it is too thick.
Pour into two glasses and serve immediately, as the cereal continues absorbing liquid.
tips: Wheat contains gluten even when puffed; this drink is not suitable for a gluten-free diet.

title: Beef rolls stuffed with ripe plantain
description: Thin steaks filled with plantain and simmered in tomato sauce with olives.
steps: Peel the plantains and cut them into thick strips. Brown in one tablespoon of oil for 6 minutes and let cool slightly.
Lay out the steaks, season with salt and pepper, and divide the plantain among them. Roll up and secure with kitchen string; count the pieces.
Brown the rolls in the remaining oil for 6 minutes and remove. Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the same pot.
Add the tomatoes, water, oregano, and olives; return the rolls and cover. Simmer gently for 35 to 40 minutes, until the meat is tender and the center reaches 74 °C.
Rest for 5 minutes, remove all the string, and serve sliced on the diagonal with the sauce.
tips: Keep the filling away from the edges so it does not escape.

title: Beef stew with sweet potato and olives
description: Beef braised with white sweet potato, bell pepper, and olives in a reduced sauce.
steps: Cut the beef into 3 cm cubes and season with salt and cumin. Brown in oil in batches for 8 minutes.
Add the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic; sauté for 7 minutes before adding the tomatoes, water, and bay leaf.
Cover and simmer gently for 80 minutes, adding a little hot water if the pot becomes dry.
Peel the sweet potato and cut into 3 cm cubes; add with the olives once the meat starts to soften. Cook for another 25 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf and check that both the meat and sweet potato are tender when pierced. Reduce uncovered for 5 minutes and adjust the salt.
tips: Add the sweet potato after the meat has started to soften so it does not fall apart.

title: Coffee and orange braised beef flank
description: Beef flank braised in the oven with mild coffee, orange, and onion.
steps: Mix the orange juice, crushed garlic, oregano, and cumin; marinate the beef and refrigerate for two hours. Preheat the oven to 170 °C.
Drain the beef and brown it in oil in an ovenproof pot for 4 minutes per side. Reserve the marinade to cook with the meat.
Add the sliced onion, coffee, water, and marinade. Bring to a boil, cover tightly, and transfer to the oven.
Braise for 2 and a half to 3 hours until the beef is very tender, turning it halfway through and checking the liquid.
Rest for 10 minutes; reduce the sauce on the stove, adjust the salt and pepper, and serve the meat sliced against the grain.
tips: Use mild coffee: a very strong espresso can overpower the sauce.

title: Beef strips with cabbage and soy sauce
description: A quick stir-fry of beef, cabbage, and carrot with garlic and ginger.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: only if needed after tasting the cooked dish

steps: Slice the meat into strips against the grain; mix with one tablespoon of soy sauce and refrigerate for 15 minutes. Slice the cabbage and cut the carrot into thin matchsticks.
Heat two tablespoons of oil and stir-fry the beef in batches for 3 minutes, until browned; set aside.
Add the remaining oil, sliced onion, chopped garlic, and ginger. Stir-fry for 2 minutes, then add the carrot and cabbage and cook for 5 minutes.
Mix the orange juice, remaining soy sauce, and cornstarch dissolved in water. Return the beef and pour in the sauce; boil for 2 minutes, stirring.
Check that the thick strips reach 63 °C and let rest off the heat for 3 minutes. Add pepper and taste before adding salt.
tips: A very hot skillet and small batches help the beef stay browned.

title: Beef meatballs with squash and cumin
description: Meatballs in a thick winter squash and tomato sauce.
steps: Mix the meat with the egg, breadcrumbs, one grated garlic clove, half a teaspoon of cumin, salt, and pepper. Shape into 16 balls.
Brown in oil for 6 minutes and set aside. Sauté the chopped onion and remaining garlic for 5 minutes.
Add the cubed squash, tomatoes, water, and remaining cumin; cover and cook for 15 minutes. Mash half the squash.
Return the meatballs to the sauce and simmer gently for 15 to 20 minutes, until their centers reach 71 °C.
Adjust the salt and consistency with a few tablespoons of water if needed. Serve without breaking up the remaining squash cubes.
tips: The squash thickens the sauce without any additional flour.

title: Beef and mashed plantain pie
description: Layers of beef with sautéed vegetables and mashed green plantain, finished in the oven.
steps: Peel the plantains, slice into rounds, and boil in the salted water for 25 minutes. Reserve 200 ml of the water and drain.
Mash the hot plantain with two tablespoons of oil, one grated garlic clove, and the reserved water added gradually, until you have a thick mash.
Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper, and remaining garlic in the remaining oil; add the beef and cumin and cook for 8 minutes. Add the tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes, until the meat reaches 71 °C.
Heat the oven to 190 °C. Spread the beef in a 24 cm baking dish, cover with the plantain mash, and scatter over the cheese.
Bake for 20 minutes, until golden and the center reaches 74 °C. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.
tips: The mash should be spreadable; add hot liquid before assembling if it is too firm.

title: Bell peppers stuffed with beef and corn
description: Baked bell peppers with a filling of beef, corn, and tomato.
steps: Halve the peppers lengthwise and remove the seeds. Bake the empty halves for 12 minutes at 190 °C in a dish with the water.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in oil for 5 minutes; add the beef and oregano and cook for 8 minutes, breaking up the meat.
Add the tomatoes and drained corn. Cook for 10 minutes, until the filling is moist and the meat reaches 71 °C.
Fill the pepper halves, top with cheese, and bake for another 20 minutes, until the filling reaches 74 °C.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve each portion with the juices left in the dish.
tips: Choose similarly sized peppers so they soften at the same time.

title: Eggplants stuffed with beef and cheese
description: Roasted eggplants filled with seasoned ground beef, eggplant flesh, and cheese.
steps: Halve the eggplants lengthwise and score the flesh without cutting through the skin. Brush with one tablespoon of oil and roast for 30 minutes at 190 °C.
Scoop out some of the flesh, leaving a one-centimeter-thick shell; chop the flesh and reserve the shells.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the remaining oil. Add the meat, oregano, salt, and pepper; cook for 8 minutes, then add the tomatoes and eggplant flesh and cook for 10 minutes.
Fill the shells, scatter over the grated cheese, and bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until the filling reaches 74 °C.
Let settle for 5 minutes and serve with a wide spatula to avoid breaking the skin.
tips: The roasted eggplant should be soft before you scoop it out.

title: Beef steak with guava sauce
description: Griddled steak with onion and a savory guava and vinegar sauce.
steps: Season the steaks with salt and pepper and keep refrigerated. Slice one onion into strips and chop the other with the garlic.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in one tablespoon of oil for 6 minutes; add the guava, vinegar, water, and cumin and boil for 8 minutes.
Blend the sauce and adjust the salt. Sauté the sliced onion in another tablespoon of oil until golden.
Cook the steaks in the remaining oil for 2 to 4 minutes per side, depending on thickness, until they reach 63 °C; rest for 3 minutes.
Serve the meat with the sautéed onion and the guava sauce on the side, to add as desired.
tips: Use unsweetened pulp; sweet guava paste requires different proportions.

title: Beef stew with chickpeas and carrots
description: A beef stew with cooked chickpeas and tender carrots.
steps: Cut the beef into pieces and pat dry; season with salt and brown in oil in batches for about 10 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic, add the paprika and tomatoes, and cook for 5 minutes without burning the paprika.
Return the meat, add the water and bay leaf, and cover and simmer over low heat for 95 minutes.
Add the sliced carrot and drained chickpeas; cook for another 30 minutes, until the meat and carrot are tender.
Remove the bay leaf and reduce uncovered for 5 minutes if there is too much liquid. Check the salt after adding the chickpeas.
tips: This recipe starts with cooked chickpeas, not dried ones.

title: Beef short ribs with wine and roasted garlic
description: Meaty beef short ribs braised with red wine and a whole head of garlic.
steps: Season the ribs with salt and pepper and brown them in oil on all sides. Preheat the oven to 170 °C.
Remove the meat and sauté the roughly chopped onion and carrot for 8 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and wine and boil for 3 minutes.
Add the water and bay leaf, return the ribs, and add the garlic head cut in half crosswise. Cover tightly.
Bake for about 3 hours until the meat is fork-tender; check the liquid every hour and add hot water if needed.
Rest for 10 minutes. Squeeze the softened garlic cloves into the sauce, remove the bay leaf, skim off the fat, and serve.
tips: Choose ribs with plenty of meat and leave some bone attached for braising.

title: Beef cheeks with malanga
description: Slow-simmered beef cheeks with malanga in a tomato sauce.
steps: Trim the outer membranes from the beef cheeks and cut them into large pieces. Season with salt and brown in oil for 10 minutes.
Add the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic; sauté for 8 minutes, then add the tomatoes, water, oregano, and bay leaf.
Cover and cook at a very gentle simmer for 2 and a half hours; the cheeks should begin to yield when pierced.
Peel and rinse the malanga, then cut into 3 cm cubes. Add to the pot and cook for 30 to 40 minutes, until both the meat and malanga are tender.
Remove the bay leaf and stir gently to thicken the sauce with the malanga's starch. Adjust the salt and serve.
tips: If the meat is still firm, cook it longer before adding the malanga.

title: Beef flank braised in dark beer
description: Large pieces of beef flank cooked with dark beer, carrot, and bell pepper.
steps: Cut the beef into three or four large pieces, season with salt and cumin, and brown in oil for 8 minutes.
Sauté the chopped onion, garlic, and bell pepper in the same pot. Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the beer and water and return the meat. Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for 2 hours.
Add the carrot chunks and continue cooking for 30 minutes, or until the meat separates easily into thick strands.
Uncover and reduce the sauce for 5 minutes, check the salt, and serve with the vegetables left intact.
tips: Choose a dark beer that is not too bitter; bitterness intensifies as the sauce reduces.

title: Beef meatloaf with spinach and carrot
description: A ground beef roll filled with sautéed spinach and carrot sticks.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 1000 ml for the carrots and 150 ml for the sauce

steps: Cook the carrot sticks in 1000 ml of water for 8 minutes and drain. Sauté the spinach with one tablespoon of oil and one garlic clove; drain very well.
Mix the beef, egg, breadcrumbs, two grated garlic cloves, salt, and half the oregano. Spread into a rectangle on parchment paper.
Spread the spinach over the meat and line up the carrots in the center. Roll up using the paper to help and seal the seams; remove the paper.

Sauté the onion and remaining garlic in the remaining oil, add the tomatoes, the remaining 150 ml of water, and the oregano, and pour into a baking dish. Add the meatloaf and bake for 50 to 60 minutes at 180 °C.
Check that the center reaches 74 °C and rest for 10 minutes before slicing. Serve with the sauce.
tips: Drain the spinach well so its moisture does not split the roll.

title: Beef skewers with plantain and bell pepper
description: Beef cubes alternating with firm ripe plantain and roasted bell pepper.
steps: Cut the beef into 2.5 cm cubes. Mix with the garlic, sour orange juice, two tablespoons of oil, cumin, and salt; refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Peel the plantain and cut into thick rounds; cut the bell pepper and onion into squares. If using wooden skewers, soak them while the meat marinates.
Thread the meat and vegetables onto skewers, leaving room for the heat to reach them. Thread the plantain onto separate skewers and brush with the remaining oil.
Cook on a hot grill or griddle for 10 to 14 minutes, turning; remove the plantain when tender. The beef must reach 63 °C.
Rest the meat for 3 to 5 minutes and serve with the plantain skewers. Discard the raw marinade.
tips: Separate plantain skewers let you remove them without waiting for the meat to finish cooking.

title: Cumin beef patties with pickled onion
description: Beef patties served without buns, with red onion and avocado.
steps: Thinly slice the onion. Bring the vinegar, water, sugar, and a pinch of salt to a boil; pour over the onion and let cool for 30 minutes.
Mix the meat with the grated garlic, cumin, salt, and pepper without overworking it. Shape into four evenly thick patties.
Oil a griddle and cook the patties for about 5 minutes per side, without pressing down on them.
Check that the centers reach 71 °C and cook longer if needed. Slice the avocado while the patties finish cooking.
Serve on plates with the drained onion and sliced avocado; refrigerate any leftover pickled onion.
tips: Do not add egg or breadcrumbs: gently pressing the meat together is enough to hold its shape.

title: Beef liver with roasted bell peppers
description: Strips of liver finished in tomato sauce with roasted bell peppers.
steps: Roast the halved peppers for 20 minutes at 220 °C, cool slightly, and remove any skin that comes away easily. Cut into strips.
Remove the membranes from the liver, cut into one-centimeter strips, and pat dry. Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in two tablespoons of oil.
Add the tomatoes, water, and cumin; cook for 10 minutes, then add the peppers and vinegar.
In another skillet, sauté the liver in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, turning it. Add it to the sauce.
Cook for another 3 to 5 minutes, until the thick strips reach 74 °C. Add salt at the end and serve immediately.
tips: Finish cooking the liver just before serving so it does not toughen in the sauce.

title: Beef tongue with lemon and parsley
description: Cooked beef tongue, browned in slices and served with a green parsley sauce.
steps: Simmer the tongue, covered with water, with the halved onion, two garlic cloves, bay leaf, and salt for about 2 and a half to 3 hours, until tender.
Cool just enough to handle, then remove the thick skin and tough base. Cut into one-centimeter slices.
Blend the parsley, remaining garlic, lemon juice, two tablespoons of oil, and four tablespoons of cooking liquid; adjust the salt and pepper.
Brown the slices in the remaining oil in batches for 2 minutes per side, until heated through.
Serve immediately, adding the green sauce at the end to preserve its fresh flavor.
tips: Peel the tongue while it is still warm; the skin clings more tightly once it is completely cold.

title: Oxtail with squash and white beans
description: Tender oxtail in a stew with winter squash and cooked white beans.
steps: Pat the oxtail pieces dry and season with salt; brown in oil for 10 minutes and remove.
Sauté the chopped onions and garlic for 7 minutes. Add the tomatoes, water, bay leaf, oregano, and oxtail.
Cover and simmer very gently for 3 hours, checking that there is enough liquid, until the meat starts to pull away from the bone.
Skim off the surface fat and add the cubed squash and drained beans. Simmer for another 25 minutes, until the squash is tender.
Remove the bay leaf, adjust the salt, and rest off the heat for 3 minutes before dividing the meat and beans among plates.
tips: Add the beans already cooked and near the end so they hold their shape.

title: Beef stew with eggplant and basil
description: Beef cubes with roasted eggplant and a fragrant tomato sauce.
steps: Cut the beef into cubes, season with salt, and brown in two tablespoons of oil. Add the chopped onion and garlic and sauté for 6 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, water, and oregano, then cover and cook for 100 minutes, until the beef is almost tender.
Meanwhile, cut the eggplant into 3 cm cubes, toss with the remaining oil, and roast for 25 minutes at 200 °C.
Add the eggplant to the stew and cook uncovered for 15 minutes so it absorbs some of the sauce.
Tear the basil by hand, stir it in off the heat, and adjust the salt. Serve with the vegetable pieces intact.
tips: Roasting the eggplant first keeps it from falling apart during the beef's long cooking time.

title: Beef eye of round stuffed with carrot and bacon
description: Beef eye of round larded with carrot and bacon, in an onion sauce.
steps: Carefully make lengthwise channels through the beef. Insert carrot and bacon sticks; tie the meat with kitchen string.
Season with salt and pepper and brown the meat in oil for 10 minutes. Remove and sauté the roughly chopped onions and garlic.
Add the tomatoes, vinegar, water, and bay leaf. Return the meat, cover, and simmer gently for about 2 and a half hours, turning occasionally.
Continue until the meat is tender and the center of the filling reaches 74 °C. Remove and rest for 10 minutes.
Remove the string and bay leaf, blend the sauce, and cut the beef into thin slices.
tips: Ask the butcher for an evenly shaped piece; a tapered cut is harder to stuff.

title: Beef steaks with mushroom and cheese topping
description: Browned steaks topped with mushrooms and cheese and briefly baked.
steps: Slice the mushrooms and chop the onion and garlic. Sauté in two tablespoons of oil for 8 minutes, until the moisture evaporates.
Dissolve the cornstarch in the cold milk, add to the mushrooms, and boil for one minute; season with salt and pepper.
Brown the steaks in the remaining oil for 2 minutes per side and place in a baking dish; preheat the oven to 220 °C.
Cover with the mushrooms and cheese and bake for 5 to 8 minutes, until the cheese melts and the meat reaches 63 °C.
Rest for 3 minutes before serving, dividing all the topping among the plates.
tips: The sauce should be thick enough to stay on top of the steak.

title: Beef meatballs in coconut sauce
description: Spiced meatballs in a coconut sauce with bell pepper and lemon.
steps: Mix the beef, egg, breadcrumbs, one grated garlic clove, cumin, and salt. Shape into 16 meatballs.
Brown in oil for 6 minutes and remove. Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper, and remaining garlic in the same pot.
Add the coconut milk and water, bring to a gentle simmer, and return the meatballs to the pot.
Cover and cook for 20 minutes, turning once, until the centers of the largest meatballs reach 71 °C.
Add the lemon juice, adjust the salt, and thicken uncovered for 3 minutes without boiling vigorously.
tips: Use unsweetened coconut milk and stir it in the container before measuring.

title: Beef stir-fry with green beans and ginger
description: Beef strips with crisp-tender green beans and a citrus and ginger sauce.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: only if needed after tasting the cooked dish

steps: Cut the beef into strips and marinate with half the soy sauce for 15 minutes in the refrigerator. Trim the green beans and cook in the water for 4 minutes; drain.
Stir-fry the beef in two tablespoons of oil in batches for 3 minutes and set aside.
Add the remaining oil, sliced onion, chopped garlic, and ginger. Cook for 3 minutes, then add the green beans and cook for 2 minutes.
Dissolve the cornstarch in the orange juice and remaining soy sauce; return the beef, pour in the mixture, and boil for 2 minutes until the sauce is glossy.
Check that the meat reaches 63 °C and rest for 3 minutes. Season with pepper and taste before adding salt.
tips: Drain the green beans very well before stir-frying so they do not cool the skillet.

title: Thick beef and potato baked omelet
description: A thick oven-baked omelet with ground beef, potatoes, and bell pepper.
steps: Peel the potatoes, cut into small cubes, and boil in the water for 12 minutes; drain and let the steam escape.
While the potatoes boil, sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in two tablespoons of oil. Add the beef, cumin, and salt and cook for 10 minutes, until the meat reaches 71 °C.
Beat the eggs with the milk and a pinch of salt. Mix with the potatoes and the warm cooked beef mixture.
Grease a 24 cm baking dish with the remaining oil, pour in the mixture, and bake at 180 °C for 25 to 30 minutes, until the center reaches 74 °C.
Rest for 5 minutes before cutting into portions; the center should be set with no liquid egg.
tips: If the beef mixture still has a lot of liquid, cook it off before combining it with the eggs.

title: Pork tenderloin with roasted mango
description: Pork medallions with mango and onion roasted together in one dish.
steps: Cut the tenderloin into 3 cm medallions. Marinate with the garlic, lemon juice, cumin, two tablespoons of oil, and salt; refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Peel the mangoes and cut into wedges; separate the onion into petals. Toss with the remaining oil in a baking dish.
Roast the mango and onion for 12 minutes at 200 °C. Meanwhile, drain the medallions and brown in a skillet for 2 minutes per side.
Arrange the pork beside the mango and bake for another 10 to 15 minutes, until the centers reach 63 °C.
Rest for 3 minutes, sprinkle with cilantro, and serve with the pan juices.
tips: Firm mango holds its shape when roasted; avoid overripe fruit.

title: Pork chops in coffee sauce
description: Pork chops with a quick coffee and onion sauce and a touch of honey.
steps: Pat the chops dry and season with salt, pepper, and cumin. Brown in oil for 3 minutes per side and remove.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the skillet for 6 minutes, scraping the bottom with a spoon.
Add the coffee, water, honey, and vinegar; boil for 3 minutes to bring the sauce together.
Return the chops, cover, and cook over low heat for 8 to 12 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 63 °C.
Rest for 3 minutes and reduce the sauce separately if it is too thin; spoon it over the chops.
tips: Mild coffee adds aroma without bitterness; taste before adding any extra sugar.

title: Guava-glazed pork ribs
description: Oven-baked ribs finished with a guava, vinegar, and garlic glaze.
steps: Remove the membrane from the underside of the ribs if present. Rub with the crushed garlic, oil, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Place in a baking dish with 150 ml of water, cover tightly, and bake for 2 hours at 175 °C, until tender.
Meanwhile, dissolve the guava paste in the remaining water with the vinegar over low heat; stir until a thick glaze forms.
Uncover the ribs, brush with the glaze, and bake at 200 °C for another 20 to 25 minutes, brushing once more and taking care not to burn them.
Rest for 10 minutes and cut between the bones. Heat the remaining glaze separately and serve.
tips: The sugar in guava browns quickly; apply the glaze only toward the end.

title: Pork shoulder with tamarind
description: Chunks of pork simmered with tamarind and onion until tender.
steps: Dilute the tamarind in 150 ml of water and strain out seeds or fibers. Marinate the cubed pork with half this mixture, garlic, cumin, and salt; refrigerate for one hour.
Drain the pork, reserve the marinade, and brown in oil for 10 minutes. Add the chopped onion and bell pepper and sauté for 7 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, marinade, remaining tamarind mixture, sugar, and remaining water. Bring to a boil and cover.
Simmer gently for 90 minutes, until the pork is tender, adding hot water if the pot becomes dry.
Uncover and reduce for 10 minutes; taste and adjust the salt, without trying to remove all the tamarind's tartness.
tips: Commercial tamarind pulp varies in strength; start with less if yours is a very strong concentrate.

title: Shredded pork with black beans
description: Shredded, browned pork served over black beans with sautéed aromatics.
steps: Cut the shoulder into three pieces and place in a pot with the sour orange juice, one onion, three garlic cloves, bay leaf, half a teaspoon of cumin, salt, and 600 ml of water.
Cover and simmer gently for about 2 hours, until the meat shreds easily. Remove the bay leaf and shred the meat once cool enough to handle.
Sauté the remaining onion and garlic in one tablespoon of oil; add the beans, remaining cumin, and 200 ml of water and simmer for 15 minutes.
Brown the shredded pork in the remaining oil in batches for 10 minutes, adding a few tablespoons of its cooking liquid to keep it juicy.
Serve the beans with the pork on top; adjust the salt in each preparation separately.
tips: The bean weight refers to beans that are already cooked and drained.

title: Pork meatballs with cilantro and lemon
description: Pork meatballs in a reduced broth scented with cilantro and lemon.
steps: Mix the pork, egg, breadcrumbs, one grated garlic clove, half the chopped cilantro, salt, and pepper. Shape into 16 meatballs.
Brown the meatballs in oil for 7 minutes and remove. Sauté the chopped onion and remaining garlic.
Add 300 ml of water and half the lemon juice; return the meatballs, cover, and cook for 18 to 20 minutes, until they reach 71 °C.
Dissolve the cornstarch in the remaining water and add; boil for one minute to thicken the broth.
Remove from the heat, add the remaining cilantro and lemon juice, and adjust the salt before serving.
tips: Adding some of the cilantro at the end preserves its aroma.

title: Pork steak coated in cassava flatbread crumbs
description: Thin pork steak coated in cassava flatbread crumbs and cooked in a skillet.

ingredients.name: oil
ingredients.note: for frying; not all of it is consumed

steps: Marinate the steaks with the crushed garlic, sour orange juice, salt, and pepper; refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Crush the cassava flatbread into small crumbs without turning it all into powder. Prepare separate plates of cornstarch and beaten egg.
Drain the meat and coat with cornstarch, egg, and cassava crumbs, pressing the coating firmly onto the meat.
Shallow-fry in oil at about 170 °C for 3 to 5 minutes per side, until the center reaches 63 °C.
Rest on a rack for at least 3 minutes and serve hot. Discard any leftover coating ingredients that touched raw meat.
tips: Check the cassava flatbread label for ingredients and possible allergens.

title: Spinach-stuffed pork tenderloin
description: Butterflied tenderloin stuffed with sautéed spinach and cheese.
steps: Butterfly the tenderloin without separating the halves. Sauté the spinach with one tablespoon of oil and two garlic cloves; drain and let cool.
Season the meat with salt and pepper, spread over the spinach and cheese strips, and roll up; tie with kitchen string. Preheat the oven to 190 °C.
Brown the roll in the remaining oil for 5 minutes. Place in a baking dish on top of the sliced onion.
Add the orange juice, water, remaining garlic, and oregano; bake for 25 to 35 minutes, until the center of the filling reaches 74 °C.
Rest for 10 minutes, remove the string, and cut into thick slices with a sharp knife.
tips: Well-drained spinach keeps the filling from making the meat too wet.

title: Pork loin with coconut and corn
description: Pork loin strips cooked in a coconut sauce with corn and bell pepper.
steps: Cut the loin into thick strips, season with salt, and brown in oil for 6 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Sauté the chopped onion and bell pepper for 6 minutes, then add the garlic and cumin and cook for half a minute.
Pour in the coconut milk and water; add the drained corn and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Return the pork and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until the thickest strips reach 63 °C.
Remove from the heat, add the lemon juice, and rest for 3 minutes; adjust the salt and serve with the creamy sauce.
tips: Do not boil the coconut sauce vigorously, so its texture stays smooth.

title: Pork stir-fry with cabbage and sesame
description: Pork strips with cabbage, carrot, and toasted sesame seeds.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: only if needed after tasting the cooked dish

steps: Cut the pork into strips, mix with one tablespoon of soy sauce, and refrigerate for 15 minutes. Cut the cabbage and carrot into thin strips.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry skillet for one minute and remove. Add two tablespoons of oil and brown the pork in batches.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the remaining oil; add the carrot and cabbage and stir-fry for 5 minutes, leaving them slightly crisp.
Return the pork and add the water, vinegar, remaining soy sauce, and cornstarch, mixed together beforehand; boil for 2 minutes and check that the pork reaches 63 °C.
Rest off the heat for 3 minutes and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Taste before adding salt.
tips: Soy sauce adds salt; do not add extra salt during marinating.

title: Pork and pineapple skewers
description: Griddled skewers of marinated pork, pineapple, and onion.
steps: Cut the pork into 2.5 cm cubes. Marinate with the garlic, sour orange juice, two tablespoons of oil, oregano, and salt for one hour in the refrigerator.
Cut the pineapple, onion, and bell pepper into pieces similar in size to the meat; soak wooden skewers if using them.
Thread the ingredients onto the skewers in alternating pieces and brush with the remaining oil. Discard the raw marinade.
Cook on a griddle or grill over medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes, turning every few minutes, until the pork reaches 63 °C.
Rest for at least 3 minutes and serve the freshly cooked skewers with the browned pineapple.
tips: Leave small gaps between pieces so the heat can reach all of the meat.

title: Pork rib stew with malanga
description: Pork ribs with malanga that naturally thickens the sauce.
steps: Season the ribs with salt and cumin and brown in oil for 10 minutes. Remove the pieces.
Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic; add the tomatoes, water, and bay leaf and return the ribs.
Cover and simmer gently for 70 minutes, until the meat begins to soften.
Peel and rinse the malanga and cut into large pieces. Add and cook for another 30 minutes, checking that enough liquid remains.
Remove the bay leaf, check that the ribs and malanga are tender, and adjust the salt; stir gently to thicken without breaking everything up.
tips: Cut the malanga into even pieces to avoid hard pieces remaining in a thick sauce.

title: Sweet and sour orange pork
description: Lightly coated pork with orange, bell peppers, and onion.

ingredients.name: oil
ingredients.note: for frying; not all of it is consumed

steps: Cut the pork into 2 cm cubes and mix with the beaten egg and half the soy sauce; coat in 70 g of cornstarch.
Fry in batches in oil at about 170 °C for 5 to 7 minutes, until the pork reaches 63 °C. Drain and rest for 3 minutes.
Leave just one tablespoon of oil in a clean skillet. Stir-fry the chopped onion, peppers, and garlic for 5 minutes.
Mix the orange juice, vinegar, sugar, remaining soy sauce, and the remaining 10 g of cornstarch; pour in and boil for 2 minutes until thickened.
Add the pork and toss for one minute, just long enough to coat it with sauce without softening the coating too much.
tips: Cook the pork completely before adding it to the sauce.

title: Pork and sweet potato pie
description: A ground pork filling topped with sweet potato mash and baked until golden.
steps: Peel and cut the sweet potato; cover with water and boil for 20 minutes. Drain and mash with the hot milk, butter, and salt.
Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic in oil. Add the pork and cumin and cook for 8 minutes, breaking up the meat.
Stir in the tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes, until the filling is thick and reaches 71 °C.
Spread the pork in a baking dish, cover with the mash and cheese, and bake at 190 °C for 20 to 25 minutes, until the center reaches 74 °C.
Rest for 10 minutes and cut into portions with a spatula, reaching all the way to the bottom.
tips: Drain the sweet potato well so the pie holds together when served.

title: Pork chops with mint sauce and twice-fried plantains
description: Griddled chops served with twice-fried plantains and a fresh herb and citrus sauce.

ingredients.name: frying oil
ingredients.note: not all of it is consumed

steps: Marinate the chops with the orange juice, two crushed garlic cloves, salt, and pepper; refrigerate for 30 minutes. Blend the spearmint, remaining garlic, lemon juice, and olive oil to make the sauce.
Peel the plantains, cut into 3 cm rounds, and fry at about 160 °C for 5 to 6 minutes. Drain and flatten between sheets of kitchen paper.
Drain the chops and cook on a hot griddle for 4 to 6 minutes per side, until they reach 63 °C; rest for 3 minutes.
Fry the plantains again at 180 °C for about 2 minutes per side, until crisp. Drain and season with salt.
Serve the chops and plantains with the fresh sauce in a separate bowl.
tips: Do not pour the sauce over all the plantains in advance, or they will lose their crispness.

title: Pork shoulder with beer and prunes
description: Chunks of pork shoulder with light-colored beer, prunes, and carrot.
steps: Cut the pork into 4 cm cubes, season with salt, and brown in oil for 10 minutes. Set aside.
Sauté the chopped onions and garlic for 7 minutes. Add the beer and water and scrape up the browned juices from the bottom.
Return the meat with the bay leaf and oregano; cover and simmer gently for 85 minutes.
Add the carrot chunks and whole prunes; simmer for another 25 minutes, until the pork is tender.
Remove the bay leaf, skim off the surface fat, reduce the sauce for a few minutes, and adjust the salt before serving.
tips: Add the prunes toward the end so they do not dissolve completely into the sauce.

title: Chilled pork loin in vinegar marinade
description: Sliced cooked pork loin with onion and carrot in a refrigerated vinegar marinade.
steps: Season the loin with salt and brown it in two tablespoons of oil. Place in a baking dish with 150 ml of water and roast at 180 °C for 45 to 60 minutes, until it reaches 63 °C.
Rest for at least 10 minutes and cut into thin slices. Arrange in a clean, shallow container.
Sauté the sliced onion, carrot, and garlic in the remaining oil for 8 minutes. Add the vinegar, remaining water, bay leaf, pepper, and salt and boil for 7 minutes.
Pour the marinade over the loin; let the strongest steam escape and refrigerate promptly, rather than leaving it out to cool for hours.
Refrigerate for at least two hours, remove the bay leaf, and serve cold with the vegetables.
tips: This dish must be kept refrigerated; it is not a shelf-stable preserve.

title: Pork stew with eggplant
description: Lean pork in a tomato sauce with eggplant browned separately.
steps: Cut the pork into 3 cm cubes and season with salt and pepper. Brown in two tablespoons of oil for 8 minutes.
Add the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic; sauté for 6 minutes, then add the tomatoes, water, and oregano.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 55 minutes, until the pork begins to soften.
Cut the eggplant into cubes and brown in the remaining oil for 8 minutes. Add it to the pot and cook for another 20 minutes.
Check that the meat is tender and the eggplant is cooked; adjust the salt and reduce uncovered if the sauce is thin.
tips: Browning the eggplant separately improves its texture in the stew.

title: Pork meatloaf with roasted peanuts
description: A ground pork loaf with peanuts and carrot, baked with tomato sauce.
steps: Chop the peanuts into small pieces. Mix with the pork, carrot, egg, breadcrumbs, two grated garlic cloves, cumin, and salt.
Shape into a firm loaf and place in a baking dish; preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Sauté the onion and remaining garlic in oil for 6 minutes; add the tomatoes and water and boil for 5 minutes. Pour around the loaf.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes, until the center reaches 74 °C, covering loosely if the top browns too much.
Rest for 10 minutes and serve in slices with the sauce, spooning up the pan juices.
tips: Chop the peanuts rather than grinding them into butter, so they add texture.

title: Pork liver with tomato and olives
description: Thoroughly cooked pork liver in a tomato and olive sauce.
steps: Remove the membranes from the liver and cut into even one-centimeter strips. Pat dry and keep refrigerated.
Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic in two tablespoons of oil for 7 minutes. Add the tomatoes, water, and oregano and cook for 12 minutes.
Sauté the liver in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, turning to cook all sides.
Add the liver and olives to the sauce and cook for another 5 minutes, until the thick pieces reach 74 °C.
Taste before adding salt, add pepper, and serve immediately to keep the liver from drying out.
tips: Do not taste the liver before it is fully cooked, and use separate utensils for raw and cooked food.

title: Pork chops with oven-roasted squash
description: Pork chops roasted over squash, onion, and whole garlic cloves.
steps: Marinate the chops with the sour orange juice, two crushed garlic cloves, oregano, salt, and pepper; refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Cut the squash and onion into wedges, toss with two tablespoons of oil and the remaining garlic cloves, and roast for 25 minutes at 200 °C.
Drain the chops and brown them in the remaining oil in a skillet for 2 minutes per side.
Place them over the squash and bake for another 12 to 18 minutes, until the meat reaches 63 °C and the vegetables are tender.
Rest for 3 minutes and serve with the softened garlic and pan juices.
tips: If the chops are very thin, check their doneness before the suggested time.

title: Pork tenderloin with orange and mustard
description: Tenderloin medallions in an orange and mustard sauce.
steps: Cut into 3 cm medallions, season with salt and pepper, and brown in oil for 3 minutes per side. Set aside.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the same skillet for 5 minutes.
Mix the orange juice, mustard, and 60 ml of water; pour into the skillet, bring to a gentle simmer, and return the pork.
Cook for 5 to 8 minutes, until the pork reaches 63 °C. Add the cornstarch dissolved in the remaining water and boil for one minute.
Rest off the heat for 3 minutes; check the sauce for salt and spoon over the medallions.
tips: Mustard already adds salt; season the sauce after reducing it.

title: Citrus-garlic lamb shoulder with potatoes
description: Oven-braised lamb shoulder with citrus and potatoes roasted in its juices.
steps: Crush the garlic, oregano, cumin, and salt; mix with the sour orange juice and oil and marinate the lamb for four hours in the refrigerator.
Place the sliced onion in a baking dish, add the lamb, and pour in the marinade and water. Cover tightly and bake at 170 °C.
Roast for 2 and a half hours, checking the liquid. Peel the potatoes and cut into large wedges.
Add the potatoes, baste with the juices, and continue cooking covered for 35 minutes. Uncover and brown for 20 to 25 minutes, until both lamb and potatoes are tender.
Rest for 10 minutes and serve the meat pulled from the bone with the skimmed pan juices.
tips: Lamb shoulder needs longer cooking than chops to soften its connective tissue.

title: Lamb with chickpeas and bell pepper
description: Lamb stew with cooked chickpeas and red bell peppers.
steps: Cut the lamb into cubes, trim excessive outer fat, and brown in oil for 10 minutes.
Add the chopped onion and garlic and sauté for 5 minutes; stir in the cumin, tomatoes, water, bay leaf, and salt.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 90 minutes, until the lamb begins to become tender.
Add the sliced peppers and drained chickpeas and cook for another 25 to 30 minutes, checking the liquid.
Remove the bay leaf, skim off the surface fat, and adjust the salt. Serve with enough sauce to coat the chickpeas, without turning it into soup.
tips: Add the cooked chickpeas toward the end; they do not need to cook as long as the meat.

title: Lamb meatballs with spearmint
description: Spearmint lamb meatballs in a tomato and lemon sauce.
steps: Mix the meat with the egg, breadcrumbs, one garlic clove, cumin, half the chopped spearmint, and salt. Shape into 16 meatballs.
Brown in oil for 6 minutes and remove. Sauté the chopped onion and remaining garlic for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and water, boil for 5 minutes, and return the meatballs.
Cover and cook over low heat for 20 minutes, until the centers of the largest meatballs reach 71 °C.
Add the lemon juice and remaining spearmint off the heat, adjust the salt, and serve with the sauce.
tips: Chop the spearmint just before using it to preserve its aroma.

title: Garlic lamb chops with eggplant
description: Griddled lamb chops served with roasted eggplant.
steps: Marinate the chops with three garlic cloves, half the lemon juice, two tablespoons of oil, oregano, salt, and pepper; refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Cut the eggplant into one-centimeter rounds, brush with the remaining oil, and roast at 200 °C for 25 minutes, turning halfway through.
Mix the remaining grated garlic with the chopped parsley and remaining lemon juice and spoon over the cooked eggplant.
Drain the chops and cook on a griddle for 3 to 5 minutes per side, depending on thickness, until they reach 63 °C.
Rest for 3 minutes and serve with the eggplant rounds; discard the raw marinade.
tips: Measure the temperature without letting the probe touch the bone.

title: Leg of lamb with orange and garlic
description: Boneless leg of lamb roasted with orange, garlic, and onion.
steps: Tie the leg to give it an even thickness. Mix the citrus juices, garlic, oil, oregano, salt, and pepper and marinate for four hours in the refrigerator.
Preheat the oven to 175 °C. Place the sliced onion in a baking dish and add the water.
Add the leg with its marinade and roast for 75 to 95 minutes, basting with the juices halfway through.
Check that the center reaches at least 63 °C, remove, and rest for 15 minutes before taking off the string.
Boil the pan juices for 5 minutes, skim off the fat, and serve with the lamb sliced against the grain.
tips: The timing is for a boneless leg; a bone-in piece needs a different estimate.

title: Lamb and okra in red sauce
description: Slow-simmered lamb finished with sautéed okra.
steps: Brown the cubed lamb with two tablespoons of oil and salt for 8 minutes.
Add the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic; sauté, then add the tomatoes, water, and cumin. Cover and simmer gently for 110 minutes.
Wash the okra, dry very well, and trim only the tough tips. Sauté in the remaining oil for 5 minutes.
Add the okra and lemon juice once the lamb is tender; simmer for another 15 to 20 minutes, without stirring too much.
Check the salt and serve with the okra whole and the sauce slightly thickened.
tips: If the lamb is still firm, wait before adding the okra.

title: Goat stew with red beans
description: Goat meat simmered with cooked red beans and bell pepper.
steps: Marinate the goat with the sour orange juice, three garlic cloves, cumin, and salt and refrigerate for two hours.
Drain and brown in oil, set aside, and sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper, and remaining garlic.
Add the tomatoes, water, bay leaf, and meat, then cover and cook for about 2 and a half hours, until the goat is tender.
Stir in the drained cooked beans and simmer for another 20 minutes, stirring gently and adding water if needed.
Remove the bay leaf, skim off the surface fat, adjust the salt, and serve the meat and beans with their sauce.
tips: Use fully cooked beans before adding them to the stew.

title: Oven-roasted goat shoulder with citrus-garlic marinade
description: Boneless goat shoulder slowly roasted with sour orange and onion.
steps: Crush the garlic, oregano, cumin, and salt and mix with the juice and oil. Rub over the goat, season with salt and pepper, and refrigerate for six hours.
Preheat the oven to 170 °C. Arrange the onion wedges in a baking dish and place the meat on top.
Add the marinade and water, cover tightly, and bake for 3 hours, turning the meat once and checking the bottom of the dish.
Uncover and roast for another 20 to 30 minutes, until browned and fork-tender.
Rest for 10 minutes, skim the fat from the juices, and slice the meat against the grain.
tips: Goat meat can vary in toughness; continue cooking covered if it still resists a fork.

title: Goat stew with squash and corn
description: Goat stew with winter squash and pieces of fresh corn on the cob.
steps: Season the goat with cumin and salt and brown in oil for 10 minutes, in several batches.
Sauté the chopped onions and garlic; add the tomatoes, oregano, and water and return the meat.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 and a half hours, until the goat starts to soften.
Cut the corn cobs into thick rounds and the peeled squash into cubes; add them and cook for another 30 to 35 minutes.
Mash two squash cubes into the broth to thicken it, adjust the salt, and serve with a piece of corn on each plate.
tips: This recipe uses fresh corn; dried corn requires soaking and a different cooking time.

title: Goat meatballs in peanut sauce
description: Goat meatballs with a roasted peanut and tomato sauce.
steps: Mix the goat meat with the egg, breadcrumbs, two grated garlic cloves, cumin, and salt. Shape into 16 meatballs and refrigerate while you prepare the sauce.
Blend the peanuts with 200 ml of water. Sauté the onion and remaining garlic in oil for 6 minutes, then add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the blended peanut mixture and remaining water, mix, and bring to a very gentle simmer.
Add the meatballs in a single layer, cover, and cook for 25 minutes, turning carefully; check that the centers reach 71 °C.
Adjust the salt and thin with hot water if the sauce becomes too thick. Serve without letting the bottom catch.
tips: Ask for ground goat meat suitable for cooking and keep it cold until you shape the meatballs.

title: Goat and cassava casserole
description: Goat stew served with sweet cassava cooked separately.
steps: Marinate the goat with the juice, three garlic cloves, cumin, and salt for two hours in the refrigerator. Drain and brown in oil.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and remaining garlic, add the tomatoes, 800 ml of water, and bay leaf, and cook the meat covered for 2 and a half hours, until tender.
Peel the cassava completely, cut into chunks, and remove the central fiber where possible. Boil in the remaining water for 25 to 35 minutes, until tender.
Discard all the cassava cooking water, remove any remaining central fibers, and add the cooked cassava to the stew.
Cook for 10 minutes to combine the flavors, remove the bay leaf, and adjust the salt. Serve carefully, watching for bones.
tips: Use commercially sold sweet cassava and boil it thoroughly; do not add its cooking water to the sauce.

title: Roasted rabbit with citrus-garlic marinade and sweet potato
description: Rabbit pieces roasted over sweet potato with garlic and citrus.
steps: Mix the garlic, juice, oil, oregano, salt, and pepper and marinate the rabbit for two hours in the refrigerator.
Peel the sweet potato, cut into wedges, and place with the onion in a baking dish; add the water and arrange the rabbit with its marinade on top.
Cover and bake at 180 °C for 45 minutes, basting once with the juices.
Uncover and continue cooking for 25 to 35 minutes, until the rabbit is tender and reaches 71 °C and the sweet potato is easily pierced.
Serve the rabbit with the sweet potato and juices; check the pieces for any bone splinters.
tips: Rabbit is lean: keep the dish covered during the first part of roasting.

title: Rabbit in beer with mushrooms
description: Rabbit simmered in light-colored beer with mushrooms browned separately.
steps: Season the rabbit with salt and brown in two tablespoons of oil for 8 minutes; remove.
Sauté the chopped onions and garlic, add the beer and water, and scrape the bottom of the pot. Return the rabbit with the bay leaf and oregano.
Cover and cook over low heat for 60 minutes, checking that it does not dry out.
Slice the mushrooms, brown them in the remaining oil, and add to the rabbit; cook for another 20 minutes, until the rabbit reaches 71 °C and is tender.
Remove the bay leaf and reduce the liquid uncovered for a few minutes. Adjust the salt and serve.
tips: Browning the mushrooms separately concentrates their flavor without watering down the stew.

title: Rabbit with olives and roasted peppers
description: Rabbit in tomato sauce with roasted bell peppers and olives.
steps: Roast the peppers for 25 minutes at 220 °C, cool slightly, peel, and cut into strips. Meanwhile, season the rabbit with salt and brown it in oil.
Remove the rabbit and sauté the chopped onion and garlic for 6 minutes; add the tomatoes and oregano and cook for 5 minutes.
Return the meat, add the water, and cover and simmer gently for 60 minutes.
Stir in the roasted peppers and olives and simmer for another 20 minutes, until the rabbit is tender and reaches 71 °C.
Taste before adding more salt and reduce the sauce if it is thin. Serve the rabbit pieces with the peppers on top.
tips: Olives add salt, so adjust the seasoning at the end of cooking.

title: Garlic rabbit with lemon and parsley
description: Rabbit browned and cooked with garlic cloves, wine, and lemon.
steps: Pat the rabbit dry and season with salt and pepper. Lightly crush the garlic cloves without mashing them.
Brown the garlic in oil over medium heat for 2 minutes and remove. Brown the rabbit in batches for 10 minutes.
Return the garlic and meat to the pot, add the wine and water, and cover and cook over low heat for 55 minutes.
Add half the lemon juice and cook for another 10 to 15 minutes, until tender and the rabbit reaches 71 °C; uncover toward the end to reduce the sauce.
Add the chopped parsley and remaining lemon juice off the heat and serve with the softened garlic.
tips: Remove the garlic while browning the rabbit so it does not burn.

title: Rabbit with coconut and squash
description: Tender rabbit in a coconut sauce with winter squash and bell pepper.
steps: Season the rabbit with salt and cumin and brown in oil for 10 minutes.
Add the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic; sauté for 6 minutes and add the water. Cover and simmer for 50 minutes.
Cut the squash into large cubes and add with the coconut milk. Stir gently.
Cook for another 25 to 30 minutes, until the rabbit is tender and reaches 71 °C and the squash is soft.
Add the lemon juice off the heat, adjust the salt, and serve without bringing back to a vigorous boil.
tips: Add the coconut milk toward the end to keep the sauce smooth.

title: Rabbit meatballs with tomato and basil
description: Ground rabbit bound with breadcrumbs and egg, in a fresh tomato sauce.
steps: Moisten the breadcrumbs with the milk and mix with the rabbit, egg, one grated garlic clove, and salt. Shape into 16 meatballs with damp hands.
Grate the tomatoes and discard the skins. Sauté the onion and remaining garlic in oil for 6 minutes.
Add the grated tomatoes and water and cook for 10 minutes, until a sauce forms.
Add the meatballs, cover, and simmer gently for 20 minutes, turning once; check that the centers reach 71 °C.
Add the torn basil, adjust the salt, and serve without breaking up the meatballs.
tips: Ask for boneless ground rabbit and check that no bone fragments remain.

title: Rabbit stuffed with spinach and raisins
description: Boneless rabbit rolled around spinach, raisins, and carrot.
steps: Sauté the spinach and grated carrot with one tablespoon of oil and two garlic cloves for 6 minutes; drain and mix with the raisins. Let cool slightly.
Lay out the boneless rabbit, season with salt and pepper, and add the oregano. Spread over the filling, roll up, and tie with kitchen string.
Brown the roll in the remaining oil and place over sliced onion in a baking dish. Add the wine, water, and remaining garlic.
Bake covered for 55 minutes at 180 °C; uncover and continue for 15 to 25 minutes, until the center of the filling reaches 74 °C.
Rest for 10 minutes, remove all the string, and cut into slices with a very sharp knife.
tips: Ask for the rabbit already boned; keeping it opened out in one piece makes it easier to form an even roll.

title: Chicken rolls with plantain and spinach
description: Chicken breasts rolled around ripe plantain and spinach and finished in the oven.
steps: Cut the plantain into strips and brown in one tablespoon of oil for 4 minutes. Sauté the spinach with one garlic clove and drain.
Season the cutlets with salt and pepper, divide the plantain and spinach among them, roll up, and secure with string or toothpicks, keeping track of how many toothpicks you use.
Brown the rolls in the remaining oil and place in a baking dish. Add the orange juice, water, remaining garlic, and oregano.
Bake at 190 °C for 25 to 30 minutes, until the center of the filling reaches 74 °C; baste once with the juices.
Rest for 5 minutes, remove every toothpick or all the string, and serve cut into slices.
tips: Open out the cutlets to an even thickness so the rolls have no overly thick sections.

title: Tamarind chicken thighs
description: Chicken thighs baked with a tamarind and orange glaze.
steps: Dilute the tamarind in the water and strain if it contains fibers. Mix with the orange juice, garlic, honey, cumin, oil, and salt.
Reserve one-third of the mixture without letting it touch the meat. Marinate the chicken in the rest for one hour in the refrigerator.
Preheat the oven to 190 °C. Place the thighs with their marinade in a baking dish, skin side up, and bake for 30 minutes.
Brush with some of the reserved mixture and continue for 15 to 20 minutes, until browned and the meat reaches 74 °C near the bone without touching it.
Boil the remaining reserved mixture for 2 minutes and serve it separately as a sauce.
tips: Set aside the sauce before it touches raw chicken so you have a clean portion for serving.

title: Guava-glazed chicken wings
description: Baked wings finished with a guava and lemon glaze.
steps: Pat the wings dry and toss with the oil, crushed garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper. Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Spread on a lined baking sheet without crowding and bake for 35 minutes, turning halfway through.
Meanwhile, dissolve the guava paste in the water with the lemon juice over low heat for 6 minutes, stirring until smooth.
Brush the wings and bake for another 10 to 15 minutes, until the meaty part reaches 74 °C, watching that the glaze does not burn.
Serve hot with any leftover glaze that has not touched the brush used on the chicken.
tips: Set aside the glaze for serving before you start brushing the wings.

title: Shredded chicken with red beans
description: Cooked, shredded chicken combined with red beans and sautéed aromatics.
steps: Cook the chicken in the water with one onion, the bay leaf, and salt for 20 to 25 minutes, until it reaches 74 °C. Reserve 300 ml of the broth.
Shred the chicken once cool enough to handle; remove the bay leaf and discard tough fibers.
Sauté the chopped remaining onion, bell pepper, and garlic in oil for 7 minutes; add the cumin and tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the drained beans, chicken, and reserved broth. Cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes.
Adjust the salt and keep the mixture moist; if using previously refrigerated chicken, reheat it to 74 °C.
tips: This recipe uses cooked beans; do not add dried beans directly.

title: Chicken with coconut and sweet potato
description: Chicken thighs in a mild coconut sauce with white sweet potato.
steps: Season the chicken with salt and cumin and brown in oil for 8 minutes. Remove.
Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic for 6 minutes; add the water and return the chicken. Cover and cook for 20 minutes.
Peel the sweet potato and cut into 3 cm cubes; add with the coconut milk.
Simmer gently for 25 minutes, until the sweet potato is tender and the chicken reaches 74 °C.
Add the lemon juice off the heat and adjust the salt; serve with a creamy sauce without mashing the sweet potato.
tips: Keep the heat at a gentle simmer so the coconut milk does not splatter or reduce too much.

title: Chicken breasts with mushrooms and cilantro
description: Thin chicken breasts in a mushroom, milk, and cilantro sauce.
steps: Season the cutlets with salt and pepper and brown in oil for 2 minutes per side; remove, remembering that they are not yet fully cooked.
Sauté the onion, garlic, and sliced mushrooms for 8 minutes, until the liquid they release evaporates.
Add the milk and the cornstarch dissolved in water; simmer for one minute to thicken.
Return the chicken, cover, and cook for 6 to 10 minutes, until the centers reach 74 °C.
Add the chopped cilantro off the heat, adjust the salt, and serve covered with sauce.
tips: If the sauce thickens before the chicken is cooked, add a little hot water.

title: Chicken and malanga pie
description: A shredded chicken filling topped with malanga mash and baked until golden.
steps: Cook the chicken in 1000 ml of salted water for about 20 minutes, until it reaches 74 °C, then shred. At the same time, peel the malanga and cook it in the remaining water in another pot for about 25 minutes.
Drain and mash the malanga with the hot milk, butter, and salt until spreadable.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in oil for 7 minutes; add the tomatoes and chicken and cook for 10 minutes, keeping the filling moist.
Spread the chicken in a baking dish, cover with the mash and cheese, and bake for 20 to 25 minutes at 190 °C, until the center reaches 74 °C.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting; the mash will firm up as it cools slightly.
tips: If the malanga has absorbed little liquid, add the milk gradually to avoid a watery mash.

title: Bell peppers stuffed with chicken and corn
description: Baked bell peppers with finely diced chicken, corn, and cheese.
steps: Halve the peppers, remove the seeds, and bake for 12 minutes at 190 °C with the water in the dish.
Cut the chicken into one-centimeter cubes. Sauté the onion and garlic in oil, then add the chicken and oregano and cook for 6 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, corn, and salt; cook for 10 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74 °C and the filling is thick.
Fill the pepper halves, top with cheese, and bake for another 20 minutes, until the peppers soften and the centers reheat to 74 °C.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve with a spatula to keep each half intact.
tips: Dice the chicken finely so it spreads evenly throughout the pepper filling.

title: Eggplants stuffed with chicken and cheese
description: Eggplant boats with chicken, tomato, and a layer of cheese.
steps: Halve the eggplants lengthwise, score the flesh, and brush with one tablespoon of oil. Roast for 30 minutes at 190 °C.
Scoop out some of the flesh without breaking the skin and chop it. Sauté the onion and garlic in the remaining oil.
Add the ground chicken, salt, and pepper and cook for 8 minutes. Stir in the tomatoes and eggplant flesh and cook for another 10 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74 °C.
Add the chopped basil, fill the shells, and cover with cheese. Bake for 15 minutes, until golden and heated through.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve one half per person with a wide spatula.
tips: Do not make the eggplant shells too thin, or they may break when served.

title: Chicken and mango skewers
description: Cumin chicken with firm mango wedges and griddled onion.
steps: Cut the chicken into 2.5 cm cubes and mix with the garlic, lemon juice, two tablespoons of oil, cumin, and salt; refrigerate for 45 minutes.
Peel and cut the mango into firm chunks and cut the onion and bell pepper into squares. Soak wooden skewers if using them.
Thread the chicken with onion and bell pepper; place the mango on separate skewers and brush with the remaining oil.
Cook the chicken on a griddle for 15 to 20 minutes, turning, until it reaches 74 °C. Grill the mango for 3 minutes per side, removing it earlier if it softens.
Serve both kinds of skewer together and discard the marinade that touched raw chicken.
tips: Cook the mango separately because it softens before the chicken is done.

title: Chicken in carrot and vinegar marinade
description: Fully cooked chicken chilled with onion, carrot, and vinegar.
steps: Divide the breasts into thick pieces and season with salt. Brown in two tablespoons of oil for 3 minutes per side.
Add 150 ml of water, cover, and cook for 15 to 20 minutes, until the centers reach 74 °C; slice and place in a shallow container.
Sauté the sliced onion, carrot, and garlic in the remaining oil for 8 minutes. Add the vinegar, remaining water, bay leaf, and pepper and boil for 7 minutes.
Pour over the chicken, let the strongest steam escape, and refrigerate promptly. Do not leave it at room temperature for several hours.
Refrigerate for two hours, remove the bay leaf, and serve cold with the vegetables.
tips: Vinegar adds flavor, but it does not make this dish safe to store outside the refrigerator.

title: Oven-baked chicken with a cassava crumb crust
description: Boneless chicken thighs coated with cassava flatbread crumbs, garlic, and parsley.
steps: Pat the thighs dry and season with the garlic, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Crush the cassava flatbread into crumbs and mix with the parsley.
Prepare separate plates of cornstarch and beaten egg. Coat each piece with cornstarch, egg, and cassava crumbs, pressing firmly.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C and grease a baking sheet with one tablespoon of oil. Arrange the chicken in a single layer.
Drizzle with the remaining oil and bake for 25 to 35 minutes, turning carefully halfway through, until the centers reach 74 °C.
Serve immediately on a dry platter to keep the crust crisp.
tips: Check the cassava flatbread label and do not mix crumbs that touched raw chicken with other foods.

title: Chicken meatballs with okra
description: Chicken meatballs in tomato sauce with whole sautéed okra.
steps: Mix the chicken, egg, breadcrumbs, two grated garlic cloves, cumin, and salt; shape into 16 meatballs and refrigerate while preparing the sauce.
Sauté the onion and remaining garlic in two tablespoons of oil; add the tomatoes and water and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the meatballs, cover, and simmer gently for 15 minutes. Wash and dry the okra and trim its tough ends.
Sauté the okra in the remaining oil for 5 minutes; add it with the lemon juice and cook for another 12 to 15 minutes, until the meatballs reach 74 °C.
Adjust the salt and serve, gently shaking the pot rather than breaking up the pieces.
tips: Add the okra once the meatballs have begun to firm up.

title: Chicken thighs with prunes and wine
description: Chicken thighs simmered with prunes in a white wine sauce.
steps: Pat the chicken dry and season with salt and pepper. Brown in oil for 4 minutes per side and set aside.
Sauté the chopped onions and garlic for 7 minutes, add the wine, and boil for 3 minutes, scraping the bottom of the pot.
Return the chicken, add the water, bay leaf, and oregano, and cover and cook for 25 minutes.
Add the prunes and cook for another 10 to 15 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74 °C and the sauce is slightly thickened.
Remove the bay leaf, skim off the surface fat, adjust the salt, and serve several prunes with each portion.
tips: Add the prunes toward the end so some remain whole.

title: Chicken with chickpeas and bell peppers
description: Chicken cooked in a pot with cooked chickpeas and bell pepper strips.
steps: Season the chicken with salt and brown in oil in batches for 10 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Sauté the chopped onion, peppers, and garlic for 7 minutes; add the cumin and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Return the chicken with the water and bay leaf, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes.
Stir in the drained chickpeas and cook for another 15 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74 °C.
Remove the bay leaf and adjust the salt; mash a tablespoon of chickpeas into the sauce if you want to thicken it.
tips: The chickpea quantity refers to the cooked, drained weight.

title: Chicken rolls stuffed with corn and cheese
description: Chicken breasts rolled around tender corn, cheese, and cilantro.
steps: Drain the corn and mix with the grated cheese and chopped cilantro. Season the cutlets with garlic, salt, and pepper.
Divide the filling among the cutlets, leaving a clear border; roll up and secure with string or toothpicks, keeping track of how many toothpicks you use.
Brown in oil for 2 minutes on each side and place in a baking dish with the orange juice and water. Preheat the oven to 190 °C.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the center of the filling reaches 74 °C; cover if any escaped cheese begins to burn.
Rest for 5 minutes and remove all the string or toothpicks before serving with the juices.
tips: Drain the corn well so the filling does not leak.

title: Crispy sesame chicken strips
description: Chicken breast strips coated in breadcrumbs and sesame seeds and baked in the oven.
steps: Cut the chicken into evenly thick strips and season with garlic, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Mix the breadcrumbs and sesame seeds. Place the flour and beaten eggs in two other containers.
Coat the chicken with flour, egg, and the breadcrumb mixture; press firmly and arrange on an oiled baking sheet without crowding.
Drizzle with the remaining oil and bake for 18 to 25 minutes, turning halfway through, until the thick strips reach 74 °C.
Serve immediately and discard any leftover coating ingredients that touched raw chicken.
tips: If the sesame browns too quickly, move the tray to a lower oven rack.

title: Coffee chicken with sweet potato
description: Chicken simmered in mild coffee with sweet potato and onion.
steps: Season the chicken with salt and cumin and brown in oil for 8 minutes. Set aside.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic for 7 minutes, add the coffee, water, and orange juice, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Return the chicken, cover, and cook for 20 minutes. Peel the sweet potato and cut into 3 cm cubes.
Add the sweet potato and cook for another 25 minutes, until it is tender and the chicken reaches 74 °C.
Uncover and reduce for a few minutes if necessary; check the salt without adding more coffee.
tips: The sweet potato balances the coffee; use a mild brew, not a bitter concentrate.

title: Chicken stir-fry with cabbage and ginger
description: Chicken strips with cabbage, carrot, and a light orange and soy sauce.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: only if needed after tasting the cooked dish

steps: Marinate the chicken strips with one tablespoon of soy sauce for 15 minutes in the refrigerator. Slice the cabbage, onion, and carrot into strips.
Stir-fry the chicken in two tablespoons of oil in batches for 6 minutes and set aside.
Add the remaining oil, chopped onion, garlic, and ginger and stir-fry for 2 minutes; add the carrot and cabbage and cook for 5 minutes.
Return the chicken and pour in the orange juice, remaining soy sauce, and cornstarch dissolved in water. Cook for 3 minutes to thicken.
Check that the chicken reaches 74 °C and serve with the vegetables still slightly crisp. Taste before adding salt.
tips: Slice the vegetables thinly so they cook during the brief stir-fry.

title: Roasted chicken with eggplant and olives
description: Chicken roasted over eggplant, tomato, and olives in a single baking dish.
steps: Dice the eggplant and cut the tomato and onion into wedges. Mix with two tablespoons of oil, chopped garlic, oregano, and a pinch of salt.
Spread in a baking dish with the water and bake for 20 minutes at 190 °C.
Pat the chicken dry, season with salt and pepper, and rub with the remaining oil. Arrange it over the vegetables, skin side up.
Bake for another 35 to 45 minutes, adding the olives during the last 10 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74 °C.
Check that the eggplant is soft and serve with the pan juices and vegetables.
tips: A wide baking dish lets the vegetables roast without becoming submerged in liquid.

title: Celebration roast turkey with citrus
description: A whole unstuffed turkey roasted with orange, lemon, and garlic.
steps: Pat the turkey dry without washing it. Mix the juices, garlic, oil, oregano, cumin, salt, and pepper and marinate, covered, for 12 hours in the refrigerator.
Preheat the oven to 175 °C. Place the onion in a roasting pan with the water and add the unstuffed turkey, breast side up.
Roast for approximately 3 to 3 and a half hours, loosely covering the breast if it browns too much and replenishing the water in the pan if it dries out.
Check for 74 °C in the innermost parts of the thigh and wing and the thickest part of the breast, without touching bone. The cooking time is only a guide.
Rest for 20 minutes before carving; boil the juices for 5 minutes, skim off the fat, and serve separately.
tips: Thawing time is not included: start with a turkey that has been fully thawed in the refrigerator.

title: Turkey thighs with malanga
description: Turkey thighs simmered with malanga and a sautéed tomato base.
steps: Season the turkey with salt and cumin and brown in oil in batches for 10 minutes.
Add the chopped onions, bell pepper, and garlic and sauté for 7 minutes. Stir in the tomatoes, water, and bay leaf.
Cover and simmer gently for 75 minutes, until the turkey starts to become tender.
Peel the malanga and cut into 3 cm cubes, add to the pot, and simmer for another 30 minutes, until soft and the turkey reaches 74 °C.
Remove the bay leaf, watch for bone splinters when serving, and adjust the salt.
tips: Ask the butcher to cut up the thighs so you do not have to cut through hard bones at home.

title: Turkey breast stuffed with guava and cheese
description: A turkey roll with a thin layer of guava and cheese in the center.
steps: Lay out the breast and season with garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper. Cut the guava paste and cheese into thin strips.
Spread the filling over the meat, leaving the edges clear, roll up, and tie with kitchen string. Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Brown the roll in oil for 5 minutes and place over onion in a baking dish; add the orange juice and water.
Bake covered for 45 minutes, then uncovered for 20 to 30 minutes, until the center of the filling reaches 74 °C.
Rest for 10 minutes, remove the string, and cut into slices; serve with the slightly reduced juices.
tips: A moderate layer of guava keeps the filling from becoming too sweet.

title: Turkey meatballs with coconut and cilantro
description: Turkey meatballs cooked in coconut milk with bell pepper and fresh cilantro.
steps: Mix the turkey, egg, breadcrumbs, one grated garlic clove, half the cilantro, and salt. Shape into 16 meatballs.
Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper, and remaining garlic in oil for 7 minutes.
Add the coconut milk and water and bring to a gentle simmer. Add the meatballs in a single layer.
Cover and cook for 22 to 25 minutes, turning carefully, until the centers reach 74 °C.
Add the lemon juice and remaining cilantro, check the salt, and serve with plenty of sauce.
tips: Lean turkey needs enough sauce to keep the dish from tasting dry.

title: Cornmeal-coated turkey cutlets
description: Turkey cutlets coated in fine cornmeal and baked in the oven.
steps: Marinate thin turkey cutlets with the garlic, lemon juice, oregano, salt, and pepper; refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Set out separate containers of cornstarch, beaten egg, and fine cornmeal. Do not use coarse meal.
Drain the turkey and coat with all three coatings in order. Place on an oiled baking sheet and drizzle with the remaining oil.
Bake at 200 °C for 20 to 30 minutes, turning halfway through, until the centers reach 74 °C.
Serve hot and uncovered to keep the coating firm.
tips: Keep the cutlets close to one centimeter thick so they cook evenly.

title: Cabbage rolls stuffed with turkey
description: Cabbage leaves filled with ground turkey and cooked rice, simmered in tomato sauce.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 2000 ml for blanching the cabbage and 350 ml for the sauce

steps: Separate 12 large cabbage leaves and blanch for 3 minutes in 2000 ml of boiling water; drain and trim down the thick ribs.
Mix the turkey, safely stored cold cooked rice, egg, two garlic cloves, cumin, and salt. Divide among the leaves and roll up, folding in the sides.
Sauté the onion and remaining garlic in oil; add the tomatoes and the remaining 350 ml of water and cook for 8 minutes.
Arrange the rolls seam side down, cover, and simmer gently for 40 to 45 minutes, until the center of the filling reaches 74 °C.
Rest off the heat for 3 minutes and serve with the sauce, lifting each roll with a spatula.
tips: If the rice was prepared in advance, it should have been refrigerated promptly and kept cold until used.

title: Turkey with white beans and carrot
description: Diced turkey simmered with cooked white beans and carrot.
steps: Cut the turkey into 3 cm cubes, season with salt, and brown in oil for 10 minutes.
Add the chopped onion and garlic; sauté for 6 minutes, then add the tomatoes, water, bay leaf, and oregano.
Cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes. Slice the carrot into rounds and drain the beans.
Add the carrot and beans and cook for another 25 minutes, until tender and the turkey reaches 74 °C.
Remove the bay leaf, adjust the salt, and mash a few beans to thicken the sauce if desired.
tips: Turkey thigh holds up to this cooking method better than lean breast meat.

title: Turkey stir-fry with pineapple and green beans
description: Turkey strips with browned pineapple and green beans in orange sauce.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: only if needed after tasting the cooked dish

steps: Trim the green beans and cook for 4 minutes in boiling water; drain. Cut the turkey into strips and the pineapple into cubes.
Brown the pineapple in one tablespoon of oil for 3 minutes and set aside. Stir-fry the turkey in another tablespoon of oil in batches for 6 minutes.
Add the remaining oil, chopped onion, and garlic and cook for 3 minutes; stir in the green beans and pineapple.
Return the turkey and add the orange juice mixed with the soy sauce and cornstarch; cook for 3 to 5 minutes, until the meat reaches 74 °C.
Taste before adding salt and serve as soon as the sauce coats the strips without becoming too thick.
tips: Blanch the green beans first because they need more cooking time than the pineapple.

title: Turkey meatloaf with carrot and olives
description: A ground turkey loaf with grated carrot and chopped olives.
steps: Moisten the breadcrumbs with the milk and mix with the turkey, egg, carrot, chopped olives, two garlic cloves, and a little salt. Shape into a loaf.
Sauté the onion and remaining garlic in oil; stir in the tomatoes, water, and oregano and cook for 8 minutes.
Pour the sauce into a baking dish, add the loaf, and preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes, until the center reaches 74 °C, covering the top if it browns too much.
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing and serve with the sauce to keep the turkey juicy.
tips: Taste the tomato sauce separately for salt; the olives already season the loaf.

title: Turkey medallions with mustard and orange
description: Turkey breast medallions in a mild orange and mustard sauce.
steps: Cut the turkey crosswise into 2 cm medallions, season with salt and pepper, and brown in oil for 2 minutes per side.
Remove and sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the same skillet for 5 minutes.
Add the orange juice, mustard, and 80 ml of water, stir, and return the medallions.
Cook over low heat for 8 to 12 minutes, until the turkey reaches 74 °C; add the cornstarch dissolved in the remaining water and boil for one minute.
Check the salt and serve immediately with the sauce spooned over the meat.
tips: Do not continue cooking once the turkey is done, or the breast meat may dry out.

title: Tamarind turkey with squash
description: Turkey thighs roasted with winter squash and a tamarind marinade.
steps: Dissolve the tamarind in 200 ml of water, strain, and mix with the garlic, sugar, cumin, oil, and salt. Marinate the turkey for two hours in the refrigerator.
Place the onion wedges in a baking dish, add the remaining water, and arrange the turkey with its marinade. Cover.
Bake at 180 °C for 70 minutes. Cut the squash into large pieces and add, basting with the juices.
Continue cooking for 35 to 45 minutes, uncovering toward the end, until the squash is tender and the turkey reaches 74 °C.
Serve portions of meat with the squash and tamarind sauce; skim off any excess surface fat.
tips: Add the squash halfway through roasting so it does not fall apart.

title: Turkey patties with mango and cilantro
description: Turkey patties served without buns, with a fresh mango salsa.
steps: Mix the turkey with the egg, breadcrumbs, grated garlic, cumin, half the cilantro, and salt. Shape into four even patties.
Peel and dice the mango; mix with the chopped onion, lemon juice, and remaining cilantro and keep refrigerated.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the patties for about 6 minutes per side, without pressing down on them.
Check that the centers reach 74 °C and continue cooking over lower heat if the outside browns before the centers are done.
Serve on plates, adding the mango salsa just before eating.
tips: The egg and breadcrumbs help hold the lean turkey mixture together.

title: Turkey with okra and corn
description: Diced turkey with whole okra and corn kernels in a sautéed vegetable sauce.
steps: Cut the turkey into cubes, season with salt and cumin, and brown in two tablespoons of oil for 8 minutes.
Add the chopped onion and garlic, sauté, and add the tomatoes and water. Cover and cook for 45 minutes.
Wash and dry the okra, trim the ends, and sauté in the remaining oil for 5 minutes.
