Stir in the okra, corn, and lemon juice and simmer for another 20 minutes, until the turkey reaches 74 °C and the vegetables are tender.
Adjust the salt and serve without stirring vigorously, to keep the okra whole.
tips: If using canned corn, drain and rinse it before adding.

title: Turkey breast in vinegar marinade with peppers
description: Roast turkey chilled in a vinegar marinade with bell peppers and onion.
steps: Season the breast with salt, rub with one tablespoon of oil, and roast in a baking dish with 150 ml of water at 180 °C for 60 to 80 minutes, until it reaches 74 °C.
Rest for 10 minutes and cut into slices; arrange in a clean, shallow container.
While the breast roasts, sauté the sliced onion, peppers, and garlic in the remaining oil for 8 minutes. Add the vinegar, remaining water, bay leaf, and pepper and boil for 8 minutes.
Cover the turkey with the vinegar marinade; let the heavy steam escape and refrigerate promptly.
Chill for at least two hours, remove the bay leaf, and serve with the vegetables; always keep refrigerated.
tips: The vinegar marinade does not replace refrigeration or make the turkey a shelf-stable preserve.

title: Whole duck with orange and garlic marinade
description: Unstuffed roast duck with sour orange, garlic, and oregano.
steps: Pat the duck dry and prick only the fatty skin, without piercing the meat. Marinate with the juice, garlic, oregano, cumin, salt, and pepper for four hours in the refrigerator.
Place the onion and water in a roasting pan and set the unstuffed duck on a rack, breast side up. Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Roast for 2 and a half to 3 hours; carefully remove any accumulated fat and replenish the water if the pan dries out.
Check that the thigh, wing, and breast reach 74 °C without touching bone. Cover any overly browned parts if the inside is not yet done.
Rest for 10 minutes, carve, and serve with the onion juices, skimmed and brought to a boil.
tips: The rack keeps the duck above the fat it releases during roasting.

title: Duck legs with tamarind
description: Duck legs braised with tamarind, tomato, and onion.
steps: Pat the legs dry and season with salt. Place skin side down in a cold pot and heat over medium heat for 12 minutes to render the fat; turn and cook for 3 minutes.
Remove the duck, leaving only two tablespoons of its fat. Sauté the chopped onion and garlic for 7 minutes.
Dissolve the tamarind in the water and strain; add to the pot with the tomatoes, sugar, and cumin and return the legs.
Cover and cook at a very gentle simmer for 95 to 110 minutes, until tender and above 74 °C.
Skim off the surface fat and reduce the sauce uncovered for 5 minutes; check the salt and serve skin side up.
tips: Do not add oil before rendering the duck fat.

title: Duck breast with guava sauce
description: Fully cooked duck breasts with a guava and vinegar sauce.
steps: Score the skin in a diamond pattern without cutting into the meat and season with salt and pepper. Place skin side down in a cold skillet and heat over medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes.
Remove excess fat, turn, and brown for 3 minutes. Transfer to a 200 °C oven for 10 to 18 minutes, until the centers reach 74 °C.
While the duck is in the oven, sauté the chopped onion and garlic in one tablespoon of its fat for 6 minutes. Add the guava, vinegar, water, and cumin.
Simmer gently for 8 minutes and blend the sauce; adjust the salt. Rest the duck for 5 minutes after cooking.
Slice the breast thinly and serve the sauce underneath or on the side to preserve some of the skin's crispness.
tips: This recipe is designed for fully cooked duck, rather than a pink, partially cooked center.

title: Duck with olives and tomato
description: Duck pieces simmered with tomato, bell pepper, and green olives.
steps: Brown the duck pieces in their own fat, starting skin side down, for 15 minutes; remove.
Leave two tablespoons of fat and sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic for 8 minutes.
Add the wine and cook for 3 minutes; stir in the tomatoes, water, bay leaf, oregano, and duck.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 100 minutes; add the olives and cook for another 15 minutes, until the duck is tender and reaches 74 °C.
Remove the bay leaf and skim off the surface fat; taste before adding salt because the olives already add salt.
tips: If cooking breasts alongside legs, check and remove pieces that become tender earlier.

title: Duck with coconut and squash
description: Duck legs in a coconut sauce with winter squash and lemon.
steps: Brown the duck skin side down in a pot over medium heat for 12 minutes, then turn and cook for 3 minutes; remove.
Leave one tablespoon of fat and sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic. Add the cumin and water and return the duck.
Cover and simmer gently for 80 minutes. Cut the squash into large cubes.
Add the squash and coconut milk and cook for another 30 to 35 minutes, until the duck is tender and reaches 74 °C.
Skim off the surface fat, add the lemon juice off the heat, and adjust the salt.
tips: Skim off excess fat before adding the coconut milk if a lot has accumulated.

title: Shredded duck with black beans
description: Cooked, shredded duck legs served over cumin-seasoned black beans.
steps: Place the duck, one onion, three garlic cloves, sour orange juice, bay leaf, salt, and 800 ml of water in a pot. Simmer gently for about 2 hours, until tender and at least 74 °C.
Remove the skin and bones and shred the meat; reserve 150 ml of skimmed broth.
Sauté the remaining onion and garlic in oil; add the beans, cumin, and remaining water and cook for 15 minutes.
Heat the shredded duck in a skillet with the reserved broth for 8 minutes, until the liquid reduces and the meat is heated through.
Serve the beans with the duck on top, adjusting the salt in each separately.
tips: Skim the broth thoroughly before using it with the shredded meat.

title: Duck legs with beer and sweet potato
description: Duck legs braised in light-colored beer, with sweet potato added toward the end.
steps: Season the duck with salt and pepper and brown the skin in a pot over medium heat for 12 minutes; turn and cook for 3 minutes.
Remove and leave only two tablespoons of fat. Sauté the onion and garlic for 7 minutes, then add the beer, water, bay leaf, and oregano.
Return the duck, cover, and simmer gently for 85 minutes. Peel the sweet potato and cut into 3 cm cubes.
Add the sweet potato and cook for another 25 to 30 minutes, until tender and the duck reaches 74 °C.
Remove the bay leaf, skim off the surface fat, adjust the salt, and serve with the reduced juices.
tips: Do not add the sweet potato at the start, or it will fall apart during braising.

title: Duck breast with orange and ginger
description: Duck breast with a fresh orange and ginger sauce.
steps: Lightly score the skin, season with salt and pepper, and start cooking skin side down in a cold skillet. Raise the heat to medium and brown for 10 to 12 minutes.
Remove excess fat, turn and cook for 3 minutes, then finish in a 200 °C oven for 10 to 18 minutes, until the duck reaches 74 °C.
Sauté the chopped onion, garlic, and ginger in one tablespoon of fat for 4 minutes. Add the orange and lemon juices and boil for 5 minutes.
Dissolve the cornstarch in the water, add, and cook for one minute. Rest the duck for 5 minutes and adjust the sauce's salt.
Slice thinly and serve with the sauce, without leaving the breast to rest in it.
tips: Finely chop fresh ginger to avoid long fibers in the sauce.

title: Duck and ripe plantain pie
description: Shredded duck with sautéed aromatics, topped with roasted ripe plantain slices.
steps: Simmer the duck with the water, one onion, bay leaf, and salt for about 2 hours, until tender and at least 74 °C. Shred and remove the skin and bones.
Peel the plantains and cut into lengthwise slices; brush with two tablespoons of oil and roast for 15 minutes at 200 °C.
Sauté the remaining onion and garlic in the remaining oil; add the tomatoes, cumin, and duck and cook for 12 minutes, adding skimmed broth if it becomes dry.
Spread the duck in a baking dish, cover with the plantain and cheese, and bake for 20 minutes at 190 °C, until the center reaches 74 °C.
Rest for 10 minutes and cut portions through all the layers with a firm spatula.
tips: The meat should still have some sauce before you cover it with plantain.

title: Duck stir-fry with pineapple and peppers
description: Duck strips with pineapple and bell peppers in a citrus sauce.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: only if needed after tasting the cooked dish

steps: Cut the duck into strips and the pineapple into cubes. Mix the orange juice, soy sauce, water, and cornstarch in a bowl.
Brown the pineapple in one tablespoon of oil for 3 minutes and remove. Stir-fry the duck in another tablespoon of oil in batches for 6 minutes.
Sauté the onion, peppers, and garlic in the remaining oil for 5 minutes. Return the duck and pineapple.
Pour in the sauce and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, until thickened and the duck strips reach 74 °C.
Serve immediately, checking the salt at the end because the soy sauce seasons the dish.
tips: This recipe uses skinless breast; the skin would need a separate step to render its fat.

title: Duck legs with lentils and carrot
description: Braised duck with cooked lentils and tender carrots.
steps: Season the duck with salt and brown, starting skin side down, for 15 minutes. Remove and leave two tablespoons of fat.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic, add the tomatoes, water, bay leaf, and oregano, and return the duck.
Cover and simmer gently for 90 minutes. Cut the carrot into thick rounds.
Add the carrot and drained lentils and cook for another 25 to 30 minutes, until tender and the duck reaches at least 74 °C.
Remove the bay leaf, skim off the surface fat, and adjust the salt. Serve the duck over the lentils.
tips: The lentils in this recipe are already cooked; do not replace them with dried lentils unless you cook them separately first.

title: Duck meatballs with prunes
description: Ground duck meatballs cooked in a prune and tomato sauce.
steps: Mix the ground duck with the egg, breadcrumbs, one grated garlic clove, cumin, and salt. Shape into 16 equal meatballs.
Sauté the onion and remaining garlic in oil for 6 minutes. Add the tomatoes, water, halved prunes, and vinegar and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the meatballs to the sauce, cover, and simmer gently for 22 to 25 minutes, turning carefully.
Check that the centers of the largest meatballs reach 74 °C and reduce uncovered if the sauce is thin.
Adjust the salt and serve with the softened prunes divided among the portions.
tips: Use ground duck without large pieces of skin to avoid an overly fatty mixture.

title: Roast goose with citrus-garlic marinade and apples
description: A whole unstuffed goose roasted with a citrus-garlic marinade and apples cooked separately.
steps: Pat the goose dry and lightly prick the fatty skin without piercing the meat. Rub with the juice, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper and refrigerate for six hours.
Place the onion and water in a roasting pan and set the unstuffed goose on a rack. Roast at 170 °C for approximately 2 and a half to 3 and a quarter hours.
Carefully remove accumulated fat during roasting and replenish the water if the pan dries out. Check that the thigh, wing, and breast reach 74 °C.
Core the apples and cut into wedges, brush with oil, and roast on another tray during the last 25 minutes, until tender.
Rest the goose for 20 minutes, carve, and serve with the apples and skimmed juices.
tips: Both names in the Spanish version refer to the same type of goose; this recipe does not use two different species.

title: Goose legs in Cuban-style tomato sauce
description: Goose legs slowly simmered with tomato, bell peppers, and wine.
steps: Season the legs with salt and brown skin side down in a pot over medium heat for 15 minutes; turn and cook for 4 minutes, then remove.
Leave two tablespoons of fat, sauté the chopped onion, peppers, and garlic for 8 minutes, and add the wine.
Stir in the tomatoes, water, bay leaf, and cumin, return the legs, and cover.
Simmer very gently for 2 to 2 and a half hours, until the meat is tender and exceeds 74 °C; check the liquid every 40 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf, skim off the surface fat, adjust the salt, and serve with the reduced sauce.
tips: Goose may need longer than chicken; check tenderness as well as temperature.

title: Goose breast with orange and honey
description: Fully cooked goose breast with an orange and honey sauce.
steps: Score the skin with shallow diamond cuts and season with salt and pepper. Start skin side down in a cold skillet and cook over medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes to render the fat.
Turn and cook for 3 minutes, then finish in a 190 °C oven for 15 to 25 minutes, until the center reaches 74 °C; adjust for thickness.
Sauté the onion and garlic in one tablespoon of the fat, add the orange juice, honey, and lemon juice, and cook for 7 minutes.
Dissolve the cornstarch in the water, add, and boil for one minute. Rest the breast for 10 minutes before slicing.
Serve in thin slices with the sauce, removing excess fat before plating.
tips: Use temperature to judge doneness; this recipe does not call for serving partially cooked goose.

title: Shredded goose with sweet potato and onion
description: Tender shredded goose with browned onion and roasted sweet potato cubes.
steps: Simmer the goose with the water, one onion, three garlic cloves, bay leaf, sour orange juice, and salt for 2 to 2 and a half hours, until tender and at least 74 °C.
Remove the skin and bones, shred, and reserve 150 ml of skimmed broth. Peel the sweet potato and cut into 3 cm cubes.
Toss the sweet potato with two tablespoons of oil and half the cumin and roast for 30 minutes at 200 °C, turning once.
Sauté the remaining onions and garlic in the remaining oil for 10 minutes; add the goose, broth, and remaining cumin and cook for 8 minutes to heat through.
Serve the goose with the roasted sweet potato and adjust the salt; if the meat was previously refrigerated, reheat to 74 °C.
tips: Skim the goose broth before adding it to the skillet.

title: Snapper in parchment with malanga
description: Snapper fillets baked in paper parcels with malanga and lemon.
steps: Peel the malanga, cut into one-centimeter slices, and boil in the water for 20 to 25 minutes, until tender; drain.
Check the snapper for bones and season with salt and pepper. Cut four large sheets of parchment paper and divide the malanga and very thinly sliced onion among them.
Place the fish on top, distribute the chopped garlic, lemon juice, oil, and parsley, and fold the edges of the paper to seal the parcels.
Bake at 190 °C for 15 to 20 minutes, carefully open one parcel, and check that the fish reaches 63 °C.
Serve the parcels on plates and open them with the steam directed away from your face.
tips: The malanga must be cooked before sealing the parcels; it would not soften during the fish's short cooking time.

title: Snapper with coconut and squash
description: Snapper in a coconut sauce with tender winter squash and sweet bell pepper.
steps: Cut the squash into 2 cm cubes and chop the onion, bell pepper, and garlic. Check the fish for bones and season with salt.
Sauté the onion and bell pepper in oil for 6 minutes; add the garlic, cumin, squash, and water, then cover and cook for 12 minutes.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer gently for 5 minutes, until the squash is almost tender.
Arrange the snapper in a single layer, cover, and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until the centers reach 63 °C.
Add the lemon juice off the heat, adjust the salt, and serve without breaking up the squash.
tips: Avoid a vigorous boil once the fish is in the sauce.

title: Griddled snapper with mango and cilantro
description: Browned snapper served with a fresh mango, onion, and cilantro salsa.
steps: Peel the mango and cut into small cubes. Mix with the onion, cilantro, half the lemon juice, and one tablespoon of oil; keep refrigerated.
Check the snapper for bones, pat dry, and season with garlic, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Heat the remaining oil on a griddle and add the fish, leaving it undisturbed for 3 to 4 minutes.
Turn with a wide spatula and cook for another 3 to 5 minutes, until it reaches 63 °C; add the remaining lemon juice off the heat.
Serve with the fresh salsa alongside, avoiding covering the fish's surface until ready to eat.
tips: Firm mango gives the salsa distinct cubes rather than turning into a purée.

title: Snapper with a cassava crumb crust
description: Oven-baked snapper fillets with a cassava flatbread, garlic, and parsley topping.
steps: Crush the cassava flatbread into crumbs and mix with the chopped garlic and parsley and three tablespoons of oil.
Pat the fish dry, season with salt and pepper, and place in a baking dish brushed with the remaining oil. Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Mix the mustard and lemon juice, brush over the fish, and press the cassava crumb mixture onto the top.
Bake for 15 to 22 minutes, depending on thickness, until the centers reach 63 °C and the crust is golden.
Serve with a wide spatula to keep the topping intact and do not cover the dish after cooking.
tips: If the crust browns early, cover loosely without touching it and finish cooking.

title: Snapper rolls with spinach and cheese
description: Thin snapper fillets rolled around spinach and mild cheese.
steps: Sauté the spinach with one tablespoon of oil and one garlic clove; drain and cool slightly. Crumble the cheese and mix with the spinach.
Season the snapper with salt and pepper, divide the filling among the fillets, and roll up; secure with toothpicks, keeping track of how many you use.
Place very thinly sliced onion in an oiled baking dish, arrange the rolls, and add the orange juice, water, and remaining garlic.
Bake at 190 °C for 20 to 25 minutes, until the center of the filling reaches 74 °C, making sure the dish does not dry out.
Remove every toothpick and serve with the orange and onion juices.
tips: Use thin fillets that bend without breaking; thick fillets are not suitable for rolling.

title: Grouper with chickpeas and sautéed vegetables
description: Grouper cubes added at the end of a chickpea stew.
steps: Cut the grouper into 4 cm cubes and check for bones. Drain the chickpeas and chop the onion, bell pepper, and garlic.
Sauté the vegetables in oil for 8 minutes. Add the cumin and tomatoes and cook for 6 minutes.
Stir in the water, bay leaf, and chickpeas and simmer gently for 10 minutes to form a sauce.
Add the fish, season with salt, and cover and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until it reaches 63 °C, without stirring vigorously.
Remove the bay leaf and serve with a wide spoon to keep the cubes whole.
tips: Add the fish once the chickpeas are already hot and tender.

title: Roasted grouper with sweet potato and orange
description: Grouper roasted over sweet potato wedges with orange and onion.
steps: Peel the sweet potato and cut into one-centimeter wedges. Toss with the onion, two tablespoons of oil, and salt and roast for 30 minutes at 200 °C.
Check and pat dry the grouper; season with garlic, oregano, and salt. Mix the juices and water.
Arrange the fish over the almost-tender sweet potato, add the juice mixture and remaining oil.
Bake for another 15 to 20 minutes, until the grouper reaches 63 °C and the sweet potato is soft.
Serve the fish and sweet potato with the pan liquid, slightly reduced if needed.
tips: Do not add the fish at the beginning: the sweet potato needs longer to cook.

title: Grouper in peanut and sweet pepper sauce
description: Firm fish in a roasted peanut sauce with sweet peppers.
steps: Blend the peanuts with 250 ml of water. Clean and chop the sweet peppers, onion, and garlic and cut the fish into portions.
Sauté the vegetables in oil for 7 minutes; add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the blended peanut mixture and remaining water and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring the bottom.
Add the grouper, season with salt, and cover and cook for 8 to 12 minutes, until it reaches 63 °C; add a little water if the sauce thickens too much.
Remove from the heat, add the lemon juice, and adjust the salt before serving.
tips: The peppers in this recipe are sweet peppers, not hot habaneros.

title: Steamed grouper with ginger and chives
description: Grouper steamed with ginger, soy sauce, and chives.
steps: Cut the ginger into very thin strips and the chives into short lengths. Check the fish for bones and place on a heatproof plate.
Distribute the chopped garlic, ginger, half the chives, and soy sauce over the fish. Bring the water to a boil beneath a steamer.
Put the plate in without letting it touch the water, cover, and steam for 12 to 18 minutes, until the fish reaches 63 °C.
Heat the oil in a small saucepan without letting it smoke, remove from the heat, and mix with the lemon juice and remaining chives.
Carefully remove the plate and spoon the aromatic oil over the fish; taste before adding salt.
tips: Check that the steamer does not run dry and that the plate allows the lid to close.

title: Grouper gratin with corn
description: Grouper fillets topped with creamy corn and cheese.
steps: Season the fish with salt and pepper and add the lemon juice. Sauté the onion and garlic in one tablespoon of oil for 6 minutes.
Dissolve the cornstarch in the cold milk and add to the skillet with the corn; cook, stirring, until thickened and adjust the salt.
Grease a baking dish with the remaining oil, arrange the fish in a single layer, and cover with the corn cream and cheese.
Bake at 190 °C for 20 to 25 minutes, until the center of the dish reaches 74 °C and the topping is golden.
Let settle for 3 minutes and serve with a spatula, dividing the creamy topping among all the portions.
tips: The cream should still be pourable when assembling; it will thicken further in the oven.

title: Corvina with green herb sauce and cassava
description: Griddled corvina with boiled sweet cassava and a cilantro sauce.
steps: Peel the cassava completely, cut into chunks, and boil in the water for 25 to 35 minutes, until tender. Discard the water and remove the central fiber.
Blend the cilantro, three garlic cloves, lemon juice, three tablespoons of oil, and a pinch of salt to make the sauce.
Pat the corvina dry, check for bones, and season with the remaining garlic, salt, and pepper.
Cook on a griddle with the remaining oil for 3 to 5 minutes per side, until the centers reach 63 °C.
Serve the fish and cassava with the sauce added at the end, without cooking the herbs further.
tips: Use commercially sold sweet cassava and do not reuse its cooking water.

title: Corvina in parchment with olives
description: Corvina fillets baked in parcels with tomato and olives.
steps: Thinly slice the tomato and onion and slice the garlic. Check the fish and season with a little salt.
Prepare four large sheets of parchment paper and divide the tomato, onion, and olives among them as a base.
Place the corvina on top, distribute the garlic, oregano, lemon juice, and oil, and tightly seal the edges of each parcel.
Bake at 190 °C for 15 to 22 minutes, until the fish reaches 63 °C, opening one parcel to check.
Serve directly on plates and open carefully because of the steam.
tips: Do not use thick onion slices, which would remain firm during the short cooking time.

title: Corvina over creamy malanga
description: Browned corvina served over a smooth malanga and garlic purée.
steps: Peel and cube the malanga and cook in the water with two garlic cloves and salt for 25 minutes, until tender.
Drain, reserving a little water; blend the malanga with the hot milk and one tablespoon of oil until thick and creamy.
Pat the corvina dry and season with the remaining garlic, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Cook in the remaining oil for 3 to 5 minutes per side, until the fish reaches 63 °C. Keep the purée warm over the lowest heat.
Spread the purée on each plate, arrange the fish on top, and finish with chopped parsley.
tips: Add liquid to the purée gradually; it should support the fish rather than resemble soup.

title: Corvina with savory guava sauce
description: Pan-cooked corvina with a guava, vinegar, and onion sauce.
steps: Chop the onion and garlic and sauté in one tablespoon of oil for 6 minutes.
Add the guava, vinegar, water, and cumin and cook over low heat for 10 minutes; blend and season with salt.
Check and pat dry the corvina, season with salt and pepper, and heat the remaining oil in a wide skillet.
Cook the fish for 3 to 5 minutes per side, until it reaches 63 °C, without moving it before it browns.
Serve the sauce separately or underneath the fish, avoiding simmering the fish in it to preserve its texture.
tips: Use unsweetened guava pulp, not firm sweet guava paste.

title: Cornmeal-coated corvina
description: Corvina coated in fine cornmeal and browned in a skillet.

ingredients.name: oil
ingredients.note: for frying; not all of it is consumed

steps: Season the fish with garlic, lemon juice, salt, and pepper and refrigerate for 10 minutes. Prepare fine cornmeal, cornstarch, and beaten egg separately.
Drain the fillets and coat in cornstarch, egg, and cornmeal; shake off the excess coating.
Heat a shallow layer of oil to about 170 °C in a skillet; fry only a few fillets at a time.
Cook for approximately 4 minutes per side, depending on thickness, until the fish reaches 63 °C and the coating is golden.
Drain on a rack and serve immediately, without covering or stacking.
tips: Use fine cornmeal suitable for cooking, not coarse polenta meal.

title: Baked tilapia with ripe plantain
description: Tilapia baked with ripe plantain, onion, and orange juice.
steps: Peel the plantains and cut into one-centimeter slices. Toss with the sliced onion and two tablespoons of oil and bake for 20 minutes at 200 °C.
Check for bones and season the tilapia with garlic, lemon juice, oregano, and salt.
Arrange the fish over the almost-tender plantains and add the orange juice and remaining oil.
Bake for another 12 to 18 minutes, until the centers of the tilapia fillets reach 63 °C.
Serve with the plantain and onion, spooning up the orange juices from the dish.
tips: Precook the plantains so the fish does not dry out while waiting for them to soften.

title: Tilapia with eggplant and basil
description: Tilapia in a tomato sauce with eggplant roasted beforehand.
steps: Cut the eggplant into cubes, toss with two tablespoons of oil, and roast for 25 minutes at 200 °C.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the remaining oil; add the tomatoes and water and cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in the tender eggplant and season with salt and pepper; mix without breaking up the cubes.
Arrange the tilapia in the sauce, cover, and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until it reaches 63 °C.
Add the torn basil off the heat and serve with a wide spatula.
tips: Roasted eggplant adds texture and keeps the sauce from becoming too watery.

title: Tilapia rolls with carrot and bell pepper
description: Tilapia fillets rolled around thinly cut vegetables and cooked in a light sauce.
steps: Cut the carrot and bell pepper into very thin matchsticks and sauté in one tablespoon of oil for 6 minutes. Let cool slightly.
Season the fish with salt and pepper, divide the vegetables among the fillets, roll up, and secure with toothpicks, keeping track of how many you use.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the remaining oil; add the tomatoes, water, and lemon juice and cook for 8 minutes.
Arrange the rolls in a single layer, cover, and simmer gently for 12 to 15 minutes, until the center of the filling reaches 74 °C.
Remove every toothpick, adjust the salt, and serve with the sauce.
tips: Thin vegetable matchsticks let you close the rolls without breaking the fillets.

title: Tilapia with coconut and cilantro
description: Tilapia in coconut milk with cilantro and a touch of lemon.
steps: Chop the onion, garlic, and tender cilantro stems; reserve the leaves. Check the fish for bones and pat dry.
Sauté the onion and garlic in oil for 6 minutes; add the cumin and cilantro stems and cook for half a minute.
Pour in the coconut milk and water and simmer gently for 5 minutes; season lightly with salt.
Arrange the tilapia in the sauce, cover, and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 63 °C.
Remove from the heat and add the lemon juice and cilantro leaves; adjust the salt and serve immediately.
tips: Use unsweetened coconut milk, not sweetened coconut cream for drinks.

title: Crispy sesame tilapia
description: Tilapia fillets coated in sesame breadcrumbs and baked in the oven.
steps: Pat the tilapia dry and season with garlic, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Mix the breadcrumbs with the sesame seeds.
Place the flour and beaten eggs on two separate plates. Coat the fillets in flour, egg, and the seed mixture.
Place on a baking sheet brushed with one tablespoon of oil and drizzle with the rest. Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Bake for 15 to 22 minutes, turning once if possible without breaking the fish, until the centers reach 63 °C.
Serve immediately and avoid covering the crisp surface with liquids.
tips: If the sesame browns quickly, move the tray down one oven rack.

title: Hake with potatoes and roasted peppers
description: Hake cooked over potatoes with roasted pepper strips and garlic.
steps: Roast the halved peppers at 220 °C for 20 minutes, cool slightly, peel, and cut into strips. Meanwhile, peel the potatoes and cut into thin rounds.
While the peppers roast, sauté the onion and garlic in oil for 6 minutes; add the potatoes, water, and salt, then cover and cook for 18 to 20 minutes.
Once the potatoes are almost tender, place the hake and roasted peppers on top.
Cover and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until the fish reaches 63 °C; gently shake the pot.
Add the lemon juice and check the salt; serve by lifting the potatoes and fish together with a spatula.
tips: Add the fish when the potatoes are nearly cooked, not at the beginning.

title: Hake in parsley sauce
description: Hake in a light green sauce of garlic, parsley, and white wine.
steps: Finely chop the onion and garlic. Reserve two tablespoons of the water to dissolve the cornstarch and blend the parsley with the rest.
Sauté the onion and garlic in oil for 5 minutes without browning too much. Add the wine and boil for 2 minutes.
Pour in the parsley water and season with salt; add the hake, cover, and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until it reaches 63 °C.
Add the dissolved cornstarch at the side of the pot and shake gently; cook for one minute to thicken.
Remove from the heat, stir in the lemon juice, and serve immediately with the green sauce.
tips: A gentle simmer keeps the fillets intact and preserves the parsley's flavor.

title: Baked hake with spinach and cheese
description: Hake baked over sautéed spinach and covered with cheese.
steps: Sauté the onion and garlic in oil for 5 minutes. Add the spinach, salt, and pepper and cook until its liquid evaporates.
Dissolve the cornstarch in the cold milk, stir into the spinach, and cook for one minute until slightly thickened.
Spread the mixture in a baking dish, place the hake seasoned with salt and pepper on top, and cover with cheese.
Bake at 190 °C for 18 to 25 minutes, until the center of the dish reaches 74 °C and the cheese is golden.
Serve with the creamy spinach underneath, taking care not to break the fillets as you lift them.
tips: Drain excess water from the spinach before adding the milk.

title: Hake fish balls in Cuban-style tomato sauce
description: Chopped hake fish balls with a sautéed tomato and bell pepper sauce.
steps: Finely chop the hake with a knife, checking for bones. Mix with the egg, breadcrumbs, one garlic clove, parsley, and salt and refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Shape into 16 balls with damp hands. Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and remaining garlic in oil for 7 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and water and cook for 10 minutes, until a mellow sauce forms.
Arrange the fish balls in a single layer, cover, and cook for 15 to 18 minutes, until their centers reach 74 °C.
Adjust the salt and serve, gently moving the pot rather than stirring the fish balls vigorously.
tips: Chopping with a knife preserves the texture better than blending the fish.

title: Hake and sweet potato pie
description: Hake in tomato sauce covered with sweet potato mash and cheese.
steps: Peel and cut the sweet potato and boil in the water for 20 minutes. Drain and mash with the hot milk, butter, and salt.
Sauté the onion and garlic in oil; add the tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the diced hake and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until it reaches 63 °C; gently separate into flakes and check for bones.
Spread the fish and sauce in a baking dish, cover with the mash and cheese, and bake for 20 minutes at 190 °C, until the center reaches 74 °C.
Rest for 10 minutes and serve with a spatula to preserve the layers.
tips: Keep the filling moist but not watery so the pie holds together.

title: Fresh cod with sautéed corn and peppers
description: Fresh cod loins over a sautéed corn and bell pepper base.
steps: Check the cod for bones and season with a little salt. Chop the onion, bell pepper, and garlic.
Sauté the vegetables in oil for 7 minutes; add the tomatoes and oregano and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the drained corn and water and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Arrange the cod in the pan, cover, and cook for 8 to 12 minutes, depending on thickness, until it reaches 63 °C.
Serve the loins with the vegetable mixture around them and adjust the sauce's salt at the end.
tips: This recipe uses fresh, unsalted cod; no desalting is needed.

title: Salt cod with chickpeas and spinach
description: Desalted cod in a chickpea and spinach stew.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: only if needed after tasting the cooked dish

steps: Desalt the cod covered in cold water in the refrigerator for about 36 hours, changing the water every 8 hours; follow the package if it specifies a different time.
Sauté the onion and garlic in oil for 7 minutes; add the paprika and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the measured water, chickpeas, and bay leaf and simmer for 12 minutes. Stir in the spinach and let it wilt.
Add the drained cod, cover, and cook for 8 to 12 minutes, until the centers reach 63 °C.
Remove the bay leaf and check for bones when serving; taste before adding salt.
tips: The cod's thickness determines desalting time; do not use the same timing for fine flakes.

title: Baked salt cod with peppers and potatoes
description: Desalted cod roasted over potatoes and peppers that have been partially cooked.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: only if needed after tasting the cooked dish

steps: Desalt the cod in the refrigerator for about 36 hours, changing the water several times and following the label's guidance for its thickness.
Peel and thinly slice the potatoes; mix with the onion, sliced peppers, garlic, and three tablespoons of oil and spread in a baking dish with the measured water.
Bake covered for 30 minutes at 200 °C, until the potatoes are almost tender.
Place the drained loins on top, add the oregano and remaining oil, and bake uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes, until the fish reaches 63 °C.
Serve with the vegetables and taste the sauce before adding extra salt.
tips: Add the cod after precooking the potatoes so it does not dry out.

title: Salt cod and onion omelet
description: A thick oven-baked omelet with desalted cod and softened onion.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: only if needed after tasting the cooked dish

steps: Desalt the cod flakes in the refrigerator for about 24 hours, changing the water several times, or follow the label. Drain and check for bones.
Peel the potatoes, cut into small cubes, and boil in the measured water for 12 minutes; drain.
While the potatoes boil, sauté the onion and garlic in three tablespoons of oil for 10 minutes; add the cod and cook for 5 minutes, until it reaches 63 °C.

Beat the eggs with the parsley and pepper and mix with the warm potatoes and cod; taste the cooked cod first and adjust the salt if needed. Pour into an oiled baking dish and bake at 180 °C for 25 to 30 minutes, until the center reaches 74 °C.
Let settle for 5 minutes and serve in portions, checking that the center is set with no liquid egg.
tips: Thoroughly check the cod flakes to keep bones out of the omelet.

title: Salt cod and malanga brandade
description: A thick purée of desalted cod, malanga, and olive oil, baked until golden.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: only if needed after tasting the cooked dish

steps: Desalt the cod in the refrigerator for about 36 hours, changing the water according to its thickness and label. Peel the malanga and cook in 1200 ml of water for 25 minutes.
Cook the drained cod in the remaining water for 5 to 8 minutes, until it reaches 63 °C; remove the skin and all the bones.
Heat the milk with the garlic for 5 minutes without scorching. Mash the malanga and cod and gradually incorporate the milk and oil until thick and creamy.
Add the parsley and pepper, check the salt, and spread in a baking dish. Sprinkle with breadcrumbs.
Bake at 200 °C for 15 to 20 minutes, until golden and the center reaches 74 °C; serve hot.
tips: Avoid overblending the malanga, which can make it gluey; mashing is preferable.

title: Griddled tuna with avocado and tomato
description: Fully cooked tuna served with fresh diced avocado and tomato.
steps: Dice the tomato, avocado, and onion. Mix with the cilantro, half the lemon juice, one tablespoon of oil, and a pinch of salt.
Pat the tuna dry and season with garlic, salt, and pepper. Keep the vegetable salsa refrigerated.
Heat the remaining oil on a griddle and cook the tuna for 3 to 4 minutes per side, adjusting for thickness.
Check that the center reaches 63 °C; if it is not hot enough, lower the heat slightly and finish cooking without burning the surface.
Add the remaining lemon juice and serve with the fresh mixture alongside.
tips: This recipe calls for tuna cooked all the way through, not merely seared on the outside.

title: Tuna with white beans and peppers
description: Tuna cubes added at the end of a quick white bean stew.
steps: Cut the tuna into 3 cm cubes and drain the beans. Chop the onion, bell pepper, and garlic.
Sauté the vegetables in oil for 8 minutes, add the tomatoes and oregano, and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the beans, water, and bay leaf and simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Add the tuna, cover, and cook for 6 to 9 minutes, until the thick cubes reach 63 °C.
Remove the bay leaf, check the salt, and serve without continuing to boil the tuna after it is done.
tips: The beans should already be cooked before you add them; the tuna needs little time.

title: Fresh tuna fish balls with lemon
description: Chopped tuna and cilantro fish balls in a light lemon sauce.
steps: Finely chop the tuna with a knife, check for bones, and mix with the egg, breadcrumbs, one garlic clove, half the cilantro, and salt. Refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Shape into 16 balls and brown in oil for 5 minutes; remove carefully.
Sauté the onion and remaining garlic, add 300 ml of water and half the lemon juice, and return the fish balls.
Cover and cook for 15 to 18 minutes, until they reach 74 °C. Stir in the cornstarch dissolved in the remaining water and boil for one minute.
Add the remaining cilantro and lemon juice off the heat, adjust the salt, and serve with the lightly thickened broth.
tips: The mixture stays firmer if the tuna is chopped rather than blended into a purée.

title: Bell peppers stuffed with tuna and rice
description: Baked bell peppers with canned tuna, cooked rice, and tomato.
steps: Halve the peppers, remove the seeds, and precook for 12 minutes at 190 °C in a baking dish with water.
Sauté the onion and garlic in oil for 6 minutes; add the tomatoes and oregano and cook for 8 minutes.
Mix the sauce with the drained tuna, cooked rice, and chopped olives. Taste before adding salt.
Fill the peppers, cover with cheese, and bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the centers reach 74 °C.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve two halves per person with the pan juices.
tips: Use freshly cooked rice or rice that was promptly refrigerated, not rice left at room temperature for hours.

title: Tuna and ripe plantain gratin
description: Layers of ripe plantain and tuna with sautéed vegetables, topped with cheese.
steps: Peel the plantains and cut into lengthwise slices; brush with two tablespoons of oil and roast for 15 minutes at 200 °C.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the remaining oil for 7 minutes; add the tomatoes and oregano and cook for 10 minutes.
Mix the drained tuna with the sautéed vegetable mixture and check the salt. Place half the plantain in a baking dish.
Spread over the tuna, cover with the remaining plantain and cheese, and bake for 20 minutes at 190 °C, until the center reaches 74 °C.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting so the layers hold their shape.
tips: Drain the tuna well so it does not make the pie too wet.

title: Salmon with orange and garlic marinade
description: A home-style variation of baked salmon with garlic, orange, and onion.
steps: Check the salmon for bones and pat dry. Mix the juices, garlic, oil, oregano, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Rub over the fish and refrigerate for 10 minutes. Preheat the oven to 190 °C.
Spread very thinly sliced onion in a baking dish and arrange the salmon and marinade on top.
Bake for 15 to 22 minutes, depending on thickness, until the center reaches 63 °C, without unnecessarily prolonging the cooking.
Serve with the onion and juices; remove the skin if it is still attached and you do not want to eat it.
tips: This is a home-style application of a Cuban citrus-garlic marinade to salmon, not a claim that the dish is a historic Cuban classic.

title: Salmon with a peanut and lemon crust
description: Baked salmon with a roasted peanut and parsley topping.
steps: Chop the peanuts without turning them into a paste and mix with the breadcrumbs, parsley, garlic, and two tablespoons of oil.
Pat the salmon dry and season with salt and pepper. Place in a baking dish brushed with the remaining oil.
Mix the mustard and lemon juice, brush over the top, and cover with the peanut mixture, pressing lightly.
Bake at 190 °C for 15 to 22 minutes, until the center reaches 63 °C; protect the crust if it begins to brown too much.
Serve with a spatula to keep the topping intact and do not cover the fish after cooking.
tips: Leave the peanuts in small pieces to give the crust a crunchy texture.

title: Salmon in parchment with cabbage and carrot
description: Salmon baked in parcels with finely cut vegetables.
steps: Cut the cabbage, carrot, and onion into very thin strips and sauté in oil for 4 minutes to soften slightly.
Divide the vegetables among four large sheets of parchment paper and place the boneless salmon on top.
Distribute the chopped garlic and ginger and the soy sauce and lemon juice mixture; seal each parcel tightly.
Bake at 190 °C for 15 to 22 minutes, until the center of the salmon reaches 63 °C, carefully opening one parcel to measure.
Serve in the parcels or transfer to plates, letting the steam escape away from your face.
tips: Briefly precooking the vegetables prevents them from remaining hard when the fish is done.

title: Salmon with mango and tamarind
description: Pan-cooked salmon with a warm mango and tamarind sauce.
steps: Dilute the tamarind in the water and strain out fibers. Peel and dice the mango; chop the onion and garlic.
Sauté the onion and garlic in one tablespoon of oil for 5 minutes; add the tamarind and honey and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the mango and cook for 3 minutes to soften without breaking it up; season with a little salt.
Season the salmon with salt and pepper and cook in the remaining oil for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until it reaches 63 °C.
Serve the fish with the warm mango sauce alongside to preserve its browned surface.
tips: Tamarind varies in acidity; taste the sauce before adding more pulp.

title: Salmon over creamy corn
description: Griddled salmon served over creamy corn with garlic and onion.
steps: Sauté the onion and two garlic cloves in one tablespoon of oil for 6 minutes. Add the corn, milk, and water and cook for 10 minutes.
Blend half or all of the mixture, depending on the desired texture; adjust the salt and keep warm over low heat.
Check the salmon for bones and season with the remaining garlic, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Cook in the remaining oil for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until it reaches 63 °C, adjusting for thickness.
Serve over the creamy corn and finish with chopped cilantro.
tips: Use cooked corn with no added sugar to keep the dish savory.

title: Baked trout with garlic and parsley
description: Whole butterflied trout baked with garlic, parsley, and lemon.
steps: Pat the cleaned trout dry and check the cavities; season inside and out with salt and pepper. Preheat the oven to 190 °C.
Mix the chopped garlic and parsley with the lemon juice and oil and spread some inside the fish.
Place the sliced onion and water in a baking dish; arrange the trout and distribute the remaining mixture over them.
Bake for 20 to 30 minutes, until the flesh near the backbone reaches 63 °C without touching the bone when measuring, adjusting for size.
Remove the backbone and small bones while portioning; serve with the pan juices.
tips: Ask for the trout gutted and butterflied to make checking for bones easier.

title: Trout with coconut and sweet peppers
description: Trout fillets in a mild coconut and sweet pepper sauce.
steps: Remove the seeds from the sweet peppers and chop them with the onion and garlic. Check the trout for bones.
Sauté the vegetables in oil for 7 minutes; add the coconut milk and water and simmer gently for 6 minutes.
Season the trout lightly and arrange in a single layer over the sauce.
Cover and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 63 °C; avoid a vigorous boil.
Add the lemon juice and cilantro off the heat and adjust the salt before serving.
tips: Use sweet peppers; do not substitute the same quantity of hot peppers.

title: Trout with almonds and twice-fried plantains
description: Pan-cooked trout with toasted almonds and freshly fried plantains.

ingredients.name: frying oil
ingredients.note: not all of it is consumed

steps: Peel the plantains and cut into 3 cm rounds. Fry at 160 °C for 5 minutes, drain, and flatten.
Season the trout with salt, pepper, and chopped garlic. Cook in the two tablespoons of oil for 3 to 5 minutes per side, until it reaches 63 °C.
Toast the almonds in a dry skillet for 2 minutes; add the butter and, off the heat, the lemon juice.
Fry the flattened plantains at 180 °C for 1 to 2 minutes per side, drain, and season with salt.
Serve the trout with the butter and toasted almonds spooned over it and the plantains alongside.
tips: Watch the almonds closely because they go from toasted to burnt quickly.

title: Vegetable-stuffed trout
description: Butterflied trout filled with sautéed carrot, zucchini, and bell pepper.
steps: Cut the carrot, zucchini, and bell pepper into thin strips; sauté with two tablespoons of oil and the garlic for 7 minutes. Let cool slightly.
Pat the butterflied trout dry and season with salt and pepper; check for bones and divide the vegetables among the cavities without overfilling.
Close with kitchen string and place over sliced onion in a baking dish with the water, lemon juice, and remaining oil.
Bake at 190 °C for 25 to 30 minutes, until the center of the filling reaches 74 °C.
Remove all the string, divide into portions, and serve carefully, watching for any small bones that may remain.
tips: Ask the fishmonger to bone the trout and check it again before stuffing.

title: Trout in orange and vinegar marinade
description: Cooked trout chilled with orange, vinegar, and carrot.
steps: Pat the trout dry, season with salt, and cook in two tablespoons of oil for 3 to 5 minutes per side, until it reaches 63 °C. Place in a shallow container.
Sauté the sliced carrot, onion, and garlic in the remaining oil for 8 minutes.
Add the orange juice, vinegar, water, bay leaf, and pepper and boil for 7 minutes; adjust the salt.
Pour over the trout, let the heavy steam escape, and refrigerate promptly, rather than leaving it out for several hours.
Chill for two hours, remove the bay leaf, and serve with the vegetables and a little marinade.
tips: The orange juice adds flavor; this dish must remain refrigerated.

title: Mackerel stew with eggplant
description: Mackerel steaks cooked in an eggplant and tomato sauce.
steps: Cut the eggplant into small cubes and brown in two tablespoons of oil for 8 minutes; remove.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the remaining oil, add the tomatoes, water, and oregano, and cook for 10 minutes.
Return the eggplant and arrange the lightly salted fish steaks in the sauce.
Cover and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, until the flesh near the bone reaches 63 °C without touching the bone when measuring.
Add the lemon juice and serve carefully, watching for the central bone and any smaller bones.
tips: The steaks should be similarly thick so they finish cooking together.

title: Baked mackerel with sweet potato and olives
description: Mackerel roasted over sliced sweet potato with olives and tomato.
steps: Peel the sweet potato and cut into half-centimeter slices. Arrange with the onion and two tablespoons of oil in a baking dish with the water.
Bake covered at 200 °C for 25 minutes, until the sweet potato begins to soften.
Add the mackerel, tomato wedges, olives, garlic, oregano, and remaining oil; season lightly with salt.
Bake uncovered for another 18 to 22 minutes, until the fish reaches 63 °C and the sweet potato is tender.
Serve with the juices and remove bones when dividing the steaks into portions.
tips: Salt sparingly because the olives add salt to the dish.

title: Baked jack with tomato and onion
description: Butterflied jack baked with fresh tomato and a layer of thinly sliced onion.
steps: Ask for cleaned jack and check for visible bones. Pat dry and season with salt and pepper; preheat the oven to 190 °C.
Slice the tomatoes and onions and spread half in a baking dish with the water and one tablespoon of oil.
Arrange the butterflied fish on top and distribute the garlic, lemon juice, remaining vegetables, and remaining oil over it.
Bake for 20 to 30 minutes, until the thickest flesh reaches 63 °C, without touching bones when measuring.
Sprinkle with parsley, divide into portions, and check for small bones before serving.
tips: Keep the fish refrigerated until you are ready to prepare it.

title: Jack with tamarind and pepper sauce
description: Browned jack fillets served with tamarind and bell peppers.
steps: Dilute the tamarind in the water and strain. Chop the onion, bell pepper, and garlic.
Sauté the vegetables in one tablespoon of oil for 7 minutes; add the tamarind, sugar, and cumin and cook for 10 minutes.
Check the jack for bones, pat dry, and season with salt. Brown in the remaining oil for 3 to 4 minutes per side.
Check that the fish reaches 63 °C and adjust the sauce's salt separately.
Serve with the sauce alongside and the peppers on top; avoid cooking the fish further in the sauce.
tips: Jack has a robust flavor; serve the sauce separately so you can control how much tartness to add.

title: Roasted sardines with a cassava crumb crust
description: Butterflied sardines baked with cassava flatbread crumbs, garlic, and parsley.
steps: Check the sardines for small bones and pat dry. Preheat the oven to 210 °C.
Crush the cassava flatbread into crumbs and mix with the garlic, parsley, and three tablespoons of oil.
Grease a baking sheet with the remaining oil and arrange the butterflied sardines skin side down; season with salt and pepper and add the lemon juice.
Lightly cover with cassava crumbs and bake for 12 to 18 minutes, until the thick parts reach 63 °C and the topping is golden.
Serve immediately, lifting with a wide spatula to keep each sardine whole.
tips: Do not make the topping so thick that you cannot check the fish's doneness.

title: Sardines in lemon and vinegar marinade
description: Cooked sardines chilled with lemon, vinegar, and carrot.
steps: Lightly salt the sardines and cook in two tablespoons of oil for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until they reach 63 °C. Arrange in a shallow container.
Sauté the sliced carrot, onion, and garlic in the remaining oil for 8 minutes.
Add the lemon juice, vinegar, water, bay leaf, and pepper and boil for 6 minutes; adjust the salt.
Pour over the sardines, let the heavy steam escape, and refrigerate promptly.
Chill for at least two hours, remove the bay leaf, and serve cold, watching for bones as you eat.
tips: Keep these marinated sardines refrigerated; this is not a home-canning recipe.

title: Sardine pie with potato and tomato
description: Layers of cooked potato, canned sardines, and a sautéed tomato sauce.
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut into half-centimeter rounds; boil in salted water for 10 minutes and drain without breaking them.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in two tablespoons of oil for 7 minutes; add the tomatoes and oregano and cook for 10 minutes.
Check the sardines and remove hard bones. Grease a baking dish and alternate layers of potatoes, sardines, and tomato sauce.
Finish with cheese and bake for 25 to 30 minutes at 190 °C, until the center reaches 74 °C and the potatoes are tender.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting and serve with a spatula that reaches all the way to the bottom.
tips: The sardine weight listed is the drained weight, not the total weight of the can.

title: Griddled mahi-mahi with pineapple and spearmint
description: Mahi-mahi with grilled pineapple and a fresh spearmint dressing.
steps: Cut the pineapple into thick rounds and thinly slice the onion. Chop the spearmint and mix with the lemon juice and one tablespoon of oil.
Pat the mahi-mahi dry, check for bones, and season with garlic, salt, and pepper.
Brown the pineapple in one tablespoon of oil for 3 minutes per side and set aside; sauté the onion on the same griddle for 2 minutes.
Cook the fish in the remaining oil for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until it reaches 63 °C.
Serve alongside the pineapple and onion and add the spearmint dressing off the heat.
tips: Brown the pineapple in batches so it does not release too much liquid onto the griddle.

title: Mahi-mahi with chickpeas and squash
description: Mahi-mahi added at the end of a winter squash and chickpea stew.
steps: Cut the squash into 2 cm cubes and the mahi-mahi into large portions. Chop the onion and garlic.
Sauté the onion and garlic in oil for 6 minutes; add the cumin, tomatoes, water, and bay leaf and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the squash and drained chickpeas, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, until the squash is almost tender.
Add the fish, season with salt, and cook for another 8 to 10 minutes, until the centers reach 63 °C.
Remove the bay leaf, adjust the salt, and serve without breaking up the squash cubes.
tips: Add the fish at the end so it keeps its firm texture.

title: Sole rolls with spinach in orange sauce
description: Sole fillets with spinach, gently cooked in an orange sauce.
steps: Sauté the spinach with one tablespoon of oil and one garlic clove; drain very well and cool slightly. Check the fillets for bones.
Season the sole with salt and pepper, divide the spinach among the fillets, and roll up; secure with toothpicks, keeping track of how many you use.
Sauté the onion and remaining garlic in the remaining oil for 5 minutes. Add the orange juice and 80 ml of water and place the rolls in the pan.
Cover and simmer gently for 10 to 14 minutes, until the center of the filling reaches 74 °C. Remove the rolls and every toothpick.
Thicken the sauce with the cornstarch dissolved in the remaining water, boil for one minute, add the lemon juice, and serve over the fish.
tips: Draining the spinach helps the rolls close and keeps the sauce from becoming watery.

title: Lobster and saffron rice
description: Rice cooked until the liquid is absorbed, with raw lobster added near the end and a delicate sofrito.
steps: Chop the onion, bell pepper, and garlic. Keep the lobster refrigerated and soak the saffron in two tablespoons of hot stock.
Sauté the onion and bell pepper in the oil for six minutes; add the garlic and tomato and reduce for four minutes.
Add the rinsed rice, stock, saffron, and salt. Once boiling, cover and cook over the lowest heat for twelve minutes.
Arrange the lobster on top and cover again; cook for eight to ten minutes, until its center is white and opaque.
Check that the rice is tender, rest for five minutes, and finish with chopped parsley.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Creamy crab rice
description: Short-grain rice with real cooked crabmeat and a tomato broth.
steps: Check the crabmeat with clean fingers and remove any shell fragments. Chop the vegetables.
Make a sofrito with the oil, onion, and bell pepper for six minutes; add the garlic, cumin, and tomato and cook for five minutes.
Add the rice and 900 ml of hot stock; simmer uncovered for eighteen minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the crabmeat, salt, and remaining stock as needed for the texture. Cook for five minutes, until the reheated crab reaches 74 °C.
Add the lime juice and serve after resting for two minutes; the rice should be creamy with some visible broth.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Conch rice with Cuban sofrito
description: Conch tenderized through a long simmer, then finished with rice and bell peppers.

ingredients.name: raw conch meat
ingredients.note: cleaned, commercially sold, and thawed in the refrigerator

steps: Gently pound the cleaned conch with a mallet between food-safe sheets. Place in a pot with the water and bay leaf.
Simmer gently for two to three hours, until a knife slides in without resistance; replenish with hot water if the level drops too much.
Remove the conch, chop it into small pieces, and reserve 650 ml of strained broth. Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil; add the tomato and oregano.
Add the rinsed rice, conch, measured broth, and salt. Cover once boiling and cook over the lowest heat for about twenty minutes.
Rest for ten minutes, remove the bay leaf, and drizzle with lime juice. Do not add the rice while the conch is still tough.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Black rice with cuttlefish
description: Dark rice with tender cuttlefish and commercial ink cooked in the stock.
steps: Cut the cuttlefish into two-centimeter cubes. Chop the onion, garlic, and bell pepper and set aside the measured stock.
Sauté the vegetables in the oil for seven minutes. Add the cuttlefish and tomato and cook for five minutes.
Pour in the wine and 200 ml of stock; cover and cook for twenty-five minutes or until the cuttlefish is tender.
Measure the remaining cuttlefish cooking liquid and add stock to make 750 ml in total. Dissolve the ink in it, add the rice and salt, and simmer gently for twenty minutes.
If the grains are still firm, add hot stock from the reserve. Rest for five minutes before serving.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Octopus rice with roasted peppers
description: Already-cooked octopus over tomato rice with strips of roasted bell pepper.
steps: Drain the roasted bell pepper and cut it into strips. Separate the octopus slices and keep chilled.
Sauté the chopped onion in the oil for five minutes; add the garlic, paprika, and tomato and cook for four minutes.
Add the rinsed rice, stock, and salt. Cover once boiling and cook over the lowest heat for fifteen minutes.
Arrange the octopus and pepper on top, cover, and cook for seven more minutes, checking that the reheated octopus reaches 74 °C.
Turn off the heat and rest for five minutes; fluff the rice without crushing the octopus slices.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Salt cod and chickpea rice
description: Rice with desalted salt cod and tender chickpeas, finished together in one pot.
steps: Check that the purchased desalted salt cod is ready to cook according to its package, and cut it into large pieces.
Sauté the chopped vegetables in the oil for six minutes. Add the paprika and tomato and reduce for five minutes.
Add the rinsed rice, chickpeas, stock, and a little salt. Cover and cook over the lowest heat for twelve minutes from the time it boils.
Place the cod on top; cover and cook for eight to ten minutes, until the fish reaches 63 °C.
Rest for five minutes and taste before adding more salt, as the cod may provide enough.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Baked rice with sardines and olives
description: Butterflied fresh sardines over tomato rice finished in the oven.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Check the sardines for bones and chop the vegetables for the sofrito.
In an ovenproof pot, sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil; add the tomato and reduce for five minutes.
Add the rinsed rice, hot stock, olives, and salt. Boil on the stovetop for five minutes.
Arrange the butterflied sardines on top, cover, and bake for eighteen to twenty minutes, until the rice is tender and the fish reaches 63 °C.
Rest outside the oven for five minutes, add the lime juice, and serve with a spatula to keep the sardines whole.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Stir-fried rice with tuna and corn
description: Cooked rice stir-fried with canned tuna, corn, and green bell pepper.
steps: Separate the grains of cold rice. Drain the tuna and corn and dice the onion and bell pepper.
Heat the oil in a wide skillet and stir-fry the onion and bell pepper for five minutes; add the chopped garlic.
Add the corn and rice in batches. Stir for four minutes to break up clumps and heat evenly.
Add the tuna and salt, mixing gently; cook until everything reaches 74 °C without drying it out too much.
Remove from the heat and sprinkle with lime juice and parsley. Serve immediately.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Mussel rice with dry wine
description: Mussels opened separately and combined with rice cooked in their strained broth.

ingredients.name: live mussels
ingredients.note: in the shell, sold for food

steps: Clean the shells and remove the beards; discard broken mussels and any open ones that do not close when tapped.
Place the mussels and wine in a pot, cover, and cook for four to six minutes until they open; discard any that stay closed.
Pass the liquid through a fine filter and add water to make 650 ml. Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil and reduce the tomato.
Add the rice, measured liquid, and a little salt; cover and cook over the lowest heat for twenty minutes. Remove one shell from each mussel.
Place the mussels on top for the last three minutes to warm them; rest for five minutes and sprinkle with parsley.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Brothy clam and garlic rice
description: Rice served with plenty of broth, separately opened clams, and a mild garlic flavor.
steps: Wash the purchased purged clams and discard broken shells or open clams that do not respond when touched.
Open them in a covered pot with the wine for four to six minutes; discard closed clams and filter the liquid.
Sauté the onion and four chopped garlic cloves in the oil; add the rice, stock, and clam liquid. Cook uncovered for eighteen minutes.
Add the clams, remaining grated garlic, and parsley; cook for three more minutes, adjusting the broth with water if too much has been absorbed.
Taste before salting and serve immediately with plenty of broth, without stirring the shells roughly.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Three-seafood rice
description: Squid, shrimp, and mussels are added at different stages to suit their cooking times.
steps: Cut the squid into rings and keep it separate from the raw shrimp and already-cooked mussels.
Sauté the chopped vegetables in the oil; add the paprika, tomato, and squid. Pour in 300 ml of stock and simmer for twenty-five minutes.
When the squid is tender, measure the broth in the pot and top up to 1000 ml. Add the rice and salt and cook for fifteen minutes.
Add the shrimp and mussels; cook for five to seven minutes, until the shrimp are opaque and the whole mixture reaches 74 °C.
Rest for two minutes and serve moist. If the rice absorbs all the broth, add a small amount of hot broth before serving.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Shrimp rice with coconut and lime
description: Shrimp in coconut milk rice with mild ginger and a final splash of lime.
steps: Pat the shrimp dry and keep chilled. Chop the onion and garlic and grate the ginger.
Sauté the onion in the oil for five minutes; add the garlic and ginger and stir for thirty seconds.
Add the rinsed rice, coconut milk, stock, and salt. Cover once boiling and cook over the lowest heat for fifteen minutes.
Place the shrimp on top and cook covered for five to seven minutes, until opaque inside.
Rest for five minutes and gently mix in the lime juice and cilantro, keeping the grains whole.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Creamy shrimp and pumpkin rice
description: Some of the pumpkin breaks down to give body to this creamy shrimp rice.
steps: Cut the pumpkin into one-centimeter cubes; chop the onion and garlic and keep the shrimp chilled.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil, add the cumin and pumpkin, and cook for four minutes.
Add the rice, hot stock, and salt. Simmer gently for fifteen minutes, stirring every few minutes.
Add the shrimp and cook for six minutes until opaque; mash a few pumpkin cubes against the side of the pot.
Remove from the heat, add the lime juice, and serve after two minutes. The rice should be creamy and moist, not dry.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Shrimp and pineapple fried rice
description: Stir-fried rice with shrimp, browned pineapple, and egg, served freshly cooked.
steps: Cut the pineapple into small cubes and pat the shrimp dry. Beat the eggs with the salt.
Cook the eggs in one tablespoon of oil until set, cut into strips, and set aside; brown the pineapple in the same skillet for two minutes.
Add another tablespoon of oil and stir-fry the shrimp with the garlic for three to four minutes until opaque; remove with the pineapple.
Stir-fry the rice in the remaining oil for four minutes, breaking up clumps. Pour the soy sauce around the hot edge.
Return the shrimp, pineapple, and egg, add the chopped scallion, and stir-fry until all the rice reaches 74 °C. Serve immediately.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Baked snapper and tomato rice
description: Snapper fillets rest on rice with oven-roasted tomato slices.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Dice half the tomatoes and cut the other half into rounds.
Sauté the onion and garlic in two tablespoons of oil; add the diced tomatoes and cook for five minutes.
Add the rinsed rice, stock, and half the salt. Boil for five minutes and place the snapper and tomato rounds on top.
Season with the remaining salt, oregano, and oil; cover and bake for twenty minutes, until the rice is tender and the fish reaches 63 °C.
Rest outside the oven for five minutes and portion the fish with a wide spatula.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Brothy grouper and boniato rice
description: Chunks of grouper over rice in a red broth with firm pieces of boniato sweet potato.
steps: Cut the boniato into small cubes and the grouper into four-centimeter pieces; keep the fish refrigerated.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil for six minutes. Add the tomato and cumin and reduce for three minutes.
Pour in the stock, add the rice and boniato, and season. Simmer gently for fifteen minutes, stirring only occasionally.
Place the grouper in the broth and cook for eight more minutes, until the fish reaches 63 °C and the rice is tender.
Add the lime juice, check that plenty of liquid remains, and serve immediately in deep bowls.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Squid rice with green beans
description: Squid tenderized first, then combined with rice cooked until the liquid is absorbed and chopped green beans.
steps: Cut the squid into rings and the green beans into two-centimeter pieces. Chop the remaining vegetables.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil; add the paprika and tomato and cook for four minutes.
Add the squid and 300 ml of stock; cover and simmer for twenty-five to thirty minutes, until tender.
Measure the liquid and add stock to make 650 ml. Add the rinsed rice, green beans, and salt and cook covered for twenty minutes.
Rest off the heat for ten minutes; fluff the grains and distribute the rings without breaking them.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Crab rice with ripe plantain
description: Rice cooked until the liquid is absorbed, with cooked crabmeat and separately browned plantain cubes.
steps: Peel the plantain and cut it into cubes. Brown in one tablespoon of oil for six minutes and set aside.
Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the remaining oil; add the tomato and cook for four minutes.
Add the rinsed rice, stock, and salt. Cover and cook over the lowest heat for fifteen minutes from the time it boils.
Add the checked crabmeat and plantain; cover for seven more minutes, until the mixture reaches 74 °C.
Rest for five minutes and mix gently to keep some of the plantain cubes whole.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Creamy oyster rice
description: Creamy rice with shucked oysters and a mild tomato sofrito.
steps: Drain the oysters, check for shell fragments, and keep chilled; do not taste them raw.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil, add the tomato, and reduce for five minutes.
Add the rice, stock, and salt and simmer gently, uncovered, for fifteen minutes.
Add the oysters and maintain a gentle simmer for five to seven minutes, until completely firm and opaque.
Add the lime juice and serve immediately with the creamy broth; extend the cooking time if any oyster still has a translucent center.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Conch rice with coconut and sweet pepper
description: Slow-cooked conch, rice, and coconut milk in a home-style Caribbean combination.

ingredients.name: cleaned raw conch
ingredients.note: commercially sold meat, out of the shell

steps: Lightly tenderize the conch with a mallet and simmer it in the water for two to three hours, until tender; replenish the water if needed.
Cut it into small slices and strain the broth. Reserve 400 ml for the rice.
Sauté the chopped onion and sweet pepper in the oil; add the garlic and grated ginger and stir for one minute.
Add the rinsed rice, conch, reserved broth, coconut milk, and salt. Cover once boiling and cook over the lowest heat for twenty minutes.
Rest for ten minutes and finish with lime juice. The conch must be fully tenderized before cooking the rice.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Fish and rice bake with béchamel
description: Layers of cooked rice and fish bound with béchamel and baked until golden.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil; add the diced fish and cook for six minutes until it reaches 63 °C.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, cook the flour for two minutes, and gradually add the milk. Cook for five minutes with the salt and nutmeg.
Mix the rice with a third of the béchamel and spread half in a dish about 23 cm wide.
Cover with the fish, another portion of béchamel, and the remaining rice. Finish with the remaining sauce and cheese.
Bake for twenty-five minutes until golden and the center reaches 74 °C. Rest for five minutes before slicing.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Scallop rice with leek
description: Separately seared scallops served over leek and dry wine rice.
steps: Wash the leek thoroughly between its layers and slice finely. Pat the scallops dry and keep chilled.
Soften the leek and garlic in half the butter for five minutes; add the wine and boil for two minutes.
Add the rinsed rice, stock, and salt. Cover and cook over the lowest heat for twenty minutes; rest for five minutes.
While the rice rests, heat the oil and remaining butter in another skillet. Sear the scallops for two or three minutes per side, until firm and opaque.
Add the lime juice to the scallops and serve over the rice, spooning over their juices.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Green rice with grouper and cilantro
description: Rice in a green stock with green beans and grouper pieces, without tomato.
steps: Blend the stock with the cilantro and bell pepper. Cut the green beans into small pieces and the grouper into four-centimeter cubes.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for five minutes. Add the rinsed rice and green beans.
Pour in the green stock and add the salt, bring to a boil, and cook covered over the lowest heat for twelve minutes.
Place the grouper on the rice and finish cooking covered for eight to ten minutes, until the fish reaches 63 °C.
Rest for five minutes, add the lime juice, and serve by lifting the rice from the bottom without breaking the fish.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Brown rice with shrimp and green beans
description: Slow-cooking brown rice with vegetables and shrimp added near the end.
steps: Rinse the brown rice and cut the green beans into small pieces; keep the shrimp chilled.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil; add the paprika and tomato and cook for four minutes.
Add the rice, stock, and salt. Cover and cook over the lowest heat for thirty minutes; check the rice variety and add hot water if it dries out.
Add the green beans and cook for ten minutes. Add the shrimp and finish for five to seven minutes, until opaque and the rice is tender.
Rest covered for five minutes. Do not add the seafood if the rice still needs a long cooking time.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Octopus fried rice with golden garlic
description: Skillet rice with cooked octopus, crisp garlic, and roasted bell pepper.
steps: Separate the rice grains and pat the octopus slices dry. Cut the pepper into strips and thinly slice the garlic.
Brown the garlic in the oil over medium-low heat and remove it before it darkens.
Increase the heat and stir-fry the octopus for two minutes; add the rice in batches and stir for four minutes.
Add the bell pepper, paprika, salt, and scallion. Heat everything to 74 °C without burning the grains on the bottom.
Turn off the heat, add the lime juice, and scatter the golden garlic over the top to preserve its texture.
tips: Times are approximate; check the texture and doneness of the main ingredient.

title: Baked beef and partially ripe plantain rice
description: Rice with stewed beef, topped with partially ripe plantain and finished in the oven.
steps: Brown the diced beef in the oil with the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic; add the cumin, tomato, and 500 ml of water.
Cover and cook for ninety minutes until tender; add hot water if needed. Measure the broth and top up to 650 ml.
Fry thick slices of peeled plantain in the separate oil for three minutes per side. Heat the oven to 190 °C.
Combine the rinsed rice, beef, measured broth, and salt in a covered baking dish; bake for twenty minutes.
Arrange the plantain on top and bake for five more minutes; check that the rice is tender and rest for ten minutes.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Baked turkey and raisin rice
description: Rice with ground turkey, raisins, and olives, finished in a baking dish.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C and chop the onion, garlic, and bell pepper. Rinse and drain the rice.
Sauté the vegetables in the oil for five minutes. Add the turkey and break it up while cooking for eight minutes, until it reaches 74 °C.
Add the tomato, oregano, raisins, and olives; cook for four minutes and mix with the rice.
Add the stock and salt, bring to a boil, and transfer to a covered ovenproof dish. Bake for twenty-five minutes.
Check the rice, rest for ten minutes, and serve, fluffing the grains with a fork.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Rice with picadillo and roasted eggplant
description: Roasted eggplant mixed into rice with ground beef and tomato.
steps: Dice the eggplant, mix with one tablespoon of oil, and roast at 210 °C for twenty-five minutes.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the main quantity of oil; add the meat and cumin and cook to 71 °C, breaking up clumps.
Stir in the tomato and reduce for five minutes. Add the rinsed rice, stock, and salt and cover once boiling.
Cook over the lowest heat for twenty minutes. Add the roasted eggplant and fold in with broad movements.
Rest covered for five minutes and serve without crushing the eggplant cubes.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Smoked pork and chickpea rice
description: Already-cooked smoked pork and chickpeas give substance to this sofrito rice.
steps: Check that the pork is an already-cooked product; dice it and drain the chickpeas.
Sauté the onion and bell pepper in the oil; add the garlic, paprika, and pork and cook for three minutes.
Add the tomato and reduce for four minutes. Add the rinsed rice, chickpeas, stock, and a little salt.
Cover and cook over the lowest heat for twenty minutes from boiling; the whole mixture must reach 74 °C.
Rest for ten minutes and mix. Taste before adjusting the salt, as the smoked pork already contributes quite a lot.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Red bean rice with corn and pork cracklings
description: Rice with cooked beans and sweet corn, topped with pork cracklings at serving time.
steps: Drain the beans and corn; keep the measured bean broth. Chop the pork cracklings separately.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil; stir in the cumin and oregano for thirty seconds.
Add the rinsed rice, broth, beans, corn, and salt. Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over the lowest heat for twenty minutes.
Rest for ten minutes and fluff the rice with a fork without breaking up too many beans.
Scatter the crisp pork cracklings over each portion just before serving.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Baked rice with chicken and ripe plantains
description: Rice with already-cooked chicken and ripe plantain, baked beneath a thin layer of cheese.

ingredients.name: shredded cooked chicken
ingredients.note: Already cooked before starting; keep refrigerated until needed.
