steps: Cut the peeled ripe plantains into rounds and brown in two tablespoons of oil; set aside. Heat the oven to 190 °C.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the remaining oil, add the tomato, and reduce for five minutes.
Add the chicken, stock, and salt; heat for five minutes. Mix with the rice and half the plantain.
Spread in a 23 cm dish, arrange the remaining plantain on top, and cover with cheese.
Bake for twenty-five minutes until golden and the center reaches 74 °C. Rest for five minutes.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Chicken gizzard rice
description: Gizzards cooked until tender before adding the rice and sofrito.
steps: Check that the gizzards have no tough membranes and cut them in half; do not rinse poultry under the tap.
Simmer them gently with the water and bay leaf for sixty to ninety minutes, until tender and above 74 °C.
Strain and measure 650 ml of broth. Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil; add the tomato, cumin, and gizzards.
Add the rinsed rice, measured broth, and salt. Cover once boiling and cook over the lowest heat for twenty minutes.
Rest for ten minutes, remove the bay leaf, and serve, distributing the gizzards evenly.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Chicken liver rice with roasted pepper
description: Fully cooked chicken livers mixed into tomato and bell pepper rice.
steps: Remove tough tissues from the livers, pat dry with paper towels, and cut into even pieces; handle separately from the vegetables.
Sauté the onion and garlic in two tablespoons of oil, add the tomato and oregano, and cook for four minutes.
Add the rinsed rice, stock, and half a teaspoon of salt; cover and cook over the lowest heat for twenty minutes.
In another skillet, cook the livers in the remaining oil for eight to ten minutes, until their centers reach 74 °C; season with the remaining salt.
Mix the livers and roasted pepper into the rice, rest for five minutes, and serve hot.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Rabbit and rosemary rice
description: Rabbit stewed with tomato, followed by rice and a subtle touch of rosemary.
steps: Brown the rabbit in the oil for eight minutes. Add the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic and sauté for five minutes.
Add the wine and tomato, boil for three minutes, and add 500 ml of water and the rosemary.
Cover and stew for forty-five minutes or until tender and at least 71 °C. Remove the rosemary and measure the broth.
Top up the liquid to 650 ml, add the rinsed rice and salt, and cook covered over the lowest heat for twenty minutes.
Rest for ten minutes and serve, checking that there are no loose small bones.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Duck and olive rice
description: Slowly stewed duck with rice cooked in its defatted broth.
steps: Brown the duck skin-side down in a pot without oil for ten minutes. Set aside and remove the excess fat, leaving one tablespoon.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic; add the tomato, duck, bay leaf, and 800 ml of water. Cover and stew for seventy to ninety minutes until tender and at 74 °C.
Remove the duck, discard the bones and skin, and pull apart the meat. Defat the broth and measure 650 ml, topping up with water.
Add the rinsed rice, olives, meat, and salt to the broth. Cover and cook over the lowest heat for twenty minutes from boiling.
Remove the bay leaf, rest for ten minutes, and fluff the grains before serving.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Brown rice with black beans and sweet pepper
description: Brown rice with already-cooked beans added near the end to preserve their shape.
steps: Rinse the brown rice and drain the beans. Chop the onion, sweet pepper, and garlic.
Sauté the onion and sweet pepper in the oil for six minutes; add the garlic and cumin and cook for one minute.
Add the rice, stock, and salt; cover and cook over the lowest heat for thirty-five minutes.
Add the beans and a little hot water if needed. Cook for ten more minutes, until the rice is tender.
Rest covered for ten minutes and mix gently so the beans do not fall apart.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Brown rice with pumpkin and peanuts
description: Brown rice with roasted pumpkin and roasted peanuts added at serving time.
steps: Dice the pumpkin and mix with one tablespoon of oil and some of the salt. Roast at 200 °C for thirty minutes.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the remaining oil; add the cumin and rinsed brown rice.
Add the water and remaining salt; cover and cook over the lowest heat for forty to forty-five minutes, until tender.
Fold in the roasted pumpkin and rest for ten minutes. If the rice dries out before becoming tender, add hot water during cooking.
Chop the peanuts and scatter over the rice when serving so they retain their crunch.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Brown rice with lentils and golden onions
description: Cooked lentils and brown rice accompanied by slowly browned onions.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook covered with the water, chopped garlic, and half a teaspoon of salt for forty to forty-five minutes.
Cut the onion into thin strips. Cook in the oil over medium-low heat for twenty-five minutes, stirring until golden, and reserve half to finish the dish.
Add the cumin and drained lentils to the half of the onion remaining in the skillet and heat for five minutes with the remaining salt.
When the rice is tender, mix with the lentils and onion from the skillet; rest for five minutes.
Add the lime juice and distribute the remaining onion over the portions.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Brown rice with mushrooms and garlic
description: Skillet-browned mushrooms folded into brown rice cooked in vegetable stock.
steps: Sauté the chopped onion and two garlic cloves in one tablespoon of oil. Add the rinsed rice, stock, and salt.
Cook covered over the lowest heat for forty to forty-five minutes, adding hot water if it dries out before becoming tender.
Clean and quarter the mushrooms. Brown them in batches in the remaining oil without crowding.
Add the remaining garlic, black pepper, and parsley to the mushrooms and cook for one more minute.
Mix with the tender rice, rest for five minutes, and serve with the browned mushrooms visible.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Spinach and garlic rice with hard-boiled egg
description: Green spinach rice accompanied by fully cooked eggs.
steps: Wash the spinach and blend half with the measured water; cut the rest into strips.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil for five minutes. Add the rinsed rice, green liquid, and salt.
Cover and cook over the lowest heat for twenty minutes; add the spinach strips during the last five minutes.
In another pot, boil the eggs for eleven minutes, cool in cold water, peel, and quarter.
Rest the rice for five minutes and serve with one hard-boiled egg divided over each plate.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Eggplant and chickpea rice with paprika
description: Browned eggplant, chickpeas, and rice with a concentrated tomato base.
steps: Dice the eggplant and brown in two tablespoons of oil for eight minutes; transfer to a plate.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the remaining oil. Add the paprika and tomato and reduce for five minutes.
Add the rinsed rice, chickpeas, eggplant, stock, and salt and bring to a boil.
Cover and cook over the lowest heat for twenty minutes without stirring, until the rice is tender.
Rest for ten minutes and fold from the edges to preserve the shape of the eggplant.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Beet rice with white cheese
description: Pink rice made with cooked beet, finished with white cheese and lime.
steps: Blend half the beet with the stock and dice the rest. Crumble the cheese separately.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil; add the rinsed rice and cook for one minute.
Pour in the beet stock and add the diced beet and salt. Cover and cook over the lowest heat for twenty minutes from boiling.
Rest for five minutes and mix in the lime juice and half the cheese with a fork.
Scatter the remaining cheese and parsley on top when serving, keeping the beet cubes whole.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Cabbage and carrot rice with cumin
description: Sautéed cabbage and finely cut carrot mixed into pot-cooked rice.
steps: Cut the cabbage and onion into thin strips and coarsely grate the carrot. Rinse the rice.
Sauté the onion in the oil; add the cabbage and carrot and stir-fry for five minutes until they reduce in volume.
Add the garlic and cumin, then the rice, stock, and salt. Bring to a boil and cover.
Cook over the lowest heat for twenty minutes and rest for ten minutes without lifting the lid.
Stir in the vinegar and mix gently, distributing the cabbage strips through the rice.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Zucchini and corn rice with lime
description: Zucchini browned separately to hold its shape in rice with corn.
steps: Dice the zucchini and brown in two tablespoons of oil over high heat; set aside uncovered.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the remaining oil. Add the rinsed rice, drained corn, stock, and salt.
Cover when boiling begins and cook over the lowest heat for twenty minutes, until the stock is absorbed.
Fold in the zucchini and rest for five minutes so it heats through without breaking apart.
Add the lime juice and serve, mixing with two forks to separate the grains.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Coconut rice with young fava beans
description: Coconut milk rice with shelled fava beans and a touch of garlic and lime.
steps: Check the fava beans and remove any thick outer skins. Rinse and drain the rice.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for five minutes without browning too much.
Add the rice, fava beans, coconut milk, water, and salt and stir only once.
Cover once boiling and cook over the lowest heat for twenty minutes, until the rice and fava beans are tender.
Rest for ten minutes, add the lime juice, and fluff the rice; use young fava beans, not uncooked dried beans.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Rice with raisins, almonds, and onion
description: Savory rice with toasted almonds and raisins plumped in stock.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry skillet for two minutes, moving them until they begin to brown; set aside.
Cut the onion into thin strips and sauté in the oil for eight minutes. Add the garlic and a small pinch of cinnamon.
Add the rinsed rice, raisins, stock, and salt. Cover once boiling and cook over the lowest heat for twenty minutes.
Rest for ten minutes and fluff the rice with a fork; the raisins should be plump.
Add the almonds when serving to keep them crisp. This is a savory side dish with home-style inspiration.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Egg and scallion fried rice
description: Skillet rice with fully set egg, scallion, and soy sauce, without meat.
steps: Beat the eggs with the salt, finely chop the scallion, and cut the carrot into tiny cubes. Separate the cold rice grains.
Scramble the eggs in one tablespoon of oil, stirring; remove when no liquid egg remains.
Stir-fry the carrot and garlic in the remaining oil for three minutes; add the rice and stir for four minutes.
Pour in the soy sauce and add the egg and scallion. Stir-fry until everything is thoroughly hot, at 74 °C.
Serve immediately; do not use rice that has been left at room temperature for several hours.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Rice, spinach, and cheese bake
description: Cooked rice bound with egg and cheese and baked with well-drained spinach.
steps: Heat the oven to 185 °C and reserve one teaspoon of oil for the dish. Sauté the onion and garlic in the remaining oil; add the washed spinach and cook until its water evaporates.
Beat the eggs with the milk, salt, and nutmeg. Fold in the rice, lukewarm spinach, and half the cheese.
Grease a dish about 23 cm wide with the reserved teaspoon of oil and spread in the mixture without pressing it down.
Scatter over the remaining cheese and bake for thirty to thirty-five minutes, until set and the center reaches 74 °C.
Rest for ten minutes before cutting so the portions hold their shape.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Cabbage rolls stuffed with rice and beans
description: Cabbage leaves wrapped around rice and beans in a pot of tomato sauce.

ingredients.name: cooked white rice
ingredients.note: Already cooked before starting; keep refrigerated until needed.

steps: Separate twelve cabbage leaves and blanch in boiling water for three minutes; drain and trim down the thick ribs.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil. Mix half with the rice, beans, cumin, and some of the salt.
Fill each leaf, fold in the sides, and roll up. Add the tomato, water, and remaining salt to the reserved sofrito.
Place the rolls seam-side down on the sauce, cover, and simmer gently for thirty minutes, until their centers reach 74 °C.
Rest for five minutes and serve two rolls per portion, spooning the sauce over them.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Peppers stuffed with rice, corn, and cheese
description: Oven-baked peppers filled with cooked rice, corn, and melted cheese.

ingredients.name: cooked white rice
ingredients.note: Already cooked before starting; keep refrigerated until needed.

steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Cut the peppers in half and remove the seeds and ribs.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil, add the tomato and oregano, and cook for five minutes.
Mix the sofrito with the rice, corn, salt, and half the cheese; fill the eight pepper halves.
Arrange in a dish with the water, cover, and bake for thirty minutes. Uncover, add the remaining cheese, and bake for ten more minutes.
Check that the peppers are tender and the filling reaches 74 °C; rest for five minutes and serve two halves per person.
tips: Adjust the liquid to suit the absorption of your rice variety.

title: Black beans with smoked ribs
description: Dried beans cooked with already-cooked smoked ribs and a cumin sofrito.
steps: Sort the beans and soak in the refrigerator for eight hours using the soaking water; drain and rinse.
Cook in fresh water with the bay leaf for sixty to ninety minutes, until the beans are tender.
Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil with the cumin; cut the cooked ribs between the bones.
Add the sofrito, ribs, and a little salt to the beans; cook for twenty minutes, until the reheated meat reaches 74 °C.
Remove the bay leaf and any loose bones and mash a ladleful of beans to thicken the broth.
tips: Legumes listed as cooked must be completely tender before you start.

title: Black beans with coconut milk
description: Beans cooked in a creamy sauce of coconut, sweet pepper, and lime.
steps: Drain the beans and measure the broth separately. Chop the onion, sweet pepper, and garlic.
Soften the onion and sweet pepper in the oil for six minutes; stir in the garlic and cumin for thirty seconds.
Add the beans and broth and simmer gently for fifteen minutes to blend in the sofrito.
Pour in the coconut milk and add the salt and cook for ten minutes without boiling hard; mash some beans if you want it thicker.
Add the lime juice off the heat and serve with the creamy broth, without reducing it until dry.
tips: Legumes listed as cooked must be completely tender before you start.

title: Black beans with roasted eggplant
description: Roasted eggplant cubes accompany black beans in a tomato broth.
steps: Dice the eggplant, mix with one tablespoon of oil, and roast at 210 °C for twenty-five minutes.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the remaining oil; add the tomato and oregano and cook for six minutes.
Add the beans, broth, and salt. Simmer gently for twenty minutes without mashing the beans.
Add the roasted eggplant and cook for five more minutes. Stir gently so it retains some shape.
Check the consistency and add hot water if it has reduced too much; serve with a thick broth.
tips: Legumes listed as cooked must be completely tender before you start.

title: Black bean and green plantain stew
description: Green plantain thickens a stew of already-cooked beans and sofrito.
steps: Peel the plantains and cut them into two-centimeter rounds. Chop the vegetables for the sofrito.
Sauté the onion and bell pepper in the oil for six minutes; stir in the garlic and cumin.
Add the broth, bay leaf, and plantain; simmer gently for fifteen minutes to soften the plantain partially.
Add the beans and salt and cook for twenty more minutes. Mash some of the rounds to thicken, leaving others whole.
Remove the bay leaf and finish with the vinegar; serve hot without letting it dry out.
tips: Legumes listed as cooked must be completely tender before you start.

title: Red beans with pork and malanga
description: Stewed pork and malanga add substance to previously cooked red beans.
steps: Dice the pork and cut the malanga into small pieces. Brown the pork in the oil for eight minutes.
Add the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic; cook for five minutes and add the tomato, cumin, bay leaf, and water.
Cover and stew for forty minutes, until the pork begins to soften.
Add the malanga, cooked beans, and salt; cook for thirty minutes, until the malanga is completely tender and the pork falls apart.
Remove the bay leaf and mash two pieces of malanga to thicken the broth before serving.
tips: Legumes listed as cooked must be completely tender before you start.

title: Red beans with corn and tomato
description: Red beans cooked in a tomato and fresh corn stew.
steps: Drain the beans and separate the corn kernels. Chop the onion, bell pepper, garlic, and scallion.
Sauté the onion and bell pepper in the oil; add the garlic, paprika, and tomato and cook for seven minutes.
Pour in the stock and add the corn. Simmer gently for ten minutes to soften the kernels.
Add the beans and salt and cook for fifteen more minutes; mash some beans if you want more body.
Scatter fresh scallion over each bowl and serve while the broth is still loose.
tips: Legumes listed as cooked must be completely tender before you start.

title: White beans with fish and lime
description: A mild white bean stew with fish added near the end.
steps: Cut the fish into large pieces and keep chilled. Chop the vegetables for the sofrito.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil; add the tomato and reduce for five minutes.
Add the beans, stock, and salt and simmer gently for twenty minutes.
Add the fish and cook for six to eight minutes, until it reaches 63 °C, shaking the pot gently without breaking the fish.
Finish with parsley and lime juice and serve, portioning the fish first and then the beans.
tips: Legumes listed as cooked must be completely tender before you start.

title: White beans with ham and pumpkin
description: Tender pumpkin and cooked ham in a creamy white bean stew.
steps: Dice the ham and pumpkin and chop the onion and garlic.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil for five minutes; add the ham and cook for two minutes.
Add the water, bay leaf, and pumpkin and simmer gently for fifteen minutes.
Add the beans and black pepper and cook for fifteen more minutes; mash a little pumpkin to thicken.
Remove the bay leaf and taste before adding salt; check that the ham is thoroughly hot and serve.
tips: Legumes listed as cooked must be completely tender before you start.

title: White beans in green broth
description: Spinach and parsley turn bean broth into a green stew.
steps: Wash the spinach and parsley. Peel and dice the potato; chop the onion and garlic.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil. Add the potato and 800 ml of stock and cook for fifteen minutes.
Blend the spinach and parsley with the remaining stock and pour into the pot.
Add the beans and salt and cook for ten minutes, until the potato is tender and the green broth is well cooked.
Mash some beans to thicken and add the lime juice at the end, without blending the whole stew.
tips: Legumes listed as cooked must be completely tender before you start.

title: Black-eyed pea soup with rice and sofrito
description: Already-cooked black-eyed peas and short-grain rice in a generous soup.
steps: Rinse the rice and drain the black-eyed peas. Chop the vegetables finely.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil, add the cumin and tomato, and cook for five minutes.
Pour in the stock, add the rice and bay leaf, and simmer gently for ten minutes.
Add the black-eyed peas and salt and cook for another ten to twelve minutes, until the rice is tender.
Remove the bay leaf and serve immediately; if the soup sits, add hot water because the rice will continue absorbing broth.
tips: Legumes listed as cooked must be completely tender before you start.

title: Black-eyed peas with boniato and spinach
description: Boniato sweet potato and spinach accompany black-eyed peas in a cumin and garlic broth.
steps: Cut the boniato into two-centimeter cubes and wash the spinach; chop the onion and garlic.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil and add the cumin. Pour in the water and add the boniato and salt.
Cook for fifteen minutes, until the boniato is almost tender; add the black-eyed peas.
Simmer for ten more minutes and add the spinach strips during the last five minutes.
Finish with lime juice and serve with whole boniato cubes and a lightly thickened broth.
tips: Legumes listed as cooked must be completely tender before you start.

title: Chickpeas with spinach and sesame
description: Chickpeas stewed with spinach, tomato, and toasted sesame seeds.
steps: Wash the spinach and cut into strips; drain the chickpeas and chop the onion and garlic.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil; add the cumin and tomato and cook for seven minutes.
Add the chickpeas, stock, and salt. Simmer gently for twenty minutes to blend the flavors.
Add the spinach and cook for five minutes. Toast the sesame seeds in a dry skillet, stirring until fragrant.
Scatter the sesame seeds over the portions when serving and keep the broth slightly thick.
tips: Legumes listed as cooked must be completely tender before you start.

title: Chickpea and salt cod stew
description: Chickpeas and potato in tomato broth with already-desalted salt cod.

ingredients.name: uncooked desalted salt cod
ingredients.note: ready to cook according to the package

steps: Check the cod and remove any bones. Peel and dice the potato.
Sauté the chopped vegetables in the oil, add the paprika and tomato, and cook for five minutes.
Pour in the stock and add the potatoes; cook for fifteen minutes. Add the chickpeas and cook for ten more minutes.
Add the cod pieces and cook for eight to ten minutes, until they reach 63 °C.
Taste before adding salt and serve without breaking the fish flakes; do not use salted cod that has not been desalted.
tips: Legumes listed as cooked must be completely tender before you start.

title: Chickpeas with pumpkin and coconut
description: A mild chickpea stew with pumpkin and coconut milk.
steps: Dice the pumpkin and grate the ginger. Chop the onion and garlic.
Sauté the onion in the oil for five minutes; add the garlic, ginger, and cumin and stir for one minute.
Add the pumpkin, chickpeas, water, and salt and simmer gently for twenty minutes.
Add the coconut milk and cook for ten more minutes; mash some pumpkin cubes to thicken.
Remove from the heat, add the lime juice, and serve with the creamy broth and some whole chickpeas.
tips: Legumes listed as cooked must be completely tender before you start.

title: Chickpeas stewed with oxtail
description: Oxtail cooked slowly before adding chickpeas and carrot.
steps: Brown the oxtail in batches in the oil. Remove and sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic.
Add the wine, tomato, bay leaves, oregano, and water; return the oxtail, cover, and cook gently for three hours.
When the meat comes away from the bone, skim off the surface fat and add the sliced carrot.
Cook for fifteen minutes and add the chickpeas and salt; cook for another twenty minutes, adding water if needed.
Remove the bay leaves and any loose bones and serve, distributing the meat and chickpeas evenly.
tips: Legumes listed as cooked must be completely tender before you start.

title: Lentils with pumpkin and paprika
description: Dried lentils cooked with pumpkin and a paprika sofrito.
steps: Sort and rinse the lentils. Dice the pumpkin and chop the vegetables.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil; add the paprika and tomato and cook for four minutes.
Add the lentils, water, and bay leaf and simmer gently for twenty minutes.
Add the pumpkin and salt; cook for twenty to twenty-five more minutes, until the lentils are tender.
Remove the bay leaf and mash some of the pumpkin to add body, adding hot water if it has become too dry.
tips: Legumes listed as cooked must be completely tender before you start.

title: Lentils with chicken and carrot
description: Diced chicken and dried lentils cook together in a sofrito broth.
steps: Dice the chicken and slice the carrot into rounds; sort and rinse the lentils.
Brown the chicken in the oil for five minutes, add the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic, and cook for another five minutes.
Add the cumin, tomato, lentils, water, and carrot and bring to a boil.
Cook gently for forty to forty-five minutes, until the lentils are tender and the chicken is above 74 °C.
Season at the end and adjust with hot water if you prefer a lighter broth.
tips: Legumes listed as cooked must be completely tender before you start.

title: Lentils with chorizo and partially ripe plantain
description: Lentils with cured chorizo and rounds of partially ripe plantain added halfway through cooking.
steps: Sort and wash the lentils; slice the chorizo into rounds and peel the plantains.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil, add the chorizo and tomato, and cook for five minutes.
Add the lentils, water, and bay leaf and simmer gently for twenty minutes.
Add thick plantain rounds and the salt; cook for twenty to twenty-five more minutes, until everything is tender.
Remove the bay leaf and serve carefully to preserve the plantain pieces.
tips: Legumes listed as cooked must be completely tender before you start.

title: Red lentil and corn soup
description: Split red lentils break down to form a thick soup with corn.
steps: Rinse the red lentils until the water is less cloudy; drain the corn.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil, add the cumin and tomato, and cook for five minutes.
Add the lentils, water, and salt; simmer gently for twenty minutes, stirring to prevent sticking.
Add the corn and cook for five more minutes; the lentils should be broken down and creamy.
Add the lime juice off the heat and adjust with hot water if the soup becomes too thick.
tips: Legumes listed as cooked must be completely tender before you start.

title: Creamy split pea and carrot soup with ginger
description: Split peas and carrot blended with a small amount of ginger.
steps: Sort and wash the split peas; chop the carrot and onion and grate the ginger.
Sauté the onion, garlic, and ginger in the oil for four minutes; add the split peas, carrot, and water.
Cook partially covered for sixty to seventy minutes, stirring along the bottom and replenishing water if it dries out.
When the split peas fall apart, add the salt and blend off the heat with an immersion blender.
Reheat for two minutes, add the lime juice, and serve the soup fairly fluid, as it will thicken as it cools.
tips: Legumes listed as cooked must be completely tender before you start.

title: Split peas with smoked pork and celery
description: Split peas with cubes of already-cooked smoked pork and celery.
steps: Sort and rinse the split peas. Dice the pork, finely slice the celery, and chop the onion and garlic.
Sauté the onion, celery, and garlic in the oil for five minutes; add the split peas, water, and bay leaf.
Simmer gently for fifty minutes, stirring occasionally to keep the peas from sticking to the bottom.
Add the cooked pork and continue for twenty to thirty minutes, until the peas break down and the reheated meat reaches 74 °C.
Remove the bay leaf and taste before adding salt; serve thick, adding hot water if you prefer it lighter.
tips: Maintain a gentle simmer and add hot water if the broth reduces before the ingredients become tender.

title: Dried fava bean stew with tomato
description: Dried peeled fava beans, soaked and cooked with tomato and sofrito.
steps: Sort the fava beans and soak in the refrigerator for twelve hours in the soaking water; drain and rinse.
Cover with fresh water and add the bay leaf; bring to a boil and simmer gently for sixty to ninety minutes, until tender.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil. Add the paprika and tomato and reduce for six minutes.
Add the sofrito and salt to the fava beans and cook for twenty more minutes, stirring so they thicken without sticking.
Remove the bay leaf and serve with some beans left whole; this recipe uses dried rather than fresh fava beans.
tips: Maintain a gentle simmer and add hot water if the broth reduces before the ingredients become tender.

title: Creamy malanga and corn soup
description: Fully cooked malanga and fresh corn in a savory soup without milk.
steps: Dice the malanga, wash the corn, and chop the onion and garlic.
Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for five minutes; add the malanga, corn, and water.
Simmer gently for thirty minutes, until the malanga is easily pierced and the corn is tender.
Season and blend off the heat with an immersion blender; pass through a strainer if you want to remove the corn skins.
Heat for two minutes and sprinkle with parsley when serving; do not taste raw malanga during preparation.
tips: Maintain a gentle simmer and add hot water if the broth reduces before the ingredients become tender.

title: Creamy cassava and leek soup
description: Sweet cassava boiled separately and then blended with leek and milk.

ingredients.name: water for boiling, to be discarded

steps: Cut up and wash the peeled cassava and boil in the water for thirty to forty minutes, until completely tender.
Drain and discard the water; remove the central fibers. Wash the leek between its layers and slice finely.
Sauté the leek and garlic in the butter for six minutes; add the cassava, stock, salt, and black pepper and boil for five minutes.
Blend off the heat with an immersion blender and gradually add the milk.
Heat gently for three minutes and serve; use sweet cassava sold for food, never bitter varieties.
tips: Maintain a gentle simmer and add hot water if the broth reduces before the ingredients become tender.

title: Creamy cauliflower soup with golden garlic
description: Cauliflower and potato cooked into a creamy soup with golden garlic slices.
steps: Separate the cauliflower into florets and peel the potato. Thinly slice two garlic cloves and chop the remaining three.
Brown the garlic slices in one tablespoon of oil and set aside. Sauté the onion and chopped garlic in the remaining oil.
Add the diced potato, cauliflower, water, and salt; cook for twenty-five minutes, until everything is tender.
Blend off the heat and add the milk and black pepper. Heat for three minutes without boiling hard.
Serve with the golden garlic on top and adjust the consistency with hot water if it is too thick.
tips: Maintain a gentle simmer and add hot water if the broth reduces before the ingredients become tender.

title: Creamy pumpkin soup with coconut and orange
description: Pumpkin cooked with coconut milk and a touch of orange, without added sugar.
steps: Dice the pumpkin and chop the onion and garlic; grate the ginger.
Sauté the onion in the oil, add the garlic and ginger, and stir for thirty seconds.
Add the pumpkin, water, and salt and cook for twenty-five minutes, until the cubes fall apart.
Blend off the heat; add the coconut milk and orange juice and heat gently for five minutes.
Check the texture and serve in bowls; the result is a savory, creamy soup with a citrus aroma.
tips: Maintain a gentle simmer and add hot water if the broth reduces before the ingredients become tender.

title: Creamy red lentil and orange soup
description: Red lentils and carrot blended with a small amount of orange.
steps: Rinse the lentils and cut the carrot into small rounds; chop the onion and garlic.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil for five minutes and add the cumin.
Add the lentils, carrot, water, and salt; cook for thirty minutes, until the lentils fall apart.
Blend off the heat and add the orange juice; reheat for two minutes without reducing too much.
Serve the soup fairly fluid and add hot water if it has thickened while standing.
tips: Maintain a gentle simmer and add hot water if the broth reduces before the ingredients become tender.

title: Onion soup with Cuban bread and melted cheese
description: Slowly browned onion, broth, and cheese-topped toast finished in the oven.
steps: Cut the onion into strips and cook in the butter and oil over medium-low heat for thirty minutes, stirring until golden.
Add the garlic and flour and stir for two minutes; gradually pour in the stock and add the bay leaf and salt.
Simmer gently for twenty minutes. Toast the bread slices and heat the broiler.
Remove the bay leaf, divide the soup among ovenproof bowls, and place a slice of toast and cheese on top.
Broil for three to five minutes, until the cheese melts; serve with a warning that the bowls retain a great deal of heat.
tips: Maintain a gentle simmer and add hot water if the broth reduces before the ingredients become tender.

title: Beef and carrot noodle soup
description: Beef slowly tenderized in broth, with noodles added at the end.
steps: Put the diced beef in a pot with the water, half the onion, garlic, celery, and bay leaf; bring to a boil and skim off the foam.
Cook gently for ninety to one hundred twenty minutes, until the meat is tender; replenish the water if it reduces too much.
Strain the broth, remove the bay leaf, and return the broth to the pot with the meat, chopped carrot, and remaining chopped onion.
Cook for fifteen minutes and add the noodles and salt; cook for the time indicated on the package, usually five to eight minutes.
Add the lime juice when serving and distribute the meat and pasta evenly before pouring over the broth.
tips: Maintain a gentle simmer and add hot water if the broth reduces before the ingredients become tender.

title: Chicken rice soup with pumpkin
description: Chicken broth with rice and pumpkin, finished with parsley.
steps: Cook the chicken with the water, half the onion, and the garlic for forty minutes, skimming off foam and checking that it reaches 74 °C.
Remove the chicken, discard the skin and bones, and strain the broth. Return the meat and broth to the pot.
Add the rinsed rice, diced carrot, and remaining chopped onion; boil for ten minutes.
Add the pumpkin and salt and cook for twelve to fifteen more minutes, until the rice and vegetables are tender.
Scatter over the parsley and serve immediately, adding hot water if the rice has left too little broth.
tips: Maintain a gentle simmer and add hot water if the broth reduces before the ingredients become tender.

title: Fish soup with tomato and noodles
description: White fish in tomato broth with thin noodles and lime.
steps: Cut the fish into four-centimeter pieces and keep refrigerated. Chop the vegetables.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil, add the tomato, and cook for seven minutes.
Pour in the stock, season, and boil for ten minutes to blend the flavors.
Add the noodles and fish and cook for seven to nine minutes, until the pasta is tender and the fish reaches 63 °C.
Add the lime juice and parsley and serve without further boiling so the fish does not break apart.
tips: Maintain a gentle simmer and add hot water if the broth reduces before the ingredients become tender.

title: Lobster and boniato soup
description: Boniato sweet potato in tomato broth with lobster cooked at the end.
steps: Dice the boniato and cut the lobster into three-centimeter medallions; keep the lobster chilled.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil and add the tomato and oregano; cook for five minutes.
Pour in the stock, add the boniato and salt, and simmer gently for twenty minutes.
Add the lobster and cook for seven to nine minutes, until the center is white and opaque.
Add the lime juice and serve, portioning the medallions first and then the broth with boniato.
tips: Maintain a gentle simmer and add hot water if the broth reduces before the ingredients become tender.

title: Conch soup with starchy vegetables
description: Conch cooked until tender in a broth with malanga, potato, and pumpkin.
steps: Lightly tenderize the conch with a mallet and place in the pot with the water and bay leaf; simmer gently for two to three hours.
When a knife slides in without resistance, remove the conch, chop it into small pieces, and strain the broth. Add water to make two liters.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil with the tomato; add the broth, conch, diced malanga, and potato.
Cook for fifteen minutes and add the pumpkin and salt; cook for twenty more minutes, until all the starchy vegetables are completely tender.
Remove the bay leaf, add the lime juice, and serve with plenty of broth. The conch must be tender before adding the vegetables.
tips: Maintain a gentle simmer and add hot water if the broth reduces before the ingredients become tender.

title: Shrimp broth with corn
description: A broth made from shrimp shells and finished with the shrimp tails and corn.
steps: Peel the shrimp, remove the digestive tracts, and keep the tails chilled. Put the shells in a pot with the water and boil for fifteen minutes.
Pass the broth through a fine filter and discard the shells. Cut the corn into rounds and chop the vegetables.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil, add the tomato, and cook for five minutes.
Pour in the broth, add the corn and salt, and cook for fifteen minutes. Add the shrimp and finish for four to six minutes, until opaque.
Add the cilantro and lime juice and serve with a round of corn and shrimp in each bowl.
tips: Maintain a gentle simmer and add hot water if the broth reduces before the ingredients become tender.

title: Creamy crab soup with roasted pepper
description: Cooked crabmeat in a light soup made with milk and fish stock.
steps: Check the crabmeat for shell fragments and keep chilled. Chop the onion and garlic; blend the roasted pepper with the stock.
Melt the butter and soften the onion and garlic for five minutes; add the flour and cook for two minutes.
Gradually whisk in the milk, followed by the pepper stock. Simmer gently for ten minutes to cook the flour.
Add the crabmeat and salt and heat for five minutes, until the whole soup reaches 74 °C.
Serve with parsley and some whole pieces of crabmeat, without blending after adding the crab.
tips: Maintain a gentle simmer and add hot water if the broth reduces before the ingredients become tender.

title: Savory ripe plantain and pumpkin soup
description: Ripe plantain and pumpkin in a garlic and cumin soup, without sugar.
steps: Peel the plantains and cut into thick rounds; dice the pumpkin and chop the onion and garlic.
Sauté the onion in the oil, add the garlic and cumin, and stir for one minute.
Add the stock, plantain, pumpkin, and salt and simmer gently for twenty-five minutes.
Blend only one third of the soup off the heat and return it to the pot, keeping some pieces whole.
Add the lime juice, boil for two minutes, and serve; the sweet contrast comes from the vegetables, not added sugar.
tips: Maintain a gentle simmer and add hot water if the broth reduces before the ingredients become tender.

title: Vegetable and corn ajiaco
description: A vegetable version with cassava, malanga, boniato sweet potato, corn, and sofrito.
steps: Boil the cassava pieces in the water for thirty to forty minutes, until tender; drain, discard the water, and remove the central fibers.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil, add the tomato and cumin, and cook for four minutes.
Pour in the stock and add the malanga, peeled plantain, and corn pieces; cook for fifteen minutes.
Add the boniato, pumpkin, and salt and cook for twenty more minutes, until completely tender; add the cooked cassava.
Mash some of the pumpkin to thicken, boil for five minutes, and finish with lime juice.
tips: Maintain a gentle simmer and add hot water if the broth reduces before the ingredients become tender.

title: Salted dried beef broth with plantain and pumpkin
description: Tasajo beef desalted and cooked before adding starchy vegetables to its mild broth.
steps: Rinse the tasajo and desalt in cold water in the refrigerator for twenty-four hours, changing the water at least four times; follow its label.
Cook in fresh water for ninety to one hundred twenty minutes, until tender; taste a small cooked piece and change the water if it is still too salty.
Shred the meat and strain its broth; use two liters only if the saltiness is moderate, topping up with fresh water.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil with the tomato and cumin. Add the broth, tasajo, and peeled plantain and cook for fifteen minutes.
Add the pumpkin and cook for twenty more minutes. Serve without automatically adding salt.
tips: Maintain a gentle simmer and add hot water if the broth reduces before the ingredients become tender.

title: Egg and spinach soup with garlic
description: Spinach broth with fully set ribbons of egg.
steps: Wash and chop the spinach; beat the eggs in a cup and chop the onion and garlic.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil for five minutes; add the paprika and immediately pour in the stock.
Boil for ten minutes and add the spinach and salt. Cook for five minutes to soften the leaves.
Pour in the egg in a thin stream while stirring slowly and maintain a gentle simmer for three minutes, until completely set.
Add the lime juice and serve the broth with the egg ribbons evenly distributed, leaving no areas of liquid egg.
tips: Maintain a gentle simmer and add hot water if the broth reduces before the ingredients become tender.

title: Chayote and cilantro soup
description: Chayote, potato, and cilantro in a mild vegetable soup.
steps: Peel the chayotes, remove any hard centers, and dice; peel and cut up the potato.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for five minutes; add the chayote and potato and cook for two minutes.
Add the stock and salt and cook for twenty-five minutes, until both vegetables are easily pierced.
Blend a ladleful of soup with the washed cilantro and return it to the pot; boil for two minutes.
Add the lime juice and serve, keeping the remaining vegetable cubes whole.
tips: Maintain a gentle simmer and add hot water if the broth reduces before the ingredients become tender.

title: Cassava mash with roasted garlic
description: Sweet cassava mashed with roasted garlic and oil, with a rustic texture and no milk.
steps: Cut the top off the garlic head, coat with one tablespoon of oil, and wrap in foil; bake at 190 °C for forty minutes.
Peel the cassava completely, removing the bark and inner pink layer; cut into pieces and boil in the 2500 ml of water for thirty to forty minutes, until very tender.
Drain the cassava, discard all the cooking water, and remove the central fibers; do not taste raw or partly cooked pieces.
Squeeze out the roasted garlic pulp and mash with the hot cassava, remaining oil, and salt; gradually add the fresh hot water.
Add the lime juice, mix with a spoon, and serve; avoid using a blender so the mash does not become sticky.
tips: Use sweet cassava sold for food; use fresh water to thin the mash.

title: Cassava gratin with cheese
description: A dish of tender cassava covered in white sauce and golden cheese.
steps: Peel the cassava completely, cut into pieces, and boil in the water for thirty to forty minutes; drain, discard the water, and remove the central fibers.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the flour, and stir over medium heat for two minutes without browning.
Gradually whisk in the milk; cook for five minutes until thickened and season with salt and nutmeg.
Place the cassava in a baking dish, pour the sauce between the pieces, and scatter the cheese on top.
Bake at 200 °C for twenty minutes, until bubbling and golden; rest for five minutes before cutting.
tips: Serve freshly made to enjoy the texture of the starchy vegetables.

title: Sautéed cassava with bell peppers
description: Previously boiled cassava pieces browned with bell peppers in two colors.
steps: Remove all the cassava skin and cook in the water for thirty to forty minutes, until tender; discard the water and central fibers.
Let the pieces drain on a tray for ten minutes and cut into large cubes without breaking them apart.
Cut the onion and bell peppers into strips; sauté in two tablespoons of oil for eight minutes and remove from the skillet.
Add the remaining oil and brown the cassava in a single layer for eight to ten minutes, turning with a spatula.
Return the peppers, add the chopped garlic, cumin, and salt, and sauté for two more minutes before serving.
tips: Serve freshly made to enjoy the texture of the starchy vegetables.

title: Baked cassava with onions
description: Boiled cassava finished in the oven with plenty of onion and sour orange.
steps: Peel the cassava thoroughly, cut into pieces, and boil in the water for thirty to forty minutes; discard the liquid and remove the central fibers.
Cut the onion into half-moons and soften in two tablespoons of oil over medium heat for ten minutes.
Mash the garlic with the salt and mix with the sour orange juice, oregano, and remaining oil.
Arrange the cassava and onion in a wide baking dish, pour over the dressing, and bake at 210 °C for twenty minutes.
Turn the pieces carefully and bake for another ten minutes, until the edges are golden and the onion retains some moisture.
tips: Serve freshly made to enjoy the texture of the starchy vegetables.

title: Cassava and spinach bake
description: Layers of cassava mash and sautéed spinach, baked with white cheese until golden.
steps: Peel the cassava completely and boil in the water for thirty to forty minutes, until very soft; discard the water and central fibers.
Mash the hot cassava with the milk, butter, and half the salt to make a thick, spreadable mash.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for five minutes; add the washed spinach and cook for six minutes until its water evaporates; season with the remaining salt and black pepper.
Spread half the mash in a dish; cover with the spinach and half the crumbled cheese, then top with the remaining mash.
Scatter over the remaining cheese and bake at 200 °C for twenty-five minutes; let set for ten minutes before serving in portions.
tips: Serve freshly made to enjoy the texture of the starchy vegetables.

title: Roasted malanga with paprika
description: Boiled malanga pieces roasted with a coating of garlic and paprika.
steps: Peel the malanga and cut into pieces about four centimeters wide; rinse and cover with the water in a pot.
Boil for twenty-five to thirty minutes, until a knife easily pierces the center; drain and let the surface water evaporate for five minutes.
Mix the oil, paprika, mashed garlic, and salt in a large bowl; add the malanga and turn carefully.
Spread on a tray without crowding and bake at 220 °C for twenty minutes; turn the pieces and bake for ten more minutes.
Drizzle with lime juice when it comes out of the oven and serve with a dry, golden exterior and completely tender center.
tips: Serve freshly made to enjoy the texture of the starchy vegetables.

title: Malanga mash with mild garlic
description: Creamy malanga mashed with garlic simmered in milk and butter.
steps: Peel the malanga, cut into cubes, and boil in the water for twenty-five to thirty minutes, until it breaks apart when pressed.
While it boils, heat the milk with the peeled garlic over very low heat for fifteen minutes, without letting it boil over.
Drain the malanga well and pass through a food mill or mash while still hot with the butter.
Mash the cooked garlic and add it with the hot milk, salt, and white pepper; mix with a spoon.
Return the mash to the lowest heat for two minutes, stirring to heat evenly, and serve without processing in a blender.
tips: Serve freshly made to enjoy the texture of the starchy vegetables.

title: Malanga stewed with tomato
description: Diced malanga in a Cuban-style tomato and sweet pepper sauce.
steps: Peel and wash the malanga and cut into three-centimeter cubes; chop the onion, sweet pepper, and garlic.
Soften the onion and sweet pepper in the oil for seven minutes; add the garlic and cumin and stir for thirty seconds.
Add the tomato and cook for eight minutes until its raw smell disappears; add the water, bay leaf, and salt.
Add the malanga and cook with the pot partially covered for thirty to forty minutes, stirring gently to prevent sticking.
Check that the malanga is completely soft in the center; uncover for five minutes if the sauce needs reducing and remove the bay leaf.
tips: Serve freshly made to enjoy the texture of the starchy vegetables.

title: Malanga and leek gratin
description: Slices of cooked malanga and leek in a light milk and cheese sauce.
steps: Peel the malanga, cut into one-centimeter slices, and boil for twenty to twenty-five minutes; check that it is tender and drain.
Wash the leek between its layers, slice finely, and cook in the butter for eight minutes without browning.
Dissolve the cornstarch in the cold milk; pour over the leek, season with salt and nutmeg, and stir until boiling, then cook for two minutes to thicken.
Arrange the slices and sauce in layers in a baking dish and finish with the grated cheese.
Bake at 200 °C for twenty minutes until the top is golden; rest for five minutes and serve.
tips: Serve freshly made to enjoy the texture of the starchy vegetables.

title: Smashed and browned malanga
description: Malanga pieces with tender centers, browned in a skillet and topped with scallion.
steps: Peel the malanga and cut into four-centimeter cylinders; boil in the water for about thirty minutes, until completely tender.
Drain and let dry for ten minutes; flatten each cylinder with a spatula to a thickness of two centimeters.
Heat half the oil in a wide skillet and brown half the pieces for five minutes per side, without moving them constantly.
Repeat with the remaining oil and malanga; lower the heat at the end and add the chopped garlic to infuse for one minute.
Scatter the salt, black pepper, and chopped scallion on top; serve the pieces hot with crisp edges.
tips: Serve freshly made to enjoy the texture of the starchy vegetables.

title: Boniato mash with orange
description: Savory white boniato sweet potato mash with fresh orange and a touch of cumin.
steps: Peel the boniato sweet potatoes and cut into equal-sized pieces; place in a pot with the water.
Boil for twenty to twenty-five minutes, until easily pierced, and drain very well.
Heat the orange juice with the cumin in a small saucepan for two minutes, without reducing excessively.
Mash the hot boniato; gradually add the oil, salt, and juice until you reach the desired consistency.
Mix in the orange zest at the end and serve as a savory side, leaving small pieces if you prefer a more rustic texture.
tips: Serve freshly made to enjoy the texture of the starchy vegetables.

title: Baked boniato stuffed with beans
description: Whole roasted boniato sweet potatoes filled with black beans and bell pepper.
steps: Wash the boniato sweet potatoes, prick several times, and place on a tray; bake at 200 °C for fifty to sixty minutes, until very soft.
Chop the onion, bell pepper, and garlic; sauté in the oil for seven minutes, stir in the cumin, and add the tomato.
Cook the tomato for eight minutes and add the beans and salt; heat for five minutes, mashing one tablespoon of beans to bind the filling.
Split each boniato lengthwise without separating the base; gently loosen the flesh with a fork and spoon the beans inside.
Return to the oven for eight minutes and finish with chopped cilantro; serve one piece per portion.
tips: Serve freshly made to enjoy the texture of the starchy vegetables.

title: Boniato stewed with pumpkin
description: Boniato sweet potato and pumpkin cubes in a mild sofrito with oregano.
steps: Peel the boniato and cut into three-centimeter cubes; cut the pumpkin slightly larger so it holds its shape.
Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil for seven minutes; add the tomato and cook for five minutes.
Add the boniato, water, salt, and oregano; cover and simmer gently for twelve minutes.
Add the pumpkin and continue cooking for fifteen to twenty minutes, until both vegetables are tender.
Uncover and reduce the sauce for five minutes if needed; shake the pot by its handles to avoid breaking up the cubes.
tips: Serve freshly made to enjoy the texture of the starchy vegetables.

title: Fried boniato batons
description: Thinly cut boniato sweet potato fried twice to create a tender center.

ingredients.name: oil for frying
ingredients.note: amount needed for cooking; not all is consumed

steps: Peel the boniato sweet potatoes and cut into one-centimeter-thick batons; rinse briefly and dry completely with a cloth.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 150 °C; fry the batons in batches for six to eight minutes, until tender but only lightly colored.
Drain on a rack and rest for ten minutes while finishing the first frying of all the batches.
Raise the oil temperature to 180 °C and fry each batch again for two to three minutes, until colored and firm on the surface.
Drain, mix the salt and paprika, and sprinkle over immediately; serve uncovered to preserve the texture.
tips: Do not fill the pot more than halfway with oil or add wet batons.

title: Boniato gratin with cheese
description: Thin boniato sweet potato slices baked in milk with cheese and oregano.
steps: Peel the boniato and cut into three-millimeter slices; grease a baking dish with half the butter.
Heat the milk with the chopped garlic, oregano, salt, and black pepper until steaming; remove from the heat.
Layer the boniato with half the cheese between the layers; pour in the milk and dot the remaining butter on top.
Cover the dish and bake at 190 °C for forty minutes; uncover, add the remaining cheese, and bake for twenty more minutes.
Insert a knife all the way to the bottom to check that every layer is soft; rest for ten minutes before serving.
tips: Serve freshly made to enjoy the texture of the starchy vegetables.

title: Boiled yam with lime mojo
description: Tender yam dressed with a hot garlic, onion, and lime mojo.
steps: Peel and wash the yam and cut into four-centimeter pieces; immediately place in the pot of water.
Boil for thirty to forty minutes, until completely tender, and drain without mashing.
Cut the onion into strips and cook in the oil for six minutes; add the mashed garlic and stir over low heat for one minute.
Remove the skillet from the heat and carefully add the lime juice, salt, and oregano, as the oil may splatter.
Place the hot yam in a dish and spoon over the mojo and onion; serve immediately.
tips: Check the center of the starchy vegetable with a knife before finishing cooking.

title: Yam mash with coconut
description: Yam mashed with coconut milk and scallion, intended as a savory side dish.
steps: Peel and cube the yam; boil in the water for thirty to forty minutes, until very tender.
Heat the oil over low heat and cook the chopped garlic for one minute without browning; add the coconut milk and heat for two minutes.
Drain the yam and mash by hand while hot; avoid blending so it does not become elastic.
Gradually add the hot coconut milk with the salt and black pepper until you have a thick, smooth mash.
Add the finely sliced scallion, return to the lowest heat for one minute, and serve in a warm dish.
tips: Check the center of the starchy vegetable with a knife before finishing cooking.

title: Sautéed yam with red onion
description: Boiled yam cubes sautéed with onion, cumin, and cilantro.
steps: Peel the yam and cut into three-centimeter cubes; boil in the water for twenty-five to thirty-five minutes, until soft but intact.
Drain and let dry on a tray for ten minutes; cut the onion into thin wedges.
Heat two tablespoons of oil and sauté the onion over medium heat for eight minutes; transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and brown the yam cubes for eight minutes; add the cumin, salt, and onion and stir for two minutes.
Turn off the heat, drizzle with lime juice, and add the chopped cilantro; turn with a wide spatula to keep the cubes intact.
tips: Check the center of the starchy vegetable with a knife before finishing cooking.

title: Yam and cabbage stew
description: Yam and cabbage slowly cooked with tomato, bay leaf, and bell pepper.
steps: Peel the yam and cut into three-centimeter cubes; remove the cabbage core and cut its leaves into wide strips.
Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil for eight minutes; add the tomato and cook for seven minutes.
Add the yam, water, bay leaf, and salt; cover and simmer gently for fifteen minutes.
Add the cabbage, press it into the broth, and cook for twenty to twenty-five more minutes, until the yam is easily pierced.
Remove the bay leaf and simmer uncovered for five minutes if there is too much liquid; serve as a side dish with sauce.
tips: Check the center of the starchy vegetable with a knife before finishing cooking.

title: Malanga and green plantain fufú
description: A mixed plantain and malanga mash with fried garlic and onion.
steps: Peel and cube the malanga; peel the plantains and cut into three-centimeter rounds.
Boil the malanga in the water for ten minutes; add the plantain and continue for twenty to twenty-five minutes, until both are very tender.
Sauté the chopped onion in the oil for eight minutes; add the mashed garlic and cook for one more minute.
Reserve 150 ml of cooking water, drain the vegetables, and mash them while hot with the salt and some of that water until moist.
Mix the sofrito and sour orange juice into the mash; heat over low heat for two minutes, stirring, and serve.
tips: Check the center of the starchy vegetable with a knife before finishing cooking.

title: Roasted green plantain with garlic
description: Green plantain wedges boiled first and then browned in the oven.
steps: Trim the ends, make a lengthwise cut through each skin, and peel the plantains; divide each into four long wedges.
Boil the wedges in the water for fifteen minutes, until they begin to soften without breaking; drain and let dry for five minutes.
Mix the oil, mashed garlic, salt, and paprika; coat the wedges with this seasoning and arrange on a tray.
Bake at 220 °C for fifteen minutes, turn, and continue for ten to fifteen more minutes, until tender and golden.
Add the lime juice when they come out of the oven and serve hot; green plantain firms up as it cools.
tips: Check the center of the starchy vegetable with a knife before finishing cooking.

title: Baked ripe plantains stuffed with cheese
description: Very ripe plantains roasted whole and split to hold melted cheese.
steps: Peel the plantains without breaking them and arrange in a baking dish; spread with the softened butter.
Bake at 200 °C for twenty minutes and turn the pieces; continue for another ten minutes, until the flesh yields when pressed.
Make a lengthwise opening in each plantain without cutting through the base and gently separate the sides with two spoons.
Cut the cheese into strips and divide among the six openings; sprinkle with salt and oregano.
Bake for eight to ten more minutes until the cheese melts; serve one piece per portion while hot.
tips: Check the center of the starchy vegetable with a knife before finishing cooking.

title: Partially ripe plantain stewed in tomato
description: Plantain at an intermediate stage of ripeness cooked in a tomato and bell pepper sauce.

ingredients.name: partially ripe plantains
ingredients.note: yellow and green skin, firm flesh

steps: Peel the plantains and cut into two-centimeter rounds; chop the onion, bell pepper, and garlic.
Sauté the onion and bell pepper in the oil for seven minutes; add the garlic and cumin and stir for one minute.
Add the tomato and cook for eight minutes; add the water and salt and bring to a boil.
Add the plantain slices and cook over low heat for twenty to twenty-five minutes, partially covered and without excessive stirring.
Check that the slices are tender and lightly coated with sauce; finish with cilantro and serve.
tips: Check the center of the starchy vegetable with a knife before finishing cooking.

title: Ripe plantain and black bean bake
description: Layers of roasted plantain and seasoned black beans with a cheese topping.
steps: Peel the plantains, cut lengthwise into one-centimeter slices, and brush with one tablespoon of oil; bake at 210 °C for twenty minutes, turning halfway through.
Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the remaining oil for eight minutes; add the tomato, cumin, and salt and cook for seven minutes.
Add the beans, mash one third with a fork, and cook for five minutes to make a thick filling.
Alternate two layers of plantain with one layer of beans in a medium dish; finish with the grated cheese.
Bake at 200 °C for twenty minutes, until the cheese is golden and the center is thoroughly hot; rest for ten minutes before cutting.
tips: Check the center of the starchy vegetable with a knife before finishing cooking.

title: Baked plantain chatinos
description: Green plantain discs softened by steaming, flattened, and toasted in the oven.
steps: Peel the plantains and cut into three-centimeter cylinders; put the water in a pot with a steamer basket that does not touch the liquid.
Steam the cylinders, covered, for twenty to twenty-five minutes, until they can be flattened easily.
Flatten each cylinder between two flat surfaces to form a one-centimeter-thick disc; brush both sides with three tablespoons of oil.
Bake on a tray at 230 °C for twelve minutes per side, until golden and dry around the edges.
Mash the garlic with the salt and mix with the lime juice and remaining oil; spoon a small amount of mojo over the hot discs.
tips: This steamed and baked version has a different texture from twice-fried tostones.

title: Cuban-style stewed potatoes
description: Tender potatoes in tomato sauce with olives, bell pepper, and bay leaf.
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut into three-centimeter pieces; chop the onion and bell pepper and slice the garlic.
Heat the oil and sauté the onion and bell pepper for eight minutes; add the garlic and cumin and cook for thirty seconds.
Add the tomato and cook for six minutes before adding the potatoes, water, bay leaf, and salt.
Cover partially and simmer for twenty-five to thirty minutes, until the potatoes are tender; add the olives during the last five minutes.
Remove the bay leaf and mash two potato pieces into the sauce to thicken it; shake the pot gently and serve.
tips: Check the center of the starchy vegetable with a knife before finishing cooking.

title: Smashed potatoes with garlic
description: Small potatoes boiled in their skins and oven-roasted with garlic and parsley.
steps: Wash and scrub the potatoes; place them whole in the water and boil for twenty to twenty-five minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Drain and let dry for five minutes; place the potatoes on a tray and flatten with the bottom of a glass to a thickness of two centimeters.
Drizzle with three tablespoons of oil and sprinkle with salt and black pepper; bake at 220 °C for twenty-five minutes.
Mix the chopped garlic with the remaining oil, distribute over the potatoes, and return to the oven for five minutes without letting the garlic burn.
Add the chopped parsley when removing the tray and serve with golden skins and soft centers.
tips: Check the center of the starchy vegetable with a knife before finishing cooking.

title: Potato and onion gratin
description: Thinly sliced potatoes with golden onions and a milk and cheese sauce.
steps: Cut the onion into strips and cook in half the butter over medium-low heat for fifteen minutes, until golden.
In another saucepan, melt the remaining butter, add the flour, and stir for two minutes; gradually add the milk, salt, and nutmeg and cook for five minutes.
Peel the potatoes and cut into three-millimeter slices; layer in a dish with the onion and half the cheese between the layers.
Cover with the sauce, cover the dish, and bake at 190 °C for forty minutes; uncover and scatter over the remaining cheese.
Bake for twenty to twenty-five more minutes, until the layers are tender and the top is golden; rest for ten minutes before serving.
tips: Check the center of the starchy vegetable with a knife before finishing cooking.

title: Sautéed potatoes with bell pepper and oregano
description: Boiled potato cubes browned in a skillet with red bell peppers.
steps: Peel the potatoes, cut into two-centimeter cubes, and boil for ten to twelve minutes, until just tender; drain and dry for five minutes.
Cut the onion and bell pepper into squares; sauté in two tablespoons of oil for eight minutes and set aside.
Heat the remaining oil and brown the potatoes in a large skillet for ten to twelve minutes, turning only once a crust forms.
Add the chopped garlic, oregano, salt, and reserved vegetables; cook for two minutes, turning with a spatula.
Drizzle the vinegar around the edge of the skillet, let evaporate for thirty seconds, and serve immediately.
tips: Check the center of the starchy vegetable with a knife before finishing cooking.

title: Roasted pumpkin with cumin
description: Pumpkin wedges browned in the oven with cumin and toasted seeds.
steps: Cut the pumpkin into two-centimeter wedges and pat dry; preheat the oven to 210 °C.
Mix the oil, cumin, mashed garlic, and salt; coat the wedges and space them apart on a tray.
Bake for twenty minutes, turn carefully, and continue for fifteen to twenty minutes, until tender and golden.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry skillet for three minutes, stirring to keep them from burning.
Drizzle the wedges with lime juice when serving and scatter the toasted seeds on top.
tips: Check the center of the starchy vegetable with a knife before finishing cooking.

title: Pumpkin and boniato mash
description: A savory mash of two starchy vegetables, with roasted pumpkin to concentrate its flavor.
steps: Cut the pumpkin into three-centimeter cubes, mix with one tablespoon of oil, and bake at 210 °C for thirty to thirty-five minutes, until tender.
Peel the boniato, cut into pieces, and boil in the water for twenty to twenty-five minutes; drain well.
Heat the remaining oil with the chopped garlic over low heat for one minute; remove as soon as it is fragrant.
Mash the hot boniato and pumpkin together, adding the garlic oil, salt, black pepper, and sour orange juice.
Heat the mash gently for three minutes, stirring to release excess moisture if necessary, and serve.
tips: Cut the vegetables into even pieces so they cook at the same rate.

title: Pumpkin stuffed with chickpeas
description: Roasted pumpkin halves with chickpeas, tomato, and bell pepper.
steps: Cut the pumpkins in half and remove the seeds; brush the flesh with one tablespoon of oil and place cut-side down on a tray.
Bake at 200 °C for forty to fifty minutes, until the flesh is tender but the halves hold their shape.
Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the remaining oil for eight minutes; add the diced tomato, cumin, and salt and cook for ten minutes.
Add the chickpeas and half the parsley, cook for five minutes, and divide the filling among the pumpkin halves.
Bake the filled halves for ten minutes and sprinkle with the remaining parsley; serve one half per portion.
tips: Cut the vegetables into even pieces so they cook at the same rate.

title: Eggplants stuffed with vegetables
description: Roasted eggplants filled with their own flesh, zucchini, and corn, with a cheese topping.
steps: Halve the eggplants lengthwise and score the flesh with shallow cuts; brush with one tablespoon of oil and roast at 200 °C for thirty minutes.
Scoop out some flesh with a spoon, leaving a one-centimeter border to support the skins; chop the flesh.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the remaining oil for five minutes; add the diced zucchini and cook for seven minutes.
Add the tomato, eggplant flesh, corn, salt, and oregano; cook for ten minutes until the filling has little free liquid.
Fill the six halves, cover with cheese, and bake for fifteen minutes, until the top is golden.
tips: Cut the vegetables into even pieces so they cook at the same rate.

title: Baked eggplant with tomato and cheese
description: Roasted eggplant slices layered with tomato sauce and white cheese.
steps: Cut the eggplant into one-centimeter slices and brush with three tablespoons of oil; roast at 220 °C for twenty minutes, turning halfway through.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the remaining oil for five minutes; add the tomato, oregano, salt, and black pepper.
Simmer the sauce for fifteen minutes, until thick enough to coat a spoon.
In a baking dish, alternate eggplant slices, sauce, and crumbled cheese; finish with sauce and some cheese.
Bake at 200 °C for twenty minutes and rest for five minutes before serving the layers with a spatula.
tips: Cut the vegetables into even pieces so they cook at the same rate.

title: Sautéed eggplant with sweet pepper
description: Browned eggplant cubes with sweet pepper and a finishing splash of vinegar.
steps: Cut the eggplant into two-centimeter cubes; seed the sweet peppers and cut into strips along with the onion.
Heat three tablespoons of oil in a wide skillet and brown the eggplant in batches for eight to ten minutes; set aside.
Add the remaining oil and sauté the onion and sweet pepper for six minutes; add the chopped garlic and cumin for thirty seconds.
Return the eggplant and add the water and salt; cover and cook for eight minutes so the centers of the cubes become soft.
Uncover, add the vinegar, and sauté for two minutes until the liquid disappears; serve hot.
tips: Cut the vegetables into even pieces so they cook at the same rate.

title: Chayote gratin with cheese
description: Tender chayote cubes in a mild mustard white sauce with cheese.
steps: Peel the chayotes, remove the centers if hard, and dice the flesh; boil in the water for fifteen to twenty minutes and drain.
Melt the butter and cook the flour for two minutes; gradually add the milk, whisking constantly.
Simmer the sauce gently for five minutes and add the mustard, salt, black pepper, and half the cheese.
Mix the well-drained chayote with the sauce in a baking dish; cover with the remaining cheese.
Bake at 210 °C for twenty minutes until bubbling and golden; rest for five minutes before serving.
tips: Cut the vegetables into even pieces so they cook at the same rate.

title: Chayote stewed with tomato and olives
description: Chayote wedges in Cuban-style sauce with green olives.
steps: Peel the chayotes and cut into two-centimeter wedges, removing the hard centers; chop the onion, garlic, and bell pepper.
Sauté the onion and bell pepper in the oil for seven minutes; add the garlic and cook for one minute.
Add the tomato and oregano and reduce for eight minutes; add the chayote, water, and salt.
Cover partially and cook for twenty-five to thirty minutes, until the wedges are tender and the sauce has reduced somewhat.
Add the halved olives and simmer for three more minutes; serve the chayote covered in sauce.
tips: Cut the vegetables into even pieces so they cook at the same rate.

title: Sautéed chayote with corn and scallion
description: Thin chayote slices sautéed with corn and finished with lime.
steps: Peel the chayote, remove any hard center, and cut into half-centimeter slices; separate the white and green parts of the scallion.
Heat the oil and sauté the chopped scallion whites and garlic for one minute.
Add the chayote and salt, sauté for four minutes, and add the water; cover and cook for eight to ten minutes, until tender but firm.
Uncover, add the corn, and cook over high heat for four minutes to evaporate the liquid and brown some edges.
Turn off the heat and add the lime juice, black pepper, and scallion greens; mix and serve.
tips: Cut the vegetables into even pieces so they cook at the same rate.

title: Roasted okra with paprika
description: Okra split lengthwise and roasted with paprika and garlic.
steps: Wash the okra and dry completely; trim only the hard end of each stem and split each pod lengthwise.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C and place a tray inside to heat up.
Mix the okra with the oil, paprika, garlic powder, and salt; spread in a single layer on the hot tray.
Bake for fifteen minutes, turn with a spatula, and continue for ten to fifteen minutes, until tender and lightly toasted.
Drizzle with lime juice just before bringing to the table; serve uncovered so the edges do not soften.
tips: Cut the vegetables into even pieces so they cook at the same rate.

title: Okra with chickpeas and sweet pepper
description: Fresh okra stewed with a small amount of chickpeas and tomato.
steps: Wash and dry the okra; trim the stems without opening the pods and leave small pods whole.
Sauté the chopped onion and sweet pepper in the oil for seven minutes; add the garlic and cumin and stir for thirty seconds.
Add the tomato, salt, and vinegar and cook for eight minutes to make the sauce.
Add the okra, chickpeas, and water; cover and cook over low heat for twenty minutes, shaking the pot instead of stirring.
Check that the okra is tender and cook for up to five more minutes if needed; serve with the thickened sauce.
tips: Cut the vegetables into even pieces so they cook at the same rate.

title: Green beans with coconut
description: Tender green beans in a lightly reduced coconut milk and garlic sauce.
steps: Wash the green beans, trim the ends, and remove any strings; cut into five-centimeter lengths.
Soften the chopped onion in the oil for five minutes; add the chopped garlic and stir for thirty seconds.
Add the green beans, water, and salt; cover and cook for eight minutes to start softening them.
Pour in the coconut milk and cook uncovered for ten to fifteen minutes, until the beans are tender and the sauce has reduced slightly.
Add the lime juice and zest off the heat, mix, and serve the green beans coated in their sauce.
tips: Cut the vegetables into even pieces so they cook at the same rate.

title: Cabbage stewed with carrot and caraway
description: Cabbage slowly cooked with carrot, tomato, and a touch of caraway.
steps: Remove the cabbage core and cut the leaves into strips; peel the carrot and cut into thin half-moons.
Sauté the sliced onion in the oil for seven minutes; add the carrot and caraway and cook for three minutes.
Add the tomato and cook for five minutes; add the cabbage in two batches, mixing so it reduces in volume.
Add the water and salt, cover, and cook over low heat for twenty to twenty-five minutes, until the cabbage is tender.
Add the vinegar and cook uncovered for three minutes; serve with only a little liquid at the bottom of the dish.
tips: Cut the vegetables into even pieces so they cook at the same rate.

title: Roasted carrots with lime
description: Thick carrot batons roasted with cumin and finished with parsley.
steps: Peel the carrots and halve or quarter lengthwise according to their thickness.
Mix with the oil, mashed garlic, cumin, and salt; spread on a tray with space between the pieces.
Bake at 210 °C for twenty minutes and turn the pieces with tongs.
Continue for fifteen to twenty minutes, until a knife pierces the thickest part and the edges are golden.
Drizzle with lime juice and add the chopped parsley when removing from the oven; serve the carrots hot.
tips: Cut the vegetables into even pieces so they cook at the same rate.

title: Cauliflower with sour orange mojo
description: Steamed cauliflower browned and dressed with hot garlic mojo.
steps: Divide the cauliflower into medium florets; put the water below a steamer basket without letting it touch the vegetables.
Steam the cauliflower for eight to ten minutes, until tender but still firm; let dry for two minutes.
Heat two tablespoons of oil in a wide skillet and brown the florets in batches for six minutes, turning once.
In a small skillet, heat the remaining oil with the chopped garlic for one minute; remove from the heat and carefully add the sour orange juice, oregano, and salt.
Pour the mojo over the hot cauliflower and finish with chopped parsley; serve without further cooking.
tips: Cut the vegetables into even pieces so they cook at the same rate.

title: Corn on the cob with garlic butter
description: Fresh corn boiled and seared in a skillet with garlic butter and lime.
steps: Remove the husks and silk from the ears of corn and rinse; halve them if they do not fit in the pot.
Bring the water to a boil, add the corn, and cook for twelve to twenty minutes according to its tenderness; check that the kernels are easy to chew and drain.
Mix the softened butter, mashed garlic, paprika, and salt; spread half the mixture over the corn.
Brown the corn in a hot ridged skillet for six to eight minutes, turning to mark several sides.
Add the remaining butter, lime juice, and chopped cilantro when serving; offer one ear per portion.
tips: Cut the vegetables into even pieces so they cook at the same rate.

title: White fish croquettes
description: Béchamel croquettes with poached fish and parsley, chilled twice.
steps: Heat the milk and poach the fish for five to eight minutes, until it reaches 63 °C; remove, flake, and reserve the strained milk.
Sauté the chopped onion in the butter for five minutes; add the 85 g of flour and stir for two minutes. Gradually add the milk and cook for eight minutes until thickened.
Add the fish, parsley, salt, and black pepper and cook for two more minutes; spread the mixture in a shallow dish and refrigerate for two hours, until firm.
Shape twenty-four small croquettes; coat in the 50 g of flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs, and refrigerate for thirty minutes.
Fry in batches at 175 °C for about four minutes, until golden and the center reaches 74 °C; drain and serve four per portion.
tips: Fry in small batches and drain on a rack to keep the coating crisp.

title: Salt cod and potato croquettes
description: Bites of potato and desalted salt cod with garlic and parsley, without béchamel.

ingredients.name: salt cod, already desalted
ingredients.note: ready to cook; prior desalting is not included

steps: Peel and cut up the potatoes; boil in 1500 ml of water for twenty minutes until tender, drain, and mash without adding liquid.
Heat the remaining 700 ml of water and cook the cod for five to eight minutes, until it flakes and reaches 63 °C; drain and remove the skin and bones.
Mix the potato, flaked cod, chopped garlic and parsley, black pepper, and dough egg; refrigerate in a shallow dish for one hour.
