Shape twenty-four pieces; coat with flour, the two beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs, and refrigerate for twenty minutes.
Fry in batches at 175 °C for three to four minutes, until golden and the center reaches 74 °C; drain before serving.
tips: The salt cod must already be desalted before starting; taste a cooked flake before deciding whether it needs salt.

title: Black bean croquettes
description: Vegetable croquettes made with black beans, potato, and cumin, with a thin cornmeal coating.
steps: Dice the potato and boil in the water for fifteen to twenty minutes; drain and mash. Dry the beans well with paper towels to remove surface liquid.
Sauté the finely chopped onion and garlic in one tablespoon of oil for five minutes; add the cumin and remove from the heat.
Mash the beans with a fork, leaving small pieces; mix with the potato, sofrito, breadcrumbs, and salt and refrigerate for one hour.
Shape eighteen short croquettes and coat in fine cornmeal, pressing to help the coating adhere.
Fry at 175 °C for three to four minutes per batch, until firm and hot, reaching 74 °C in the center; serve three per portion.
tips: Fry in small batches and drain on a rack to keep the coating crisp.

title: Rice and cheese croquettes
description: Round cooked-rice croquettes with melting cheese in the center.
steps: Mix the cold rice with the grated cheese, dough egg, chopped parsley, and salt; mash some of the grains to bind the mixture.
Divide into eighteen portions and enclose a cheese cube in each, pressing firmly with lightly dampened hands.
Coat the balls in flour, the two beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs, covering the seams completely.
Refrigerate on a tray for thirty minutes; meanwhile, heat the oil in a deep pot to 175 °C.
Fry in batches for four to five minutes, until golden and the center reaches 74 °C; drain and serve three per person.
tips: Fry in small batches and drain on a rack to keep the coating crisp.

title: Spinach croquettes
description: Thick béchamel with well-drained spinach and a touch of nutmeg.
steps: Wash the spinach and cook in the water clinging to its leaves for five minutes; let cool slightly, squeeze very well, and chop finely.
Sauté the chopped onion in the butter for five minutes; add the 80 g of flour and stir for two minutes. Gradually add the milk and cook for eight minutes.
Add the spinach, cheese, salt, and nutmeg; cook for two minutes until the mixture pulls away from the pot, then spread out and refrigerate for two hours.
Shape twenty-four croquettes, coat in the flour for coating, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs, and refrigerate for thirty minutes.
Fry in batches at 175 °C for four minutes, checking that the center reaches 74 °C; drain and serve hot.
tips: Fry in small batches and drain on a rack to keep the coating crisp.

title: Boniato and ham croquettes
description: Mashed white boniato sweet potato with ham and scallion inside a crisp coating.
steps: Peel and cut up the boniato; boil in the water for twenty to twenty-five minutes, drain, and mash. Spread in a dish and refrigerate for twenty minutes to cool.
Finely chop the ham and scallion; mix with the boniato, dough egg, 40 g of flour, salt, and black pepper.
Refrigerate for forty more minutes to firm up the mixture and shape eighteen evenly sized oblong croquettes.
Coat in the remaining flour, the two beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs; gently press the crumbs to seal the surface.
Fry at 175 °C for four minutes per batch, until golden and the center reaches 74 °C; drain and serve three per portion.
tips: Fry in small batches and drain on a rack to keep the coating crisp.

title: Savory pumpkin fritters
description: Small roasted pumpkin fritters with garlic, scallion, and cumin.
steps: Dice the pumpkin, mix with one tablespoon of oil, and roast at 210 °C for thirty to thirty-five minutes, until tender and fairly dry.
Mash and let cool slightly for ten minutes; mix with the egg, mashed garlic, scallion, salt, and cumin.
Add the flour and baking powder; stir just until you have a thick batter that stays on the spoon.
Heat the oil to 170 °C and drop in small spoonfuls; flatten slightly and fry for four to five minutes, turning halfway through.
Open the first fritter to check that the center is set with no raw batter; adjust the size if needed and finish the batches.
tips: Fry in small batches and drain on a rack to keep the coating crisp.

title: Corn and shrimp fritters
description: Ground fresh corn and chopped raw shrimp in small garlic-seasoned fritters.
steps: Pulse the corn, leaving some kernels whole; cut the shrimp into half-centimeter pieces.
Beat the eggs and mix with the corn, mashed garlic, chopped scallion, and salt; add the flour and baking powder.
Add the shrimp and mix; keep the batter refrigerated until the oil reaches 170 °C.
Fry small spoonfuls, one centimeter thick, for four to five minutes, turning to brown both sides.
Check that the batter is set and the shrimp are completely opaque and firm; drain the batches and serve hot.
tips: Fry in small batches and drain on a rack to keep the coating crisp.

title: Cooked cassava fritters with garlic
description: Sweet cassava boiled and mashed with garlic to form small savory patties.
steps: Peel the cassava completely, cut into pieces, and boil in the water for thirty to forty minutes, until tender; discard all the water and remove the central fibers.
Mash the hot cassava and spread in a dish to cool slightly for ten minutes; add the mashed garlic, chopped parsley, and salt.
Add the egg and flour and knead gently; divide into eighteen portions and flatten to one centimeter thick.
Heat the oil to 175 °C and fry the patties in batches for four minutes, turning once, until golden on both sides.
Check that the centers are firm with no raw egg; drain on a rack and serve three per portion.
tips: Fry in small batches and drain on a rack to keep the coating crisp.

title: Green plantain and cheese fritters
description: Finely grated green plantain with white cheese, fried in small patties.
steps: Peel the plantains and grate on the fine side of a grater; grate the onion as well and crumble the cheese.
Mix the plantain, onion, cheese, mashed garlic, egg, flour, and salt into a compact mixture.
Heat the oil to 170 °C; take spoonfuls of the mixture and flatten to no more than one centimeter thick.
Fry the patties for five to six minutes, turning halfway through, so the plantain cooks fully without burning the outside.
Open the first one to confirm that the center is tender and set; drain the batches and serve immediately.
tips: Fry in small batches and drain on a rack to keep the coating crisp.

title: Malanga and crab fritters
description: Grated malanga with cooked crabmeat, garlic, and cilantro.
steps: Grate the malanga on the finest side of the grater; flake the crabmeat and check that no hard fragments remain.
Mix the malanga, crabmeat, egg, flour, mashed garlic, chopped cilantro, salt, and black pepper; keep chilled while the oil heats.
Heat the oil to 170 °C and add small spoonfuls of the mixture, flattened to one centimeter thick.
Fry for five to six minutes, turning to brown evenly; the center must reach 74 °C and the malanga must be completely cooked, with no hard or raw areas.
Drain on a rack and repeat without overcrowding the skillet; serve hot to keep the edges crisp.
tips: Fry in small batches and drain on a rack to keep the coating crisp.

title: Savory yam fritters
description: Boiled yam mixed with egg and garlic, fried into light bites.
steps: Peel and cube the yam and boil in the water for thirty to forty minutes, until very tender; drain and mash.
Spread out the mash and let cool slightly for ten minutes; mix with the beaten eggs, mashed garlic, chopped parsley, and salt.
Sift the flour and baking powder over the mash and mix until combined, without beating excessively.
Heat the oil to 170 °C and fry tablespoon-sized portions for five minutes, turning so they cook on all sides.
Open the first piece to check that the interior is set with no wet raw batter; drain and continue with the rest.
tips: Fry in small batches and drain on a rack to keep the coating crisp.

title: Cassava balls stuffed with cheese
description: Cooked cassava dough enclosing small cubes of melting cheese.
steps: Peel the cassava completely and boil in the water for thirty to forty minutes; once very tender, discard the water and remove all the central fibers.
Mash the hot cassava with the butter and salt; let cool slightly for ten minutes before adding the egg and cornstarch.
Divide the dough into twenty-four portions; flatten each, insert a cheese cube, and seal without cracks to form a ball.
Refrigerate for thirty minutes and heat the oil to 175 °C; fry the balls in batches for four to five minutes.
When golden and the cheese is hot, drain on a rack; rest for two minutes before eating to avoid an excessively hot filling.
tips: Fry in small batches and drain on a rack to keep the coating crisp.

title: Ripe plantain balls with picadillo
description: Mashed ripe plantain wrapped around beef picadillo with olives.
steps: Peel the plantains and cut into pieces; boil in the water for twelve to fifteen minutes, drain, and mash. Spread the mash in a dish and refrigerate for thirty minutes.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in one tablespoon of oil for five minutes; add the beef and cumin and cook for six minutes, breaking it up.
Add the tomato, olives, and half the salt; cook for eight minutes until the filling is dry and the beef reaches 71 °C. Spread out and refrigerate for thirty minutes.
Mix the cold mash with the egg, flour, and remaining salt; divide into eighteen portions, distribute all the picadillo among them, and close each ball, sealing well.
Fry at 170 °C for four to five minutes per batch, until golden and the center reaches 74 °C; drain and serve three per portion.
tips: The mash and filling can chill at the same time; the picadillo must be dry enough for the balls to seal.

title: Potato balls stuffed with chicken and olives
description: Breaded mashed potato balls filled with cooked chicken and sofrito.

ingredients.name: shredded cooked chicken
ingredients.note: Already cooked before starting; keep refrigerated until needed.

steps: Peel the potatoes, cut into pieces, and boil in the water for twenty to twenty-five minutes; drain, mash with half the salt, spread out, and refrigerate for thirty minutes.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in one tablespoon of oil for six minutes; add the tomato, olives, chicken, and remaining salt.
Cook the filling for eight minutes, until the liquid reduces and it reaches 74 °C; refrigerate in a shallow container for thirty minutes.
Mix the cold mash with 30 g of flour; divide into twelve portions, flatten in your hand, and distribute all the filling among them before closing the balls.
Coat the balls in the remaining 60 g of flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs; refrigerate for twenty minutes.
Fry at 170 °C for five to six minutes per batch, until golden and the center reaches 74 °C; drain and serve two per portion.
tips: Chill the mash and filling at the same time; sealing the balls with cold chicken helps prevent them from opening during frying.

title: Tostones stuffed with shrimp
description: Twice-fried green plantain cups filled with shrimp in sofrito.
steps: Peel the plantains and cut each into four thick cylinders; fry at 150 °C for eight to ten minutes, until softened without much browning.
Drain and, while hot, press the center of each cylinder with a small glass inside a sturdy mold to form a cup; rest for five minutes.
Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic in one tablespoon of oil for six minutes; add the tomato and half the salt and reduce for seven minutes.
Cut the shrimp into two or three pieces, add to the sauce, and cook for three to five minutes, until firm and opaque; finish with lime juice.
Fry the cups at 180 °C for two to three minutes, drain, and season with the remaining salt; divide the hot filling among them and serve four per portion.
tips: Fill just before serving so the sauce does not soften the plantain.

title: Plantain cups with black beans
description: Crisp green plantain with mashed beans and crumbled white cheese.
steps: Peel and divide each plantain into four cylinders; fry at 150 °C for eight to ten minutes, until softened, and drain.
Make a hollow in each hot cylinder by pressing with a small glass inside a sturdy mold; rest for five minutes.
Sauté the onion and garlic in one tablespoon of oil for five minutes; add the beans, water, cumin, and half the salt.
Mash the beans and cook for eight minutes, until thick; keep warm while frying the cups at 180 °C for two to three minutes.
Drain, add the remaining salt, and fill with beans; scatter over the cheese and cilantro and serve four cups per portion.
tips: The filling should be thick; let any extra water evaporate before spooning it into the cups.

title: Chicken tamales with sofrito
description: Fresh corn parcels with cooked chicken, wrapped in husks and steamed.

ingredients.name: shredded cooked chicken
ingredients.note: Already cooked before starting; keep refrigerated until needed.

ingredients.name: water for soaking the husks and steaming

steps: Soak the husks in 2000 ml of hot water for twenty minutes; wash and drain. Blend the corn with the stock into a thick paste with a little texture.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in 30 ml of oil for eight minutes; add the tomato, chicken, and cumin and cook for eight minutes, until it reaches 74 °C and the sauce reduces.
Mix the ground corn with the cornmeal, remaining oil, and salt; fold in the chicken sofrito until evenly distributed through the dough.
Make twelve parcels, overlapping husks if they are small: add a portion of dough, close the sides, and fold the ends; tie with strips from the remaining husks.
Place the remaining 2000 ml of water below a steamer basket without touching the parcels; cook covered for seventy-five to ninety minutes, replenishing with hot water if the level drops.
Check that the dough is firm, releases from the husk, and reaches 74 °C in the center; rest for ten minutes and serve two tamales per portion.
tips: The water in the steamer must stay below the husks; add hot water without wetting the parcels.

title: Pumpkin and cheese tamales
description: Corn dough with roasted pumpkin and white cheese cubes, wrapped in husks.

ingredients.name: water for the husks and steaming

steps: Dice the pumpkin and roast at 210 °C for thirty minutes, until tender; soak the husks in 2000 ml of hot water for twenty minutes and drain.
Blend the corn with the milk and pumpkin; cook the finely chopped onion in the butter for five minutes and add to the paste.
Add the cornmeal, salt, and black pepper and mix; cut the cheese into small cubes and distribute through the dough.
Divide the mixture among twelve corn husk parcels, folding the sides and ends and tying with strips from the remaining husks.

Fill the pot with the remaining 2000 ml of water and place the steamer basket above it without contact with the water; cook the parcels for eighty to ninety minutes, replenishing with hot water as needed.
Open one to check that the dough is firm and releases from the husk; rest for ten minutes before serving two per portion.
tips: Roasting the pumpkin helps keep the dough from becoming too wet.

title: Savory corn and coconut tamales
description: Fresh corn tamales with coconut milk, sweet pepper, and onion.

ingredients.name: water for the husks and steaming

steps: Soak the husks in 2000 ml of hot water for twenty minutes; rinse and drain. Blend the corn with the coconut milk to make a thick paste.
Sauté the chopped onion and sweet pepper in the oil for eight minutes; add the garlic and cook for one more minute.
Mix the sofrito with the corn paste, add the cornmeal and salt, and stir until no pockets of dry flour remain.
Divide among twelve parcels, overlapping husks where necessary; fold the sides and ends and tie with strips of husk.
Steam over the remaining 2000 ml of water, without letting the parcels touch the liquid, for eighty to ninety minutes; replenish with hot water when the level drops.
Check that a tamal releases from its husk and has a firm center; rest for ten minutes and serve two per portion.
tips: Use unsweetened coconut milk; this preparation is seasoned as a savory dish.

title: Shrimp tamal en cazuela
description: Ground fresh corn cooked into a thick cream, with shrimp added at the end.
steps: Blend the corn with 450 ml of stock until no whole kernels remain; reserve the other 200 ml to adjust during cooking.
Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil for eight minutes; add the tomato, cumin, and salt and cook for eight minutes.
Pour in the ground corn and cook over low heat for thirty to thirty-five minutes, stirring frequently and adding the reserved stock in stages.
When the corn is cooked and the mixture is thick, add the shrimp and stir for five to seven minutes, until firm and opaque.
Add the lime juice and serve in small bowls; the cream should fall slowly from the spoon and should not taste of raw corn.
tips: Stir along the bottom and corners to keep the corn from sticking to the pot.

title: Baked beef and olive empanadas
description: Homemade shortcrust pastry filled with beef picadillo and olives.
steps: Mix the flour and dough salt; rub in the cubed butter with your fingertips and add cold water until combined, without overkneading. Wrap and refrigerate for thirty minutes.
Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil for six minutes; add the beef and cumin and cook for seven minutes, breaking it up.
Add the tomato, olives, and filling salt; cook for ten minutes until reduced and at 71 °C. Spread in a shallow container and refrigerate for thirty minutes.
Divide the dough into twelve portions and roll into discs about thirteen centimeters wide; divide the cold filling among them, leaving a border clear.
Lightly moisten the edge with water, fold, and seal with a fork; place on a tray and brush with beaten egg.
Bake at 200 °C for twenty-five to thirty minutes, until golden and the center reaches 74 °C; rest for five minutes before serving.
tips: Serve hot and promptly refrigerate any leftover portions.

title: Chicken and bell pepper empanadas
description: Baked empanadas with an oil-based dough and shredded chicken filling.

ingredients.name: shredded cooked chicken
ingredients.note: Already cooked before starting; keep refrigerated until needed.

steps: Mix the flour and dough salt, add 70 ml of oil and the lukewarm water, and knead for two minutes until combined; cover and rest for twenty minutes.
Sauté the chopped onion and bell pepper in one tablespoon of oil for eight minutes; add the garlic and tomato and reduce for seven minutes.
Add the chicken, oregano, and filling salt; cook for five minutes, until the center reaches 74 °C and no free liquid remains. Spread out and refrigerate for thirty minutes.
Divide the dough into twelve portions, roll into thin thirteen-centimeter discs, and place the cold filling in the centers.
Fold each disc, press the edges, and seal with a fork; arrange on a tray and brush with beaten egg.
Bake at 200 °C for twenty-five to thirty minutes, until the pastry is golden and the filling reaches 74 °C; rest for five minutes before serving.
tips: Serve hot and promptly refrigerate any leftover portions.

title: Tuna, tomato, and egg empanadas
description: Baked empanadas with canned tuna, reduced tomato sauce, and hard-boiled egg.
steps: Combine the flour, dough salt, and cold butter until crumbly; add the water, bring the dough together, and refrigerate wrapped for thirty minutes.
Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil for eight minutes; add the tomato, oregano, and filling salt and reduce for fifteen minutes.
Remove from the heat and fold in the flaked tuna and chopped hard-boiled eggs; spread out the filling and refrigerate for thirty minutes.
Divide the dough into twelve portions and roll into thirteen-centimeter discs; add the cold filling and fold in half.
Seal the edges with a fork and brush with the beaten egg; arrange on a tray with space between the pieces.
Bake at 200 °C for twenty-five to thirty minutes, until golden and the filling reaches 74 °C; rest for five minutes and serve.
tips: Serve hot and promptly refrigerate any leftover portions.

title: Spinach and white cheese empanadas
description: Homemade pastry empanadas with very well-drained spinach and white cheese.
steps: Rub together the flour, dough salt, and cold butter until crumbly; add the water, combine without much kneading, and refrigerate for thirty minutes.
Wash the spinach and cook in the water clinging to its leaves for five minutes; let cool slightly for five minutes, squeeze thoroughly, and chop.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil for six minutes; add the spinach, nutmeg, and salt and stir for two minutes. Refrigerate for twenty minutes and mix with the crumbled cheese.
Make twelve thirteen-centimeter dough discs and divide the cold filling among them; leave a two-centimeter border uncovered.
Fold the discs and seal firmly with a fork; place on a tray and brush with beaten egg.
Bake at 200 °C for twenty-five to thirty minutes, until golden and hot in the center; rest for five minutes before serving.
tips: Serve hot and promptly refrigerate any leftover portions.

title: Roast pork and onion empanadas
description: Shredded roast pork and onion with sour orange in baked pastry.
steps: Mix the flour and dough salt; add 70 ml of oil and the lukewarm water, knead for two minutes, and rest covered for twenty minutes.
Cut the onion into thin strips and sauté in one tablespoon of oil for ten minutes; add the chopped garlic and stir for one minute.
Add the pork, sour orange juice, oregano, and filling salt; cook for seven minutes, until the liquid evaporates and the pork reaches 74 °C. Spread out and refrigerate for thirty minutes.
Divide the dough into twelve portions and roll into thin discs; put the cold pork in each and fold into half-moons.
Seal the seams with a fork and brush with beaten egg; arrange on a baking tray.
Bake at 200 °C for twenty-five to thirty minutes, until golden and the center reaches 74 °C; rest for five minutes before serving.
tips: Serve hot and promptly refrigerate any leftover portions.

title: Cooked conch fritters
description: Bites of previously tenderized conch, finely chopped with sweet pepper and a light batter.

ingredients.name: cooked tender conch
ingredients.note: previously boiled until tender; do not substitute raw conch

steps: Chop the cooked conch into half-centimeter pieces; finely chop the bell pepper and onion and mash the garlic.
Mix the flour, baking powder, salt, and black pepper; beat the egg and water separately and combine to make a thick batter.
Add the conch and vegetables; keep the mixture refrigerated while heating the oil to 170 °C.
Fry small spoonfuls for five minutes per batch, turning halfway through, until the batter is cooked and the center reaches 74 °C.
Drain the fritters on a rack and serve immediately; do not use this brief frying time to tenderize raw conch.
tips: This recipe starts with cooked conch: cleaned raw conch may need two to three hours of simmering to become tender.

title: Mushrooms stuffed with ham
description: Baked mushrooms filled with their stems and ham, with a thin cheese crust.
steps: Clean the mushrooms, remove the stems, and chop them very finely; place the caps cavity-side up on a tray.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in two tablespoons of oil for five minutes; add the stems and cook for seven minutes until their water evaporates.
Off the heat, mix with the chopped ham, breadcrumbs, parsley, black pepper, and half the cheese.
Fill the caps, scatter over the remaining cheese, and drizzle with the reserved tablespoon of oil.
Bake at 200 °C for eighteen to twenty-two minutes, until the mushrooms are tender and the center of the filling reaches 74 °C; serve three per portion.
tips: Serve hot and promptly refrigerate any leftover portions.

title: Baked stuffed eggs with tuna
description: Hard-boiled eggs filled with tuna and yolk, covered with white sauce and cheese.
steps: Place the eggs in the water and cook for ten to twelve minutes from the time it reaches a gentle boil; cool under running water, peel, and halve lengthwise.
Sauté the chopped onion in the oil for four minutes; add the tomato and cook for seven minutes until thickened. Mix with the tuna and mashed yolks.
Fill the twelve halves with this mixture and arrange in a baking dish so they do not tip over.
Melt the butter, add the flour, and stir for two minutes; gradually pour in the milk, add the salt and black pepper, and cook for five minutes until thickened.
Cover the eggs with the sauce and cheese; bake at 210 °C for fifteen to twenty minutes, until golden and the center reaches 74 °C, and serve two halves per person.
tips: Serve hot and promptly refrigerate any leftover portions.

title: Breaded zucchini bites
description: Thick zucchini slices coated with breadcrumbs, garlic, and oregano.
steps: Wash the zucchini and cut into one-centimeter slices; dry very well so the coating sticks.
Mix the breadcrumbs with the cheese, garlic powder, and oregano; beat the eggs in another plate and put the flour in a third.
Season the slices with the salt and coat in flour, egg, and the breadcrumb mixture, pressing gently.
Fry in batches at 175 °C for three to four minutes, turning halfway through, until golden and tender inside.
Drain on a rack and serve hot with the lime cut into wedges; avoid stacking them to preserve the crust.
tips: Small zucchini have fewer seeds and hold their shape better when fried.

title: Guava tres leches cake
description: Airy sponge cake soaked in three milks and finished with a layer of guava.
steps: Line a 23 × 33 cm pan and heat the oven to 175 °C. Separate the egg whites and yolks.
Beat the whites, adding the sugar gradually until soft peaks form. Fold in the yolks and vanilla.
Fold in the flour sifted with the baking powder. Spread in the pan and bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the center is cooked.
Mix the three milks. Let the sponge cool for 20 minutes, prick it and pour over the mixture in several additions so it can absorb.
Refrigerate covered for at least 4 hours. Spread the jam over the surface and serve in cold squares.
tips: Keep the soaked cake refrigerated at all times.

title: Pineapple upside-down cake
description: An upside-down cake with pineapple rings and a brown sugar and butter topping.

ingredients.name: Butter
ingredients.note: 40 g for the bottom and 110 g for the batter

steps: Grease a 23 cm pan. Melt the butter allocated to the bottom with the brown sugar and spread it over the base.
Arrange the pineapple rings without overlapping them; first pat their surfaces dry with paper towels.
Beat the remaining butter with the white sugar. Add the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Add the flour mixed with baking powder alternately with the milk. Pour over the pineapple and bake at 175 °C for 40 to 45 minutes.
When a skewer comes out clean, rest for 15 minutes. Loosen the edges and invert onto a rimmed plate before the caramel hardens.
tips: Use a one-piece pan to prevent caramel from leaking.

title: Coconut and lemon sponge cake
description: Sponge cake with shredded coconut, coconut milk and the fragrance of lemon zest.
steps: Grease and line a 22 cm round pan. Preheat the oven to 175 °C.
Beat the eggs and sugar for 4 minutes. Add the oil, coconut milk, zest and juice.
Mix the flour, baking powder, coconut and salt. Fold into the liquids with a spatula without overmixing.
Pour into the pan and bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until a skewer comes out without wet batter.
Rest in the pan for 15 minutes, then finish cooling on a rack before slicing.
tips: Shake the coconut milk to blend in its fat before measuring.

title: Spiced sweet potato loaf cake
description: A loaf cake with sweet potato purée, cinnamon and nutmeg.
steps: Mash the cooked sweet potato into a smooth purée. Line a 23 × 10 cm loaf pan.
Beat the eggs and sugar; add the oil, milk and lukewarm purée, never hot.
Mix the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt. Fold gently into the wet mixture.
Fill the pan and bake at 170 °C for 45 to 50 minutes, checking the center with a skewer.
Leave in the pan for 15 minutes, then unmold and wait at least another 25 minutes before slicing.
tips: Weigh the sweet potato after cooking and draining; excess water makes the crumb heavy.

title: Coffee and cocoa marble cake
description: A butter cake with swirls of cocoa and concentrated coffee.
steps: Line a 25 × 11 cm loaf pan and heat the oven to 175 °C.
Beat the butter and sugar for 4 minutes; add the eggs and vanilla. Add the flour and baking powder alternately with the milk.
Divide the batter in half. Mix the cocoa with the cold coffee and add it to one half.
Alternate spoonfuls of the two batters in the pan and run a skewer through them twice to create swirls.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the pan for 15 minutes, then on a rack for 30.
tips: Do not overmix the two batters or the pattern will disappear.

title: Orange cake with honey syrup
description: Orange cake soaked while warm with a juice and honey syrup.

ingredients.name: Orange juice
ingredients.note: 100 ml for the batter and 80 ml for the syrup

steps: Grease a 22 cm pan and preheat to 175 °C. Beat the butter and sugar until pale.
Add the eggs one at a time, then the zest. Add the flour and baking powder alternately with the juice allocated to the batter.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes and check with a skewer. Rest for 10 minutes before unmolding onto a plate.
Heat the reserved juice with the honey for 2 minutes without reducing it too far.
Prick the warm cake and brush on the syrup in three additions. Wait 35 minutes before slicing.
tips: The syrup spreads more evenly with a brush than when poured on all at once.

title: Peanut cake with cocoa topping
description: Ground peanut cake with a smooth dark chocolate topping.
steps: Line a 22 cm pan. Grind the peanuts in pulses, taking care not to turn them into butter.
Beat the butter and sugar, then add the eggs. Alternate the milk with the flour mixed with peanuts and baking powder.
Bake at 175 °C for 35 to 40 minutes, until the center is cooked. Cool completely.
Heat the cream until steaming and pour it over the chopped chocolate. Wait 2 minutes and stir into a smooth cream.
Spread the topping over the cold cake and let it set for 20 minutes before serving.
tips: Check the chocolate label for possible traces of allergens or added milk.

title: Banana and coconut ring cake
description: Banana and coconut cake baked in a ring pan.
steps: Grease and flour a 24 cm ring pan. Mash the banana with a fork.
Beat the eggs and sugar; add the oil, yogurt and mashed banana.
Mix the flour, coconut, baking powder, cinnamon and salt; fold in without overmixing.
Pour into the pan and bake at 175 °C for 45 to 50 minutes, checking the thickest part.
Rest for 15 minutes, invert onto a rack and cool for another 25 minutes.
tips: This recipe uses dessert bananas, not cooking plantains.

title: Carrot and pineapple cake
description: Grated carrot and pineapple cake with a cream cheese and lemon topping.
steps: Line a 23 × 23 cm pan. Pat the pineapple dry with paper towels and finely grate the carrot.
Beat the eggs, sugar and oil. Add the flour mixed with baking powder and cinnamon, then fold in the carrot and pineapple.
Bake at 175 °C for 40 to 45 minutes, until the center is cooked. Cool completely.
Mix the cream cheese, powdered sugar and lemon into a smooth topping.
Cover the cold cake, cut into twelve squares and keep refrigerated until serving.
tips: Drain the pineapple thoroughly to avoid a wet layer at the bottom.

title: Mango and yogurt cake
description: Yogurt cake with mango pulp and lime zest.
steps: Prepare a 22 cm pan by lining the base. Blend the mango pulp without adding water.
Beat the eggs and sugar. Add the oil, yogurt, mango and lime zest.
Fold in the sifted flour, baking powder and salt, mixing only until no dry patches remain.
Bake at 175 °C for 40 to 45 minutes; a skewer inserted in the center should come out without raw batter.
Rest in the pan for 15 minutes and cool on a rack before slicing.
tips: Very runny pulp changes the crumb; use thick, ripe mango pulp.

title: Steamed chocolate sponge cake
description: Cocoa sponge cooked in a steamer, with no oven required.
steps: Grease an 18 cm metal pan that fits in your steamer without touching the water. Heat the water in the pot.
Beat the eggs and sugar; add the oil, milk and vanilla. Fold in the sifted flour, cocoa and baking powder.
Pour into the pan, cover with a slightly domed piece of foil and place on the steamer rack.
Cover and cook over steady steam for 45 to 50 minutes. Add hot water down one side if needed, without wetting the batter.
Check with a skewer, remove using oven gloves and wait 15 minutes before unmolding. Cool for another 15 minutes.
tips: Use a conventional pot without sealing it under pressure.

title: Lemon and cream cheese loaf cake
description: Loaf cake with cream cheese, butter, lemon juice and zest.
steps: Line a 23 × 11 cm loaf pan and heat the oven to 170 °C.
Beat the cream cheese, butter and sugar until smooth. Add the eggs one at a time, then the juice and zest.
Fold in the sifted flour, baking powder and salt; mix briefly to keep the crumb tender.
Fill the pan and bake for 50 to 55 minutes. Cover with foil if it browns before the center is cooked.
Rest in the pan for 15 minutes and cool on a rack for 30 minutes before slicing.
tips: Ingredients at a similar temperature blend without forming lumps.

title: Guava crumble cake
description: Yogurt cake with guava cubes and crisp butter and cinnamon crumbs.

ingredients.name: Wheat flour
ingredients.note: 220 g for the batter and 60 g for the crumble

ingredients.name: Butter
ingredients.note: 110 g for the batter and 40 g for the crumble

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 110 g for the batter and 40 g for the crumble

steps: Rub the ingredients reserved for the crumble with the cinnamon until clumps form. Keep cold.
Beat the butter and sugar for the batter; add the eggs and yogurt. Fold in the flour for the batter and the baking powder.
Spread in a lined 23 × 23 cm pan. Scatter small guava cubes over the top and press them in lightly.
Cover with the crumble and bake at 175 °C for 40 to 45 minutes, until the center is cooked.
Cool for 40 minutes before lifting out of the pan and cutting into twelve portions.
tips: The skewer may pick up guava; also check a spot without filling.

title: Mamey and almond cake
description: Mamey cake with ground almonds and a tender crumb.
steps: Grease a 22 cm pan. Blend the mamey with the milk to make a purée without large fibers.
Beat the eggs and sugar for 3 minutes; add the lukewarm butter, vanilla and mamey purée.
Mix the flour, almonds and baking powder, then fold in with a spatula.
Bake at 175 °C for 40 to 45 minutes and check that the center is cooked.
Leave in the pan for 15 minutes and cool on a rack before slicing.
tips: Remove all the mamey seed and skin before weighing the pulp.

title: Cocoa sponge cake with custard filling
description: Cocoa sponge cut into two layers and filled with vanilla custard.

ingredients.name: Egg
ingredients.note: 3 whole eggs for the cake and 2 yolks for the custard

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 100 g for the cake and 60 g for the custard

steps: Beat the three whole eggs with the sugar for the sponge until tripled in volume. Fold in the sifted flour and cocoa.
Bake the batter in a lined 20 cm pan at 175 °C for 25 minutes. Cool and slice horizontally.
Mix the two yolks with the sugar for the custard, cornstarch and some cold milk. Gradually add the remaining milk, heated.
Cook, stirring, until gently boiling and continue for 1 minute. Add the vanilla, transfer to a shallow container, cover the surface directly and chill in the refrigerator.
Fill the sponge with the cold custard and replace the top layer. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour and dust with powdered sugar before serving.
tips: Keep the leftover egg whites refrigerated for another recipe.

title: Oat and coconut cookies
description: Rolled oats and toasted coconut in cookies with crisp edges.
steps: Beat the softened butter and sugar; add the egg and mix until incorporated.
Mix the oats, flour, coconut, baking powder and salt. Combine the mixtures without kneading and rest for 10 minutes.
Divide into twenty balls on two lined baking sheets and flatten to 1 cm thick.
Bake at 175 °C for 14 to 16 minutes, until the edges are golden.
Leave on the baking sheet for 10 minutes, then finish cooling on a rack.
tips: Do not replace rolled oats with oat flour: their absorption differs.

title: Crunchy peanut cookies
description: Fork-pressed cookies made with smooth peanut butter.
steps: Mix both butters with the sugar until smooth. Incorporate the egg.
Add the flour, baking powder and salt; bring the dough together and refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Form eighteen balls and flatten with a fork in two directions to mark a crisscross pattern.
Bake on parchment at 175 °C for 12 to 15 minutes, until lightly golden.
Rest for 10 minutes before moving; the cookies will firm up as they cool.
tips: If oil has separated from the peanut butter, stir it in before weighing.

title: Cocoa and coffee cookies
description: Dark cocoa cookies with a tender center and coffee aroma.
steps: Dissolve the coffee in the water and cool. Beat the butter and sugar; add the egg and coffee.
Mix the flour, cocoa and baking powder. Add to the creamed mixture, then fold in the chopped chocolate.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes and form twenty mounds, spaced apart on parchment.
Bake at 175 °C for 10 to 12 minutes, until the edges are set but the centers are still tender.
Wait 10 minutes before transferring to a rack; do not keep baking until the cookies feel hard while hot.
tips: These cookies contain caffeine from both coffee and cocoa.

title: Dulce de leche sandwich cookies
description: Two delicate cornstarch cookies enclose a dulce de leche filling.
steps: Beat the butter with the powdered sugar; add the yolks and milk. Fold in the flour, cornstarch and baking powder.
Chill the dough for 30 minutes and roll to 4 mm thick between sheets of parchment. Cut thirty-two 5 cm discs.
Bake at 170 °C for 10 to 12 minutes; they should remain pale.
Cool completely and divide the dulce de leche among sixteen discs. Cover with the others without pressing too firmly.
Roll the edges in shredded coconut and store the filled cookies in a closed container in the refrigerator.
tips: Fill only after cooling so the dulce de leche does not become runny.

title: Orange and sesame cookies
description: Thin orange-scented cookies coated in sesame seeds.
steps: Beat the butter and sugar; add the egg, orange juice and zest.
Fold in the flour and baking powder. Form a 4 cm log and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Roll the log in the sesame seeds, pressing to adhere, and cut into twenty-four discs.
Place apart on a baking sheet and bake at 175 °C for 12 to 15 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes and transfer to a rack to cool completely.
tips: Toasted sesame seeds darken faster; use raw seeds here.

title: Vanilla, raisin and almond biscotti
description: Twice-baked cake slices for dipping into coffee.
steps: Beat the butter, sugar, eggs and vanilla. Fold in the flour, baking powder and salt.
Add the almonds and raisins; shape into two 25 × 6 cm logs with slightly damp hands.
Bake at 175 °C for 25 minutes. Let cool for 15 minutes so they can be sliced.
Cut diagonal slices 1 cm thick and lay them on their sides. Bake at 150 °C for 10 minutes per side.
Cool on a rack until all the heat has dissipated before closing the storage container.
tips: A serrated knife helps keep the logs from breaking when sliced.

title: Lemon and cornmeal cookies
description: Yellow cookies with a sandy texture and lemon zest.
steps: Beat the butter and sugar; add the egg, zest and juice.
Mix the two flours with the baking powder and incorporate into the creamed mixture without kneading.
Refrigerate for 25 minutes. Shape twenty-two balls and flatten to about 7 mm.
Bake at 170 °C for 15 to 18 minutes, until the bottoms are lightly golden.
Leave on the baking sheet for 10 minutes and finish cooling on a rack.
tips: Use fine cornmeal, not coarse polenta or cornstarch.

title: Soft pumpkin and chocolate cookies
description: Soft pumpkin purée cookies with chocolate pieces.
steps: Drain the purée in a sieve if it contains visible water. Heat the oven to 180 °C.
Beat the butter and sugar; add the egg and pumpkin. Separately mix the flour, baking powder and cinnamon.
Combine the mixtures and add the chocolate. Rest for 10 minutes to let the flour hydrate.
Place twenty mounds apart on a baking sheet and flatten slightly. Bake for 15 to 18 minutes.
Check that there is no raw batter inside and cool on a rack; the final texture will remain soft.
tips: Do not expect a dry cookie: the purée creates a soft crumb.

title: Ginger and molasses cookies
description: Spiced cookies with cane molasses and a thin sugar crust.
steps: Beat the butter and brown sugar; incorporate the egg and molasses.
Mix the flour, ginger, cinnamon and baking soda. Add to the creamed mixture and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Form twenty-four balls and roll in white sugar. Space apart on two baking sheets.
Bake at 175 °C for 11 to 13 minutes, until cracked and set around the edges.
Wait 15 minutes before moving them; finish cooling off the baking sheet.
tips: Molasses provides acidity; do not substitute it without adjusting the baking soda.

title: Oat and guava bars
description: An oat base and crumble surround a thick layer of guava.
steps: Heat the guava and water into a thick paste; let cool until lukewarm. Line a 20 × 20 cm pan.
Mix the oats, flour, sugar, baking powder and salt. Rub in the cubed butter to make crumbs.
Press two-thirds of the crumbs into the pan. Spread on the guava and scatter the remaining third over the top.
Bake at 180 °C for 28 to 30 minutes, until golden on top.
Cool for an hour before removing from the pan and cutting into sixteen bars.
tips: Cooling is necessary to keep the bars from falling apart when cut.

title: Pineapple and meringue tartlets
description: Pastry baskets filled with cooked pineapple and topped with meringue heated over a water bath.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 70 g for the filling and 150 g for the meringue

steps: Rub together the flour, butter and powdered sugar. Add the egg, bring together and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Line twelve 7 cm tartlet molds with pastry rolled to 3 mm. Prick, cover with parchment and weights and bake at 180 °C for 12 minutes; remove the weights and brown for 8 minutes.
Cook the pineapple and filling sugar for 8 minutes. Add the cornstarch dissolved in water, boil gently for 2 minutes and cool.
Heat the egg whites, meringue sugar and lemon over a water bath to 71 °C; beat off the heat until cool and forming peaks.
Divide the cold pineapple among the pastry shells, top with meringue and refrigerate until serving.
tips: Place baking weights on parchment so they do not touch the pastry.

title: Mango and yogurt tart with an oat crust
description: Baked mango filling on a compact oat crust.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 30 g for the crust and 90 g for the filling

steps: Mix the oats, melted butter and crust sugar. Press into the bottom of a 22 cm springform pan.
Bake the crust for 10 minutes at 180 °C. Then reduce the oven to 165 °C.
Blend the mango, yogurt, eggs, filling sugar, cornstarch and zest without incorporating much foam.
Pour over the crust and bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until set and the center reaches 71 °C.
Let cool for 30 minutes, then refrigerate for at least 3 hours before unmolding.
tips: Use thick yogurt; excess whey leaves the filling watery.

title: Guava lattice pie
description: Shortcrust pie with a guava filling and crisscross pastry strips.
steps: Rub together the flour, butter and sugar. Add the egg and cold water until the dough comes together; refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Heat the guava, filling water and lemon into a thick paste. Cool while rolling out the dough.
Line a 24 cm pan with two-thirds of the dough and spread in the cold filling.
Cut strips from the remaining dough, weave over the pie and join the edges. Brush the strips with milk.
Bake at 185 °C for 35 to 40 minutes, until the crust and top are golden. Cool for 40 minutes before slicing.
tips: If the dough softens while making the lattice, chill it again before handling.

title: Chilled banana and custard tart
description: A biscuit base with fresh banana and chilled pastry cream.
steps: Crush the biscuits and mix with the melted butter. Press onto the base and sides of a 22 cm pan and refrigerate.
Mix the yolks, sugar, cornstarch and a little cold milk. Heat the remaining milk and add it gradually.
Return to the saucepan, stir until gently boiling and cook for 1 minute. Add the vanilla and cool in a shallow container with the surface covered.
Slice the banana into rounds and gently mix with the lemon. Arrange over the base and cover with the cold custard.
Refrigerate for at least 3 hours before unmolding and serve cold.
tips: Add the banana on the day of serving to preserve its color.

title: Spiced sweet potato pie
description: Shortcrust pastry filled with sweet potato, milk and sweet spices.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 30 g for the crust and 90 g for the filling

ingredients.name: Egg
ingredients.note: 1 for the crust and 2 for the filling

steps: Rub the flour, butter and crust sugar into crumbs. Incorporate one egg and the water; chill for 30 minutes.
Roll out and line a 24 cm pan. Bake with parchment and weights for 15 minutes at 180 °C; remove the weights.
Blend the sweet potato, milk, two eggs, remaining sugar and spices into a smooth filling.
Pour into the crust and bake at 170 °C for 40 to 45 minutes, until set and the center reaches 71 °C.
Let cool for 30 minutes and refrigerate for 90 minutes before slicing so the filling can settle.
tips: Weigh the sweet potato after cooking, draining and peeling.

title: Baked coconut cheesecake
description: Creamy cheesecake with coconut milk on a biscuit base.
steps: Crush the biscuits and mix with the butter. Press into a lined 22 cm pan and bake for 10 minutes at 180 °C.
Mix the cheese and sugar without overbeating; add the eggs one at a time, then the coconut milk, cornstarch and vanilla.
Fold in the coconut, pour over the base and bake at 155 °C for 50 to 55 minutes, until set and the center reaches 71 °C.
Turn off the oven and leave the door ajar for 20 minutes. Remove and wait another 25 minutes.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours before unmolding. Cut with a knife dampened between portions.
tips: Gentle baking reduces cracks; do not expect the center to be completely rigid while hot.

title: Lime and condensed milk tart
description: An oven-set citrus filling on a crisp base.
steps: Crush the biscuits, mix with the melted butter and press into a 22 cm pan.
Bake the base for 10 minutes at 180 °C and reduce the oven to 165 °C.
Mix the yolks, condensed milk, lime juice and zest without incorporating foam.
Pour into the base and bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until set and the center reaches at least 71 °C.
Let cool for 30 minutes and refrigerate for at least 3 hours before slicing.
tips: Grate only the green part of the peel to avoid bitter white pith.

title: Mango and ginger galette
description: An open rustic tart with mango wedges and fresh ginger.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 25 g for the pastry and 45 g for the filling

steps: Rub together the flour, butter and pastry sugar. Add the cold water, bring together and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Mix the mango, filling sugar, cornstarch, ginger and lemon just before assembling.
Roll the pastry into a 30 cm circle on parchment. Place the mango in the center, leaving 5 cm uncovered around the edge.
Fold the edges over the fruit, pleating as you go, and brush with milk. Bake at 190 °C for 30 to 35 minutes.
Check that the base is golden and let cool on the baking sheet for 15 minutes.
tips: Use firm, ripe mango so the wedges retain their shape.

title: Pineapple and coconut crumble tart
description: Cooked pineapple and coconut on shortcrust pastry, topped with crumble.

ingredients.name: Wheat flour
ingredients.note: 220 g for the crust and 60 g for the crumble

ingredients.name: Butter
ingredients.note: 110 g for the crust and 40 g for the crumble

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 50 g for the crust, 50 g for the filling and 40 g for the crumble

steps: Combine the crust ingredients with the egg, form a disc and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Line a 24 cm pan.
Cook the pineapple and filling sugar for 8 minutes. Add the cornstarch dissolved in water and the coconut; cook for 2 minutes and cool.
Rub together the crumble flour, butter and sugar without bringing them into a solid dough.
Spread the filling in the crust, top with crumble and bake at 180 °C for 35 to 40 minutes.
Cool for an hour before removing from the pan so the filling can settle.
tips: Cool the filling before putting it on the raw pastry.

title: Peanut and cocoa tart
description: A cocoa crust with a baked peanut and honey filling.

ingredients.name: Butter
ingredients.note: 110 g for the crust and 50 g for the filling

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 60 g for the crust and 70 g for the filling

ingredients.name: Egg
ingredients.note: 1 for the crust and 2 for the filling

steps: Rub the flour, cocoa, crust butter and sugar into crumbs. Add one egg and chill for 30 minutes.
Line a 24 cm pan; bake with parchment and weights for 12 minutes at 180 °C, then remove them.
Beat the two remaining eggs with the filling sugar, honey, melted butter and milk. Add the chopped peanuts.
Pour into the crust and bake at 170 °C for 25 to 28 minutes, until the filling sets and reaches 71 °C.
Let cool and chill for at least an hour before cutting into small portions.
tips: Chop the peanuts with a knife to preserve distinct pieces.

title: Guava-filled buns
description: Enriched dough rolls enclosing a cube of guava paste.
steps: Combine the flour, yeast, sugar, milk, egg and salt. Knead for 5 minutes and add the butter in stages.
Continue for 10 minutes until the dough is elastic. Cover and let rise for 60 to 90 minutes.
Divide into twelve portions, flatten each one and enclose a cube of guava. Pinch the seam shut and place it underneath.
Let rise on a baking sheet for 45 minutes and brush with milk. Bake at 180 °C for 22 to 25 minutes.
Cool on a rack for 15 minutes before serving, because the guava stays very hot.
tips: Keep the sealing edge free of filling so the bun does not open.

title: Coconut and raisin braided bread
description: Sweet braided bread with coconut milk and raisins throughout the crumb.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, coconut milk, water, egg and salt. Knead until combined and incorporate the butter.
Knead for 10 minutes; add the coconut and raisins at the end. Cover and let rise for 75 to 90 minutes.
Divide into six portions and roll into 30 cm ropes. Make two three-strand braids and tuck in the ends.
Let rise for 45 to 60 minutes. Bake at 180 °C for 25 to 30 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
Cool on a rack for 25 minutes before slicing to avoid compressing the crumb.
tips: Keep the raisins inside the dough when possible; exposed raisins burn sooner.

title: Pumpkin milk bread
description: A soft sandwich loaf with pumpkin purée worked into the dough.
steps: Blend the pumpkin and milk. Mix with the flour, yeast, sugar, egg and salt until a dough forms.
Add the softened butter and knead for 10 minutes. Cover and let rise for 75 to 90 minutes.
Gently deflate, shape into a log and place seam-side down in a greased 25 × 12 cm loaf pan.
Let rise for 45 to 60 minutes, until close to the rim. Bake at 180 °C for 30 to 35 minutes.
Unmold after 10 minutes and cool on a rack for at least 30 minutes before slicing.
tips: The purée should be thick; drain it before adding.

title: Cinnamon and orange rolls
description: Sweet bread spirals with cinnamon filling and citrus glaze.

ingredients.name: Butter
ingredients.note: 50 g for the dough and 50 g for the filling

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 60 g for the dough and 80 g for the filling

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, dough sugar, milk, egg and salt. Knead and add the dough butter; work for 10 minutes.
Let rise for 60 to 90 minutes. Roll into a 30 × 40 cm rectangle and spread with the filling butter.
Scatter over the filling sugar, cinnamon and zest. Roll up from the long side and cut into twelve spirals.
Place in a 23 × 33 cm pan and let rise for 45 minutes. Bake at 180 °C for 25 to 28 minutes.
Mix the powdered sugar and juice. Let the rolls cool for 15 minutes and drizzle with the glaze.
tips: Cut with clean, uncoated kitchen twine to preserve the spirals.

title: Sweet potato rolls
description: Soft rolls made with cooked sweet potato for breakfast and small sandwiches.
steps: Mash the sweet potato until smooth and mix with the milk and egg. Add the flour, yeast, sugar and salt.
Knead for 5 minutes, add the butter and continue for another 8 minutes. Cover and let rise for 75 to 90 minutes.
Divide into twelve equal pieces, shape into balls and space apart on a baking sheet.
Let rise for 45 minutes and bake at 185 °C for 20 to 25 minutes, until evenly golden.
Transfer to a rack and wait 15 minutes before splitting open.
tips: Do not add too much flour to a slightly sticky dough; resting makes it easier to handle.

title: Coffee and walnut bread
description: Yeasted bread flavored with coffee and chopped walnuts.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast and sugar. Add the coffee, salt and softened butter and knead for 10 minutes.
Add the chopped walnuts and knead just until distributed. Cover and let rise for 75 minutes.
Divide into two oval loaves and place on a lined baking sheet. Let rise for 45 minutes.
Make two shallow slashes and bake at 185 °C for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cool on a rack for at least 30 minutes before slicing.
tips: The coffee should be cold or lukewarm so it does not harm the yeast.

title: Cocoa bread with guava cubes
description: Yeasted cocoa dough with pieces of guava paste.
steps: Mix the flour, cocoa, yeast and sugar. Add the milk, egg and salt; knead and incorporate the butter.
Work for 10 minutes and let rise for 75 to 90 minutes. Cut the guava into 1 cm cubes.
Flatten the dough, scatter over the guava and fold. Divide into ten pieces and shape into buns.
Let rise on a baking sheet for 45 minutes. Bake at 180 °C for 22 to 25 minutes.
Cool on a rack for 15 minutes so the filling can cool down before eating.
tips: Cocoa darkens the dough; check the time and the base for doneness, not just the color.

title: Whole-wheat honey and sesame bread
description: A sandwich loaf with whole-wheat flour, honey and sesame seeds.
steps: Mix the two flours with the water and rest for 20 minutes to hydrate.
Add the honey, yeast, salt and oil. Knead for 10 minutes and incorporate three-quarters of the sesame seeds.
Cover and let rise for 60 to 90 minutes. Shape into a log and place in a 25 × 12 cm loaf pan.
Let rise for 45 minutes, dampen the surface and sprinkle with the remaining seeds. Bake at 185 °C for 35 to 40 minutes.
Unmold and cool on a rack for at least 35 minutes before slicing.
tips: This bread contains wheat; whole grain does not mean gluten free.

title: Cream cheese and herb bread
description: Savory cream cheese bread with parsley and chives.
steps: Mix the cream cheese with the lukewarm milk and oil. Add the flour, yeast, sugar and salt.
Knead for 10 minutes and incorporate the thoroughly dried herbs. Cover and let rise for 75 minutes.
Divide into ten buns and place on a baking sheet; let rise for another 45 minutes.
Make a shallow slash and bake at 185 °C for 22 to 25 minutes.
Cool on a rack for 20 minutes before slicing or filling.
tips: Dry the herbs after washing so you do not add unmeasured water.

title: Lemon and anise buns
description: Small yeasted buns with citrus zest and anise.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, anise and zest. Add the milk, egg and salt and bring the dough together.
Add the butter and knead for 10 minutes. Cover and let rise for 75 to 90 minutes.
Divide into twelve portions and shape into round buns, tightening the surface without tearing it.
Let rise for 45 minutes, brush with milk and bake at 180 °C for 20 to 22 minutes.
Cool on a rack for 15 minutes and serve warm or at room temperature.
tips: Lightly crush the anise seeds to distribute their aroma.

title: Sweet pineapple and coconut empanadas
description: Homemade pastry half-moons with a reduced pineapple and coconut filling.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 30 g for the pastry and 60 g for the filling

steps: Cook the pineapple and filling sugar for 12 minutes, until its juice reduces; add the coconut, cook for another 3 minutes and cool.
Rub together the flour, butter, pastry sugar and salt. Add the water, bring together without overworking and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Roll to 3 mm thick and cut twelve 12 cm discs. Divide the cold filling among their centers.
Dampen the edges, fold and seal with a fork. Brush with beaten egg and cut a vent.
Bake at 190 °C for 23 to 25 minutes, until golden. Let cool for 15 minutes.
tips: The filling must be thick and cold so it does not tear the pastry.

title: Mango and cheese mini empanadas
description: Shortcrust pastry with thick mango compote and cream cheese.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 35 g for the pastry and 20 g for the filling

steps: Cook the mango, filling sugar and lemon for 6 minutes. Dissolve the cornstarch in the 15 ml of filling water, add it and cook for 2 minutes; leave to cool.
Rub together the flour, butter and pastry sugar. Add the egg and cold water, bring together and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Roll to 3 mm thick and cut ten 12 cm discs. Add the mango and cheese, keeping the edges clean.
Fold closed, seal with a fork and brush with milk. Place on baking parchment.
Bake at 190 °C for 23 to 27 minutes, until the base is golden; let cool slightly before eating.
tips: Do not mix the cheese with hot mango.

title: Banana and chocolate puff pastries
description: Puff pastry parcels with banana and dark chocolate.
steps: Dice the banana and mix with the lemon and cinnamon. Chop the chocolate.
Cut the cold puff pastry into sixteen equal rectangles and place eight on a baking sheet.
Divide the banana and chocolate among them, leaving a 1 cm border. Dampen the edges and close with the remaining pieces.
Brush with egg and cut a steam vent. Bake at 200 °C for 22 to 25 minutes.
Cool for 20 minutes before serving so the filling is no longer scalding hot.
tips: Choose ripe but firm banana to avoid a runny filling.
allergens: Milk (depending on puff pastry and chocolate)

title: Puff pastry baskets with orange custard
description: Crisp pastry baskets filled with citrus pastry cream.
steps: Cut the puff pastry into eight squares and line 90 ml muffin cavities. Prick, cover with parchment and weights and bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes.
Remove the weights and parchment and brown for another 5 minutes. Cool the baskets outside the pan.
Mix the yolks, sugar, cornstarch and a little cold milk. Heat the remaining milk with the zest and add to the mixture.
Cook, stirring, until gently boiling for 1 minute. Add the juice, cook for 1 minute more and cool in a shallow container.
Refrigerate the custard until completely cold. Fill the baskets just before serving.
tips: The custard must be cold to keep the puff pastry crisp.

title: Coconut and coffee puff pastry spirals
description: Crisp spirals with a coffee-flavored coconut paste.
steps: Mix the softened butter, sugar, coconut and coffee into a spreadable paste.
Roll the puff pastry into a 25 × 35 cm rectangle and spread with the filling, leaving 1 cm bare at the far edge.
Roll up from the long side and refrigerate for 20 minutes to firm up the log.
Cut into sixteen slices, space apart and brush with egg. Bake at 195 °C for 20 to 22 minutes.
Leave on the baking sheet for 10 minutes and finish cooling on a rack.
tips: The coffee must be cold so it does not melt the butter in the puff pastry.

title: Guava and almond puff pastry braid
description: Woven puff pastry with cheese, guava and ground almonds.
steps: Mix the cream cheese, almonds and sugar. Roll the puff pastry into a 30 × 40 cm rectangle.
Imagine three long strips; spread the cream mixture down the middle one and cover with guava slices.
Cut diagonal strips 2 cm wide along the sides. Cross them alternately over the filling and close the ends.
Brush with egg and bake on parchment at 195 °C for 25 to 30 minutes.
Wait 25 minutes before cutting into eight portions with a serrated knife.
tips: Keep the filling away from the ends so you can close the braid.

title: Mango and coconut cream mille-feuille
description: Puff pastry sheets layered with coconut custard and fresh mango.
steps: Cut three 12 × 30 cm rectangles of puff pastry. Prick and bake between parchment and two baking sheets at 190 °C for 20 minutes.
Remove the top baking sheet and brown for another 5 minutes. Cool the pastry sheets on a rack.
Mix the yolks, sugar and cornstarch with some of the cold coconut milk. Add the rest, heated, and cook, stirring, until gently boiling for 1 minute.
Cool the custard in a shallow container with its surface covered directly. Dice the mango, mix with the lime and drain.
Alternate the pastry sheets, cold custard and mango in two layers. Refrigerate for 30 minutes, dust with powdered sugar and cut with a serrated knife.
tips: Assemble close to serving time to preserve the crisp layers.

title: Peanut and cocoa puff pastry fans
description: Folded puff pastry filled with ground peanuts and cocoa.
steps: Mix the ground peanuts, sugar and cocoa. Roll the puff pastry into a 25 × 35 cm rectangle.
Brush with lukewarm butter and scatter over the dry mixture, pressing gently.
Fold both long sides toward the middle twice, then bring the halves together. Chill for 20 minutes.
Cut into sixteen slices and slightly open their ends. Bake at 195 °C for 12 minutes, turn and brown for another 6 to 8 minutes.
Let cool for 10 minutes, then cool fully on a rack before storing.
tips: Cocoa disguises browning: make sure the bottoms do not burn.

title: Mushroom and cheese vol-au-vents
description: Puff pastry baskets with a savory mushroom and cream cheese filling.
steps: Cut twenty 8 cm puff pastry discs. Remove the centers from ten and place the rings over the bases brushed with egg.
Prick only the centers, brush the rings and bake at 200 °C for 20 to 25 minutes. Cool and gently press down the centers if they have risen.
Sauté the onion in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the chopped mushrooms and cook for 8 minutes, until their water evaporates.
Add the milk mixed with cornstarch, salt and pepper; boil for 1 minute. Off the heat, stir in the cream cheese.
Fill the vol-au-vents and heat at 180 °C for 5 minutes. Serve immediately.
tips: Do not pile in a runny filling: it should be thick and creamy.

title: Spinach and white cheese puff pastries
description: Savory parcels of drained spinach and pasteurized white cheese.

ingredients.name: Egg
ingredients.note: 1 for the filling and 1 for brushing

steps: Sauté the onion in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the spinach, cook until wilted and squeeze out the liquid once cooled slightly.
Chop the spinach and mix with the crumbled cheese, one egg, nutmeg and salt.
Cut the puff pastry into ten squares. Divide the filling among them and join opposite corners to form parcels.
Brush with the remaining egg and bake at 195 °C for 25 to 30 minutes, until golden and the filling reaches 71 °C in the center.
Wait 10 minutes before serving and refrigerate leftover portions.
tips: Draining the spinach keeps the pastry base from becoming wet.

title: Coconut cream profiteroles
description: Hollow choux puffs filled with cooked coconut custard.
steps: Mix the yolks, sugar, cornstarch and coconut milk. Cook, stirring, until gently boiling for 1 minute; cool in a shallow container with the surface covered directly.
Bring the water, milk, butter and salt to a boil. Add the flour all at once and stir over low heat for 2 minutes, until the dough pulls away from the pan.
Let cool for 5 minutes. Add the beaten eggs gradually until the dough is glossy and falls slowly from the spatula; a little egg may be left over.
Pipe sixteen mounds onto parchment. Bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes and at 175 °C for another 15 to 20, without opening before they can hold their shape.
Make a small hole and dry for 5 minutes in the switched-off oven. Cool on a rack.
Pipe in the completely cold custard and refrigerate until serving.
tips: Choux pastry needs to dry inside so it does not collapse after baking.

title: Coffee and cocoa éclairs
description: Long choux pastries with coffee custard and a chocolate topping.
steps: Mix the custard milk, coffee, yolks, sugar and cornstarch; cook, stirring, until gently boiling for 1 minute. Cool with the surface covered directly.
Bring the water, dough milk and butter to a boil. Add the flour and dry the dough by stirring over low heat for 2 minutes.
Let cool for 5 minutes and gradually incorporate the beaten eggs into a thick, glossy dough.
Pipe twelve 10 cm strips. Bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes and at 175 °C for another 18 to 20 minutes.
Pierce one end to release steam and cool completely. Fill with the cold coffee custard.
Heat the cream, pour over the chopped chocolate and stir. Coat the tops and refrigerate for 30 minutes to set.
tips: Leave space between the strips because they expand during baking.

title: Orange choux fritters
description: Light balls of fried cooked dough finished with citrus sugar.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 20 g for the dough and 60 g for finishing

steps: Bring the water, butter, dough sugar and salt to a boil. Add the flour all at once and stir for 2 minutes, until it pulls away from the pan.
Let cool for 5 minutes and add the beaten eggs in stages until the dough is thick and glossy. Add half the zest.
Heat the oil to 165 °C. Drop in small portions using two spoons without crowding the pan.
Fry for 5 to 6 minutes per batch, turning, until puffed, golden and cooked inside without wet paste.
Drain and coat while still warm in the remaining sugar mixed with the reserved zest.
tips: Oil that is too hot browns the outside before the center cooks.

title: Cheese and lemon doughnut rings
description: Fried cream cheese doughnut rings with lemon zest.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 60 g for the dough and 30 g for finishing

steps: Mix the cheese, butter, dough sugar, egg, milk and zest until smooth.
Add the flour and baking powder; bring together without overworking and rest for 15 minutes.
Divide into eighteen short ropes and join into rings, leaving a wide hole.
Fry at 165 °C for 3 to 4 minutes per batch, turning, until golden and cooked through.
Drain, let cool for 5 minutes and sprinkle with the finishing sugar.
tips: The rings expand; make the holes large so they do not close.

title: Glazed sweet potato doughnuts
description: Yeasted dough rings with sweet potato purée and a milk glaze.
steps: Mash the sweet potato and mix with the milk and egg. Add the flour, yeast, sugar and salt; knead and incorporate the butter.
Work until elastic and let rise for 75 minutes. Roll to 1.5 cm thick and cut twelve 8 cm rings.
Place on parchment squares and let rise for 40 minutes. Heat the oil to 170 °C.
Fry for 2 minutes per side, removing the parchment with tongs as each doughnut is released. Check that there is no raw dough inside.
Drain and cool for 15 minutes. Mix the powdered sugar and glaze milk, coat one side and dry for 20 minutes.
tips: The dough must rise again after cutting to become light.

title: Cooked cassava and coconut cake
description: A dense cake of previously boiled cassava with coconut and milk.

ingredients.name: Cooked commercially sourced sweet cassava
ingredients.note: central fiber removed and well drained

steps: Use fully boiled cassava; discard its cooking water and remove the central fiber. Mash while still warm.
Beat the eggs and sugar. Add the milk, melted butter, vanilla and mashed cassava.
Add the coconut and baking powder and mix until distributed. Pour into a greased and lined 22 cm pan.
Bake at 175 °C for 45 to 55 minutes, until set and golden; check that the center is firm and cooked.
Let cool for 30 minutes and chill before slicing. The texture will be compact, rather than an airy sponge.
tips: The weight is for cooked cassava; this formula does not use raw grated root.

title: Guava crêpe cake
description: Thin crêpe layers alternating with cream and guava.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 20 g for the crêpes and 25 g for the cream

steps: Blend the flour, milk, eggs, butter, crêpe sugar and salt. Rest for 20 minutes.
Heat a 20 cm nonstick skillet. Cook ten thin crêpes for about 1 minute per side, until set with no raw batter.
Cool the crêpes separately. Whip the very cold cream with the reserved sugar until firm peaks form.
Build layers of crêpe, cream and a thin film of guava, dividing the filling among all the layers.
Refrigerate for 2 hours before cutting with a thin knife, and keep cold until serving.
tips: Hot crêpes melt the cream; cool them before assembling.

title: Cocoa cream sponge rolls
description: Small sponge spirals filled with cream and cocoa.
steps: Beat the eggs and sugar for 8 minutes until thick and foamy. Gently fold in the vanilla and sifted flour.
Spread in a lined 30 × 40 cm baking sheet. Bake at 180 °C for 10 to 12 minutes without drying it out.
Turn onto clean parchment and roll up while warm. Let cool completely in this shape.
Whip the cold cream with the cocoa and powdered sugar into a firm cream. Unroll the sponge and spread with the filling.
Roll up again, refrigerate for 1 hour and cut into ten thick slices with a serrated knife.
tips: Rolling while warm helps prevent cracks when filling.

title: Almond and lemon kisses
description: Baked bites of ground almonds and egg whites, without wheat flour.
steps: Mix the almonds, powdered sugar and zest. Add the whites and juice to make a sticky paste.
Cover and rest for 20 minutes so the almonds absorb the moisture.
Form twenty-four balls with barely damp hands and roll in powdered sugar.
Bake on parchment at 170 °C for 15 to 18 minutes, until lightly cracked with golden bottoms.
Leave on the baking sheet for 10 minutes and cool completely on a rack.
tips: Although they contain no wheat flour, check packaged almonds for possible traces.

title: Guava crumble muffins
description: Guava-filled muffins with a crisp butter topping.

ingredients.name: Wheat flour
ingredients.note: 230 g for the batter and 50 g for the crumble

ingredients.name: Butter
ingredients.note: 100 g for the batter and 35 g for the crumble

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 100 g for the batter and 35 g for the crumble

steps: Rub together the crumble ingredients and keep cold. Place twelve liners in a pan with 100 ml cavities.
Beat the butter and sugar for the batter; add the eggs, milk and vanilla. Fold in the batter flour and baking powder.
Divide half the batter among the cavities, place a guava cube in each and cover with the rest.
Add the crumble and bake at 180 °C for 22 to 25 minutes, until the batter is cooked.
Rest in the pan for 5 minutes, then cool on a rack for 15 minutes before serving.
tips: Leave room in the liners so the muffins can rise without overflowing.

title: Coconut and brown butter financiers
description: Small egg white and almond cakes with nutty browned butter.
steps: Heat the butter over medium heat until the solids are golden and smell nutty; remove before they burn and let cool slightly.
Mix the almonds, coconut, flour, powdered sugar and salt. Add the egg whites without whipping them.
Add the lukewarm butter, mix and refrigerate the batter for 20 minutes.
Divide among twelve greased 60 ml cavities and bake at 190 °C for 15 to 18 minutes, until golden.
Rest for 5 minutes, unmold and finish cooling on a rack.
tips: Do not use the butter if its solids turn black and bitter.

title: Mamey soufflés
description: Small hot soufflés of mamey pulp and whipped egg whites.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 70 g for the mixture and 15 g for the ramekins

steps: Grease six 150 ml ramekins and coat with the sugar allocated to the molds. Preheat the oven to 190 °C.
Mix the milk, cornstarch, yolks and half the sugar for the mixture. Cook, stirring, until thickened and gently boiling for 1 minute.
Add the blended mamey and let cool for 10 minutes. Beat the whites with the lemon and remaining sugar to soft peaks.
Stir one-third of the whites into the base, then fold in the rest. Fill the ramekins to 1 cm below the rim.
Bake for 16 to 20 minutes without opening the oven; the centers should set and reach 71 °C. Serve immediately before they lose volume.
tips: Have the table ready before taking the soufflés out of the oven.

title: Cocoa and black bean squares
description: Moist cocoa bites made with cooked, puréed black beans.
steps: Rinse and drain the cooked beans; they should contain no garlic, onion or other savory seasonings.
Melt the chocolate and butter over a gentle water bath and let cool slightly.
Blend the beans, eggs, sugar and vanilla until smooth. Add the chocolate, cocoa, baking powder and salt.
Pour into a lined 20 × 20 cm pan and bake at 175 °C for 25 to 28 minutes, until set in the center.
Cool for an hour before cutting into twelve squares; they will retain a moist, compact texture.
tips: This is a creative adaptation using beans, not a historic Cuban sweet.

title: Fresh corn and cheese cake
description: A baked fresh corn cake with crumbled white cheese.
steps: Blend the corn and milk until finely textured. Grease and line a 23 cm pan.
Beat the eggs, sugar and lukewarm melted butter. Add the blended corn.
Add the flour, baking powder and salt, followed by the crumbled cheese. Mix without overbeating.
Bake at 175 °C for 45 to 55 minutes, until the center is set and cooked.
Rest in the pan for 20 minutes and cool for another 25 before slicing; serve warm.
tips: Use mild pasteurized cheese to balance the corn.

title: Pineapple phyllo rolls
description: Thin, crisp rolls filled with cooked pineapple and coconut.
steps: Cook the pineapple and sugar for 8 minutes. Add the cornstarch dissolved in water, coconut and cinnamon; boil for 2 minutes and cool.
Keep the phyllo under a barely damp cloth. Stack three thin layers brushed with butter.
Cut rectangles, place filling at one end, fold in the sides and roll up. Repeat to make ten rolls.
Place seam-side down, brush with butter and bake at 190 °C for 20 to 25 minutes, until golden.
Wait 15 minutes before serving; the pineapple retains a lot of heat.
tips: Do not soak the cloth or the filling: phyllo tears when wet.

title: Coffee flan
description: Milk and concentrated coffee flan with light caramel.
steps: Make an amber caramel with the sugar and water and coat the bottom of a 20 cm mold.
Mix the eggs, condensed milk, whole milk and cold coffee without foaming. Strain over the caramel.
Cover with foil and place in a roasting pan with hot water halfway up the sides.
Bake at 170 °C for 60 to 70 minutes, until set and the center reaches 71 °C.
Cool outside the water bath for 30 minutes and refrigerate for 4 hours. Loosen the edges and unmold cold.
tips: The strength depends on the coffee; do not replace it with the same volume of instant coffee powder.

title: Cream cheese flan
description: A firmer, creamier flan made with cream cheese.
steps: Caramelize the sugar and water and spread in a 22 cm mold. Let harden.
Mix the cream cheese and condensed milk until smooth; add the milk, eggs and vanilla without vigorous beating.
Strain into the mold, cover and place in a roasting pan with hot water halfway up the sides.
Bake at 165 °C for 65 to 75 minutes, until set and the center registers at least 71 °C.
Cool for 30 minutes and refrigerate for at least 4 hours before unmolding.
tips: Slightly softened cream cheese blends with fewer lumps.

title: Mamey flan
description: Mamey pulp blended into a milk and caramel flan.
steps: Make caramel with the sugar and water and coat the base of a 22 cm mold.
Blend the mamey and milk; strain if fibers remain. Add the condensed milk, eggs and vanilla.
Pour over the caramel, cover and set the mold in a roasting pan with hot water for a water bath.
Bake at 170 °C for 65 to 75 minutes, until set and the center reaches 71 °C.
Cool for 30 minutes and refrigerate for at least 4 hours before inverting onto a deep plate.
tips: The pulp should be ripe and completely free of seed and skin.

title: Coconut and pineapple bread pudding
description: Bread soaked in coconut milk with cooked pineapple and shredded coconut.
steps: Soak the torn bread in both milks for 15 minutes. Grease a 22 cm pan with the butter.
Cook the pineapple with one-third of the sugar for 8 minutes, until the liquid reduces; let cool slightly.
Mix the eggs, remaining sugar and vanilla; combine with the bread, pineapple and coconut.
Pour into the pan and bake in a water bath at 175 °C for 50 to 60 minutes, until set and reaching 71 °C.
Cool for 30 minutes and refrigerate for 2 hours before slicing, or serve warm with a spoon.
tips: Drain the pineapple well so it does not create a watery layer.

title: Sweet potato and raisin pudding
description: A soft pudding of cooked sweet potato, milk and raisins.
steps: Mash the sweet potato and mix with the milk until smooth. Grease a 20 cm pan with some of the butter.
Beat the eggs and sugar; add the remaining melted butter, cinnamon and vanilla.
Combine with the purée and fold in the raisins. Pour into the pan and cover with foil.
Bake in a water bath at 175 °C for 45 to 55 minutes, until set and the center reaches 71 °C.
Cool for 30 minutes and refrigerate for 2 hours before slicing.
tips: Use sweet potato cooked without salt or seasonings from a savory dish.

title: Coconut milk rice pudding with mango
description: Sweet rice cooked with coconut and finished with fresh mango.
steps: Cook the rice, water, cinnamon and salt over low heat for 15 minutes, until much of the water is absorbed.
Add the coconut milk and cook for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring to prevent sticking.
When the rice is tender, add the sugar and cook for another 5 minutes. Remove the cinnamon.
Divide among bowls and cool in shallow containers; refrigerate when no longer steaming.
Add the mango and lime zest just before serving.
tips: Add the mango at the end to preserve its freshness and texture.

title: Chocolate and orange custard
description: Cooked cocoa custard with orange zest.
steps: Mix the cocoa, cornstarch, sugar and yolks with some of the cold milk until free of lumps.
Heat the remaining milk with the zest. Gradually add it to the yolk mixture.
Return to the saucepan and stir over medium-low heat until thickened and gently boiling for 1 minute.
Remove from the heat and add the chopped chocolate; stir until melted.
Divide among six bowls, cover the surface and chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
tips: Avoid grating the white pith of the orange.

title: Egg-free coffee custard
