description: Coffee cream thickened with cornstarch and served cold.
steps: Dissolve the cornstarch and sugar in some of the cold milk.
Heat the remaining milk with the coffee, without letting it boil over.
Add the cornstarch mixture while stirring. Bring to a gentle boil and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the vanilla and divide among six bowls. Sprinkle the cinnamon over the surface.
Cool and refrigerate for 2 hours to let it thicken.
tips: Without eggs, its texture depends on the final boil of the starch.

title: Corn and coconut cream
description: Sweet cream made with strained fresh corn and coconut milk.
steps: Blend the corn with the water and strain, pressing to extract the liquid.
Dissolve the cornstarch in some of the cold coconut milk and mix with the corn liquid.
Add the remaining coconut milk, sugar, cinnamon and salt. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring.
Once thickened, maintain a gentle boil for 4 minutes to cook the corn and starch. Remove the cinnamon.
Divide among shallow containers, cool and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
tips: The cornstarch quantity compensates for variations in fresh corn's starch content.

title: Guava and yogurt mousse
description: Chilled yogurt, cream and guava mousse set with gelatin.
steps: Bloom the gelatin in the cold water for 10 minutes. Mix the yogurt and guava until smooth.
Gently heat the gelatin until dissolved without boiling. Add two tablespoons of the yogurt mixture to temper it.
Stir this mixture into the remaining yogurt to avoid strands of gelatin.
Whip the cold cream with the powdered sugar to soft peaks and gently fold it in.
Divide among eight small glasses and refrigerate for 4 hours before serving.
tips: Do not add very hot gelatin directly to whipped cream.

title: Egg-free mango mousse
description: Mango and whipped cream in a soft mousse stabilized with gelatin.
steps: Blend the mango with the lime juice. Bring to a gentle boil for 5 minutes and cool completely in a shallow container, about 30 minutes.
Bloom the gelatin in cold water for 10 minutes. Heat gently until dissolved, without boiling.
Mix the gelatin with a few spoonfuls of room-temperature mango purée, then stir in the rest to avoid lumps.
Whip the cold cream with the powdered sugar to soft peaks, without turning it into butter.
Gently fold the mango into the cream and divide among six glasses.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, until the mousse holds an airy, firm texture when a spoon is inserted.
tips: The mango and gelatin mixture should be lukewarm, not hot, when folding in the cream.

title: Cocoa and avocado cream
description: A cold dessert of avocado blended with cocoa and coconut milk.
steps: Open the avocados, remove the pits and skins and discard any darkened parts.
Place the flesh in a blender with the cocoa, coconut milk, honey, vanilla and salt.
Blend until smooth, stopping the machine to scrape the mixture down the sides.
Divide among four glasses and cover the surface directly to limit contact with air.
Refrigerate for an hour and serve cold the same day.
tips: This is a creative combination, not a historic Cuban dessert.

title: Egg-free coconut ice cream
description: Coconut milk and cream ice cream with hydrated shredded coconut.
steps: Heat the coconut milk with the sugar and shredded coconut for 5 minutes, stirring to dissolve.
Cool the saucepan over ice water and refrigerate the mixture for 2 hours.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold in the cold coconut base and vanilla.
Transfer to a wide container and freeze. Stir every 30 minutes during the first 2 hours.
Freeze for another 6 hours and soften for 5 to 10 minutes before serving.
tips: Light coconut milk produces a more icy, less creamy texture.

title: Guava and cheese ice cream
description: Creamy cheese ice cream with guava swirls.
steps: Mix the cream cheese, condensed milk, milk and vanilla until free of lumps.
Whip the very cold cream to soft peaks and fold into the cheese mixture.
Pour half into a wide container and add half the guava in spoonfuls.
Repeat the layers and draw a spoon through twice to create swirls without fully blending.
Freeze for at least 8 hours and soften for a few minutes before scooping.
tips: The guava must be thick; a very runny sauce forms large ice crystals.

title: Mango and lemon sorbet
description: Fruit sorbet with light syrup and lemon juice.
steps: Boil the water and sugar for 2 minutes to make a light syrup. Cool completely.
Blend the mango, lemon and syrup until smooth.
Transfer to a wide container and freeze for 2 hours, until firm around the edges.
Break up the crystals with a fork and briefly blend with an immersion blender; return to the freezer.
Repeat once and freeze for a total of about 6 hours. Soften for 5 minutes before serving.
tips: A ripe mango with few fibers produces a finer texture.

title: Mamey and coconut milk ice pops
description: Fruit ice pops with coconut milk, without cow's milk.
steps: Remove the mamey skin, seed and thick fibers before weighing the pulp.
Blend the pulp with the coconut milk, sugar and vanilla until smooth.
Divide among eight food-safe 100 ml molds, leaving 1 cm of space for expansion.
Insert the sticks and freeze for at least 6 hours.
Briefly wet the outside of each mold with water to release the ice pop, without letting water enter.
tips: Stir the coconut milk well to incorporate the fat before blending.

title: Cooked pineapple gelatin
description: Fresh pineapple gelatin made with previously boiled fruit so it can set.
steps: Reserve 70 ml of the water to bloom the gelatin for 10 minutes, leaving it undisturbed until swollen.
Blend the pineapple and remaining water; bring to a boil with the sugar and boil for 10 minutes.
Strain and measure about 700 ml of liquid; top up with drinking water if it has reduced too much.
Off the heat, dissolve the bloomed gelatin and add the lemon. Divide among eight small molds.
Let the strong heat dissipate and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, until set.
tips: Boil the pineapple before adding gelatin; raw pineapple may prevent it from setting.

title: Oranges filled with chilled cream
description: Orange skins used as bowls for a citrus cream dessert.

ingredients.name: Large oranges
ingredients.note: to serve the cream in 8 halves; reserve the extracted juice

ingredients.name: Juice extracted from the oranges
ingredients.note: 400 ml total: extracted from the 4 oranges above; add extra juice only to make up any shortfall

steps: Wash and halve the four oranges. Remove the flesh without breaking the skins, squeeze it and measure 400 ml of juice; add only enough extra juice to make up any shortfall.
Mix the juice, yolks, sugar and cornstarch. Cook, stirring, until thickened and gently boiling for 1 minute.
Add the butter and transfer the custard to a shallow container. Cool completely in the refrigerator.
Whip the cold cream to soft peaks and fold into the orange custard. Divide among the clean, dry orange skins.
Refrigerate for 2 hours before serving with a teaspoon.
tips: The skins are serving containers and do not need to be eaten.

title: Spiced roasted pineapple
description: Pineapple wedges browned in the oven with cinnamon and honey.
steps: Cut the pineapple into 2 cm wedges, removing the tough core.
Mix the honey, melted butter, cinnamon, lime and ginger.
Coat the wedges and arrange in a baking dish in a single layer.
Bake at 210 °C for 20 to 25 minutes, turning halfway through and basting with the juices.
Let cool for 10 minutes and serve with the sauce from the dish.
tips: Firm pineapple holds its shape better than very ripe pineapple.

title: Ripe plantains filled with cheese and honey
description: Roasted plantains with white cheese melted in the center.
steps: Peel the plantains and place them whole in a lightly greased baking dish.
Spread with butter and sprinkle with cinnamon. Bake at 200 °C for 20 minutes.
Cut a lengthwise slit without cutting through the bottom and fill with crumbled cheese.
Bake for another 10 to 15 minutes, until the plantain is tender and the cheese hot.
Add the honey after removing from the oven and let cool for 10 minutes before serving.
tips: You need plantains with very dark skins for a sweet, soft result.

title: Sweet potato in orange syrup
description: Sweet potato cubes cooked in citrus syrup while keeping their shape.
steps: Cut the sweet potato into 3 cm cubes and rinse to remove surface starch.
Boil the water, juice, sugar, cinnamon and orange peel for 5 minutes.
Add the sweet potato and simmer gently for 25 to 30 minutes without vigorous stirring.
When tender, remove the cinnamon and peel. If the syrup needs thickening, lift out the cubes and reduce only the liquid.
Cool the sweet potato in the syrup and refrigerate until serving.
tips: Gently shaking the pan preserves the cubes better than stirring with a spoon.

title: Peanut cream cups
description: Cooked milk and peanut cream finished with roasted peanuts.
steps: Dissolve the cornstarch and sugar in some of the cold milk.
Heat the remaining milk with the peanut butter, stirring until incorporated.
Add the dissolved cornstarch and cook, stirring, until gently boiling for 2 minutes.
Add the vanilla and divide among six glasses. Cool and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Scatter the chopped peanuts over the top just before serving to preserve their texture.
tips: Stir the bottom of the saucepan continuously: peanut butter can stick.

title: Layered coconut and coffee gelatin
description: Two firm layers of coconut and coffee served in clear glasses.
steps: Bloom half the gelatin in half the water for 10 minutes.
Heat the coconut milk with its sugar and vanilla, remove from the heat and dissolve the bloomed gelatin.
Divide among six glasses and refrigerate for 45 to 60 minutes, until the surface can support another layer.
Bloom the remaining gelatin in the reserved water. Dissolve in the hot coffee with its sugar.
Let the coffee cool and slowly pour it over a spoon held just above the coconut layer.
Refrigerate for another 3 hours, until both layers are set.
tips: Hot coffee would melt the first layer; add it lukewarm and still liquid.

title: Water-based soursop champola
description: A drink of soursop pulp, water and lemon, without milk.
steps: Check the pulp and remove all black seeds and any remaining skin.
Dissolve the sugar in some of the cold water.
Blend the soursop with the remaining water, sweetened water and lemon just until combined.
Strain if you prefer to remove coarse fibers; add the ice to the pitcher.
Stir and immediately serve in four glasses.
tips: Remove the seeds before blending, not afterward.

title: Homemade cortadito
description: Concentrated coffee mellowed with a small amount of hot milk.
steps: Prepare concentrated coffee in your coffee maker according to its instructions.
Heat the milk in a saucepan without letting it boil over.
Dissolve the sugar in the freshly brewed coffee.
Divide the coffee among four small cups and add the same quantity of hot milk.
Stir each cup to blend the coffee and milk and serve immediately while hot and aromatic.
tips: Serve in small portions; this drink contains caffeine.

title: Iced coffee with condensed milk
description: Chilled coffee mixed with condensed milk and ice.
steps: Prepare the coffee and add the condensed milk while it is hot.
Stir until completely dissolved and let the strong heat dissipate.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes so the ice does not melt immediately.
Divide the ice between two glasses and add the sweetened coffee.
Top up with cold milk and stir before drinking.
tips: You can make coffee ice cubes to dilute the drink less.

title: Pineapple and cinnamon infusion
description: A drink of thoroughly washed pineapple peel boiled with cinnamon.
steps: Wash and scrub the whole pineapple under running water before peeling. Discard damaged parts and reserve the clean peel.
Place the peel, water, cinnamon and cloves in a pot and bring to a boil.
Simmer gently for 20 minutes, cover and steep for 10 minutes.
Strain through a fine sieve and add the sugar and lemon to the liquid.
Serve warm, or cool and refrigerate before drinking; do not leave it to ferment.
tips: This is a culinary drink, without claims of medicinal or detoxifying effects.

title: Warm corn and coconut drink
description: Fine cornmeal cooked into a slightly thick drink.
steps: Mix the cornmeal into some of the cold water.
Heat the remaining water, coconut milk, cinnamon and salt in a saucepan.
Pour in the corn mixture in a thin stream while stirring to prevent lumps.
Cook over low heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring; add the sugar during the final 5 minutes.
Remove the cinnamon and serve warm in cups; add hot water if you prefer a thinner texture.
tips: Use fine cornmeal, not cornstarch or nixtamalized masa.

title: Coconut-crusted shrimp
description: Large shrimp with a crisp breadcrumb and coconut coating.
steps: Pat the shrimp dry and season with salt. Prepare separate dishes of flour, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs mixed with coconut.
Coat each shrimp in flour, egg and the coconut mixture, pressing gently to adhere.
Let the coating rest in the refrigerator for 10 minutes. Heat the oil to 170 °C.
Fry in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until golden with firm, opaque flesh; check for 63 °C if their size allows measurement.
Drain on a rack and serve with freshly squeezed lemon.
tips: Coconut browns quickly; lower the heat slightly if it darkens before the shrimp cooks.

title: Griddled shrimp with orange mojo
description: Browned shrimp finished with a quick orange, garlic and oregano mojo.
steps: Crush the garlic and mix with the juices, oil, oregano, salt and pepper. Reserve half in a clean container.
Marinate the shrimp in the other half for 10 minutes in the refrigerator.
Drain and discard the used marinade. Heat a griddle and cook the shrimp for about 2 minutes per side.
Check that the flesh is firm, pearly and opaque. Heat the reserved mojo in a saucepan for 2 minutes.
Pour the hot mojo over the shrimp and serve immediately.
tips: Reserve the sauce before it touches raw shrimp so it can be used at the end.

title: Shrimp in mango sauce
description: Ripe mango sauce and mild sofrito with shrimp cooked at the end.
steps: Sauté the chopped onion and bell pepper in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and cumin for 30 seconds.
Blend the mango with the water and lime into a smooth sauce.
Add to the sofrito with the salt and cook over low heat for 8 minutes.
Add the shrimp and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until firm and opaque.
Check the seasoning and serve with the hot sauce.
tips: Use ripe mango that has not fermented; no added sugar is needed.

title: Shrimp with okra and tomato
description: Okra stewed with tomato and shrimp added at the end.
steps: Wash and dry the okra and trim the ends without opening the small pods. Halve the large ones.
Sauté the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, add the garlic, then the okra for 4 minutes.
Add the tomato, stock, bay leaf, salt and lemon. Cover and cook for 15 minutes, until the okra softens.
Add the shrimp and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until the flesh is opaque and firm.
Remove the bay leaf, adjust the consistency with a small amount of hot water if needed and serve.
tips: Avoid vigorous stirring so the pods do not break.

title: Shrimp and pineapple skewers
description: Shrimp alternated with pineapple and bell pepper for cooking on a griddle.
steps: Mix the oil, lime, crushed garlic, salt and paprika. Marinate the shrimp for 10 minutes in the refrigerator.
Cut the pineapple and pepper into pieces about 2 cm across so they cook at a similar rate.
Thread onto metal skewers, alternating shrimp, pineapple and pepper without packing tightly.
Cook on a hot griddle for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until browned and the shrimp are fully cooked.
Serve immediately; the shrimp flesh should be firm and opaque all the way through.
tips: You can blanch the pepper for 2 minutes before threading if you prefer it very tender.

title: Shrimp with pumpkin and coconut
description: Pumpkin cubes cooked in coconut milk with shrimp and ginger.
steps: Cut the pumpkin into 2 cm cubes. Sauté the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 6 minutes.
Add the pumpkin, stock, coconut milk and salt. Simmer gently for 15 to 18 minutes, until softened.
Mash a few cubes against the side of the pan to thicken the sauce.
Add the shrimp and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until firm, pearly and opaque.
Stir in the lemon off the heat and serve hot.
tips: Add the shellfish only when the pumpkin is already tender.

title: Cheesy shrimp gratin
description: Shrimp in a light white sauce with cheese and golden breadcrumbs.
steps: Sauté the chopped onion in the butter for 5 minutes. Add the flour and stir for 1 minute.
Whisk in the milk gradually; cook for 4 minutes until thickened. Season with salt and pepper.
Add the raw shrimp and mix. Divide among four small ovenproof dishes.
Top with cheese and breadcrumbs; bake at 200 °C for 12 to 15 minutes, until bubbling, golden and reaching 74 °C in the center.
Rest for 5 minutes before bringing the dishes to the table.
tips: Use shallow dishes so the filling heats evenly.

title: Ham-wrapped shrimp
description: Large shrimp wrapped in strips of cooked ham and browned in a skillet.
steps: Pat the shrimp dry and season with pepper. Cut the ham into strips and wrap each shrimp.
Secure with short wooden toothpicks and place on a clean plate.
Heat the oil with the chopped garlic for 30 seconds. Brown the shrimp for about 2 minutes on each side.
Add the orange juice, cover and cook for another 2 minutes, until the shrimp are opaque and firm.
Remove all toothpicks before serving and sprinkle with chopped parsley.
tips: Ham already adds salt; taste before adding more.

title: Shrimp-stuffed squid
description: Squid tubes stewed with a shrimp and vegetable filling.
steps: Chop the tentacles and shrimp. Sauté half the onion, pepper and garlic in half the oil for 6 minutes.
Add the chopped shellfish and cook for 4 minutes, until opaque. Mix with the breadcrumbs and cool for 10 minutes.
Fill the tubes three-quarters full and close with toothpicks without compressing the filling.
Sauté the remaining vegetables in the remaining oil; add the tomato, stock, salt and bay leaf.
Add the squid, cover and cook gently for 30 to 40 minutes, until tender and the center reaches 74 °C.
Remove the bay leaf and all toothpicks before serving with the sauce.
tips: Leave space because the tubes contract during cooking.

title: Griddled squid with parsley
description: Squid opened out and briefly seared, finished with garlic, lemon and parsley.
steps: Open the squid tubes into sheets, pat dry and lightly score the inside in a crosshatch without cutting through.
Mix half the oil with the chopped garlic and parsley; reserve separately for finishing.
Coat the squid with the remaining oil and season. Cook in batches on a very hot griddle for 1 to 2 minutes per side.
Check that the inside is opaque and reaches 63 °C when measurable. Transfer to a serving dish.
Heat the reserved dressing for 30 seconds, add the lemon and spoon over the squid.
tips: Drying squid thoroughly lets it brown instead of boiling in its own liquid.

title: Cornmeal-crusted squid rings
description: Squid rings coated with fine cornmeal and breadcrumbs.
steps: Pat the rings dry and season with salt. Prepare wheat flour, beaten egg, and a cornmeal, breadcrumb and paprika mixture in three dishes.
Coat each ring in that order and rest in the refrigerator for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil to 175 °C and fry in small batches to prevent the temperature from dropping too much.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until golden and the squid is fully opaque; check for 63 °C if the thickness allows measurement.
Drain on a rack and serve with lemon wedges.
tips: Very thick rings need more time than thin ones; do not mix widely different sizes.

title: Squid stewed with coconut and sweet potato
description: A slow squid stew with sweet potato and coconut milk.
steps: Cut the squid into large pieces and the sweet potato into 2 cm cubes.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil for 7 minutes. Add the tomato and cumin and cook for another 5 minutes.
Add the squid, water, coconut milk and salt; cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes.
Add the sweet potato and cook for another 20 to 25 minutes, until both are tender; add hot water if the sauce dries out.
Uncover for the final minutes to adjust the consistency and serve hot.
tips: Add the sweet potato later so it does not fall apart while the squid cooks.

title: Squid stir-fry with pineapple and pepper
description: A quick stir-fry with pineapple, pepper and a light sweet-and-sour sauce.
steps: Mix the soy sauce, lime, water, cornstarch and sugar until dissolved. Pat the squid strips dry.
Heat half the oil and briefly stir-fry the squid in batches until opaque; remove to a clean plate.
Add the remaining oil, garlic, pepper and pineapple; sauté for 5 minutes, retaining some firmness.
Stir the sauce and add it; boil for 1 minute to thicken.
Return the squid, toss for 1 minute and serve when completely cooked and hot.
tips: Soy sauce often contains wheat; check its label.

title: Griddled octopus with green mojo
description: Previously cooked octopus browned on a griddle and served with herb mojo.
steps: Pat the cooked octopus dry and divide the tentacles into manageable pieces.
Blend the parsley, cilantro, garlic, lemon, water, salt and two-thirds of the oil into a mojo.
Coat the octopus with the remaining oil and heat a griddle thoroughly.
Brown in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until the center reaches 74 °C.
Serve with the freshly prepared mojo over the octopus or in a separate bowl.
tips: The recipe starts with cooked octopus; the griddle is used to brown and reheat it.

title: Octopus in citrus vinaigrette
description: Cooked octopus served cold with peppers and an orange and lemon dressing.
steps: Slice the cold cooked octopus into rounds about 1 cm thick.
Wash the vegetables and finely dice the peppers and onion.
Whisk the citrus juices with the oil, oregano and salt until lightly emulsified.
Mix the octopus and vegetables with the vinaigrette and refrigerate in a covered container for 45 minutes.
Stir once before serving and keep the remainder chilled.
tips: The citrus is a dressing: the octopus used here must already be fully cooked.

title: Octopus with tomato and olives
description: Cooked octopus finished in a tomato, olive and white wine sauce.
steps: Sauté the onion in the oil for 7 minutes. Add the garlic and paprika and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the wine and boil for 3 minutes. Add the tomato, bay leaf and salt and cook for 10 minutes.
Cut the octopus into pieces and add it with the drained olives.
Cook over low heat for 8 to 10 minutes, until the octopus is hot in the center and reaches 74 °C.
Remove the bay leaf and adjust the salt after tasting the olives.
tips: Use tender cooked octopus; a brief stew will not tenderize raw octopus.

title: Individual crab gratins
description: Crabmeat in white sauce with a golden cheese topping.
steps: Carefully check the crabmeat for small shell fragments and remove them.
Sauté the chopped onion and pepper in the butter for 6 minutes. Add the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually add the milk, stirring to form a sauce. Add the crab, lemon, salt and pepper.
Divide among four small dishes, cover with cheese and breadcrumbs and bake at 200 °C for 12 to 15 minutes, until the center reaches 74 °C.
Rest for 5 minutes on a heatproof surface before taking the dishes to the table.
tips: Fold in the crab gently to preserve its strands.

title: Crab and corn cakes
description: Crab cakes with corn, pepper and a light crust.
steps: Check the crab for shell fragments and remove them. Very finely chop the onion and pepper.
Mix the egg, mayonnaise, mustard, lemon and salt. Add the vegetables, corn, crab and breadcrumbs without breaking up the mixture too much.
Shape into eight cakes 1.5 cm thick and refrigerate for 30 minutes to help them hold their shape.
Heat the oil over medium heat and cook for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until golden and the center reaches 74 °C.
Drain briefly and serve two cakes per portion.
tips: If they break during shaping, chill the mixture before adding more breadcrumbs.

title: Crab stewed with pumpkin
description: Tender pumpkin and cooked crabmeat in tomato sofrito.
steps: Cut the pumpkin into 2 cm cubes and check the crab for any shell fragments.
Sauté the onion and pepper in the oil for 7 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the pumpkin, stock, bay leaf and salt; cover and cook for 15 to 18 minutes, until softened.
Add the crab and heat gently for 5 to 7 minutes, until the center of the stew reaches 74 °C.
Remove the bay leaf and serve without excessive stirring.
tips: Adding the crab at the end keeps its meat from breaking apart.

title: Baked lobster with orange butter
description: Opened lobster tails baked with garlic and orange.

ingredients.name: Raw lobster tails
ingredients.note: 4 tails of about 250 g each, in their shells

steps: Use kitchen shears to cut along the tops of the shells. Open slightly, remove the intestinal vein and keep the meat attached at the base.
Melt the butter with the chopped garlic; add the orange, paprika and salt and cook for 2 minutes.
Place the tails in a baking dish and distribute the sauce over the exposed meat.
Bake at 200 °C for 12 to 18 minutes, depending on thickness, until the meat is firm and opaque and reaches 63 °C.
Rest for 5 minutes and sprinkle with parsley before serving.
tips: Measure the temperature in the thickest part without touching the shell.

title: Lobster in coconut and ginger sauce
description: Lobster meat briefly cooked in a coconut and ginger sauce.
steps: Cut the lobster meat into 3 cm medallions and keep refrigerated while preparing the sauce.
Sauté the onion and pepper in the oil for 7 minutes. Add the garlic and grated ginger for 1 minute.
Add the coconut milk, stock and salt and cook over low heat for 8 minutes.
Add the lobster and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, until the meat is firm and opaque and reaches 63 °C.
Stir in the lime off the heat and serve hot.
tips: Keep the sauce at a gentle simmer to avoid unnecessarily toughening the lobster.

title: Shrimp-stuffed lobster
description: Opened lobster tails topped with a shrimp, breadcrumb and cream stuffing.
steps: Open the shells along the top, remove the intestinal vein and keep the meat attached at the base. Place in a baking dish.
Sauté the onion in half the butter for 5 minutes. Add the chopped shrimp and cook until opaque, about 3 minutes.
Add the cream, breadcrumbs, parsley, lemon, salt and pepper. Mix and let cool for 10 minutes.
Divide the stuffing over the tails and scatter small pieces of the remaining butter over the top.
Bake at 190 °C for 18 to 22 minutes, until the meat is opaque and the center of the stuffing reaches 74 °C.
tips: Do not press down the stuffing: a loose layer heats more easily.

title: Mussels in creole sauce
description: Mussels steamed open in a tomato and pepper sofrito.
steps: Scrub the shells under cold water and remove the beards. Discard broken shells and open mussels that do not close when tapped.
Sauté the onion and pepper in the oil for 7 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato and cook for 8 minutes.
Pour in the wine and boil for 2 minutes. Add the mussels and cover the pan.
Cook for 5 to 7 minutes, gently shaking the pan, until they open. Discard any that remain closed.
Add the parsley and pepper and serve with the sauce, tasting before adding salt.
tips: Buy shellfish from a controlled commercial source and keep them chilled until cooking.

title: Clams in mojo broth
description: Clams steamed open in a quick garlic and citrus broth.
steps: Rinse the purged clams under cold water. Discard broken shells and open clams that do not close when tapped.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil over medium-low heat for 7 minutes.
Add the water, orange and oregano and boil for 3 minutes.
Add the clams, cover and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, until they open. Discard any that remain closed.
Add the lemon and parsley at the end and serve with the hot broth.
tips: Do not add salt before tasting: clams contribute their own salinity.

title: Conch stewed with tomato
description: Conch meat tenderized first and finished in creole sauce.

ingredients.name: Cleaned conch meat
ingredients.note: edible portion only, from a food supplier

steps: Inspect the cleaned meat, remove any remaining tough membranes and gently flatten with a kitchen mallet.
Place in a pot with the water, half the onion, one garlic clove and bay leaf. Simmer gently with the pot partially covered for 45 to 60 minutes or longer, until a fork enters without resistance.
Remove, reserve a cup of the broth and cut the conch into small pieces; discard the bay leaf.
Sauté the remaining onion, pepper and garlic in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the cumin, tomato, vinegar and salt and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the conch and reserved broth and cook covered for another 10 to 15 minutes, until the sauce comes together.
Check the tenderness before serving; if still resistant, continue cooking with small additions of hot water.
tips: Lemon or vinegar cannot replace cooking the conch.

title: Chickpea Salad with Avocado and Sweet Pepper
description: Tender chickpeas with avocado, sweet pepper, and a lemon and cumin vinaigrette.
steps: Rinse the chickpeas if canned and drain thoroughly. Wash and dry the vegetables before cutting them.
Remove the seeds from the peppers. Dice the peppers, tomato, and onion finely and chop the cilantro.
Whisk the lemon juice, oil, cumin, and salt in the bottom of a salad bowl until combined.
Add the chickpeas and chopped vegetables; mix, cover, and refrigerate for 15 minutes to absorb the dressing.
Cut the avocado at the end, fold it in gently, and divide into four servings.
tips: A firm, ripe avocado holds its shape better when mixed.

title: Black Bean and Mango Salad
description: Black beans with firm mango, bell pepper, and a sour orange dressing.
steps: Drain the beans without crushing them; if canned, rinse and let excess water drain away.
Cut the mango flesh and bell pepper into one-centimeter dice. Finely chop the onion and cilantro.
Mix the sour orange juice, oil, oregano, and salt in a large container with a lid.
Add the beans, mango, pepper, and onion. Stir from the bottom with a wide spoon.
Refrigerate for 20 minutes, add the cilantro, and taste the dressing before serving the salad cold.
tips: Overripe mango falls apart; choose one firm enough to cut into distinct cubes.

title: Chilled Sweet Potato and Orange Salad
description: Cooked sweet potato with orange segments, red onion, and parsley.
steps: Cut the sweet potato into two-centimeter cubes and boil for 12 to 18 minutes, until tender but intact.
Drain and spread in a shallow container. Let the steam subside for a few minutes, then refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Peel the oranges over a bowl to catch their juice; separate the segments and remove seeds and thick membranes.
Whisk the collected juice with the oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper. Slice the onion very thinly.
Gently mix the cold sweet potato, orange, and onion with the dressing; finish with chopped parsley and serve.
tips: Test the sweet potato early with a fork so it does not turn into a mash.

title: Cassava Salad with Cilantro and Cucumber
description: Cooked and chilled sweet cassava with cucumber and a light mojo dressing.
steps: Check that the cassava is completely peeled. Cut into pieces and boil in plenty of water for 25 to 35 minutes, until very tender.
Discard all the cooking water, remove the central fibrous core, and cut the cassava into bite-sized cubes.
Spread the cubes in a shallow container and refrigerate for 40 minutes once the steam has subsided.
Chop the garlic and cilantro; whisk with the lemon juice, oil, and salt. Slice cucumber and onion into thin half-moons.
Combine the cold cassava with the vegetables and mojo. Mix gently to keep the cubes intact.
tips: Use only commercially sold sweet cassava; discard the cooking water.

title: Malanga Salad with Egg and Parsley
description: Diced malanga with hard-boiled eggs and a mild mustard dressing.
steps: Cut the malanga into even cubes and boil for 18 to 25 minutes, until tender in the center. Drain.
In a separate saucepan, gently boil the eggs in water for about 10 to 12 minutes, until whites and yolks are firm.
Cool the eggs in cold water and peel them. Spread the malanga in a shallow container and refrigerate for 40 minutes.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, mustard, and salt. Finely chop the onion and quarter the eggs.
Dress the cold malanga with onion and parsley; arrange the eggs on top so they do not break up when mixed.
tips: If the malanga is very floury, add the dressing in two batches to distribute it evenly.

title: Potato and Beet Salad with Yogurt
description: Potatoes and beets with pickles and a creamy plain yogurt dressing.
steps: Cut the potatoes into two-centimeter cubes and boil for 15 to 22 minutes, until tender but not falling apart.
Drain the potatoes, spread them in a shallow container, and chill in the refrigerator for about 40 minutes.
Dice the beets and pickles. Chop the chives, reserving some for the garnish.
Whisk the yogurt, lemon juice, oil, salt, and pepper. First mix the cold potatoes with half of the dressing.
Fold in the beets, pickles, and remaining dressing; stir briefly and finish with chives.
tips: Add the beets at the end for a marbled color instead of tinting the entire salad.

title: Red Cabbage, Pineapple, and Peanut Salad
description: Crunchy cabbage with fresh pineapple and toasted peanuts in a lemon dressing.
steps: Remove any damaged outer cabbage leaves; wash, dry, and cut the remaining cabbage into very thin strips.
Mix the strips with the salt and gently squeeze for one minute to soften them slightly.
Grate the carrot and dice the cored pineapple. Add both to the cabbage.
Whisk the lemon juice, oil, and honey until dissolved. Pour over the salad and refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Roughly chop the peanuts and add just before serving to keep them crunchy.
tips: Keep the peanuts out during the resting time: they absorb the dressing and lose their crunch.

title: Roasted Pumpkin and White Cheese Salad
description: Chilled roasted pumpkin over greens with white cheese and toasted pumpkin seeds.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: 15 ml for roasting and 25 ml for dressing

steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Cut the pumpkin into three-centimeter cubes and mix with 15 ml of oil and half the salt.
Spread in a single layer and roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden and tender.
Transfer the pumpkin to a shallow container and refrigerate for about 30 minutes to serve it cold.
Whisk the remaining oil with vinegar, grated garlic, oregano, and the remaining salt. Wash and dry the lettuce.
Arrange the lettuce, pumpkin, and crumbled cheese; add the dressing and finish with toasted pumpkin seeds.
tips: Drying the leaves keeps their water from diluting the vinaigrette.

title: Ripe Plantain and Watercress Salad
description: Roasted and chilled plantain slices with watercress, tomato, and lemon.

ingredients.name: oil
ingredients.note: 10 ml for roasting and 25 ml for dressing

steps: Peel the plantains and cut into slices one and a half centimeters thick. Brush with 10 ml of oil and arrange on a baking tray.
Bake at 200 °C for 18 to 22 minutes, turning once, until golden without falling apart.
Let the steam subside, then refrigerate the slices in a single layer for 25 minutes. Wash and thoroughly dry the watercress.
Slice the tomato and onion. Whisk the lemon juice, remaining oil, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Arrange the watercress on a platter and add the cold plantain, tomato, and onion; dress just before serving.
tips: Choose yellow plantains with dark spots that are still firm enough to slice.

title: Green Bean and Tomato Salad
description: Just-tender green beans with tomato, olives, and a garlic vinaigrette.
steps: Wash the green beans, trim the ends, and cut each into two or three pieces depending on its length.
Boil for 6 to 8 minutes, until tender with some firmness. Cool in cold water and drain.
Dice the tomato and onion; halve the olives and finely chop the garlic and parsley.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, garlic, and salt. Combine with the drained beans, tomato, onion, and olives.
Refrigerate for 15 minutes and scatter the parsley over the salad before serving.
tips: Drain the green beans thoroughly so the vinaigrette clings to them.

title: Corn and Roasted Pepper Salad
description: Sweet corn, roasted pepper, and onion with a lemon and cilantro dressing.
steps: Drain the corn and pat it lightly dry. If cooked at home, use it already cooled and refrigerated.
Remove any loose skin and seeds from the roasted pepper and cut into short strips. Finely dice the onion.
Whisk the lemon juice, oil, cumin, and salt in a salad bowl until the dressing is evenly combined.
Add the corn, peppers, and onion; mix, cover, and refrigerate for 20 minutes to let the flavors mingle.
Chop the cilantro, fold it in at the end, and stir the salad before dividing it into servings.
tips: Draining jarred peppers helps keep their liquid from diluting the lemon flavor.

title: Lentil Salad with Pickled Onion
description: Whole lentils with carrot and onion softened in vinegar.
steps: Sort and rinse the lentils. Cook with the water and bay leaf for 20 to 30 minutes, until tender but still intact.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the onion and mix with vinegar, sugar, and half the salt; let stand for 20 minutes.
Drain the lentils, discard the bay leaf, and spread in a shallow container. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Grate the carrot and chop the parsley. Whisk the onion pickling liquid with the oil and remaining salt.
Combine the cold lentils, carrot, onion, and parsley; add the dressing and mix without crushing the lentils.
tips: Start testing the lentils after 20 minutes: some varieties soften sooner.

title: Cold Rice and Vegetable Salad
description: Fluffy rice with cucumber, carrot, corn, and an orange vinaigrette.
steps: Rinse and drain the rice. Put it in a pan with the water and half the salt; bring to a boil, cover, and cook over very low heat for 16 to 18 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let stand for five minutes. Fluff the grains and spread the rice in a shallow container so it can be refrigerated promptly.
Chill in the refrigerator for about 40 minutes. Finely dice the cucumber and carrot, and chop the chives.
Whisk the orange juice, lemon juice, oil, and remaining salt. Drain the corn well before adding it to the bowl.
Mix the cold rice with the vegetables and dressing; serve immediately or keep covered in the refrigerator.
tips: Do not leave rice cooling on the counter for hours; spread it out and refrigerate once the steam subsides.

title: Macaroni Salad with Tuna and Olives
description: Short pasta with tuna, pepper, and olives in a yogurt and mayonnaise dressing.
steps: Cook the macaroni in water according to its package, usually 8 to 12 minutes, until tender but firm.
Drain and briefly cool under cold drinking water. Drain again thoroughly so the dressing does not become watery.
Whisk the yogurt, mayonnaise, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Cut the pepper and olives into small pieces.
Mix the pasta, flaked tuna, pepper, and olives with the dressing. Add the chopped parsley.
Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes before serving; stir once to redistribute the dressing at the bottom.
tips: The saltiness of tuna and olives varies; taste the mixture before adding more salt.

title: Beet Salad with Orange and Cumin
description: Cooked beets with orange segments and a cumin vinaigrette.
steps: Cut the cold beets into thin half-moons and place in a container that will not stain easily.
Peel the oranges over a bowl, collect their juice, and separate the segments, removing seeds and thick membranes.
Thinly slice the onion. Whisk the collected juice with the oil, vinegar, cumin, and salt.
Dress the beets and onion, cover, and refrigerate for 20 minutes so they absorb the dressing.
Add the orange segments and cilantro when serving, arranging them carefully over the beets.
tips: Prepare the orange on a separate cutting board if you want to keep its bright color.

title: Hearts of Palm, Cucumber, and Avocado Salad
description: Canned hearts of palm with fresh vegetables and a simple lime dressing.
steps: Drain and briefly rinse the hearts of palm; cut into one-centimeter rounds and drain again.
Wash and dry the cucumber and tomato. Cut into bite-sized pieces, removing very watery seeds if necessary.
Whisk the lime juice, oil, salt, and pepper. Chop the parsley and add half to the dressing.
Halve the avocado, remove its pit and skin, dice the flesh, and immediately mix with some of the dressing.
Arrange all the ingredients on a platter, drizzle with the remaining dressing, and finish with the remaining parsley.
tips: If preparing the vegetables ahead, add the avocado and dressing just before serving.

title: Chayote Salad with Onion and Lemon
description: Cooked and chilled chayote with onion, cilantro, and a touch of oregano.
steps: Wash and peel the chayotes, remove the firm center, and cut into slices half a centimeter thick.
Boil for 12 to 18 minutes, until tender without falling apart. Drain well.
Spread in a shallow container and refrigerate for 35 minutes. Thinly slice the onion.
Mix the lemon juice, oil, oregano, salt, and pepper; leave the onion in this dressing for ten minutes while the chayote cools.
Combine the cold chayote, onion, and dressing. Fold in chopped cilantro and serve on a shallow platter.
tips: Chayote has a mild flavor: cut it thinly so the dressing coats it evenly.

title: Carrot Salad with Raisins and Coconut
description: Grated carrot with raisins softened in orange juice and toasted coconut.
steps: Soak the raisins in the orange juice for 15 minutes to soften them slightly.
Wash, peel, and coarsely grate the carrots; place them in a salad bowl.
Toast the coconut in a dry skillet over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, and remove as soon as it colors.
Whisk the raisin soaking juice with the lemon juice, oil, salt, and cinnamon. Mix with the carrot and raisins.
Add the cooled coconut when serving, reserving a little to scatter on top.
tips: Remove the coconut from the heat as soon as it turns golden: it keeps toasting in the hot pan.

title: Tomato Salad with Crisp Cassava Flatbread
description: Tomato and cucumber with basil and pieces of toasted commercial cassava flatbread.
steps: Wash the tomato and cucumber and cut into bite-sized pieces. Slice the onion very thinly.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper; mix with the vegetables and let stand in the refrigerator for ten minutes.
Meanwhile, toast the ready-made cassava flatbread in a 180 °C oven for 3 to 5 minutes, watching that it does not darken.
Let the flatbread cool on a rack and break it into small pieces with your hands.
Add torn basil to the salad and scatter over the flatbread just before serving so it stays crisp.
tips: Use prepared, ready-to-eat cassava flatbread; this recipe does not start with raw cassava.

title: Chicken Salad with Guava and Celery
description: Cold cooked chicken with fresh guava and celery in a yogurt dressing.
steps: Check that the chicken is cold and shred it into short strands. Keep it refrigerated while preparing the other ingredients.
Wash the guava and celery. Remove the hard seeds from the fruit, dice the flesh, and thinly slice the celery.
Whisk the yogurt, lemon juice, mustard, salt, and pepper into a smooth dressing.
Mix the chicken, guava, and celery with the dressing; cover and refrigerate for 20 minutes before serving.
Wash and dry the lettuce, arrange it on plates, and spoon the cold chicken salad on top.
tips: If cooking chicken for this recipe, cook it to 74 °C at the center and cool it promptly in a shallow container.

title: Ham and Pineapple Party Rolls
description: Small rolls filled with a smooth ham, cream cheese, and drained pineapple spread.

ingredients.name: pineapple packed in its own juice

steps: Drain the pineapple and press it gently with paper towels. Chop it very finely to keep the filling from becoming watery.
Chop the ham and pulse with the cream cheese and mustard until you have a spreadable paste.
Fold in the pineapple, chopped parsley, and pepper with a spoon, leaving small pieces of fruit.
Cover and refrigerate the spread for 20 minutes. Split the rolls without separating their halves completely.
Divide the filling among the twelve rolls, close them, and keep refrigerated until serving.
tips: Ham already contains salt; taste the filling before considering adding more.

title: Chicken Sandwich with Cilantro Mojo
description: Griddled chicken with a fresh cilantro and lemon mojo on toasted bread.
steps: Blend the cilantro, garlic, lemon juice, oil, salt, and cumin. Reserve half the mojo in a clean bowl for serving.
Coat the chicken with the other half of the mojo and marinate in the refrigerator for 20 minutes. Wash and dry the lettuce and tomato.
Cook the cutlets on a hot griddle for about 4 to 6 minutes per side, until the thickest part reaches 74 °C.
Split the rolls and toast their cut sides on the clean griddle for 2 minutes. Slice the tomato.
Fill with lettuce, tomato, and chicken; add the reserved mojo that did not touch raw meat and serve immediately.
tips: Reserving some mojo before marinating keeps the serving sauce separate from raw chicken.

title: Tamarind Pork and Cucumber Roll
description: Cooked pork tossed in a quick tamarind sauce, with fresh cucumber.
steps: Mix the tamarind, water, and sugar until dissolved. Thinly slice the onion and chop the garlic.
Sauté the onion in oil for 5 minutes; add the garlic and stir for half a minute without letting it burn.
Add the pork, tamarind sauce, and salt. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until the sauce reduces and the meat reheats to 74 °C.
Wash and thinly slice the cucumber. Split the rolls and lightly toast the cut sides.
Divide the juicy meat among the rolls, add the cucumber at the end, and serve before the bread gets soggy.
tips: Tamarind varies in acidity; taste the sauce before mixing it with all the meat.

title: Cream Cheese and Roasted Pepper Tea Sandwiches
description: Bread triangles filled with a roasted pepper and cream cheese spread.
steps: Drain the roasted pepper and pat dry with paper towels. Remove any seeds or remaining skin.
Blend the pepper and cream cheese with lemon juice, oregano, and pepper into a thick spread.
Finely chop the olives and fold in with a spoon. Cover and refrigerate the spread for 20 minutes.
Spread the filling over four slices of bread, cover with the other four, and press gently.
Cut each sandwich into four triangles to make sixteen small sandwiches; keep chilled until serving.
tips: A thoroughly chilled spread makes it easier to cut cleanly without squeezing out the filling.

title: Tuna and Avocado Sandwich
description: Canned tuna with avocado, onion, and lemon on toasted bread.
steps: Drain the tuna and flake it into a bowl. Finely chop the onion and cilantro.
Scoop out the avocado flesh and mash with lemon juice, salt, and pepper, leaving a few small chunks.
Gently fold the tuna, onion, and cilantro into the avocado. Taste and adjust the salt.
Toast the eight bread slices for 3 to 4 minutes in total. Wash and slice the tomato.
Divide the filling among four slices of toast, add tomato, and cover with the remaining slices; serve freshly assembled.
tips: If making the filling ahead, cover and refrigerate it; toast the bread just before serving.

title: Pumpkin Omelet Roll
description: Warm bread filled with a skillet-cooked pumpkin and onion omelet.
steps: Thinly slice the pumpkin and chop the onion. Heat 20 ml of oil in a medium skillet.
Add the pumpkin, onion, water, and half the salt. Cover and cook for 10 to 12 minutes; uncover to evaporate the remaining liquid.
Beat the eggs with the cheese, parsley, and remaining salt. Fold in the vegetables once they have cooled slightly.
Heat the remaining oil, add the mixture, and cook over low heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until the center reaches 71 °C.
Cut the omelet into four portions, split and toast the rolls, then fill and serve while the omelet is hot.
tips: Turn the omelet using a plate large enough to cover the entire skillet.

title: Roasted Eggplant and White Cheese Sandwich
description: Golden eggplant, white cheese, and tomato in a pressed sandwich.
steps: Preheat the oven to 210 °C. Cut the eggplant into one-centimeter slices and arrange on a baking tray.
Mix the oil, grated garlic, and salt; brush onto the slices and roast for 20 to 25 minutes, turning halfway through.
Slice the cheese and tomato. Drizzle the roasted eggplant with lemon juice as it comes out of the oven.
Assemble four sandwiches with eggplant, tomato, cheese, and basil, spreading the filling almost to the edges.
Toast in a sandwich press or skillet with gentle pressure for 3 to 5 minutes, until the bread is golden and the center is hot.
tips: Firm white cheese holds its shape better; not every fresh cheese melts.

title: Black Bean and Ripe Plantain Party Rolls
description: Small rolls filled with cumin-scented black bean spread and golden ripe plantain.
steps: Peel the plantains and cut twelve long slices. Finely chop the onion and garlic.
Sauté the onion in 15 ml of oil for 4 minutes; add the garlic, cumin, beans, water, and salt.
Cook for 6 minutes, stirring, until thoroughly reheated; mash into a thick spread and finish with lemon juice.
Brown the plantain slices in the remaining oil for about 3 minutes per side, until tender and caramelized.
Split the rolls, divide the bean spread among them, and place one plantain slice in each; serve warm.
tips: If using refrigerated leftover beans, reheat them to 74 °C before assembling the rolls.

title: Shredded Beef and Melted Cheese Sandwich
description: Previously cooked beef sautéed with sofrito and topped with cheese in pressed bread.
steps: Chop the onion, pepper, and garlic. Sauté the onion and pepper in oil for 5 minutes in a large skillet.
Add the garlic and cumin, stir for half a minute, then add the tomato, water, and salt; cook for 4 minutes.
Add the shredded beef and stir for 5 to 6 minutes, until the filling reaches 74 °C and the sauce is thick.
Split the rolls, divide the beef among them, and cover with cheese. Close without squeezing the filling out.
Press in a sandwich maker or skillet for 3 to 4 minutes, until the cheese melts and the bread is golden; serve cut diagonally.
tips: The filling should be juicy but have no loose liquid that could soak the bread.

title: Lemon Fish and Cabbage Roll
description: Griddled fish fillets with dressed cabbage and a yogurt sauce.

ingredients.name: lemon juice
ingredients.note: 20 ml for the cabbage and 20 ml for the cream

steps: Wash and finely shred the cabbage; mix with 20 ml of lemon juice and one-third of the salt, then let stand for ten minutes.
Mix the yogurt, remaining lemon juice, grated garlic, and chopped parsley. Refrigerate this sauce.
Pat the fillets dry, check for any remaining bones, and season with the remaining salt and pepper.
Cook in oil on a hot griddle for 3 to 5 minutes per side, depending on thickness, until the center reaches 63 °C.
Split and toast the rolls, spread with the sauce, add the fish and drained cabbage, and serve immediately.
tips: Turn the fish only once with a wide spatula to keep the fillets intact.

title: Egg and Olive Tea Sandwiches
description: Hard-boiled egg and olive spread with mustard, served in small triangles.
steps: Put the eggs in a saucepan and cover with water. Gently boil for about 10 to 12 minutes, until whites and yolks are firm.
Transfer the eggs to cold water, peel, and finely chop. Chop the olives and chives into small pieces.
Whisk the mayonnaise, mustard, lemon juice, and pepper. Fold in the egg, olives, and chives with a spoon.
Cover and refrigerate the filling for 25 minutes. Spread over four bread slices and cover with the other four.
Cut each sandwich into four triangles to make sixteen small sandwiches; keep chilled until serving.
tips: Taste the spread before adding salt, because the olives and mustard already contain it.

title: Guava, Cheese, and Sesame Toast
description: Bread slices topped with guava and cheese, baked and finished with sesame seeds.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C and arrange the bread slices on a baking tray without overlapping.
Butter the bread and toast for 3 minutes, just until the surface begins to dry.
Thinly slice the guava paste and cheese. Arrange the guava over the bread and cover with cheese.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and bake for another 4 to 5 minutes, until the cheese is hot and the bread edges are golden.
Remove from the oven, add lemon zest, and serve the eight toasts while the bread is still crisp.
tips: Guava paste slices more easily when cold; use thin slices to balance its sweetness.

title: Turkey Sandwich with Orange Mojo
description: Griddled turkey cutlets with orange and garlic over a layer of avocado.
steps: Mix the orange juice, crushed garlic, oil, oregano, and half the salt. Add the turkey and marinate in the refrigerator for 20 minutes.
Wash and dry the lettuce. Mash the avocado flesh with lemon juice and the remaining salt, and keep chilled.
Drain the cutlets and discard the used marinade. Cook on a hot griddle for 4 to 6 minutes per side, until the center reaches 74 °C.
Toast the bread slices and spread four of them with the seasoned avocado.
Add the lettuce and turkey, cover with the remaining toast, and cut each sandwich in half to serve hot.
tips: Evenly thick cutlets cook more uniformly and help prevent the turkey from drying out.

title: Malanga and Cumin Patty Roll
description: Skillet-browned patties made from cooked malanga, served in bread with yogurt sauce.
steps: Cut the malanga and boil for 20 to 25 minutes, until completely tender. Drain, mash, and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Mix the cold malanga with the egg, fine cornmeal, cumin, and two-thirds of the salt. Form four patties one centimeter thick.
Heat the oil in a skillet and brown the patties over medium heat for about 4 to 5 minutes per side, until the center reaches 71 °C.
Whisk the yogurt, lemon juice, chopped cilantro, and remaining salt. Wash and dry the lettuce, then split the rolls.
Toast the bread, put lettuce and one patty in each roll, and finish with yogurt sauce; serve freshly made.
tips: Drain and cool the malanga thoroughly before adding the egg so the patties hold their shape.

title: Chickpea and Roasted Garlic Tea Sandwiches
description: Chickpea spread with roasted garlic, lemon, and pepper between slices of bread.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: 10 ml for roasting and 25 ml for the spread

steps: Cut the top off the garlic head, drizzle with 10 ml of oil, and wrap in baking parchment and foil.
Roast at 190 °C for 30 to 35 minutes, until the cloves are very soft; let cool for ten minutes.
Squeeze out the garlic flesh and blend with the chickpeas, remaining oil, lemon juice, cumin, and salt; add the water gradually.
Chop the roasted pepper and fold it into the spread. Refrigerate for ten minutes, then spread over four bread slices.
Cover with the remaining slices and cut each sandwich into four squares to make sixteen small sandwiches.
tips: Add only enough water to make a spreadable paste that will not run out at the edges.

title: Chicken with cassava and sweet peppers
description: Tender chicken thighs and cassava in a sofrito and sour orange stew.
steps: Fully peel the cassava, removing the pink layer, and cut it into 5 cm pieces. Boil it in the water listed for cassava for 20 minutes.
Drain and discard that water; remove the central fiber. Meanwhile, pat the chicken dry, season it, and brown it in the oil for 8 minutes.
Transfer the chicken to a plate. Sauté the chopped onion and peppers for 6 minutes; add garlic and oregano and stir for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, sour orange juice, the stew water, and the chicken with its juices. Cover and simmer gently for 25 minutes.
Add the cassava and cook for 15 to 20 minutes, until tender and the chicken reaches 74 °C near but not touching the bone. Adjust the salt and serve.
tips: Use food-grade cassava; do not add its initial cooking water to the stew.

title: Chicken livers with browned onions
description: Fully cooked chicken livers with sweet onion, garlic, and a splash of vinegar.
steps: Remove membranes and any greenish areas from the livers; cut large pieces in half and pat them dry with paper towels.
Slice the onions. Cook them in 2 tablespoons of oil with a pinch of salt for 12 minutes, stirring until browned.
Transfer the onions to a plate and add the remaining oil. Brown the livers in a single layer for 3 minutes on each side.
Add chopped garlic, cumin, pepper, vinegar, and water. Return the onions to the pan and cook, covered, for 4 to 7 minutes.
Use a thermometer to check that the livers reach 74 °C in their thickest part; continue cooking if needed. Adjust the salt and finish with parsley.
tips: Color is not a substitute for measuring the temperature of poultry livers.

title: Chicken gizzards with potatoes and tomatoes
description: Slow-simmered gizzards finished in a tomato sofrito sauce with potatoes.
steps: Check the cleaned gizzards and remove any remaining tough membrane. Put them in a pot with the water, bay leaves, and a pinch of salt.
Bring to a boil, reduce the heat, and simmer, covered, for 90 to 120 minutes, until a knife enters easily and the gizzards have reached 74 °C.
Reserve 500 ml of broth and discard the bay leaves. Cut large gizzards into pieces and peel and dice the potatoes into 3 cm cubes.
Sauté chopped onion and pepper in the oil for 7 minutes. Add garlic and cumin, stir, then add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Add gizzards, potatoes, and reserved broth; simmer, covered, for 20 to 25 minutes until the potatoes are tender. Adjust the salt and serve with the thickened sauce.
tips: Tenderness takes longer than reaching the minimum temperature; test a gizzard before adding the potatoes.

title: Garlic chicken hearts with peppers
description: Halved chicken hearts sautéed with peppers, garlic, and lime.
steps: Trim vessels and excess fat from the hearts, split them lengthwise, and remove clots with paper towels. Season with salt and oregano.
Cut the pepper and onion into strips. Sauté them in 1 tablespoon of oil for 7 minutes and transfer to a plate.
Heat the remaining oil and add the hearts in one layer. Brown for 5 to 6 minutes, turning them to color all sides.
Add sliced garlic, stir for 1 minute, and pour in the water. Cover and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until the thickest pieces reach 74 °C.
Return the vegetables to the pan, add lime juice, and cook for 2 more minutes. If the hearts remain tough, continue cooking, covered, with a little hot water.
tips: Splitting the hearts lets you remove clots and cook them more evenly.

title: Chicken thighs stuffed with spinach and peanuts
description: Chicken thigh rolls filled with spinach, peanuts, and garlic, baked in their juices.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Sauté chopped onion and garlic in half the oil for 5 minutes; add the spinach and let it wilt.
Drain the spinach thoroughly, chop it, and mix with the crushed peanuts. Open out the thighs and season with cumin and salt.
Divide the filling among the thighs, roll each one, and tie with kitchen string. Arrange seam-side down in a baking dish.
Add the sour orange juice, water, and remaining oil. Cover the dish and bake for 30 minutes; uncover and continue for 10 to 15 minutes.
Check for 74 °C in both the meat and the center of the filling. Rest for 5 minutes, remove all string, and serve sliced with the pan juices.
tips: Do not pack the filling too tightly; each roll should close without tearing the meat.

title: Chicken breast with avocado sauce
description: Skillet chicken cutlets with a fresh avocado, cilantro, and lime sauce.
steps: Use cutlets about 2 cm thick. Season the chicken with cumin, salt, and half the crushed garlic; keep the raw meat separate from the sauce ingredients.
Blend avocado, cilantro, lime juice, remaining garlic, and water into a smooth sauce. Transfer to a clean container and keep refrigerated.
Heat the oil in a wide skillet. Cook the cutlets for 5 to 7 minutes on each side without crowding the pan.
Measure 74 °C in the center of the thickest cutlet; if needed, lower the heat and finish cooking before transferring to clean plates.
Serve the freshly cooked chicken with the cold sauce spooned over it. Adjust the sauce seasoning and avoid boiling it to preserve its texture.
tips: Make the sauce shortly before serving to preserve its color and freshness.

title: Chicken and chayote gratin
description: Chicken and tender chayote under a light milk and cheese sauce.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Peel the chayote, remove any tough core, and dice it; boil in the water for 12 minutes and drain.
Season the chicken and brown it in 1 tablespoon of oil for 8 minutes. Remove it and cook chopped onion and garlic in the remaining oil for 5 minutes.
Add the flour and stir for 1 minute. Gradually pour in the milk, whisk, and cook for 4 minutes until thickened; add nutmeg and salt.
Combine chicken, chayote, and sauce in a baking dish. Top with cheese and bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the surface is golden and the center is hot.
Check for 74 °C in the center of the gratin and in the chicken. Rest for 5 minutes before serving so the sauce can settle.
tips: Drain the chayote thoroughly so it does not water down the sauce during baking.

title: Chicken with skillet corn tamal
description: Chicken in sofrito thickened with ground sweet corn into a creamy casserole.
steps: Cut the chicken into 3 cm cubes and season it. Blend the corn with 350 ml of the stock into a thick mixture, leaving some texture.
Brown the chicken in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes. Remove it and sauté chopped onion and pepper for 6 minutes.
Add garlic and cumin, stir, then add tomatoes, chicken, and the remaining stock. Cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes.
Gradually stir in the ground corn. Cook uncovered for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring the bottom frequently to prevent sticking.
Check that the corn no longer tastes raw and the chicken reaches 74 °C. Adjust the salt; the mixture should fall from the spoon with a creamy consistency.
tips: The sweetness and moisture of corn vary; add hot stock gradually if the casserole becomes too thick.

title: Chicken and sweet potato patties
description: Golden patties of ground chicken and sweet potato, seasoned with garlic and scallions.
steps: Peel and dice the sweet potato. Boil it in the water for 15 minutes, drain, and mash; cool for 10 minutes.
Mix the mash with ground chicken, egg, breadcrumbs, crushed garlic, chopped scallions, cumin, and salt using a clean spoon.
Shape into 12 patties about 2 cm thick. Place on a plate without stacking and refrigerate any patties waiting to be cooked.
Heat the oil and cook in 2 batches for 5 to 6 minutes per side over medium heat, turning with a spatula so they do not break.
Check for 74 °C in the center of several patties. If they brown before reaching that temperature, lower the heat and finish cooking with a lid.
tips: The mash should be dry and cool before mixing with the chicken so the patties hold their shape.

title: Chicken with roasted tomato mojo
description: Browned chicken thighs with a roasted tomato, garlic, and sour orange sauce.
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C. Quarter the tomatoes and onion and place them with the peeled garlic in a dish; add 1 tablespoon of oil.
Roast the vegetables for 25 minutes, until soft with browned edges. Blend with sour orange juice, water, oregano, and a pinch of salt.
Season the chicken and brown it in the remaining oil in a wide skillet for 5 minutes on each side.
Pour the tomato mojo over the chicken. Cover and simmer gently for 15 to 20 minutes, shaking the pan to keep the sauce from sticking.
Check for 74 °C in the thickest part of the chicken. Uncover to thicken for a few minutes if needed and adjust the salt before serving.
tips: Use the roasted tomato juices to give the sauce body.

title: Hen in peanut and egg sauce
description: Stewed hen with a thick sauce of toasted peanuts and hard-boiled egg yolk.
steps: Season the hen and brown it in the oil in a heavy pot for 12 minutes. Remove it and sauté chopped onion and garlic for 6 minutes.
Add wine and boil for 2 minutes. Return the hen with the stew water and bay leaf; cover and simmer for 120 to 150 minutes, until tender.
While the hen cooks, boil the eggs in the listed water for 10 minutes after the water reaches a boil. Cool with water, peel, and separate yolks from whites.
Blend peanuts, yolks, and 250 ml of the stew broth into a paste. Add it to the pot and cook uncovered for 10 minutes.
Check that the hen reaches 74 °C near but not touching the bone and yields to a fork. Remove the bay leaf, adjust the salt, and serve with the chopped egg whites.
tips: An adult hen needs long, gentle cooking; add hot water if the broth gets too low.

title: Hen with cassava and sour orange
description: Slow-cooked hen with tender cassava and a citrus sofrito.
steps: Season the hen with salt and cumin. Brown it in the oil for 12 minutes, then add chopped onion, pepper, and garlic; sauté for 6 minutes.
Pour in the sour orange juice and water for the hen. Cover and simmer gently for 120 to 150 minutes, adding hot water if too much meat becomes exposed.
Peel the cassava, removing the entire pink layer, and cut into 5 cm pieces. Boil separately in its water for 25 minutes.
Discard the cassava cooking water and remove the central fiber. Once the hen is tender, add the cassava and simmer together for 15 minutes.
Check that the hen reaches 74 °C and the cassava is completely tender. Adjust the salt and serve with the broth reduced to a sauce.
tips: The separate initial boiling lets you discard the cassava water before adding it to the stew.

title: Shredded hen with okra
description: Shredded hen and okra in tomato sauce with a touch of lime.
steps: Put the hen in a pot with water, bay leaf, half the onion, and salt. Cover and simmer gently for 120 to 150 minutes, until tender and at 74 °C.
Remove the hen and reserve 350 ml of broth. When cool enough to handle, discard skin, bones, and bay leaf; shred the meat with clean utensils.
Wash and dry the okra, trimming the stems without opening small pods. Sauté the remaining onion and chopped garlic in the oil for 6 minutes.
Add tomatoes, oregano, broth, and okra. Simmer gently for 15 minutes, shaking the pot to avoid breaking the pods.
Add the hen and lime juice and cook for 8 minutes, until everything is hot; if the meat was refrigerated, reheat to 74 °C. Adjust the salt.
tips: Choose small pods so they become tender without falling apart.

title: Hen stewed with olives and raisins
description: Hen in a tomato, olive, and raisin sauce flavored with sofrito.
steps: Season the hen and brown it in batches in the oil for 12 minutes. Transfer to a plate, keeping any juices it releases.
Chop onion, pepper, and garlic; sauté in the same pot for 7 minutes. Add cumin, tomatoes, and vinegar and cook for 5 minutes.
Return the hen and its juices, pour in the water, and cover. Simmer gently for 120 to 150 minutes, until the meat begins to pull away from the bone.
Add olives and raisins during the final 15 minutes so they flavor the sauce without falling apart. Watch the liquid level and stir gently.
Check for 74 °C in the thickest part without touching bone. Uncover to reduce the sauce if needed and adjust the salt after tasting the olives.
tips: Olives vary in saltiness; season lightly at the start.

title: Roasted hen with pumpkin mash
description: Hen simmered until tender, then browned in the oven and served over smooth pumpkin mash.
steps: Simmer the hen with water, quartered onion, bay leaf, salt, and half the garlic for 120 to 150 minutes, covered over low heat, until tender and at 74 °C.
Heat the oven to 210 °C. Transfer the hen to a baking dish and mix sour orange juice, oil, and remaining crushed garlic; brush the pieces with this mixture.
Strain 600 ml of broth into another pot, add the diced pumpkin, and cook for 20 minutes, until easily mashed. Reserve a little broth.
While the pumpkin cooks, roast the hen for 20 to 25 minutes, until the skin browns. Brush again with the pan juices halfway through cooking.
Mash the drained pumpkin with butter and enough reserved broth for the desired texture. Adjust the salt and serve the hot hen over the mash; if cooled, reheat to 74 °C.
tips: The initial simmer makes the meat tender; the oven then browns the surface.

title: Turkey in green mango sauce
description: Turkey cubes stewed with firm mango, sweet peppers, and a mild sofrito.
steps: Cut the turkey into 3 cm cubes and season with salt and cumin. Cut the mango into chunks and chop the onion, peppers, and garlic.
Heat the oil in a pot and brown the turkey for 8 minutes. Remove it and sauté onion, sweet peppers, and garlic for 6 minutes.
Add stock and orange juice, return the turkey, and cover. Simmer gently for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the mango and cook for 12 to 15 more minutes, until tender without falling apart and the turkey reaches 74 °C.
Mash a few mango chunks into the sauce to thicken it. Taste for salt and serve the turkey with the remaining mango pieces intact.
tips: Choose firm mango that is not excessively sour; its ripeness changes the balance of the sauce.

title: Turkey medallions with black bean puree
description: Skillet turkey served over black beans pureed with sofrito and lime.
steps: Cut the turkey into 2 cm thick medallions. Season with salt, half the cumin, and half the crushed garlic.
Sauté chopped onion, pepper, and remaining garlic in 1 tablespoon of oil for 7 minutes. Add beans, water, and the remaining cumin.
Cook the beans for 10 minutes and blend with the lime juice into a puree. Keep warm over low heat and adjust the salt.
Heat the remaining oil in another skillet. Brown the medallions for 5 to 7 minutes per side, working in batches if needed.
Check for 74 °C in the center of the turkey; extend cooking over low heat if necessary. Divide the puree among plates and place the medallions on top.
tips: Use fully cooked beans; the listed time only reheats them and combines them with the sofrito.

title: Shredded turkey with roasted pepper mojo
description: Shredded turkey thigh with roasted peppers, garlic, and sour orange.
steps: Simmer the turkey with water, bay leaf, half the onion, and salt for 70 to 90 minutes, until it can be shredded and reaches 74 °C.
Meanwhile, roast the peppers at 220 °C for 25 minutes, turning once. Let them cool slightly, covered, then remove skins and seeds.
Remove and shred the turkey with clean utensils and reserve 150 ml of broth. Discard the bay leaf and cut the peppers into strips.
Sauté the remaining onion and chopped garlic in the oil for 7 minutes. Add sour orange juice, oregano, broth, and peppers; cook for 3 minutes.
Add the turkey and cook for 8 minutes so it absorbs the mojo. If previously refrigerated, reheat to 74 °C; adjust the salt before serving.
tips: Remove the blackened pepper skins without rinsing to preserve their roasted juices.

title: Zucchini stuffed with turkey and plantain
description: Baked zucchini filled with ground turkey and diced ripe plantain.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Halve the zucchini lengthwise and scoop out the centers, leaving sturdy walls; chop the removed flesh.
Dice the plantain finely and brown it in 1 tablespoon of oil for 5 minutes. Remove it and sauté onion and garlic in the remaining oil for 5 minutes.
Add ground turkey, salt, and oregano; break up the clumps and cook for 8 minutes. Add tomatoes and zucchini flesh and cook for 7 minutes.
Mix the plantain into the filling and divide among the zucchini halves. Place in a dish with water, cover, and bake for 20 minutes; uncover for 5 minutes.
Check that the zucchini is tender and the center of the filling reaches 74 °C. Rest for 5 minutes and serve 2 halves per person.
tips: A ripe but firm plantain keeps its shape while the filling cooks.

title: Turkey stewed with eggplant and tomatoes
description: Turkey thigh with browned eggplant in an oregano tomato sauce.
steps: Cut the eggplant into 3 cm cubes and the turkey into similar pieces. Season the turkey and keep utensils that touch raw meat separate.
Brown the eggplant in half the oil for 8 minutes, in batches if needed. Remove it and brown the turkey in the remaining oil for 8 minutes.
Add chopped onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in tomatoes, water, oregano, and vinegar and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes. Return the eggplant to the pot and cook for 15 to 20 more minutes, stirring gently.
Check that the turkey is tender and reaches 74 °C. Uncover to reduce the sauce if too thin and adjust the salt before serving.
tips: Adding the eggplant near the end keeps it from dissolving into the sauce during the turkey’s longer cooking time.

title: Turkey roll stuffed with egg and spinach
description: Turkey breast rolled around spinach and hard-boiled eggs, roasted with sour orange.
steps: Boil the eggs in the listed water for 10 minutes after it reaches a boil. Cool, peel, and set aside; heat the oven to 180 °C.
Sauté chopped onion and garlic in 1 tablespoon of oil for 5 minutes. Add spinach, cook until wilted, and drain any liquid.
Open the turkey into an even layer, season with salt and oregano, and spread over the spinach. Place the eggs in a central row and roll firmly.
Tie with kitchen string, place in a roasting dish, and add sour orange juice, roasting water, and remaining oil. Cover and bake for 45 minutes.
Uncover and bake for 20 to 30 more minutes, until both the meat and the center of the filling reach 74 °C. Add hot water if the dish dries out.
Let rest for 10 minutes. Remove all string, slice, and serve with the hot roasting juices.
tips: Ask for the breast to be butterflied for stuffing; an even thickness helps the roll cook evenly.

title: Turkey strips with sesame and lime sauce
description: Browned turkey strips with a creamy toasted sesame and lime sauce.
steps: Toast the sesame in a dry skillet for 3 minutes, stirring until fragrant. Blend with stock and lime juice into a sauce.
Cut the turkey into strips 2 cm wide. Season with salt and cumin and brown in half the oil for 6 minutes.
Transfer the turkey to a plate. Sauté chopped onion and garlic in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, keeping the garlic from burning.
Return the turkey and add the sesame sauce. Simmer very gently for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring so the sauce does not stick.
Check for 74 °C in the thickest strips, adjust the salt, and add chopped cilantro. If the sauce becomes too thick, stir in a little hot water.
tips: Toast sesame only until lightly golden; burned seeds make the whole sauce bitter.

title: Duck legs with chickpeas and spinach
description: Duck legs braised with cooked chickpeas and spinach in tomato sofrito.
steps: Pat the legs dry and season. Place skin-side down in a cold heavy pot and heat over medium heat for 12 minutes to render the fat.
Turn and brown for 4 minutes. Remove the duck and leave only 2 tablespoons of fat in the pot; sauté chopped onion and garlic for 6 minutes.
Add paprika and tomatoes, stir, and pour in the water. Return the duck, add the bay leaf, and cover; simmer gently for 90 to 120 minutes.
When the duck is tender, add chickpeas and spinach. Cook for 12 minutes, stirring carefully to avoid breaking the chickpeas.
Check for 74 °C in the legs without touching bone. Remove the bay leaf and excess surface fat, adjust the salt, and serve the duck over the chickpeas.
tips: The chickpeas must be fully cooked before adding them; here they only heat through in the sauce.

title: Duck stew with malanga and sweet peppers
description: Tender duck with malanga that naturally thickens a sofrito broth.
steps: Season the duck and place skin-side down in a cold pot. Heat over medium heat for 12 minutes; turn and brown for 5 minutes.
Remove the duck and keep only 2 tablespoons of fat. Sauté chopped onion, peppers, and garlic for 7 minutes; add cumin and stir.
Return the duck and add sour orange juice, water, and bay leaf. Cover and simmer gently for 75 to 100 minutes, until the meat begins to soften.
Peel the malanga and cut into 3 cm cubes. Add to the stew and cook for 25 to 30 minutes, until soft and fully cooked.
Check that the duck is tender and reaches 74 °C. Mash a few malanga cubes to thicken the sauce, remove the bay leaf, and adjust the salt.
tips: Add the malanga after the duck softens so some pieces keep their shape.

title: Duck breast with roasted garlic mojo
description: Golden-skinned duck breast served with a mellow roasted garlic mojo.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Wrap the unpeeled garlic with the oil in foil and roast for 30 minutes; then squeeze out the pulp.
Score the breast skin in a diamond pattern without cutting the meat and season. Place skin-side down in a cold skillet and heat over medium-low heat for 12 minutes.
Pour off rendered fat periodically, turn, and cook for 5 minutes. Transfer to a dish and roast for 10 to 20 minutes, until the center reaches 74 °C.
Leave 1 tablespoon of fat in the skillet and sauté chopped onion for 6 minutes. Add garlic pulp, sour orange juice, water, and oregano; simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Rest the duck for 5 minutes after checking the temperature. Slice and serve with the hot mojo underneath to preserve the browned skin.
tips: Breast thickness determines the final oven time; use the thermometer as your guide.

title: Shredded duck with chayote and onion
description: Shredded duck sautéed with tender chayote and browned onion.
steps: Simmer the duck with water, bay leaf, salt, and 100 g of onion for 110 to 140 minutes, until tender and at 74 °C.
Remove skin and bones, shred the meat, and reserve 200 ml of skimmed broth. Peel the chayote, remove any tough core, and cut into strips.
Slice the remaining onion and brown in the oil for 10 minutes. Add garlic and cumin, stir, and add the chayote.
Pour in the reserved broth, cover, and cook for 12 minutes, until the chayote softens. Add the duck and cook uncovered for 8 minutes.
Add lime juice, adjust the salt, and allow excess broth to evaporate. If the meat was refrigerated, check for 74 °C before serving.
tips: Skim the broth with a spoon before adding it so the sauté does not become greasy.

title: Duck with mango and dry wine sauce
description: Braised duck legs finished with a ripe mango and wine sauce.
steps: Season the duck with salt and pepper. Place the legs skin-side down in a cold pot and cook over medium heat for 12 minutes.
Turn and brown for 4 minutes. Remove the duck, leave 2 tablespoons of fat, and sauté chopped onion, garlic, and ginger for 6 minutes.
Pour in the wine and boil for 3 minutes; add water and return the duck. Cover and simmer gently for 100 to 125 minutes, until tender.
Blend half the mango with 150 ml of sauce from the pot. Add this puree, the remaining diced mango, and lime juice; cook for 10 minutes.
Check for 74 °C in the thickest part of the legs without touching bone. Skim excess surface fat, adjust the salt, and serve with the mango sauce.
tips: Add the mango once the duck is tender to preserve its fresh aroma.

title: Goose legs with red beans
description: Slow-cooked goose legs with red beans and Cuban-style sofrito.
