steps: Pat the goose dry and season with salt. Place the pieces skin-side down in a cold pot and heat over medium heat for 15 minutes; turn for 5 minutes.
Remove the meat and leave only 2 tablespoons of fat. Sauté chopped onion, pepper, and garlic for 7 minutes; add cumin and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Return the goose and add water, sour orange juice, and bay leaves. Cover and simmer gently for 140 to 170 minutes, until the meat is tender.
Add the fully cooked beans and simmer for 15 minutes. Mash a ladleful of beans into the sauce if you want it thicker.
Check for 74 °C in thick areas without touching bone and make sure the meat yields to a fork. Remove bay leaves and surface fat; adjust the salt at the end.
tips: Use canned or fully precooked beans; do not add dried beans to this stew.

title: Goose with cabbage and semi-ripe plantain
description: Braised goose with tender cabbage and firm pieces of semi-ripe plantain.
steps: Season the goose and brown it starting in a cold pot, skin-side down, for 15 minutes over medium heat. Turn and cook for 5 minutes.
Remove the goose and keep 2 tablespoons of fat. Sauté chopped onion and garlic for 6 minutes; add cumin and vinegar and stir.
Return the goose with water and bay leaves. Cover and simmer gently for 130 to 160 minutes, adding hot water if the pot dries out.
Cut the cabbage into thick strips and the plantain into 3 cm rounds. Add when the goose is nearly tender and cook for 25 to 30 more minutes.
Check that the goose reaches 74 °C and is tender, and that the plantain is easily pierced. Remove bay leaves and surface fat; adjust the salt.
tips: Semi-ripe plantain has yellow skin with green patches and holds up better in the stew than very ripe plantain.

title: Goose breast with prune sauce
description: Roasted goose breast served with a prune and orange sauce.
steps: Heat the oven to 170 °C. Score the goose skin in a diamond pattern without cutting the meat; season with salt, pepper, and half the thyme.
Place the breasts skin-side down in a cold skillet. Cook over medium-low heat for 15 minutes, pouring off fat; turn for 5 minutes.
Transfer the breasts to a dish and roast for 25 to 40 minutes, until the center of each piece reaches 74 °C. Thickness determines the final cooking time.
Leave 1 tablespoon of fat in the skillet and sauté chopped onion and garlic for 7 minutes. Add prunes, orange juice, water, vinegar, and remaining thyme.
Simmer the sauce gently for 20 minutes. Blend half and return it to the skillet to keep some prune pieces; adjust salt and pepper.
Rest the goose for 10 minutes after checking its temperature. Cut into thin slices and serve with the hot sauce.
tips: Goose refers to the same bird called oca or ganso in Spanish; this recipe uses breast, not a whole bird.

title: Soupy rice with shrimp and taro
description: A brothy rice dish with tender taro, shrimp, and a sweet-pepper sofrito.
steps: Cut the taro into 1 cm cubes and chop the onion, sweet pepper, and garlic. Keep the shrimp refrigerated while preparing the base.
Sauté the onion and sweet pepper in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin, and tomatoes and cook for 4 more minutes.
Pour in the stock and add the taro and salt. Simmer gently for 10 minutes; add the rinsed and drained rice.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add the shrimp and cook for 4 to 6 minutes, until opaque.
Check that the taro is fully tender and the rice is cooked; add the lime juice and serve immediately with plenty of broth.
tips: If the rice absorbs too much broth, add small amounts of boiling water before serving.

title: Baked rice with horse mackerel and onion
description: Horse mackerel fillets over tomato rice, finished in the oven with softened onion.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Check the horse mackerel for bones and slice the onion; keep the fish chilled.
In an ovenproof casserole, sauté the onion in the oil for 10 minutes. Add the chopped garlic and oregano; cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 4 minutes. Stir in the rinsed rice, hot stock, and salt; once boiling, cover and bake for 15 minutes.
Place the fish over the rice, drizzle with lime juice, and cover again. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the fish reaches 63 °C and the rice is tender.
Let stand covered for 5 minutes out of the oven. Lift the fillets with a spatula and divide the rice without breaking up the fish.
tips: Use a wide casserole so the fish fits in a single layer.

title: Brothy rice with conch and okra
description: Previously tenderized conch and okra in juicy rice with tomato and lime.

ingredients.name: tender cooked conch
ingredients.note: Cooked weight, without shell; it must be fully tender before starting and kept refrigerated.

steps: Slice the cooked conch thinly. Wash and dry the okra, trim the ends, and cut it into 2 cm pieces.
Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil for 7 minutes. Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, until slightly thickened.
Add the stock, rinsed rice, conch, and salt. Bring to a boil and cook uncovered over medium-low heat for 12 minutes.
Add the okra and lime juice; cook for 8 to 10 more minutes, until the rice and okra are tender and the reheated conch reaches 74 °C.
Stir gently and serve in deep bowls. If necessary, loosen with a little boiling water to keep the dish brothy.
tips: The rice cooking time cannot tenderize raw conch: always start with conch that is already tender.

title: Rice with mahi-mahi and seared pineapple
description: Sofrito rice served with mahi-mahi chunks and pan-seared pineapple.
steps: Cut the pineapple and fish into 3 cm cubes, using separate cutting boards. Chop the onion, bell pepper, and garlic.
Sauté the chopped vegetables in 2 tablespoons of oil for 7 minutes. Add the cumin, rinsed rice, stock, and half the salt.
Once boiling, cover and cook over low heat for 20 minutes; turn off the heat and let stand for 5 minutes without uncovering.
While the rice cooks, brown the pineapple in a skillet with the remaining oil for 5 minutes. Remove it and cook the fish with the remaining salt for 6 to 8 minutes, turning until it reaches 63 °C.
Add the lime juice to the skillet, return the pineapple, and toss carefully. Serve the fish and fruit over the rice, freshly fluffed with a fork.
tips: Pat the pineapple dry before browning so it colors without releasing too much water.

title: Brothy fish and shrimp rice
description: A rice casserole with sea fish, shrimp, and a gently seasoned sofrito broth.
steps: Cut the snapper into 3 cm pieces and keep chilled with the shrimp. Chop the onion, bell pepper, garlic, and parsley separately.
Sauté the onion and bell pepper in the oil for 7 minutes. Add the garlic and paprika; stir and immediately add the tomatoes.
Cook the sofrito for 5 minutes and pour in the stock. Once boiling, add the rinsed rice and salt; simmer gently for 15 minutes.
Add the fish and shrimp and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until the fish reaches 63 °C and the shrimp are opaque. Check that the rice is tender.
Turn off the heat, add the parsley, and serve without a long resting period. Keep enough broth for the rice to be eaten with a spoon.
tips: Add the seafood near the end so it does not toughen while the rice softens.

title: Rice with mussels and chickpeas
description: Tomato rice with tender chickpeas and cooked shelled mussels.

ingredients.name: cooked mussel meat
ingredients.note: Weight without shells; keep refrigerated until adding.

ingredients.name: drained cooked chickpeas
ingredients.note: Canned and rinsed, or previously cooked until tender.

steps: Check the mussels for any shell fragments. Drain the chickpeas thoroughly and rinse and drain the rice.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the paprika and tomatoes and cook for 5 more minutes.
Add the rice, hot stock, chickpeas, and salt. Once boiling, cover and cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
Spread the mussels over the rice and cover again. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until the rice is tender and the reheated mussels reach 74 °C.
Let stand off the heat for 5 minutes, add the lime juice, and mix gently to keep the chickpeas and mussels whole.
tips: The mussel weight refers only to the meat, not the shells.

title: Rice with prawns and okra
description: Long-grain rice with prawns, sautéed okra, and red bell pepper.
steps: Wash and dry the okra, trim the ends, and cut into thick rounds. Chop the onion, bell pepper, and garlic; keep the prawns chilled.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a skillet and sauté the okra for 6 minutes. Remove it when lightly browned in places.
In a casserole, sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the remaining oil for 6 minutes. Add the cumin, rinsed rice, stock, and salt.
Once boiling, cover and cook over low heat for 15 minutes. Add the okra and prawns, cover, and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until the rice is tender and the prawns are opaque.
Remove from the heat, rest for 5 minutes, and finish with the lime juice. Separate the grains with a fork without crushing the okra.
tips: Drying the okra thoroughly before sautéing helps it brown.

title: Fresh cod and fava bean rice
description: Mild rice with fresh cod, tender fava beans, and a touch of parsley.

ingredients.name: skinless boneless fresh cod
ingredients.note: Use fresh or thawed fish, not salt cod.

steps: Cut the cod into 4 cm pieces and keep refrigerated. Chop the onion, garlic, and parsley separately.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil for 7 minutes over medium heat, keeping the garlic from browning too much.
Add the rinsed rice, fava beans, hot stock, and salt. Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over the lowest heat for 14 minutes.
Arrange the cod over the rice and cover. Cook for 8 to 10 more minutes, until it reaches 63 °C and the rice and beans are tender.
Rest off the heat for 5 minutes. Add the lime juice and parsley and serve by lifting the fish pieces so they stay intact.
tips: If the fava beans have thick skins, remove them before weighing for a softer texture.

title: Crab and egg fried rice
description: Home-style stir-fried rice with crab, egg, and scallions.

ingredients.name: cooked white rice
ingredients.note: Previously cooked and cooled promptly in shallow containers; keep refrigerated, never cool for hours on the counter.

steps: Check the crab meat and remove any cartilage. Finely dice the carrot, chop the garlic and scallions, and beat the eggs.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large skillet. Scramble the eggs for 2 minutes until firm, then transfer to a clean plate.
Add the remaining oil and sauté the carrot and garlic for 5 minutes. Add the separated cold rice grains and stir-fry for 4 minutes.
Add the crab, eggs, soy sauce, and scallions. Stir-fry for 4 to 6 minutes, until the reheated mixture reaches 74 °C in several places.
Finish with the lime juice and serve immediately. If the skillet is crowded, work in batches to heat the rice evenly.
tips: Taste before adding salt: the soy sauce and crab already contribute saltiness.

title: Rice with sardines and pumpkin
description: Stovetop rice with diced pumpkin and canned sardines added near the end.
steps: Cut the pumpkin into 1 cm cubes. Open and drain the sardines, keeping them in large pieces; chop the onion and garlic.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the tomatoes and oregano and cook for 5 more minutes.
Add the rinsed rice, pumpkin, stock, and salt. Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for 18 minutes.
Arrange the sardines over the rice, cover, and heat for 5 minutes, until piping hot and the pumpkin is tender.
Turn off the heat and let stand for 5 minutes. Add the lime juice and serve with a wide spoon to avoid crushing the sardines.
tips: Drain the sardines thoroughly to keep the rice liquid ratio as specified.

title: Hen and cassava rice
description: Slow-simmered hen and tender cassava folded into rice cooked in homemade broth.
steps: Place the hen in a pot with its water, half the onion, the bay leaf, and half the salt. Simmer gently for 90 to 120 minutes, until tender and at least 74 °C.
In another pot, cut the cassava into pieces and boil it in its measured water for 25 to 35 minutes, until tender. Drain and discard all that water; remove the central fiber.
Remove the hen skin and bones and separate the meat into pieces. Strain the broth, discard the bay leaf, and measure 750 ml; top up with hot water if needed.
Chop the remaining onion, the bell pepper, and the garlic. Sauté in the oil for 7 minutes and add the cumin and rinsed rice.
Pour in the measured broth and add the hen, diced cassava, and remaining salt. Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over the lowest heat for 22 minutes.
Check that the rice is tender; rest off the heat for 10 minutes. Mix carefully and serve hot, removing any remaining bones.
tips: Stewing hen can take longer than chicken; start the rice only once the meat is tender.

title: Rice with shredded goat
description: Sofrito rice with tender goat, tomato, and bell peppers, made with previously cooked meat.

ingredients.name: cooked shredded goat meat
ingredients.note: Without bones or tough fat; cook until tender beforehand and keep refrigerated.

steps: Check and shred the cooked goat into medium strands. Rinse and drain the rice; chop the onion, bell pepper, and garlic.
Sauté the onion and bell pepper in the oil for 7 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin, and oregano and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the meat, rice, hot stock, and salt, distributing the strands evenly.
Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for 22 minutes. Check that the rice is tender and the reheated meat reaches 74 °C.
Remove from the heat and let stand covered for 10 minutes. Separate the grains with a fork and serve, distributing the meat evenly.
tips: The stated time starts with cooked goat; do not substitute raw meat without fully cooking it first.

title: Rice with pork loin and pineapple
description: Browned pork loin cubes with fresh pineapple over pepper-and-garlic rice.
steps: Cut the pork into 2 cm cubes and the pineapple into similar cubes using separate cutting boards. Chop the onion, bell pepper, and garlic.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and half the garlic in 2 tablespoons of oil for 7 minutes. Add the rinsed rice, stock, and half the salt.
Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for 20 minutes. Remove from the heat and rest covered for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a skillet and brown the pork for 8 to 10 minutes. Add the remaining garlic, cumin, remaining salt, pineapple, and sour orange juice; cook for 4 more minutes.
Check that the pork centers reach 63 °C and let rest off the heat for 3 minutes. Serve over the rice with the pan juices.
tips: Brown the pork in batches if the skillet is small, so it does not steam in its own juices.

title: Rice with beef meatballs
description: Small meatballs cooked with rice in a light tomato-and-sofrito sauce.
steps: Mix the beef, egg, breadcrumbs, chopped parsley, and half the salt. Form 3 cm meatballs; chop the onion and garlic.
Brown the meatballs in the oil for 7 minutes, turning them; they will not yet be fully cooked. Transfer them to a plate.
In the same casserole, sauté the onion and garlic for 6 minutes. Add the cumin and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, gently scraping the bottom.
Add the rinsed rice, stock, remaining salt, and meatballs. Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over the lowest heat for 22 minutes.
Check that the rice is tender and the meatballs reach at least 71 °C in the center. Let stand covered for 5 minutes and serve without breaking them.
tips: Make the meatballs equal in size so they finish cooking together.

title: Rice with fresh sausage and cabbage
description: One-pot rice with fresh pork sausage, shredded cabbage, and tomato.

ingredients.name: fresh pork sausage
ingredients.note: Raw; check the brand label for allergens.

steps: Remove the sausage casing and divide the meat into bite-sized pieces. Thinly shred the cabbage and chop the onion and garlic.
Heat the oil in a wide pot and brown the sausage for 7 minutes, breaking it up with a spoon.
Add the onion, garlic, and cabbage and sauté for 6 minutes. Stir in the paprika and tomatoes and cook for 4 more minutes.
Add the rinsed rice, stock, and salt. Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for 22 minutes, until the rice is tender and the sausage reaches at least 71 °C.
Let stand covered for 10 minutes and mix gently. Taste before adding more salt because the sausage contributes seasoning.
tips: Choose fresh pork sausage; if using poultry sausage, it must reach 74 °C.
allergens: As listed on the sausage label

title: Rice with duck and white beans
description: Shredded duck and white beans in rice cooked with skimmed stock.

ingredients.name: cooked duck meat
ingredients.note: Skinless and boneless, already tender and refrigerated until needed.

ingredients.name: drained cooked white beans
ingredients.note: Canned and rinsed, or previously cooked until tender.

steps: Shred the duck and remove any small bones. Finely dice the carrot and chop the onion and garlic.
Sauté the onion and carrot in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and oregano and cook for 1 minute.
Add the rinsed rice, hot stock, duck, beans, bay leaf, and salt. Stir once and bring to a boil.
Cover and cook over low heat for 22 minutes. Check that the rice is cooked and the reheated meat reaches 74 °C.
Rest for 10 minutes, remove the bay leaf, and fluff the rice with a fork. Serve without crushing the beans.
tips: Skim fat from the surface of the stock to avoid overly greasy rice.

title: Rice with beef tongue and olives
description: Tender diced beef tongue with rice, olives, and a creole-style tomato sauce.

ingredients.name: cooked peeled beef tongue
ingredients.note: Previously cooked until tender with the outer membrane removed; keep refrigerated.

steps: Cut the cooked tongue into 1.5 cm cubes. Drain the olives and chop the onion, bell pepper, and garlic.
Sauté the onion and bell pepper in the oil for 7 minutes. Add the garlic and cumin and cook for 1 more minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the tongue, rinsed rice, olives, stock, and salt gently.
Once boiling, cover and cook over the lowest heat for 22 minutes. Check that the rice is tender and the reheated tongue reaches 74 °C.
Remove from the heat, rest covered for 10 minutes, and fluff the grains. Taste for salt after resting, accounting for the olives.
tips: This recipe starts with cooked tongue: tenderizing it requires a long preliminary cooking stage that cannot be skipped.

title: Rice with ground turkey and carrot
description: Crumbled ground turkey with carrot, peas, and rice in one casserole.
steps: Peel and finely dice the carrot. Chop the onion and garlic; rinse and drain the rice.
Heat the oil and cook the turkey for 7 minutes, breaking it up with a spoon to avoid large clumps.
Add the onion, garlic, and carrot and sauté for 6 minutes. Stir in the tomatoes and oregano and cook for 3 more minutes.
Add the rice, stock, peas, and salt. Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for 22 minutes, until the rice is tender and the turkey reaches 74 °C.
Rest off the heat for 5 minutes and fluff with a fork. Serve, evenly distributing the crumbled meat and vegetables.
tips: Cut the carrot small so it finishes softening at the same time as the rice.

title: Baked rice with eggplant and cheese
description: Browned eggplant with tomato rice and a thin layer of melted cheese.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Cut the eggplant into 2 cm cubes and chop the onion and garlic.
In an ovenproof casserole, brown the eggplant in 2 tablespoons of oil for 10 minutes; transfer it to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, onion, and garlic and sauté for 6 minutes. Stir in the tomatoes and oregano and cook for 5 more minutes.
Add the rinsed rice, hot stock, eggplant, and salt. Bring to a boil, cover tightly, and bake for 25 minutes.
Uncover, check that the rice is tender, spread the cheese over it, and bake for 5 to 8 minutes, until melted and the center of the casserole reaches 74 °C. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
tips: A tight-fitting lid prevents too much stock from evaporating before the rice cooks.

title: Rice with pumpkin and black-eyed peas
description: Mild rice with previously cooked black-eyed peas, pumpkin, and pepper sofrito.

ingredients.name: drained cooked black-eyed peas
ingredients.note: Canned and rinsed, or previously cooked until tender.

steps: Cut the pumpkin into 1 cm cubes. Drain the beans and rinse the rice until the water runs less cloudy.
Chop the onion, sweet pepper, and garlic and sauté them in the oil for 7 minutes. Add the cumin and stir briefly.
Add the rice, pumpkin, beans, hot stock, bay leaf, and salt. Stir once and bring to a boil.
Cover and cook over low heat for 22 minutes. Check that the rice and pumpkin are tender and the liquid has been absorbed.
Turn off the heat and rest covered for 10 minutes. Remove the bay leaf and fluff carefully to avoid mashing the pumpkin.
tips: If the pumpkin is very watery, let the cubes drain before adding them to the pot.

title: Brown rice with okra and tomato
description: Brown rice grains with sautéed okra and reduced tomato sofrito.
steps: Rinse and drain the brown rice. Wash and dry the okra, trim its ends, and cut it into 2 cm pieces.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in 2 tablespoons of oil for 6 minutes. Add the cumin and tomatoes and cook for 6 more minutes.
Add the rice, stock, and salt. Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for 35 minutes without stirring repeatedly.
Meanwhile, sauté the okra in the remaining oil for 8 minutes. Add it to the rice and cook covered for 10 to 15 more minutes, until the grains are tender.
If the rice is still firm and has dried out, add a little boiling water. Once done, rest for 10 minutes and finish with lime juice.
tips: Brown rice varies by brand: use its texture as well as the clock to judge when it is done.

title: Rice with taro and leek
description: Cubed taro and softened leek accompany white rice cooked in vegetable stock.
steps: Cut the taro into 1 cm cubes. Split the leek lengthwise, rinse between the layers, and slice thinly.
Sauté the leek and chopped garlic in the oil for 8 minutes over medium-low heat, until the leek softens without browning.
Add the taro and stock; simmer gently for 5 minutes. Stir in the rinsed rice and salt and bring back to a boil.
Cover and cook over the lowest heat for 22 minutes. Check that the taro is completely soft and the rice has absorbed the liquid.
Let stand covered off the heat for 10 minutes. Add the chopped parsley and separate the grains with a fork before serving.
tips: Small taro cubes cook more evenly within the rice.

title: Rice with green plantain and black beans
description: Rice with cooked black beans and small green plantain cubes seasoned with cumin.

ingredients.name: drained cooked black beans
ingredients.note: Canned and rinsed, or previously cooked until tender.

steps: Peel the green plantain and cut it into 1 cm cubes. Drain the beans, rinse the rice, and chop the onion, bell pepper, and garlic.
Sauté the onion and bell pepper in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin, and plantain and cook for 4 minutes, stirring.
Add the rice, beans, hot stock, bay leaf, and salt. Stir gently and bring to a boil.
Cover and cook over low heat for 25 minutes. Check that the plantain can be pierced with a fork and the rice is tender.
Remove from the heat and rest for 10 minutes without uncovering. Discard the bay leaf and mix from the edges toward the center without crushing the beans.
tips: Choose fully green plantain so the cubes hold their shape.

title: Baked rice with cauliflower and sesame
description: Sofrito rice baked with small cauliflower florets and toasted sesame seeds.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Divide the cauliflower into 3 cm florets and chop the onion, bell pepper, and garlic.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the oil in an ovenproof casserole for 8 minutes. Add the paprika and rinsed rice.
Pour in the hot stock and add the cauliflower and salt. Bring to a boil, cover tightly, and bake for 30 minutes.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry skillet for 2 minutes, moving them around. Check that the rice is tender and the casserole reaches 74 °C in the center.
Remove from the oven and rest covered for 5 minutes. Mix carefully and scatter the toasted sesame seeds on top just before serving.
tips: Cut the florets to similar sizes so they soften at the same time.

title: Rice with carrot, coconut, and peanuts
description: Coconut rice with finely cut carrot and toasted peanuts added for crunch.
steps: Peel and coarsely grate the carrot. Chop the onion and garlic and roughly chop the peanuts, keeping them separate.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the carrot and cook for 3 minutes to soften it slightly.
Add the rinsed rice, coconut milk, stock, and salt. Stir well, bring to a gentle boil, and cover.
Cook over very low heat for 22 minutes, keeping the coconut milk from sticking to the bottom. Check that the rice is tender.
Remove from the heat, rest covered for 10 minutes, and fluff with a fork. Add the lime juice and peanuts just before serving to preserve their texture.
tips: Use unsweetened coconut milk, not sweetened cream of coconut for drinks.

title: Rice with Swiss chard and sesame
description: White rice with Swiss chard stems and leaves, finished with toasted sesame seeds.
steps: Wash the chard well and separate the stems and leaves. Thinly slice the stems and shred the leaves; chop the onion and garlic.
Sauté the onion, garlic, and chard stems in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the rinsed rice and stir briefly.
Pour in the stock and salt, bring to a boil, and cook covered over low heat for 15 minutes. Spread the leaves over the rice.
Cover and cook for 7 to 9 more minutes, until the leaves are soft and the rice is tender. Toast the sesame seeds in a dry skillet for 2 minutes.
Rest the rice for 5 minutes, add the lime juice, and mix the leaves through the grains. Finish with the toasted sesame seeds before serving.
tips: Cook the stems before the leaves because they take longer to soften.

title: Baked rice with eggs and sofrito
description: Tomato-and-pepper rice with eggs baked in small wells on the surface.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Chop the onion, bell pepper, and garlic and rinse and drain the rice.
In an ovenproof casserole, sauté the vegetables in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the tomatoes and oregano and cook for 5 more minutes.
Add the rice, hot stock, and salt. Bring to a boil, cover, and bake for 22 minutes.
Check that the rice is almost tender. Make 4 shallow wells and crack an egg into each; cover and bake for 10 to 14 more minutes.
Check that the egg whites and yolks are firm and the center of the casserole reaches at least 74 °C. Rest for 5 minutes and serve an egg with each portion of rice.
tips: Crack each egg into a clean cup first so any shell fragments can be removed easily.

title: Rice and zucchini patties
description: Savory patties of cooked rice, drained zucchini, and cheese, browned in a skillet.

ingredients.name: cooked white rice
ingredients.note: Previously cooked, cooled promptly, and refrigerated until needed; do not leave for hours at room temperature.

steps: Grate the zucchini, mix with half the salt, and let drain for 10 minutes while preparing the rest. Squeeze it in a clean cloth.
Mix the separated cold rice grains, squeezed zucchini, beaten eggs, cheese, breadcrumbs, chopped scallions, and remaining salt.
Shape into 12 compact patties approximately 1 cm thick. Avoid making them thick so the centers heat thoroughly.
Heat some of the oil over medium heat and cook the patties in batches for 5 to 6 minutes per side. Add the remaining oil as needed for later batches.
Check that the centers of the patties reach 74 °C. Drain briefly on kitchen paper and serve hot, allowing 3 per person.
tips: If the mixture will not hold its shape, squeeze the zucchini more thoroughly before adding extra dry ingredients.

title: Rice with celery, olives, and lime
description: Aromatic rice with softened celery, green olives, and lime added at the end.
steps: Remove tough celery strings and thinly slice the stalks. Chop the onion and garlic and halve the olives.
Sauté the celery, onion, and garlic in the oil for 9 minutes, until the vegetables begin to soften.
Add the rinsed rice, olives, hot stock, and salt. Bring to a boil, stir once, and cover.
Cook over low heat for 22 minutes, until the rice is tender. Turn off the heat and rest covered for 10 minutes.
Add the lime juice and chopped parsley, fluff the rice with a fork, and taste before adding more salt. Serve as a light dish or side.
tips: Adding the lime juice at the end preserves its fresh aroma.

title: Rice with toasted corn and frying cheese
description: Garlic rice served with browned corn and cheese cubes that hold their shape when fried.

ingredients.name: frying cheese
ingredients.note: Firm cheese labeled for frying, not a cheese that melts easily.

steps: Chop the onion and garlic, pat the drained corn dry, and cut the cheese into 2 cm cubes. Rinse and drain the rice.
Sauté the onion and garlic in 1 tablespoon of oil for 6 minutes. Add the rice, stock, and salt; bring to a boil and cover.
Cook the rice over low heat for 20 minutes and rest covered for 5 minutes. Meanwhile, heat another tablespoon of oil in a skillet.
Sauté the corn for 8 minutes, until browned in places, and remove it. Add the remaining oil and brown the cheese for 2 to 3 minutes per side.
Mix the rice with the corn, chopped cilantro, and lime juice. Place the hot cheese on top and serve immediately to preserve its browned surface.
tips: Taste the cheese before adjusting the rice seasoning, as some brands are quite salty.

title: Black beans with mushrooms and roasted pepper
description: A thick stew of cooked black beans with browned mushrooms and roasted pepper strips.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained black beans
ingredients.note: Cooked and drained weight; use canned beans or pulses fully cooked beforehand.

ingredients.name: roasted and peeled red bell pepper

steps: Quarter the mushrooms and slice the roasted pepper into strips; finely chop the onion and garlic.
Brown the mushrooms in the oil in a wide pot for 7 minutes, stirring only occasionally.
Add the onion, garlic, and cumin; cook for 5 minutes without letting the garlic burn.
Add the beans, stock, pepper, and salt; simmer gently for 15 minutes, stirring along the bottom.
Mash a ladleful of beans against the side of the pot, stir, and cook for 3 minutes to thicken the broth.
tips: Brown the mushrooms before adding liquid for a deeper flavor.

title: Warm black bean and roasted corn salad
description: Black beans with skillet-browned corn, fresh pepper, and a lime dressing.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained black beans
ingredients.note: Cooked and drained weight; use canned beans or pulses fully cooked beforehand.

steps: Rinse the canned beans and drain well; finely dice the pepper and onion.
Heat one third of the oil and toast the corn for 8 minutes, until golden spots appear.
Add the beans and cumin; sauté for 4 minutes, folding gently to keep the beans whole.
Whisk the remaining oil with the lime juice and salt; wash, dry, and chop the cilantro into the dressing.
Toss the hot beans and corn with the pepper, onion, and dressing; serve immediately to retain the contrast.
tips: Drain the beans thoroughly so the dressing does not become watery.

title: Black bean soup with plantain chips
description: Smooth black bean soup with a mild sofrito and baked green plantain slices.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained black beans
ingredients.note: Cooked and drained weight; use canned beans or pulses fully cooked beforehand.

steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C and carefully slice the plantain 2 mm thick, keeping your fingers clear.
Coat the slices with one third of the oil and some salt; bake for 18 minutes, turning halfway through.
Meanwhile, sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the remaining oil for 6 minutes; add the cumin.
Add the beans, stock, and remaining salt; simmer gently for 18 minutes to blend the flavors.
Blend off the heat with an immersion blender, add the lime juice, and serve with the crisp chips on top.
tips: Add the chips just before serving so they do not soften in the soup.

title: Red beans with beef meatballs
description: Red kidney beans in tomato sauce with small oregano-seasoned beef meatballs.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained red kidney beans
ingredients.note: Cooked and drained weight; use canned beans or pulses fully cooked beforehand.

steps: Mix the beef with half the salt and oregano; shape into 3 cm meatballs and keep refrigerated.
Chop the onion and garlic and sauté in the oil for 6 minutes in a wide casserole.
Add the tomatoes, stock, and remaining salt and oregano; simmer for 8 minutes to make the sauce.
Add the meatballs and beans; cover and simmer gently for 18 minutes, shaking the casserole occasionally.
Use a thermometer to check that the meatball centers reach 71 °C; cook longer if needed, then serve.
tips: Use fully cooked beans; this short cooking time is unsuitable for dried beans.

title: Red beans with beetroot and cumin
description: Red bean stew with tender beetroot cubes and a touch of vinegar.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained red kidney beans
ingredients.note: Cooked and drained weight; use canned beans or pulses fully cooked beforehand.

steps: Peel the beetroot and cut into 1 cm cubes; chop the onion and crush the garlic.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes; add the cumin and beetroot and stir well.
Pour in the stock, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes, until the beetroot can be pierced easily.
Add the beans and salt; uncover and cook for 12 minutes to give the broth body.
Mash a small portion of the beans, stir in the vinegar, and serve without crushing the beetroot cubes.
tips: Small, evenly sized cubes help the beetroot soften evenly.

title: Red bean salad with avocado and tomato
description: A fresh red bean, avocado, and tomato salad with onion and lime.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained red kidney beans
ingredients.note: Cooked and drained weight; use canned beans or pulses fully cooked beforehand.

steps: Rinse and drain the canned beans; if home-cooked, use beans already chilled in the refrigerator.
Wash the tomatoes and cilantro; dice the tomatoes and chop the onion very finely.
Whisk the oil, lime juice, and salt in a salad bowl until the dressing is combined.
Add the beans, tomatoes, and onion; mix with a broad spoon to keep the beans intact.
Cut the avocado last, add it with chopped cilantro, and serve; keep refrigerated until ready to eat.
tips: A firm, ripe avocado holds its shape better when mixed.

title: Pinto bean stew with fresh pork ribs
description: Pork ribs slowly simmered with pinto beans and green pepper.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained pinto beans
ingredients.note: Cooked and drained weight; use canned beans or pulses fully cooked beforehand.

steps: Separate the ribs into individual pieces; chop the onion and pepper and crush the garlic.
Brown the ribs in the oil for 8 minutes; add the onion, pepper, and garlic and sauté for 6 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, water, bay leaf, and salt; cover and simmer gently for 75 minutes, until the ribs are tender.
Add the beans and cook for 15 more minutes; check for at least 63 °C in the meat without touching bone, and cook longer if needed.
Remove the bay leaf and any loose bone fragments; rest off the heat for 3 minutes before serving.
tips: Tender ribs need longer cooking than simply reaching their minimum temperature.

title: Pinto beans with eggplant and tomato
description: A vegetable stew of pinto beans, browned eggplant, and oregano tomato sauce.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained pinto beans
ingredients.note: Cooked and drained weight; use canned beans or pulses fully cooked beforehand.

steps: Cut the eggplant into 2 cm cubes and chop the onion and garlic; drain the fully cooked beans.
Brown the eggplant in two thirds of the oil for 10 minutes in a wide casserole, then remove it.
Add the remaining oil, onion, and garlic; sauté for 5 minutes, then add the tomatoes and oregano.
Return the eggplant, add the beans, stock, and salt, and cook covered over low heat for 18 minutes.
Uncover and cook for 5 more minutes; serve when the eggplant is creamy and the broth lightly coats the beans.
tips: A wide casserole lets the eggplant brown without crowding.

title: White beans with chicken and celery
description: A light white bean stew with chicken cubes and tender celery.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained white beans
ingredients.note: Cooked and drained weight; use canned beans or pulses fully cooked beforehand.

steps: Chop the onion, garlic, and celery; cut the chicken into 2 cm cubes on a board separate from ready-to-eat vegetables.
Sauté the onion, garlic, and celery in the oil for 6 minutes in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Add the chicken, stock, bay leaf, and salt; bring to a gentle simmer and cook covered for 15 minutes.
Add the beans and cook for 10 more minutes; check for 74 °C in the centers of several chicken cubes.
Remove the bay leaf, add the washed, chopped parsley, and serve the stew with its light broth.
tips: Add the beans toward the end to keep their shape as the chicken finishes cooking.

title: Baked white beans with a breadcrumb crust
description: White beans in tomato sauce topped with golden garlic breadcrumbs.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained white beans
ingredients.note: Cooked and drained weight; use canned beans or pulses fully cooked beforehand.

steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C; chop the onion, garlic, and parsley, reserving half the garlic for the topping.
Sauté the onion and the garlic intended for the sauce in two thirds of the oil for 6 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, stock, oregano, salt, and beans; cook for 10 minutes, then transfer to a shallow baking dish.
Mix the breadcrumbs, parsley, reserved garlic, and remaining oil; spread loosely over the beans.
Bake for 20 minutes, until the topping is golden and the center reaches 74 °C; rest for 5 minutes before serving.
tips: Use a wide baking dish to make a thin, crisp breadcrumb layer.

title: White bean and asparagus soup
description: A smooth white bean soup with green asparagus and a little lime juice.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained white beans
ingredients.note: Cooked and drained weight; use canned beans or pulses fully cooked beforehand.

steps: Wash the asparagus, remove the woody bases, and set aside the tips; slice the tender stems.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes without letting them brown too much.
Add the asparagus stems, beans, stock, and salt; cook at a gentle simmer for 15 minutes.
Blend off the heat with an immersion blender; return to the heat and add the asparagus tips.
Cook for 5 more minutes, until the tips soften; add the lime juice and divide the soup among bowls.
tips: Keeping the tips whole makes the asparagus visible in the blended soup.

title: Black-eyed peas with okra and tomato
description: Black-eyed peas in a stew of okra, tomatoes, and green pepper.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained black-eyed peas
ingredients.note: Cooked and drained weight; use canned beans or pulses fully cooked beforehand.

steps: Wash and dry the okra, trim the stems, and cut into large pieces; chop the other vegetables.
Sauté the onion, pepper, and garlic in the oil for 7 minutes in a wide casserole.
Add the tomatoes, stock, and salt and simmer for 8 minutes to concentrate the base.
Add the okra and black-eyed peas; cover and cook for 15 minutes, shaking the casserole without stirring excessively.
Check that the okra is tender, add the lime juice, and serve while the beans still hold their shape.
tips: Cut the okra into large pieces so it retains its texture in the stew.

title: Black-eyed pea salad with cucumber and orange
description: Chilled black-eyed peas with crunchy cucumber, orange segments, and cilantro.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained black-eyed peas
ingredients.note: Cooked and drained weight; use canned beans or pulses fully cooked beforehand.

steps: Rinse and drain canned black-eyed peas; keep previously home-cooked peas chilled.
Wash the cucumber and slice it into thin half-moons; chop the onion and cilantro.
Separate the orange into segments, remove thick white pith, and collect the juice in a salad bowl.
Whisk the collected juice with the oil, vinegar, and salt; add the peas, cucumber, and onion.
Gently fold in the orange segments and cilantro; serve chilled or keep covered in the refrigerator until eating.
tips: Remove large cucumber seeds to reduce the water released into the salad.

title: Chickpeas with eggplant and hard-boiled egg
description: Chickpeas stewed with eggplant and tomatoes, finished with hard-boiled egg wedges.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained chickpeas
ingredients.note: Cooked and drained weight; use canned beans or pulses fully cooked beforehand.

steps: Cover the eggs with the water, bring to a boil, and simmer gently for 11 minutes; cool under running water and peel when safe to handle.
Dice the eggplant and sauté in the oil for 8 minutes; add the chopped onion and garlic.
Cook for 5 more minutes, then add the tomatoes, cumin, salt, and stock, stirring along the bottom.
Add the chickpeas, cover, and simmer for 18 minutes, until the eggplant can be mashed easily.
Cut the eggs and check that whites and yolks are firm; arrange over the hot stew and serve immediately.
tips: Cook the eggs while preparing the stew to reduce the total time.

title: Crisp chickpeas with roasted cauliflower
description: Golden chickpeas and roasted cauliflower with paprika, garlic, and lime.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained chickpeas
ingredients.note: Cooked and drained weight; use canned beans or pulses fully cooked beforehand.

steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C; dry the chickpeas thoroughly and cut the cauliflower into medium florets.
Mix the oil, crushed garlic, paprika, cumin, and salt in a large bowl.
Add the chickpeas and cauliflower, toss, and spread on a large baking tray without piling them deeply.
Roast for 30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the cauliflower is tender and the chickpeas are golden.
Add the lime juice and washed, chopped parsley when the tray leaves the oven; serve immediately to keep the edges crisp.
tips: If the tray is crowded, divide the contents among more trays to encourage browning.

title: Chickpea soup with elbow pasta and chard
description: Chickpea soup with short pasta, tender chard, and tomato sofrito.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained chickpeas
ingredients.note: Cooked and drained weight; use canned beans or pulses fully cooked beforehand.

steps: Wash the chard and separate the stems from the leaves; finely chop the stems and slice the leaves.
Sauté the onion, garlic, and stems in the oil for 6 minutes; add the tomatoes and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the stock, chickpeas, and salt; bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 8 minutes.
Add the elbow pasta and cook for the time stated on the package, stirring to prevent sticking.
Add the leaves during the final 4 minutes of the pasta cooking time; serve with tender pasta and plenty of broth.
tips: Pasta absorbs broth as it stands, so this soup is best served immediately.

title: Lentils with turkey sausage and pepper
description: Lentils with sliced fully cooked turkey sausage and red bell pepper.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained lentils
ingredients.note: Cooked and drained weight; use canned beans or pulses fully cooked beforehand.

ingredients.name: fully cooked turkey sausage
ingredients.note: Check that the label states fully cooked; also check its allergens.

steps: Slice the fully cooked sausage; chop the onion, pepper, and garlic into small pieces.
Brown the sausage in half the oil for 4 minutes, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and vegetables; sauté for 7 minutes, then add the tomatoes and oregano.
Add the stock, lentils, salt, and sausage; simmer gently for 15 minutes, stirring without breaking up the lentils.
Check that the sausage slices reach 74 °C in the center; cook longer if needed, then serve.
tips: Taste the broth before adding more salt, as the sausage may already contribute plenty.

title: Lentils with sweet potato and green beans
description: Lentil stew with sweet potato, green beans, and cumin-seasoned tomatoes.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained lentils
ingredients.note: Cooked and drained weight; use canned beans or pulses fully cooked beforehand.

steps: Peel the sweet potato and cut into 2 cm cubes; trim the green beans and cut into short pieces.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes; add the cumin and tomatoes and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the sweet potato, stock, and salt and simmer gently, covered, for 12 minutes.
Add the lentils and green beans; cook for 12 more minutes, until both vegetables are tender.
Gently shake the pot to combine the broth; serve without crushing the tender sweet potato cubes.
tips: Cut the sweet potato evenly to avoid hard pieces alongside broken-down ones.

title: Warm lentil and roasted pumpkin salad
description: Lentils with roasted pumpkin, browned onion, and parsley dressing.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained lentils
ingredients.note: Cooked and drained weight; use canned beans or pulses fully cooked beforehand.

steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C; peel and seed the pumpkin and cut into 2 cm cubes.
Cut the onion into wedges and toss with the pumpkin, cumin, some salt, and two thirds of the oil.
Spread on a baking tray and roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until the edges are golden.
Whisk the remaining oil, vinegar, chopped parsley, and remaining salt; mix with the drained lentils.
Fold in the freshly roasted pumpkin and onion and serve warm without leaving it to stand at room temperature.
tips: The pumpkin should retain its shape to contrast with the lentils.

title: Lentil soup with roasted red pepper
description: Smooth lentil and roasted pepper soup with garlic, cumin, and a lime finish.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained lentils
ingredients.note: Cooked and drained weight; use canned beans or pulses fully cooked beforehand.

ingredients.name: roasted and peeled red bell pepper

steps: Drain the cooked lentils and chop the roasted pepper; reserve a few strips for serving.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes; add the cumin and stir briefly.
Add the lentils, pepper, stock, and salt; cook at a gentle simmer for 18 minutes.
Remove the pot from the heat and blend with an immersion blender, keeping the head submerged to avoid splashes.
Add the lime juice, heat for 2 more minutes, and serve with the reserved pepper strips.
tips: If using jarred peppers, drain them before weighing so they do not dilute the soup.

title: Split peas with corn and pumpkin
description: A split pea stew slowly thickened with pumpkin and sweet corn.
steps: Sort and rinse the split peas; peel the pumpkin and cut into medium cubes.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes; add the cumin, split peas, and water.
Bring to a boil and simmer gently for 35 minutes, skimming foam and occasionally stirring along the bottom.
Add the pumpkin, corn, and salt; cook for 25 more minutes, until the split peas break down and the pumpkin is tender.
Stir to blend some of the pumpkin into the broth; if the peas remain firm, continue cooking before serving.
tips: Thick split peas stick easily, so stir especially often toward the end of cooking.

title: Tender fava bean soup with potato and leek
description: A mild soup of tender fava beans, potatoes, and leeks, finished with fresh parsley.

ingredients.name: shelled tender fava beans
ingredients.note: Fresh or frozen and removed from their pods; not dried fava beans.

steps: Wash between the leek layers and slice; peel the potatoes and cut into 1 cm cubes.
Sauté the leek and chopped garlic in the oil for 6 minutes over low heat to prevent burning.
Add the potato, stock, and salt; simmer gently for 12 minutes with the pot partially covered.
Add the tender fava beans and cook for 12 more minutes, or until easily crushed with a fork.
Mash a few potatoes to thicken the broth, fold in washed, chopped parsley, and serve hot.
tips: If the fava beans have tough outer skins, remove them before adding to the soup.

title: Barley and vegetable sofrito soup
description: Pearl barley with carrots, celery, and tomatoes in vegetable broth.
steps: Rinse and drain the barley; peel the carrots and dice all the vegetables finely.
Sauté the onion, celery, carrots, and garlic in the oil for 8 minutes, stirring to soften them.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes; add the barley, stock, bay leaf, and salt.
Simmer gently for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the barley is tender but retains texture.
Remove the bay leaf and serve with plenty of broth; if the barley remains firm, cook longer according to its package.
tips: Barley continues absorbing broth as it stands, so serve the soup freshly made.

title: Savory oat and chicken soup
description: A thick oat soup with chicken, carrots, and celery, seasoned with a mild sofrito.
steps: Chop the onion, garlic, celery, and carrots; cut the chicken into small cubes on a separate board.
Sauté the vegetables in the oil for 7 minutes in a large pot, stirring to soften them.
Add the stock, salt, and chicken; simmer gently for 18 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74 °C in the center.
Sprinkle in the oats and cook for 7 minutes, stirring along the bottom until the flakes are soft.
Add the washed, chopped parsley; serve immediately before the oats absorb too much broth.
tips: Choose plain oats without sugar or added flavors to keep the soup savory.

title: Turkey broth with yam and carrot
description: Homemade broth with tender turkey, yam, and large carrot pieces.
steps: Place the turkey in a pot with the water, quartered onion, garlic, celery, bay leaves, and salt; bring to a gentle simmer.
Skim the foam and cook covered for 60 minutes, or until the meat reaches 74 °C without touching the bone.
Transfer the turkey to a clean tray, discard skin and bones when safe to handle, and separate into pieces.
Strain the broth, return it to the pot, and add the peeled yam and carrots in 3 cm chunks; cook for 25 minutes.
Return the turkey, simmer gently for 5 minutes, and add the washed cilantro; serve when the yam is easily pierced.
tips: The meat should be tender as well as reach its safe temperature; cook longer if it still resists a fork.

title: Chicken meatball and rice soup
description: Small chicken meatballs with rice cooked in the broth and tender carrots.
steps: Mix the ground chicken with oregano and some salt; shape into 3 cm balls and refrigerate while preparing the broth.
Sauté the chopped onion, garlic, and carrots in the oil for 7 minutes; add the stock and remaining salt.
Bring to a boil, add the rinsed rice and meatballs one at a time, and stir gently to separate them.
Simmer gently for 20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the meatball centers reach 74 °C.
Add the washed, chopped parsley and serve immediately, distributing rice, broth, and meatballs evenly.
tips: Shape the meatballs evenly so they cook at the same rate.

title: Pork soup with cabbage and potato
description: Pork shoulder simmered in broth with cabbage strips and tender potatoes.
steps: Cut the pork into 3 cm cubes; peel the potatoes and slice the cabbage into wide strips.
Brown the pork in the oil for 8 minutes; add the chopped onion and garlic and sauté for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, water, cumin, and salt; cover and simmer for 55 minutes until the meat begins to soften.
Add the potatoes and cabbage and cook for 25 more minutes; check that the meat is tender and at least 63 °C inside.
Rest off the heat for 3 minutes, then serve the meat and vegetables with their broth.
tips: Use a pork cut suitable for stewing; very lean cuts can become dry.

title: Beef broth with chickpeas and celery
description: Slow-simmered beef with chickpeas, celery, and carrots in a clear broth.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained chickpeas
ingredients.note: Cooked and drained weight; use canned beans or pulses fully cooked beforehand.

steps: Cut the beef into 4 cm pieces and place in a pot with the water, quartered onion, garlic, and bay leaves.
Bring to a gentle simmer, skim the foam, and cook covered for 90 minutes; avoid a vigorous boil that clouds the broth.
Add the chopped celery and carrots, salt, and chickpeas; cook for 30 more minutes until the beef is tender.
Check for at least 63 °C in the center of the meat; cook longer if it still resists a fork.
Remove the bay leaves, add the washed parsley, and rest for 3 minutes before serving with the broth.
tips: Skim surface fat with a spoon for a cleaner-tasting broth.

title: Squid soup with potatoes and pepper
description: Squid slowly simmered with potatoes, tomatoes, and red pepper in a savory broth.
steps: Cut the cleaned squid into rings; peel the potatoes and cut into 2 cm cubes, and chop the other vegetables.
Sauté the onion, pepper, and garlic in the oil for 7 minutes; add the paprika and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the squid, water, and salt; cover and cook at a gentle simmer for 25 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cook for 20 more minutes, until tender and the squid yields easily when bitten.
Check that the squid is fully opaque and at least 63 °C; add the washed, chopped parsley and serve.
tips: If the squid remains tough, continue simmering gently rather than increasing the heat.

title: Mussel soup with tomato and corn
description: Mussels steamed open in a tomato, corn, and sofrito broth.
steps: Scrub the shells and remove the beards; discard broken mussels or open ones that do not close when gently tapped.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes; add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the water, corn, and salt; simmer for 10 minutes to cook the corn and blend the flavors.
Add the mussels and cover; cook for 6 minutes, shaking the pot, and extend briefly if needed for them to open.
Discard all mussels that remain closed; add the washed parsley and serve immediately with the broth.
tips: Buy shellfish from a regulated food supplier and keep refrigerated until cooking.

title: Shrimp soup with noodles and coconut
description: Shrimp and thin noodles in a coconut, tomato, and pepper broth.
steps: Chop the onion, garlic, and pepper; keep the cleaned shrimp refrigerated while preparing the base.
Sauté the vegetables in the oil for 7 minutes; add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the water, coconut milk, and salt; simmer for 8 minutes, stirring to blend the coconut milk.
Add the noodles and cook according to the package; add the shrimp during the final 5 minutes.
Check that the shrimp are firm, pearly, and opaque; cook longer if necessary and finish with lime juice and washed cilantro.
tips: Use noodles requiring at least the stated shrimp cooking time, or add them after the shrimp.

title: Fish soup with okra and lime
description: White fish pieces and okra in a tomato broth finished with lime juice.
steps: Wash and cut the okra into pieces; cut the fish into large cubes and check for remaining bones.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes; add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the water, salt, and okra; simmer gently for 15 minutes until the pods soften.
Add the fish and cook for 7 minutes without stirring vigorously; check for 63 °C in the centers of the pieces.
Add the lime juice and washed, chopped cilantro; serve immediately, keeping the fish pieces whole.
tips: Firm-fleshed fish holds its shape better in this broth.

title: Carrot soup with roasted peanuts
description: Carrot and potato soup thickened with roasted peanuts and lightly seasoned with cumin.
steps: Peel the carrots and potato and dice them; reserve a small portion of the peanuts for serving.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes; add the cumin and diced vegetables.
Add the stock, salt, and peanuts intended for blending; simmer for 25 minutes until the vegetables soften.
Remove from the heat and blend with an immersion blender until no hard peanut pieces remain.
Add the lime juice, heat for 2 minutes, and serve with the reserved peanuts finely chopped on top.
tips: Peanuts give the soup body; check their texture while blending before finishing the soup.

title: Beetroot soup with plain yogurt
description: Blended beetroot and potato soup finished with mild plain yogurt.
steps: Peel the beetroot and potato and dice finely; chop the onion and garlic and keep the yogurt refrigerated.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes; add the vegetables and stir to coat them.
Add the stock and salt; cover and simmer for 40 minutes, until the beetroot can be pierced without resistance.
Blend off the heat with an immersion blender; add the lime juice and stir until smooth.
Serve the soup hot and divide the yogurt among the bowls, stirring gently without boiling again.
tips: Add the yogurt at serving time for a creamy contrast without curdling it by boiling.

title: Potato and watercress soup
description: Potato and leek soup with watercress added near the end to preserve its color.
steps: Wash the watercress thoroughly and remove tough stems; clean the leek and peel the potatoes.
Slice the leek and sauté with the chopped garlic and oil for 6 minutes without excessive browning.
Add the diced potatoes, stock, salt, and pepper; cook covered for 22 minutes until the potatoes soften.
Add the washed watercress and cook for 4 minutes until the leaves are tender.
Remove from the heat and blend briefly with an immersion blender; serve without overblending to avoid a gluey texture.
tips: Cooked potato needs little blending; stop once the soup is smooth.

title: Roasted eggplant and tomato soup
description: Roasted eggplant and tomatoes blended with garlic and stock into a deeply flavored soup.
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C; halve the eggplants and quarter the tomatoes and onion.
Place the vegetables and peeled garlic in a baking dish; coat with oil and season with salt and oregano.
Roast for 35 minutes, until the eggplant flesh can be scooped out easily with a spoon.
Remove the eggplant skins and transfer the flesh to a pot with the other vegetables, their juices, and the stock.
Blend with an immersion blender and simmer gently for 8 minutes; stir and serve with an even texture.
tips: Keep the roasting juices, as they add flavor and make full use of the roasted vegetables.

title: Cabbage and green plantain soup
description: Cabbage and green plantain in a tomato broth with cumin and garlic.
steps: Slice the cabbage into strips and the peeled plantain into 1 cm half-moons; chop the onion and garlic.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes; add the tomatoes and cumin and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the plantain, stock, and salt and simmer for 15 minutes with the pot partially covered.
Add the cabbage and cook for 15 more minutes, until the plantain can be mashed easily with a fork.
Mash a few plantain pieces to give the broth body; add the washed cilantro and serve hot.
tips: Green plantain is used as a starchy vegetable here and should become completely tender.

title: Zucchini soup with cheese dumplings
description: A zucchini broth with small dumplings made from white cheese, flour, and egg.
steps: Crumble the cheese and mix with the egg and flour; shape into 2 cm balls and refrigerate while preparing the soup.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes; add the diced zucchini.
Add the stock and salt; simmer gently for 10 minutes until the zucchini begins to soften.
Add the dumplings one at a time and simmer gently for 12 minutes; check for at least 71 °C in the center and fully cooked dough.
Add the washed, chopped parsley; serve with a broad spoon to avoid breaking the tender dumplings.
tips: Drain the cheese well so the mixture holds its shape in the broth.

title: Broccoli soup with white cheese
description: Broccoli and potato blended with milk, finished with crumbled white cheese.
steps: Wash the broccoli and separate the florets; peel the tender stems and dice them along with the peeled potato.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes; add the potato, stems, stock, salt, and pepper.
Simmer gently for 15 minutes; add the florets and cook for 8 more minutes until tender.
Remove from the heat and blend briefly; add the milk and heat for 3 minutes, stirring without a vigorous boil.
Divide the crumbled white cheese among bowls and pour the hot soup over it to serve.
tips: Add the florets after the stems so they do not break down while cooking.

title: Mushroom soup with corn and parsley
description: Browned mushrooms with corn and small potato cubes in vegetable broth.
steps: Clean the mushrooms and cut into thick slices; peel the potato and cut into 1 cm cubes.
Brown the mushrooms in two thirds of the oil for 8 minutes in a wide pot, then remove them.
Add the remaining oil and chopped onion and garlic; sauté for 5 minutes, then add the potato, corn, stock, salt, and pepper.
Simmer gently for 18 minutes, until the potatoes soften; return the mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the washed, chopped parsley and serve immediately, dividing the browned mushroom slices among the bowls.
tips: Set the browned mushrooms aside while cooking the potatoes so they retain more texture.

title: Cassava stew with okra and tomato
description: Tender cassava and okra in a thick tomato and sweet pepper sauce.
steps: Boil the cassava in 1500 ml of the water for 25 to 35 minutes, until completely tender.
Drain the cassava, discard all its cooking water and remove the tough central fiber; cut into chunks.
Wash and dry the okra and cut it into rounds; chop the onion and garlic.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes; add tomato, oregano, salt and the remaining 300 ml water.
Add the okra, cover and simmer for 12 minutes; add the cassava and cook for 5 more minutes, stirring gently.
tips: Use commercially sold sweet cassava and discard its cooking water; make the sauce with fresh water.

title: Warm yam salad with green beans and roasted pepper
description: Diced yam with tender green beans and a roasted pepper dressing.
steps: Roast the whole pepper at 220 °C for 25 minutes, turning halfway through cooking.
Peel the yam and cut into 2 cm cubes; boil in the water for 18 to 25 minutes until tender.
Cook the green beans in the same pot for the final 6 minutes; drain both vegetables well.
Remove the roasted pepper skin and seeds and blend it with the garlic, oil, lime juice and salt.
Toss the warm vegetables with the dressing in a serving dish without crushing the yam cubes.
tips: The yam must be completely cooked before tossing it with the dressing.

title: Layered taro with pumpkin and coconut milk
description: Slices of taro and pumpkin baked in a light coconut and garlic sauce.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C and grease a 22 cm baking dish with the measured oil.
Slice the peeled taro and pumpkin into even 3 mm slices for uniform cooking.
Heat the coconut milk, water, crushed garlic, nutmeg and salt until the mixture begins to steam.
Alternate layers of the root and pumpkin slices, add the hot mixture, cover and bake for 50 minutes.
Uncover and bake for 15 more minutes, until the taro is easily pierced; let stand for 5 minutes.
tips: Do not taste raw taro: the slices must soften completely during baking.

title: Semi-ripe plantain mash with garlic and leek
description: Savory semi-ripe plantain mash with softened leek and garlic oil.
steps: Cut the peeled plantain into chunks and boil in the water for 20 to 25 minutes, until very tender.
Split the leek, wash between its layers and chop only the white and light green parts; crush the garlic.
Heat the oil over medium heat and soften the leek for 8 minutes without browning; add garlic for 1 minute.
Reserve 200 ml of the plantain cooking water and drain the rest; mash the hot plantain with salt and pepper.
Fold in the leek and add the reserved water a little at a time, just until smooth; serve the mash hot.
tips: Choose firm yellow plantains with some green areas and few black patches.

title: Roasted sweet potato with peanut and lime sauce
description: Sweet potato wedges with a creamy roasted peanut, lime and cumin sauce.
steps: Heat the oven to 205 °C and cut the sweet potato into wedges of similar thickness.
Toss the sweet potato with the oil and half the salt; spread on a tray without crowding.
Roast for 35 to 40 minutes, turning the wedges halfway through, until tender and golden.
Blend the peanuts, lime juice, water, garlic, cumin and remaining salt into a thick, smooth sauce.
Arrange the hot sweet potato and spoon some sauce over it; serve the remaining sauce separately.
tips: If your blender is small, grind the peanuts first and then add the liquids.

title: Chayotes stuffed with corn and red beans
description: Chayote halves filled with red beans, corn and melted cheese.
steps: Halve the chayotes and boil in the water for 20 to 25 minutes, until tender but still holding their shape.
Drain, remove the hard centers and scoop out some flesh, leaving thick walls; chop the scooped flesh.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes; add the flesh, beans, corn and salt and cook for 4 minutes.
Fill the chayote halves, scatter the cheese over them and place on a tray; bake at 190 °C for 20 minutes.
Check that the filling reaches 74 °C and serve two chayote halves per person.
tips: The beans must be fully cooked; rinse and drain canned beans before measuring them.

title: Pumpkin in a mild orange escabeche
description: Roasted pumpkin cubes and onion with a warm orange and vinegar dressing.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C and cut the pumpkin into 3 cm cubes so it holds its shape.
Toss the pumpkin with two tablespoons of oil and half the salt; roast for 25 minutes until tender.
Slice the onion and sauté it in the remaining oil with the chopped garlic for 5 minutes.
Add the orange juice, vinegar, bay leaf and remaining salt and simmer for 3 minutes to combine the dressing.
Pour over the pumpkin, remove the bay leaf and serve warm or refrigerate in a shallow container to serve cold.
tips: Keep this dish refrigerated; this mild escabeche is not suitable for room-temperature preservation.

title: Roasted eggplant with white bean cream
description: Roasted eggplant served over a savory white bean, garlic and lime cream.
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C and cut the eggplants into thick 2 cm rounds.
Brush the slices with two tablespoons of oil and add half the salt; spread them on a baking tray.
Roast for 30 minutes, turning halfway through, until the centers are soft and the edges golden.
Blend the beans, water, lime juice, garlic, paprika and remaining oil and salt; heat in a saucepan for 5 minutes.
Spread the hot bean cream on a serving dish and arrange the roasted eggplant slices on top.
tips: Well-drained canned beans make a smooth cream without additional bean cooking time.

title: Baked ripe plantain with onion and cumin
description: Ripe plantain in a savory preparation with browned onion and cumin.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C and slice the peeled plantains diagonally into 2 cm pieces.
Cut the onion into thin wedges and combine it with the plantains in a large bowl.
Add the oil, cumin and salt; toss gently and spread everything in one layer on a tray.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until the plantain is tender and the onion begins to brown.
Transfer to a serving dish, drizzle with the lime juice and serve hot alongside a stew or rice.
tips: Very soft plantain falls apart when tossed; choose ripe plantain that is still firm.

title: Cauliflower gratin with taro mash
description: Cauliflower covered with smooth taro mash and a golden cheese topping.
steps: Dice the taro and boil it in the water for 25 minutes, until completely tender.
Remove the taro and boil the cauliflower in the same pot for 6 minutes; drain well and place in a baking dish.
Heat the milk with the crushed garlic for 3 minutes; mash the taro with that milk, butter and salt.
Cover the cauliflower with the mash, scatter over the cheese and bake at 200 °C for 20 minutes.
Check that the center is thoroughly hot at 74 °C and let stand for 5 minutes before serving.
tips: Drain the cauliflower well so it does not release excess water into the mash during baking.

title: Watercress, mango and pumpkin seed salad
description: Watercress leaves with fresh mango and toasted seeds in a citrus dressing.
steps: Pick over the watercress, remove tough stems and wash the leaves under running water; drain and dry.
Cut the mango into cubes and the cucumber into thin half-moons; keep them separate.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan for 3 minutes, shaking the pan so they do not burn.
Whisk the oil, lime juice and salt in a salad bowl; gently fold in the watercress, mango and cucumber.
Scatter the seeds over the salad just before serving so they retain their crisp texture.
tips: Wash the leaves before cutting them and dry them thoroughly so the dressing is not diluted.

title: Cucumber, pineapple and sweet pepper salad
description: Crisp cucumber with fresh pineapple, sweet pepper and mint.
steps: Wash the cucumber, pepper and mint under running water; dry the leaves before chopping.
Remove the fibrous pineapple core and dice the fruit; cut the cucumber into thin half-moons.
Remove the pepper seeds and dice the pepper finely; chop the mint and combine it with the pepper.
Whisk the oil, lime juice and salt; toss with the pineapple, cucumber and pepper without crushing the fruit.
Refrigerate the covered salad for 15 minutes and serve with a spoon to include its juices.
tips: Use ripe but firm pineapple so the cubes retain their shape.

title: Beet, chickpea and mint salad
description: Cooked beets with chickpeas, red onion and a lime dressing.
steps: Drain the chickpeas; if canned, rinse them first and allow excess water to drain away.
Dice the already cooked beets and slice the red onion into very thin strips.
Wash and dry the mint; chop the leaves and reserve a few small pieces for finishing.
Whisk the oil, lime juice, cumin and salt; toss with the beets, chickpeas, onion and mint.
Let stand in the refrigerator for 20 minutes; toss again and serve with the reserved mint.
tips: Measure the beets after cooking; their color will naturally tint the chickpeas.

title: Roasted tomato, avocado and onion salad
description: Roasted and cooled tomatoes with creamy avocado and fresh onion.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C, wash the tomatoes and cut them into thick wedges.
Toss the tomatoes with one tablespoon of oil, oregano and half the salt; roast for 20 minutes.
Transfer the tomatoes to a shallow dish and refrigerate for 20 minutes, until no longer hot.
Slice the onion finely and dice the avocado; whisk the lime juice with the remaining oil and salt.
Gently toss the tomatoes, avocado and onion with the dressing without crushing the roasted wedges.
tips: Keep the roasted tomato juices and mix them into the dressing.

title: Cabbage, guava and yogurt slaw
description: Finely shredded cabbage with fresh guava and a light yogurt-lime dressing.
steps: Wash the cabbage and remove damaged leaves; shred it finely and place in a salad bowl.
Wash, peel and grate the carrot; wash the guavas, remove the seeded centers and thinly slice the flesh.
Whisk the yogurt, lime juice, honey and salt in a bowl until the dressing is smooth.
Mix the cabbage and carrot with the dressing; fold in the guava last to keep the slices intact.
Refrigerate for 20 minutes before serving and stir gently to redistribute the dressing.
tips: Removing the hard seeds makes the guava more pleasant to eat in the slaw.

title: Green bean, potato and olive salad
description: Potatoes and green beans with green olives and a parsley dressing.
steps: Dice the potatoes and boil them in the water for 15 to 20 minutes, until tender but still intact.
Trim the green beans and add them to the pot for the final 6 minutes of cooking.
Drain both vegetables, spread in a shallow container and refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Chop the parsley and olives; whisk the oil, lime juice and salt and stir the parsley into the dressing.
Toss the vegetables and olives with the dressing; serve the salad cold or slightly warm.
tips: Taste the olives before adjusting seasoning: some canned olives add substantial salt.

title: Chayote, corn and white cheese salad
description: Cool cooked chayote with corn, white cheese and cilantro.
steps: Peel the chayotes, remove the hard centers and cut into evenly sized cubes.
Boil the cubes in the water for 12 to 15 minutes, until tender; drain thoroughly.
Spread the chayote in a shallow container and refrigerate for 20 minutes before adding the cheese.
Chop the onion and cilantro; dice the cheese and whisk the oil, lime juice and salt in a salad bowl.
Add the chayote, corn, cheese, onion and cilantro to the dressing; toss and serve while cool.
tips: Drying the chayote well keeps the dressing from becoming watery as it stands.

title: Cassava, tuna and tomato salad
description: Cooked cassava with canned tuna, fresh tomato and parsley.
steps: Boil the cassava in the water for 25 to 35 minutes, until completely tender.
Discard the water, remove the central fiber and dice the cassava; refrigerate in a shallow dish for 25 minutes.
Wash and cut the tomato, chop the onion and parsley and thoroughly drain the canned tuna.
Whisk the oil, lime juice and salt; toss first with the cooled cassava and then add tomato and onion.
Gently fold in the tuna and parsley and keep the salad refrigerated until serving.
tips: Use commercially canned tuna and measure the quantity after draining it.

title: Yam, avocado and radish salad
description: Cooked yam with avocado, radishes and a lime-chive dressing.
steps: Cut the peeled yam into 2 cm cubes and boil in the water for 20 to 25 minutes until completely tender.
Drain the yam, spread it in a shallow container and refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Wash the radishes and chives; thinly slice the radishes and finely chop the chives.
Cut the avocado and coat with some of the lime juice; whisk the remaining juice with oil and salt.
Toss the yam and radishes with the dressing, gently fold in the avocado and finish with the chives.
tips: Fold in the avocado last so it does not turn into a mash while mixing.

title: Spinach, roasted plantain and peanut salad
description: Fresh spinach with roasted ripe plantain, tomato and toasted peanuts.
steps: Heat the oven to 205 °C and cut the plantain diagonally into 1 cm slices.
Toss the plantain with one tablespoon of oil and roast for 20 minutes, turning halfway through.
Transfer the plantain to a plate and let it cool for 5 minutes while washing and drying the spinach and tomato.
Cut the tomato into wedges and whisk the lime juice with the remaining oil and salt.
Toss the spinach, tomato and warm plantain with the dressing; add the roasted peanuts and serve immediately.
tips: Do not put plantain straight from the oven onto the leaves, which would make them wilt.

title: Turkey and corn croquettes
description: Fine-crusted croquettes with a creamy turkey and corn filling.
steps: Finely chop the cooked turkey and drain the corn; keep both chilled while preparing the base.
Chop the onion and soften it in the butter for 5 minutes; add 80 g of flour and stir for 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in the milk; cook for 5 minutes until thick and fold in the prepared filling, salt and pepper.
Stir for 3 minutes, spread the mixture in a shallow dish and refrigerate for 120 minutes until firm.
Shape 16 croquettes; coat with the remaining 20 g flour, the beaten eggs and the breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil to 175 °C and fry in batches for 4 to 6 minutes, until golden and 74 °C at the center; drain.
tips: Keep the uncooked breaded croquettes refrigerated until frying so the coating holds together.

title: Pumpkin and white cheese croquettes
description: Fine-crusted croquettes with a creamy pumpkin and white cheese filling.

ingredients.name: drained cooked pumpkin puree
ingredients.note: Thick and cold; without cooking liquid.

steps: Thoroughly drain the cooked pumpkin puree and crumble the cheese; the filling must not release water.
Chop the onion and soften it in the butter for 5 minutes; add 80 g of flour and stir for 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in the milk; cook for 5 minutes until thick and fold in the prepared filling, salt and pepper.
Stir for 3 minutes, spread the mixture in a shallow dish and refrigerate for 120 minutes until firm.
Shape 16 croquettes; coat with the remaining 20 g flour, the beaten eggs and the breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil to 175 °C and fry in batches for 4 to 6 minutes, until golden and 74 °C at the center; drain.
tips: Keep the uncooked breaded croquettes refrigerated until frying so the coating holds together.

title: Lentil and cumin croquettes
description: Fine-crusted croquettes with a creamy lentil and cumin filling.
steps: Mash the cooked, thoroughly drained lentils with the cumin into a paste that retains some texture.
Chop the onion and soften it in the butter for 5 minutes; add 80 g of flour and stir for 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in the milk; cook for 5 minutes until thick and fold in the prepared filling, salt and pepper.
Stir for 3 minutes, spread the mixture in a shallow dish and refrigerate for 120 minutes until firm.
Shape 16 croquettes; coat with the remaining 20 g flour, the beaten eggs and the breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil to 175 °C and fry in batches for 4 to 6 minutes, until golden and 74 °C at the center; drain.
tips: Keep the uncooked breaded croquettes refrigerated until frying so the coating holds together.

title: Ripe plantain and onion croquettes
description: Fine-crusted croquettes with a creamy ripe plantain and onion filling.

ingredients.name: cooked mashed ripe plantain
ingredients.note: Weighed without peel, already cooked and refrigerated.

steps: Check that the cooked plantain mash is cold and contains no water; break up lumps with a fork.
Chop the onion and soften it in the butter for 5 minutes; add 80 g of flour and stir for 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in the milk; cook for 5 minutes until thick and fold in the prepared filling, salt and pepper.
Stir for 3 minutes, spread the mixture in a shallow dish and refrigerate for 120 minutes until firm.
Shape 16 croquettes; coat with the remaining 20 g flour, the beaten eggs and the breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil to 175 °C and fry in batches for 4 to 6 minutes, until golden and 74 °C at the center; drain.
tips: Keep the uncooked breaded croquettes refrigerated until frying so the coating holds together.

title: Tuna and pepper croquettes
description: Fine-crusted croquettes with a creamy tuna and pepper filling.
steps: Drain the tuna and roasted pepper, chop the pepper and flake the fish without mashing it into a paste.
Chop the onion and soften it in the butter for 5 minutes; add 80 g of flour and stir for 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in the milk; cook for 5 minutes until thick and fold in the prepared filling, salt and pepper.
Stir for 3 minutes, spread the mixture in a shallow dish and refrigerate for 120 minutes until firm.
Shape 16 croquettes; coat with the remaining 20 g flour, the beaten eggs and the breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil to 175 °C and fry in batches for 4 to 6 minutes, until golden and 74 °C at the center; drain.
