tips: Keep the uncooked breaded croquettes refrigerated until frying so the coating holds together.

title: Potato, corn and chive patties
description: Savory pan-browned patties with tender centers, portioned for sharing.
steps: Mash the already cooked potato, drain the corn and wash and chop the chives; combine in a bowl.
Finely chop the onion and crush the garlic; beat the eggs in a separate bowl.
Mix the prepared base with onion, garlic, eggs, flour, oregano and salt; let stand for 10 minutes.
Divide into 12 portions and flatten to 1 cm thick; heat half the oil in a wide skillet.
Cook half the patties for 4 to 5 minutes per side over medium heat, until the centers reach 74 °C.
Repeat with the remaining patties and oil; drain on a rack and serve three per person.
tips: If the mixture seems wet, check that the vegetables are well drained before adding more flour.

title: Carrot and cheese patties
description: Savory pan-browned patties with tender centers, portioned for sharing.
steps: Finely grate the carrot, squeeze in a clean cloth to remove excess water and mix with the cheese.
Finely chop the onion and crush the garlic; beat the eggs in a separate bowl.
Mix the prepared base with onion, garlic, eggs, flour, oregano and salt; let stand for 10 minutes.
Divide into 12 portions and flatten to 1 cm thick; heat half the oil in a wide skillet.
Cook half the patties for 4 to 5 minutes per side over medium heat, until the centers reach 74 °C.
Repeat with the remaining patties and oil; drain on a rack and serve three per person.
tips: If the mixture seems wet, check that the vegetables are well drained before adding more flour.

title: Chickpea and sweet pepper patties
description: Savory pan-browned patties with tender centers, portioned for sharing.
steps: Mash the cooked chickpeas without completely pureeing them; wash, trim and finely dice the sweet pepper.
Finely chop the onion and crush the garlic; beat the eggs in a separate bowl.
Mix the prepared base with onion, garlic, eggs, flour, oregano and salt; let stand for 10 minutes.
Divide into 12 portions and flatten to 1 cm thick; heat half the oil in a wide skillet.
Cook half the patties for 4 to 5 minutes per side over medium heat, until the centers reach 74 °C.
Repeat with the remaining patties and oil; drain on a rack and serve three per person.
tips: If the mixture seems wet, check that the vegetables are well drained before adding more flour.

title: Zucchini and oat patties
description: Savory pan-browned patties with tender centers, portioned for sharing.
steps: Grate the zucchini and squeeze it thoroughly in a clean cloth; mix the drained pulp with the oats.
Finely chop the onion and crush the garlic; beat the eggs in a separate bowl.
Mix the prepared base with onion, garlic, eggs, flour, oregano and salt; let stand for 10 minutes.
Divide into 12 portions and flatten to 1 cm thick; heat half the oil in a wide skillet.
Cook half the patties for 4 to 5 minutes per side over medium heat, until the centers reach 74 °C.
Repeat with the remaining patties and oil; drain on a rack and serve three per person.
tips: If the mixture seems wet, check that the vegetables are well drained before adding more flour.

title: Sweet potato and black bean patties
description: Savory pan-browned patties with tender centers, portioned for sharing.
steps: Mash the already cooked sweet potato with the well-drained beans; leave some beans whole for texture.
Finely chop the onion and crush the garlic; beat the eggs in a separate bowl.
Mix the prepared base with onion, garlic, eggs, flour, oregano and salt; let stand for 10 minutes.
Divide into 12 portions and flatten to 1 cm thick; heat half the oil in a wide skillet.
Cook half the patties for 4 to 5 minutes per side over medium heat, until the centers reach 74 °C.
Repeat with the remaining patties and oil; drain on a rack and serve three per person.
tips: If the mixture seems wet, check that the vegetables are well drained before adding more flour.

title: Cassava crispbread with crab and lime
description: Crisp cassava flatbread topped with cooked crab, yogurt and fresh cilantro.
steps: Divide the crispbread into 12 pieces and toast at 160 °C for 5 minutes to restore its crispness.
Check the cooked crabmeat for any remaining shell fragments and keep it refrigerated.
Wash the cilantro and finely chop its leaves along with the red onion.
Gently combine the crab, yogurt, onion, cilantro, lime juice and salt, leaving some crab pieces intact.
Spoon the mixture onto the crispbread immediately before serving; refrigerate any remaining filling.
tips: Use commercially cooked, pasteurized crabmeat; this preparation does not cook raw crab.

title: Cuban bread toasts with ground beef
description: Crisp bread slices topped with ground beef and olives.
steps: Cut the bread into 12 slices and toast at 190 °C for 8 minutes, until the edges are crisp.
Chop the onion, garlic and olives; sauté the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the beef, cumin and salt and cook for 8 minutes, breaking up clumps with a spoon.
Add the tomato and olives and simmer for 10 minutes, until thickened and the beef reaches 71 °C.
Spoon the hot beef mixture onto the toast and serve immediately to keep the bread crisp.
tips: The sauce should be thick; if watery, reduce it for a few minutes before topping the bread.

title: Cassava crispbread with eggplant and garlic tomato
description: A roasted eggplant and fresh tomato topping served on cassava crispbread.
steps: Halve the eggplant, score the flesh and brush it with two tablespoons of oil.
Roast at 200 °C for 35 minutes with the garlic wrapped in foil; check that the flesh is tender.
Scoop out the flesh and mash with the roasted garlic, lime juice, oregano, salt and remaining oil.
Wash the tomato, remove some of the seeds and dice finely; fold into the eggplant mixture.
Divide the crispbread into 12 pieces and add the topping immediately before serving.
tips: If preparing the topping ahead, refrigerate it and assemble the crispbread just before serving.

title: Sardine and roasted pepper toasts
description: Crisp bread with canned sardines, roasted pepper and onion.
steps: Cut the bread into 12 slices and lightly brush them with the oil.
Toast the bread at 190 °C for 8 minutes, until the edges become golden.
Drain and inspect the sardines, remove any visible bones you prefer not to serve and cut into pieces.
Chop the pepper, onion and parsley and gently mix with the sardines and lime juice without crushing the fish.
Divide the topping among the toasts and serve immediately while the bread is still crisp.
tips: The sardines already contribute salt; taste the topping before deciding whether it needs more.

title: Cucumber canapes with tuna and yogurt
description: Thick cucumber rounds topped with a chilled tuna and celery mixture.
steps: Wash the cucumber thoroughly and cut into 12 thick rounds of similar size.
Pat the surfaces of the cucumber rounds dry with kitchen paper so the topping does not slide.
Wash and finely chop the celery and parsley; drain the tuna well and flake it with a fork.
Mix the tuna, yogurt, celery, parsley, lime juice and salt and keep chilled until assembly.
Place a portion of filling on each cucumber round and serve the freshly assembled canapes.
tips: Refrigerate the cucumber and filling separately to preserve their texture.

title: Eggs stuffed with avocado and chives
description: Hard-boiled egg halves filled with yolk, avocado and lime.
steps: Cover the eggs with the water, bring to a gentle boil and cook for 11 minutes, until whites and yolks are firm.
Cool the eggs under cold running water, peel and cut them in half lengthwise.
Remove the yolks and mash them with the avocado, lime juice and salt until smooth.
Wash and chop the chives and stir most into the filling; divide the mixture among the 12 halves.
Sprinkle with the paprika and remaining chives and refrigerate for 15 minutes before serving.
tips: Lime juice helps preserve the avocado color, but the filling must still be kept refrigerated.

title: Ham rolls with cheese and carrot
description: Cooked ham slices filled with cream cheese, carrot and sweet pepper.

ingredients.name: sliced cooked ham
ingredients.note: Eight slices of ready-to-eat ham, refrigerated.

steps: Wash, peel and finely grate the carrot; wash the pepper, remove seeds and dice finely.
Wash and chop the parsley; beat the cold cream cheese with the lime juice until spreadable.
Mix the cheese, carrot, pepper and parsley, distributing the vegetables evenly through the filling.
Lay out the eight ham slices, divide the filling among them and roll firmly without squeezing it out.
Refrigerate for 20 minutes, cut each roll in half and serve the 16 bites cold.
tips: Use fully cooked ham and keep the rolls refrigerated until serving.

title: White cheese, tomato and guava skewers
description: White cheese and guava paste bites paired with fresh tomato.
steps: Wash the cherry tomatoes under running water, remove the stems and dry them carefully.
Cut the white cheese into 16 cubes of similar size to divide it evenly.
Cut the guava paste into 16 small cubes and prepare 16 clean skewers for assembly.
Thread a tomato, a cheese cube and a guava cube onto each skewer, keeping the base stable.
Mix the oil and oregano, lightly brush the cheese and serve; keep the skewers chilled until then.
tips: The guava paste should be firm and sliceable, not a runny jam.

title: Chicken, corn and celery mini sandwiches
description: Small bread rolls with a chilled cooked chicken and vegetable filling.
steps: Finely shred the already cooked chicken and keep it cold while preparing the remaining ingredients.
Wash and finely dice the celery; drain the corn so it does not make the filling watery.
Mix the mayonnaise with the lime juice and pepper; fold in the chicken, corn and celery until evenly combined.
Split the eight rolls without completely separating the halves and divide the filling among them.
Serve the mini sandwiches immediately or cover and refrigerate until ready to bring them to the table.
tips: Measure the chicken after cooking and chilling; this recipe does not include cooking raw chicken.

title: Pumpkin cream and seed toasts
description: Toasted bread spread with garlicky pumpkin and crisp seeds.
steps: Cut the bread into 12 slices and toast at 190 °C for 8 minutes, until crisp.
Toast the seeds in a dry skillet for 3 minutes, stirring, and transfer them to a plate.
Chop the garlic and cook it gently in the oil for 1 minute, without letting it burn.
Add the pumpkin puree, salt and paprika; heat for 5 minutes, stirring, until it reaches 74 °C.
Spread the hot pumpkin cream over the toast, scatter the seeds over it and serve immediately.
tips: A thick puree keeps the toast crisp for longer than a watery cream.

title: Red bean and cheese hand pies
description: Baked hand pies with a savory red bean and cheese filling.

ingredients.name: wheat empanada dough discs
ingredients.note: 14 cm discs, about 400 g total; thawed in the refrigerator.

steps: Mash some of the cooked beans, combine with the crumbled cheese and keep chilled.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes; add the tomato, oregano and salt.
Add the prepared filling and cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until no loose liquid remains.
Transfer the filling to a shallow dish and refrigerate for 30 minutes; heat the oven to 190 °C.
Divide the filling among the 12 discs, fold and seal the edges with a fork; brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until golden and the filling reaches 74 °C; rest for 5 minutes before serving.
tips: The filling should be cold before sealing the dough so the edges close securely.

title: Mushroom and onion hand pies
description: Baked hand pies with a savory mushroom and onion filling.

ingredients.name: wheat empanada dough discs
ingredients.note: 14 cm discs, about 400 g total; thawed in the refrigerator.

steps: Wipe the mushrooms clean and cut into small dice; do not leave them soaking.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes; add the tomato, oregano and salt.
Add the prepared filling and cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until no loose liquid remains.
Transfer the filling to a shallow dish and refrigerate for 30 minutes; heat the oven to 190 °C.
Divide the filling among the 12 discs, fold and seal the edges with a fork; brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until golden and the filling reaches 74 °C; rest for 5 minutes before serving.
tips: The filling should be cold before sealing the dough so the edges close securely.

title: Turkey and pumpkin hand pies
description: Baked hand pies with a savory turkey and pumpkin filling.

ingredients.name: wheat empanada dough discs
ingredients.note: 14 cm discs, about 400 g total; thawed in the refrigerator.

steps: Shred the already cooked turkey and dice the roasted pumpkin finely; keep chilled.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes; add the tomato, oregano and salt.
Add the prepared filling and cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until no loose liquid remains.
Transfer the filling to a shallow dish and refrigerate for 30 minutes; heat the oven to 190 °C.
Divide the filling among the 12 discs, fold and seal the edges with a fork; brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until golden and the filling reaches 74 °C; rest for 5 minutes before serving.
tips: The filling should be cold before sealing the dough so the edges close securely.

title: Crab and corn hand pies
description: Baked hand pies with a savory crab and corn filling.

ingredients.name: wheat empanada dough discs
ingredients.note: 14 cm discs, about 400 g total; thawed in the refrigerator.

steps: Check the cooked crab for shell fragments; drain the corn thoroughly and keep both refrigerated.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes; add the tomato, oregano and salt.
Add the prepared filling and cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until no loose liquid remains.
Transfer the filling to a shallow dish and refrigerate for 30 minutes; heat the oven to 190 °C.
Divide the filling among the 12 discs, fold and seal the edges with a fork; brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until golden and the filling reaches 74 °C; rest for 5 minutes before serving.
tips: The filling should be cold before sealing the dough so the edges close securely.

title: Plantain and black bean hand pies
description: Baked hand pies with a savory plantain and black bean filling.

ingredients.name: wheat empanada dough discs
ingredients.note: 14 cm discs, about 400 g total; thawed in the refrigerator.

steps: Mash the already cooked plantain with some of the beans; fold in the rest whole for texture.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes; add the tomato, oregano and salt.
Add the prepared filling and cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until no loose liquid remains.
Transfer the filling to a shallow dish and refrigerate for 30 minutes; heat the oven to 190 °C.
Divide the filling among the 12 discs, fold and seal the edges with a fork; brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until golden and the filling reaches 74 °C; rest for 5 minutes before serving.
tips: The filling should be cold before sealing the dough so the edges close securely.

title: Mini spinach and pepper quiches
description: Small savory spinach and pepper tarts to share freshly baked.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C; cut 12 pastry discs and line 12 muffin cavities of 120 ml each.
Prick the bases with a fork and bake empty for 8 minutes; gently press down any bubbles with a spoon.
Chop the well-drained spinach and pepper; sauté with the oil and chopped garlic for 5 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the milk, cheese, salt and pepper; divide the sautéed filling among the pastry cases.
Pour in the egg mixture without filling each cavity more than three quarters full and bake for 20 to 25 minutes.
Check that the centers are set and reach 74 °C; wait for 5 minutes before unmolding.
tips: Drain cooked vegetables thoroughly so the pastry bases do not become soggy.

title: Mini sweet potato and cheese quiches
description: Small savory sweet potato and cheese tarts to share freshly baked.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C; cut 12 pastry discs and line 12 muffin cavities of 120 ml each.
Prick the bases with a fork and bake empty for 8 minutes; gently press down any bubbles with a spoon.
Cut the already cooked sweet potato into 1 cm dice and sauté with the oil and garlic for 4 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the milk, cheese, salt and pepper; divide the sautéed filling among the pastry cases.
Pour in the egg mixture without filling each cavity more than three quarters full and bake for 20 to 25 minutes.
Check that the centers are set and reach 74 °C; wait for 5 minutes before unmolding.
tips: Drain cooked vegetables thoroughly so the pastry bases do not become soggy.

title: Mini shrimp and leek quiches
description: Small savory shrimp and leek tarts to share freshly baked.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C; cut 12 pastry discs and line 12 muffin cavities of 120 ml each.
Prick the bases with a fork and bake empty for 8 minutes; gently press down any bubbles with a spoon.
Wash and chop the leek; sauté with the oil and garlic for 5 minutes, add chopped shrimp and cook for 3 minutes until opaque.
Beat the eggs with the milk, cheese, salt and pepper; divide the sautéed filling among the pastry cases.
Pour in the egg mixture without filling each cavity more than three quarters full and bake for 20 to 25 minutes.
Check that the centers are set and reach 74 °C; wait for 5 minutes before unmolding.
tips: Drain cooked vegetables thoroughly so the pastry bases do not become soggy.

title: Mini corn and chive quiches
description: Small savory corn and chive tarts to share freshly baked.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C; cut 12 pastry discs and line 12 muffin cavities of 120 ml each.
Prick the bases with a fork and bake empty for 8 minutes; gently press down any bubbles with a spoon.
Drain the corn, wash and chop the chives; sauté both with the oil and garlic for 3 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the milk, cheese, salt and pepper; divide the sautéed filling among the pastry cases.
Pour in the egg mixture without filling each cavity more than three quarters full and bake for 20 to 25 minutes.
Check that the centers are set and reach 74 °C; wait for 5 minutes before unmolding.
tips: Drain cooked vegetables thoroughly so the pastry bases do not become soggy.

title: Mini ham and pumpkin quiches
description: Small savory ham and pumpkin tarts to share freshly baked.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C; cut 12 pastry discs and line 12 muffin cavities of 120 ml each.
Prick the bases with a fork and bake empty for 8 minutes; gently press down any bubbles with a spoon.
Dice the cooked ham and roasted pumpkin finely; sauté with the oil and garlic for 4 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the milk, cheese, salt and pepper; divide the sautéed filling among the pastry cases.
Pour in the egg mixture without filling each cavity more than three quarters full and bake for 20 to 25 minutes.
Check that the centers are set and reach 74 °C; wait for 5 minutes before unmolding.
tips: Drain cooked vegetables thoroughly so the pastry bases do not become soggy.

title: Eggplant rolls stuffed with ground beef
description: Roasted eggplant slices wrapped around a thick ground beef filling.
steps: Cut the eggplants into 12 long slices, brush with two tablespoons of oil and roast for 15 minutes at 210 °C.
Chop the onion and garlic and sauté in the remaining oil for 5 minutes; add the beef, cumin and salt.
Cook the beef for 8 minutes, breaking up clumps; add half the tomatoes and chopped olives and cook for 8 more minutes.
Check that the beef reaches 71 °C; divide among the eggplant slices and roll with the seams underneath.
Spread the remaining tomatoes in a baking dish, add the rolls and bake at 190 °C for 15 minutes, until the centers reach 74 °C.
tips: The slices should be flexible before rolling; thicker areas may need additional roasting.

title: Mini peppers stuffed with tuna and potato
description: Baked sweet mini peppers with a soft potato, tuna and parsley filling.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C; wash and halve the peppers and remove the seeds.
Mash the already cooked potato, drain the tuna and wash and finely chop the parsley.
Mix the potato, tuna, parsley, lime juice, salt and half the cheese into an even filling.
Brush the peppers with the oil, divide the filling among them and top with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 25 minutes, until the peppers are tender and the centers reach 74 °C; serve four halves per person.
tips: Use small sweet peppers rather than hot chilies to keep the flavor mild.

title: Tomatoes stuffed with chickpeas and hard-boiled egg
description: Fresh tomatoes filled with chickpeas, hard-boiled egg and lime dressing.
steps: Wash the tomatoes, cut off their tops and scoop out some flesh without breaking the walls.
Chop and drain the scooped flesh; reserve 100 g for the filling and save the rest for another dish. Meanwhile, place the tomatoes upside down.
Chop the washed cucumber, parsley and hard-boiled eggs; lightly mash half the chickpeas.
Combine all the chickpeas with the egg, cucumber, parsley, drained tomato flesh, oil, lime juice and salt.
Fill the tomatoes, replace their tops and refrigerate for 20 minutes before serving.
tips: The eggs should be fully hard-boiled and cold before adding them.

title: Zucchini boats with sofrito chicken
description: Baked zucchini filled with shredded chicken, sofrito and cheese.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C; halve the zucchini lengthwise and scoop out some flesh, leaving sturdy edges.
Chop the scooped flesh, onion and garlic; sauté in the oil for 6 minutes until excess water evaporates.
Add the tomatoes, oregano and salt and cook for 5 minutes; fold in the already cooked chicken.
Divide the filling among the eight zucchini boats, add the cheese and arrange in a baking dish.
Bake for 30 minutes, until the zucchini is tender and the filling reaches 74 °C.
tips: Weigh the chicken after cooking; refrigerate the filling if preparing it ahead.

title: Mushrooms stuffed with black beans and corn
description: Large mushrooms baked with black beans, corn and sweet pepper.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C; clean the mushrooms and remove the stems without breaking the caps.
Chop the stems, pepper and garlic; sauté with one tablespoon of oil for 6 minutes.
Mash half the beans and combine with the remaining beans, corn, sautéed vegetables, cumin and salt.
Brush the mushroom caps with the remaining oil and fill them with small mounds of the mixture.
Bake for 20 minutes, until the mushrooms are tender and the filling reaches 74 °C; serve three per person.
tips: Choose mushrooms with wide caps so the filling stays securely in place.

title: Plantain cups with shredded beef
description: Baked green plantain cups filled with prepared Cuban-style shredded beef.

ingredients.name: cooked refrigerated Cuban-style shredded beef
ingredients.note: A finished dish, without excess liquid sauce.

steps: Cut the peeled plantain into chunks and boil in the water for 20 to 25 minutes, until tender.
Drain and mash while hot with the salt and two tablespoons of oil; do not add water to the dough.
Grease 12 muffin cavities with the remaining oil and line them with mashed plantain, building up the sides.
Bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes; add the shredded beef and bake for 12 more minutes until the filling reaches 74 °C.
Wait for 5 minutes before unmolding, finish with washed chopped cilantro and serve the cups hot.
tips: Use fully prepared shredded beef; check its ingredients and allergens if it comes from another recipe.
allergens: Sulfites if the shredded beef contains wine

title: Baked corn and cheese fritters
description: Baked corn, cheese and chive bites with soft centers.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C and grease 12 muffin cavities with the oil.
Drain the corn and blend half with the milk and eggs; keep the remaining corn whole.
Mix the flour, baking powder and salt; add the liquid mixture and stir until no dry flour remains.
Fold in the cheese, whole corn and washed chopped chives; divide the batter among the cavities.
Bake for 22 to 27 minutes, until golden and the centers reach 74 °C; wait for 5 minutes before unmolding.
tips: These are baked fritters made with thick batter; fill each cavity only three quarters full.

title: Rice balls with tuna and parsley
description: Cooked rice and tuna balls with a crisp oven-baked coating.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C and line a tray with baking paper; keep the rice cold until needed.
Drain the tuna and chop the washed parsley; combine with the rice, cheese, salt, one egg and 40 g breadcrumbs.
Press the mixture into 16 small balls and place them on a clean plate.
Beat the remaining egg and coat the balls in it and the remaining 80 g breadcrumbs; brush with the oil.
Bake for 25 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden and the centers reach 74 °C.
tips: The rice must have been promptly refrigerated after cooking; do not use rice left at room temperature for hours.

title: Fish strips with a cassava crispbread crust
description: White fish strips coated with crushed cassava crispbread and baked.
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C and line a tray with baking paper; inspect the fish and remove any bones.
Pat the fish dry and cut into 2 cm thick strips; season with the salt, garlic powder and paprika.
Crush the crispbread into small crumbs; place the flour, beaten eggs and crumbs in three separate dishes.
Coat each strip in flour, egg and crispbread crumbs; arrange without crowding and brush with the oil.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, turning once, until the fish is opaque and at least 63 °C; serve with lime wedges.
tips: Uniform thickness helps all the strips cook without drying out the smallest ones.

title: Mojo chicken and pineapple skewers
description: Chicken, pineapple and pepper bites marinated with sour orange and cooked on a griddle.
steps: Cut the chicken into 2 cm cubes without washing it; use a separate board to cut similar-sized pineapple and pepper pieces.
Mix the sour orange juice, crushed garlic, oil, oregano and salt; marinate the covered chicken in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Alternate chicken, pineapple and pepper on 12 metal skewers; discard the marinade that touched raw chicken.
Heat a griddle over medium heat and cook the skewers for 12 to 16 minutes, turning several times.
Check for 74 °C in the thickest chicken pieces and serve three skewers per person on a clean platter.
tips: If the outside browns before reaching the required temperature, lower the heat and continue cooking.

title: Sour orange and semolina sponge cake
description: Fine-textured cake with semolina, yogurt, and citrus aroma.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line the base and sides of a round pan 20 cm in diameter and 6 cm deep with baking parchment.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt, along with the semolina. Break up lumps with a whisk before adding the wet ingredients.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar for 2 minutes. Add the oil, yogurt, orange juice, and zest and mix until no separate streaks remain.
Fold in the dry ingredients with a spatula just until the flour is moistened. Make sure the semolina is evenly distributed. Pour into the pan and smooth gently.
Bake for 40 to 48 minutes, until the center is firm, springs back when touched, and a skewer comes out without raw batter.
Rest in the pan for 10 minutes; unmold onto a rack and cool for 40 minutes before cutting into 10 servings.
tips: Use fine semolina so the crumb does not feel gritty.

title: Soursop and coconut cake
description: Moist cake made with seedless soursop pulp and shredded coconut.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line the base and sides of a round pan 22 cm in diameter and 6 cm deep with baking parchment.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt. Break up lumps with a whisk before adding the wet ingredients.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar for 2 minutes. Add the oil, soursop, coconut milk, and vanilla and mix until no separate streaks remain.
Fold in the dry ingredients with a spatula just until the flour is moistened. Fold in the shredded coconut gently. Pour into the pan and smooth gently.
Bake for 45 to 55 minutes, until the center is firm, springs back when touched, and a skewer comes out without raw batter.
Rest in the pan for 10 minutes; unmold onto a rack and cool for 40 minutes before cutting into 10 servings.
tips: Check the pulp carefully and remove every seed before blending it.

title: Banana and cocoa cake
description: Dark, tender cake with ripe bananas and unsweetened cocoa.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line the base and sides of a round pan 22 cm in diameter and 6 cm deep with baking parchment.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt, along with cocoa and cinnamon. Break up lumps with a whisk before adding the wet ingredients.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar for 2 minutes. Add the oil, mashed banana and milk and mix until no separate streaks remain.
Fold in the dry ingredients with a spatula just until the flour is moistened. Stop stirring as soon as the flour disappears. Pour into the pan and smooth gently.
Bake for 45 to 55 minutes, until the center is firm, springs back when touched, and a skewer comes out without raw batter.
Rest in the pan for 10 minutes; unmold onto a rack and cool for 40 minutes before cutting into 10 servings.
tips: The banana should be very ripe and free of hard chunks so it blends into the crumb.

title: Pumpkin and pumpkin seed cake
description: Cooked-pumpkin cake with pumpkin seeds and a gently spiced crumb.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line the base and sides of a round pan 22 cm in diameter and 6 cm deep with baking parchment.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt, along with cinnamon and ginger. Break up lumps with a whisk before adding the wet ingredients.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar for 2 minutes. Add the oil, pumpkin puree and milk and mix until no separate streaks remain.
Fold in the dry ingredients with a spatula just until the flour is moistened. Add the pumpkin seeds and distribute them throughout the batter. Pour into the pan and smooth gently.
Bake for 45 to 55 minutes, until the center is firm, springs back when touched, and a skewer comes out without raw batter.
Rest in the pan for 10 minutes; unmold onto a rack and cool for 40 minutes before cutting into 10 servings.
tips: If the puree is watery, drain it before weighing the listed amount.

title: Passion fruit oil sponge cake
description: Light sponge cake with passion fruit juice and a soft oil-based crumb.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line the base and sides of a round pan 22 cm in diameter and 6 cm deep with baking parchment.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt. Break up lumps with a whisk before adding the wet ingredients.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar for 2 minutes. Add the oil, passion fruit juice, water, and lime zest and mix until no separate streaks remain.
Fold in the dry ingredients with a spatula just until the flour is moistened. Avoid overmixing to preserve the air in the eggs. Pour into the pan and smooth gently.
Bake for 38 to 45 minutes, until the center is firm, springs back when touched, and a skewer comes out without raw batter.
Rest in the pan for 10 minutes; unmold onto a rack and cool for 40 minutes before cutting into 10 servings.
tips: Use unsweetened seedless juice; dilute a concentrate according to its label.

title: Papaya and ginger cake
description: Ripe-papaya cake with fresh ginger and small pieces of fruit.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line the base and sides of a round pan 22 cm in diameter and 6 cm deep with baking parchment.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt. Break up lumps with a whisk before adding the wet ingredients.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar for 2 minutes. Add the oil, half the papaya pureed, yogurt, ginger, and zest and mix until no separate streaks remain.
Fold in the dry ingredients with a spatula just until the flour is moistened. Cut the remaining papaya into 1 cm cubes and fold it in last. Pour into the pan and smooth gently.
Bake for 45 to 55 minutes, until the center is firm, springs back when touched, and a skewer comes out without raw batter.
Rest in the pan for 10 minutes; unmold onto a rack and cool for 40 minutes before cutting into 10 servings.
tips: Choose ripe but firm papaya so the cubes hold their shape in the oven.

title: Whole-wheat honey and walnut cake
description: Cake made with mixed flours, honey, and walnuts, designed for slicing.
steps: Heat the oven to 170 °C. Line the base and sides of a round pan 22 cm in diameter and 6 cm deep with baking parchment.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt, along with the whole-wheat flour. Break up lumps with a whisk before adding the wet ingredients.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar for 2 minutes. Add the oil, honey, yogurt, and vanilla and mix until no separate streaks remain.
Fold in the dry ingredients with a spatula just until the flour is moistened. Fold in the chopped walnuts without overmixing. Pour into the pan and smooth gently.
Bake for 45 to 55 minutes, until the center is firm, springs back when touched, and a skewer comes out without raw batter.
Rest in the pan for 10 minutes; unmold onto a rack and cool for 40 minutes before cutting into 10 servings.
tips: Cover loosely with foil if the honey browns the surface before the center is baked.

title: Tamarind and molasses cake
description: Dark cake with seedless tamarind pulp, molasses, and spices.
steps: Heat the oven to 170 °C. Line the base and sides of a round pan 22 cm in diameter and 6 cm deep with baking parchment.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt, along with cinnamon and cloves. Break up lumps with a whisk before adding the wet ingredients.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar for 2 minutes. Add the oil, tamarind pulp, molasses, and milk and mix until no separate streaks remain.
Fold in the dry ingredients with a spatula just until the flour is moistened. Scrape the bottom of the bowl to incorporate the molasses fully. Pour into the pan and smooth gently.
Bake for 45 to 55 minutes, until the center is firm, springs back when touched, and a skewer comes out without raw batter.
Rest in the pan for 10 minutes; unmold onto a rack and cool for 40 minutes before cutting into 10 servings.
tips: Use strained pulp with a puree-like consistency; avoid undiluted thick concentrate.

title: Apple and oat cake
description: Fresh apple cake with oats and cinnamon, with a tender rustic crumb.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line the base and sides of a round pan 22 cm in diameter and 6 cm deep with baking parchment.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt, along with oats and cinnamon. Break up lumps with a whisk before adding the wet ingredients.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar for 2 minutes. Add the oil, yogurt and lime juice and mix until no separate streaks remain.
Fold in the dry ingredients with a spatula just until the flour is moistened. Cut the apple into 1 cm cubes and fold into the batter. Pour into the pan and smooth gently.
Bake for 45 to 55 minutes, until the center is firm, springs back when touched, and a skewer comes out without raw batter.
Rest in the pan for 10 minutes; unmold onto a rack and cool for 40 minutes before cutting into 10 servings.
tips: Dice the apple finely so it cooks at the same rate as the crumb.

title: Anise and lime sponge cake
description: Aromatic sponge cake with ground anise and lime zest.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line the base and sides of a round pan 22 cm in diameter and 6 cm deep with baking parchment.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt, along with cornstarch and anise. Break up lumps with a whisk before adding the wet ingredients.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar for 2 minutes. Add the oil, milk and lime zest and mix until no separate streaks remain.
Fold in the dry ingredients with a spatula just until the flour is moistened. Scrape the bottom with the spatula to check for pockets of dry flour. Pour into the pan and smooth gently.
Bake for 35 to 43 minutes, until the center is firm, springs back when touched, and a skewer comes out without raw batter.
Rest in the pan for 10 minutes; unmold onto a rack and cool for 40 minutes before cutting into 10 servings.
tips: Grate only the colored part of the lime peel to avoid bitter white pith.

title: Cooked cassava and lime cookies
description: Soft cookies with cooked cassava mash, butter, and lime zest.
steps: Line 2 trays measuring 30 × 40 cm with baking parchment. Use softened, unmelted butter and a room-temperature egg.
Beat butter and sugar for 2 minutes. Add the egg, cassava mash and lime zest and mix until incorporated.
Mix flour, baking powder, and salt. Add to the creamed mixture and stir just until a dough forms. The dough should be manageable and free of tough cassava fibers.
Cover the dough and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 175 °C. Divide into 24 equal portions, roll into balls, and flatten to 8 mm thick. Leave 4 cm between them on the trays.
Bake one tray at a time for 15 to 18 minutes, until the edges are set and the base is lightly golden; the center finishes setting as it cools.
Leave the cookies on the tray for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 20 minutes. Store only when completely cool.
tips: The cassava must be fully cooked, drained, and free of its central fiber; do not use raw cassava.

title: Coconut and white chocolate cookies
description: Crisp-edged cookies with shredded coconut and white chocolate chunks.
steps: Line 2 trays measuring 30 × 40 cm with baking parchment. Use softened, unmelted butter and a room-temperature egg.
Beat butter and sugar for 2 minutes. Add the egg and vanilla and mix until incorporated.
Mix flour, baking powder, and salt. Add to the creamed mixture and stir just until a dough forms. Fold in the coconut and white chocolate with a spatula.
Cover the dough and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 175 °C. Divide into 24 equal portions, roll into balls, and flatten to 8 mm thick. Leave 4 cm between them on the trays.
Bake one tray at a time for 12 to 16 minutes, until the edges are set and the base is lightly golden; the center finishes setting as it cools.
Leave the cookies on the tray for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 20 minutes. Store only when completely cool.
tips: Chop the chocolate into small pieces so it spreads evenly without making the cookies hard to shape.

title: Whole-wheat banana and walnut cookies
description: Tender cookies with whole-wheat flour, banana, and walnuts.
steps: Line 2 trays measuring 30 × 40 cm with baking parchment. Use softened, unmelted butter and a room-temperature egg.
Beat butter and sugar for 2 minutes. Add the egg and mashed banana and mix until incorporated.
Mix flour, baking powder, and salt, along with whole-wheat flour and cinnamon. Add to the creamed mixture and stir just until a dough forms. Add the chopped walnuts and distribute them evenly.
Cover the dough and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 175 °C. Divide into 24 equal portions, roll into balls, and flatten to 8 mm thick. Leave 4 cm between them on the trays.
Bake one tray at a time for 14 to 18 minutes, until the edges are set and the base is lightly golden; the center finishes setting as it cools.
Leave the cookies on the tray for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 20 minutes. Store only when completely cool.
tips: These cookies stay tender; cool them completely before stacking.

title: Peanut cookies with guava centers
description: Ground-peanut cookies with a small guava paste center.
steps: Line 2 trays measuring 30 × 40 cm with baking parchment. Use softened, unmelted butter and a room-temperature egg.
Beat butter and sugar for 2 minutes. Add the egg and vanilla and mix until incorporated.
Mix flour, baking powder, and salt, along with the ground peanuts. Add to the creamed mixture and stir just until a dough forms. Reserve the guava paste for filling the cookies.

Cover the dough and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 175 °C. Shape 24 balls, flatten slightly, and make an indentation. Divide the diced guava among the centers; leave 4 cm between cookies.
Bake one tray at a time for 12 to 16 minutes, until the edges are set and the base is lightly golden; the center finishes setting as it cools.
Leave the cookies on the tray for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 20 minutes. Store only when completely cool.
tips: Make the indentation without piercing the base so the guava stays in the center.

title: Cream cheese and orange cookies
description: Soft aromatic cookies with cream cheese and orange zest.
steps: Line 2 trays measuring 30 × 40 cm with baking parchment. Use softened, unmelted butter and a room-temperature egg.
Beat butter and sugar for 2 minutes. Add the egg, cream cheese, orange zest, and juice and mix until incorporated.
Mix flour, baking powder, and salt. Add to the creamed mixture and stir just until a dough forms. Mix without overworking to preserve a tender texture.
Cover the dough and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 175 °C. Divide into 24 equal portions, roll into balls, and flatten to 8 mm thick. Leave 4 cm between them on the trays.
Bake one tray at a time for 14 to 18 minutes, until the edges are set and the base is lightly golden; the center finishes setting as it cools.
Leave the cookies on the tray for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 20 minutes. Store only when completely cool.
tips: The cream cheese should be softened so it does not leave lumps in the dough.

title: Cornmeal and anise cookies
description: Crisp cookies made with fine cornmeal, wheat flour, and anise.
steps: Line 2 trays measuring 30 × 40 cm with baking parchment. Use softened, unmelted butter and a room-temperature egg.
Beat butter and sugar for 2 minutes. Add the egg and milk and mix until incorporated.
Mix flour, baking powder, and salt, along with cornmeal and anise. Add to the creamed mixture and stir just until a dough forms. Make sure the cornmeal is distributed evenly.
Cover the dough and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 175 °C. Divide into 24 equal portions, roll into balls, and flatten to 8 mm thick. Leave 4 cm between them on the trays.
Bake one tray at a time for 14 to 17 minutes, until the edges are set and the base is lightly golden; the center finishes setting as it cools.
Leave the cookies on the tray for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 20 minutes. Store only when completely cool.
tips: Use finely ground cornmeal; coarse cornmeal changes the cookie texture.

title: Oat and dried papaya cookies
description: Oat cookies with diced dried papaya and vanilla aroma.
steps: Line 2 trays measuring 30 × 40 cm with baking parchment. Use softened, unmelted butter and a room-temperature egg.
Beat butter and sugar for 2 minutes. Add the egg and vanilla and mix until incorporated.
Mix flour, baking powder, and salt, along with the oats. Add to the creamed mixture and stir just until a dough forms. Add the dried papaya cut into small pieces.
Cover the dough and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 175 °C. Divide into 24 equal portions, roll into balls, and flatten to 8 mm thick. Leave 4 cm between them on the trays.
Bake one tray at a time for 13 to 17 minutes, until the edges are set and the base is lightly golden; the center finishes setting as it cools.
Leave the cookies on the tray for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 20 minutes. Store only when completely cool.
tips: If the papaya is heavily sugared, do not add extra sugar on top.

title: Cinnamon cookies filled with prune paste
description: Closed cinnamon cookies with a soft prune filling.
steps: Line 2 trays measuring 30 × 40 cm with baking parchment. Use softened, unmelted butter and a room-temperature egg.
Beat butter and sugar for 2 minutes. Add the egg and mix until incorporated.
Mix flour, baking powder, and salt, along with the cinnamon. Add to the creamed mixture and stir just until a dough forms. Separately blend the prunes with the hot water into a paste and let cool.

Cover the dough and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 175 °C. Divide the dough into 24 portions, flatten, and divide the prune paste among the centers. Close into low balls and leave 4 cm between them.
Bake one tray at a time for 15 to 19 minutes, until the edges are set and the base is lightly golden; the center finishes setting as it cools.
Leave the cookies on the tray for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 20 minutes. Store only when completely cool.
tips: The filling should be thick; cool it before sealing the dough around it.

title: Sesame and molasses cookies
description: Dark crisp cookies with sesame seeds and cane molasses.
steps: Line 2 trays measuring 30 × 40 cm with baking parchment. Use softened, unmelted butter and a room-temperature egg.
Beat butter and sugar for 2 minutes. Add the egg and molasses and mix until incorporated.
Mix flour, baking powder, and salt, along with the ginger. Add to the creamed mixture and stir just until a dough forms. Fold in the sesame, making sure it does not settle at the bottom.
Cover the dough and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 175 °C. Divide into 24 equal portions, roll into balls, and flatten to 8 mm thick. Leave 4 cm between them on the trays.
Bake one tray at a time for 12 to 16 minutes, until the edges are set and the base is lightly golden; the center finishes setting as it cools.
Leave the cookies on the tray for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 20 minutes. Store only when completely cool.
tips: Molasses darkens the dough; watch the browning underneath to avoid burning.

title: Cocoa cookies with coconut centers
description: Cocoa cookies filled with coconut bound with condensed milk.
steps: Line 2 trays measuring 30 × 40 cm with baking parchment. Use softened, unmelted butter and a room-temperature egg.
Beat butter and sugar for 2 minutes. Add the egg and milk and mix until incorporated.
Mix flour, baking powder, and salt, along with the cocoa. Add to the creamed mixture and stir just until a dough forms. Separately mix coconut and condensed milk to make the filling.

Cover the dough and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 175 °C. Divide the dough into 24 portions, flatten, and divide the coconut filling among the centers. Close and flatten gently; leave 4 cm between pieces.
Bake one tray at a time for 15 to 18 minutes, until the edges are set and the base is lightly golden; the center finishes setting as it cools.
Leave the cookies on the tray for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 20 minutes. Store only when completely cool.
tips: Seal the dough well around the coconut so it holds the filling during baking.

title: Savory cheese and cumin cookies
description: Savory snack cookies with grated cheese and cumin, with a crumbly texture.
steps: Line 2 trays measuring 30 × 40 cm with baking parchment. Use softened, unmelted butter and a room-temperature egg.
Beat butter and sugar for 2 minutes. Add the egg and milk and mix until incorporated.
Mix flour, baking powder, and salt, along with cumin and pepper. Add to the creamed mixture and stir just until a dough forms. Add the grated cheese and mix until distributed throughout the dough.
Cover the dough and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 175 °C. Divide into 24 equal portions, roll into balls, and flatten to 8 mm thick. Leave 4 cm between them on the trays.
Bake one tray at a time for 15 to 19 minutes, until the edges are set and the base is lightly golden; the center finishes setting as it cools.
Leave the cookies on the tray for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 20 minutes. Store only when completely cool.
tips: The small amount of sugar balances the flavor; cheese provides the main savory note.

title: Almond and guava cookies
description: Ground-almond cookies with small pieces of guava paste.
steps: Line 2 trays measuring 30 × 40 cm with baking parchment. Use softened, unmelted butter and a room-temperature egg.
Beat butter and sugar for 2 minutes. Add the egg and lime zest and mix until incorporated.
Mix flour, baking powder, and salt, along with the ground almonds. Add to the creamed mixture and stir just until a dough forms. Distribute the guava cubes through the dough with a spatula.
Cover the dough and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 175 °C. Divide into 24 equal portions, roll into balls, and flatten to 8 mm thick. Leave 4 cm between them on the trays.
Bake one tray at a time for 14 to 18 minutes, until the edges are set and the base is lightly golden; the center finishes setting as it cools.
Leave the cookies on the tray for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 20 minutes. Store only when completely cool.
tips: Keep most of the guava inside the dough so it does not stick to the tray.

title: Pineapple and toasted coconut squares
description: Moist squares with drained pineapple and toasted coconut that hold their shape when cut.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line a square pan measuring 20 × 20 cm and 5 cm deep, leaving paper overhanging the sides. Melt the butter and let it cool slightly.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt, breaking up lumps before continuing.
Whisk eggs and sugar just to combine, without whipping. Add the cooled melted butter, pineapple and vanilla and stir evenly.
Fold in the dry mixture with a spatula and stop stirring when the flour disappears. Add the toasted coconut and distribute evenly. Spread into the corners of the pan.
Bake for 32 to 40 minutes, until the edges are set and the center shows no liquid batter when tested with a skewer.
Cool in the pan for 20 minutes; lift out with the paper and cool on a rack for 60 minutes. Cut into 16 squares once firm.
tips: Drain the pineapple with gentle pressure so excess juice does not prevent the squares from setting.

title: Peanut and chocolate bars
description: Peanut butter bars studded with dark chocolate chunks.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line a square pan measuring 20 × 20 cm and 5 cm deep, leaving paper overhanging the sides. Melt the butter and let it cool slightly.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt, breaking up lumps before continuing.
Whisk eggs and sugar just to combine, without whipping. Add the cooled melted butter, peanut butter, milk, and vanilla and stir evenly.
Fold in the dry mixture with a spatula and stop stirring when the flour disappears. Fold in the chopped chocolate, reserving a few chunks for the top. Spread into the corners of the pan.
Bake for 28 to 35 minutes, until the edges are set and the center shows no liquid batter when tested with a skewer.
Cool in the pan for 20 minutes; lift out with the paper and cool on a rack for 60 minutes. Cut into 16 squares once firm.
tips: Stir the peanut butter well so it has no separate oil layer.

title: Mamey and vanilla squares
description: Dense tender squares made with ripe mamey and vanilla.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line a square pan measuring 20 × 20 cm and 5 cm deep, leaving paper overhanging the sides. Melt the butter and let it cool slightly.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt, breaking up lumps before continuing.
Whisk eggs and sugar just to combine, without whipping. Add the cooled melted butter, pureed mamey, vanilla, and zest and stir evenly.
Fold in the dry mixture with a spatula and stop stirring when the flour disappears. Check that the mixture contains no hard pieces of fruit. Spread into the corners of the pan.
Bake for 32 to 40 minutes, until the edges are set and the center shows no liquid batter when tested with a skewer.
Cool in the pan for 20 minutes; lift out with the paper and cool on a rack for 60 minutes. Cut into 16 squares once firm.
tips: The mamey should be ripe and soft; firm flesh does not blend well into this dense batter.

title: Banana and oat bars
description: Tender bars made with banana, oats, and raisins.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line a square pan measuring 20 × 20 cm and 5 cm deep, leaving paper overhanging the sides. Melt the butter and let it cool slightly.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt, along with oats and cinnamon, breaking up lumps before continuing.
Whisk eggs and sugar just to combine, without whipping. Add the cooled melted butter and mashed banana and stir evenly.
Fold in the dry mixture with a spatula and stop stirring when the flour disappears. Add the raisins and distribute them throughout the batter. Spread into the corners of the pan.
Bake for 32 to 40 minutes, until the edges are set and the center shows no liquid batter when tested with a skewer.
Cool in the pan for 20 minutes; lift out with the paper and cool on a rack for 60 minutes. Cut into 16 squares once firm.
tips: Use fine oats so they hydrate during baking without leaving overly firm flakes.

title: Lime squares with cornmeal crust
description: Crumbly cornmeal and wheat crust topped with a creamy lime layer.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a pan measuring 20 × 20 cm and 5 cm deep with overhanging parchment for lifting out the squares.
Mix the crust flours with the crust sugar and salt. Rub in the cold diced butter with your fingers until moist crumbs form.
Press the crumbs into an even layer and bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until the edges begin to brown. Lower the oven to 160 °C.
Whisk the eggs with the filling sugar; add the filling flour, lime juice, and zest. Mix without incorporating too much foam.
Pour the filling over the hot crust and bake for 20 to 28 minutes, until the center barely jiggles and reaches at least 71 °C.
Cool slightly for 20 minutes and refrigerate for 120 minutes. Lift out with the paper and cut into 16 squares with a clean knife.
tips: Keep the squares refrigerated in a covered container; the filling contains eggs and moisture.

title: Coconut and dulce de leche bars
description: Coconut bars with dulce de leche swirls baked into the surface.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line a square pan measuring 20 × 20 cm and 5 cm deep, leaving paper overhanging the sides. Melt the butter and let it cool slightly.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt, breaking up lumps before continuing.
Whisk eggs and sugar just to combine, without whipping. Add the cooled melted butter, milk and vanilla and stir evenly.
Fold in the dry ingredients and coconut without overmixing. Spread into the pan, dot with teaspoons of dulce de leche, and drag a knife through to create swirls.
Bake for 30 to 38 minutes, until the edges are set and the center shows no liquid batter when tested with a skewer.
Cool in the pan for 20 minutes; lift out with the paper and cool on a rack for 60 minutes. Cut into 16 squares once firm.
tips: Use thick dulce de leche so the swirls stay visible rather than blending completely.

title: Coffee and walnut squares
description: Golden squares flavored with strong coffee and chopped walnuts.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line a square pan measuring 20 × 20 cm and 5 cm deep, leaving paper overhanging the sides. Melt the butter and let it cool slightly.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt, breaking up lumps before continuing.
Whisk eggs and sugar just to combine, without whipping. Add the cooled melted butter, coffee and vanilla and stir evenly.
Fold in the dry mixture with a spatula and stop stirring when the flour disappears. Fold in the walnuts with a spatula to distribute them evenly. Spread into the corners of the pan.
Bake for 28 to 35 minutes, until the edges are set and the center shows no liquid batter when tested with a skewer.
Cool in the pan for 20 minutes; lift out with the paper and cool on a rack for 60 minutes. Cut into 16 squares once firm.
tips: Let the coffee cool before adding it so it does not heat the eggs.

title: Pumpkin and cream cheese bars
description: Pumpkin bars with soft cream cheese swirls.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line a square pan measuring 20 × 20 cm and 5 cm deep, leaving paper overhanging the sides. Melt the butter and let it cool slightly.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt, along with the cinnamon, breaking up lumps before continuing.
Whisk eggs and sugar just to combine, without whipping. Add the cooled melted butter, pumpkin puree and vanilla and stir evenly.
Fold the dry ingredients into the batter and spread into the pan. Beat the cream cheese with its sugar, dot over the batter, and make shallow swirls with a knife.
Bake for 35 to 43 minutes, until the edges are set and the center shows no liquid batter when tested with a skewer.
Cool in the pan for 20 minutes; lift out with the paper and cool on a rack for 60 minutes. Cut into 16 squares once firm.
tips: Keep these bars refrigerated because of the cream cheese topping.

title: Guava and cocoa squares
description: Dense cocoa squares with soft pieces of guava paste.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line a square pan measuring 20 × 20 cm and 5 cm deep, leaving paper overhanging the sides. Melt the butter and let it cool slightly.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt, along with the cocoa, breaking up lumps before continuing.
Whisk eggs and sugar just to combine, without whipping. Add the cooled melted butter, milk and vanilla and stir evenly.
Fold in the dry mixture with a spatula and stop stirring when the flour disappears. Add the guava cubes and distribute them throughout the batter. Spread into the corners of the pan.
Bake for 27 to 34 minutes, until the edges are set and the center shows no liquid batter when tested with a skewer.
Cool in the pan for 20 minutes; lift out with the paper and cool on a rack for 60 minutes. Cut into 16 squares once firm.
tips: Test the center away from guava pieces to distinguish melted paste from raw batter.

title: Crunchy sesame and honey bars
description: Baked bars of sesame, oats, and peanuts bound together with honey.
steps: Heat the oven to 160 °C and line a pan measuring 20 × 20 cm and 5 cm deep with parchment, leaving overhang to lift the mixture out.
Toast the sesame in a dry skillet for 3 minutes, stirring. Combine in a bowl with oats, peanuts, cinnamon, and salt.
Heat honey, butter, and brown sugar in a saucepan until the butter melts. Simmer gently for 1 minute and remove from the heat.
Pour the syrup over the dry mixture and stir to coat every grain. Transfer to the pan and press firmly using another piece of parchment on top.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the edges are golden. Cool slightly for 10 minutes and score into 16 bars without separating them.
Cool for another 40 minutes and separate along the scored lines. Store in a dry sealed container once the mixture is completely firm.
tips: Compact the mixture firmly before baking to keep it from crumbling when cut.

title: Sweet potato and orange muffins
description: Tender muffins with sweet potato mash and orange juice.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Line a muffin pan with 12 cavities, each holding 120 ml, with paper liners. Prepare all ingredients before mixing.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt, along with the cinnamon. Break up lumps with a whisk to distribute the leavener evenly.
Whisk the eggs with the oil, sweet potato, juice, milk, and orange zest in another bowl until the mixture looks even.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and fold just until moistened. Check for pockets of dry flour at the bottom. Divide among the 12 liners, filling them no more than 3/4 full.
Bake for 24 to 30 minutes, until the domes are firm and a skewer inserted into the crumb comes out without raw batter.
Leave the muffins in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 25 minutes. Avoid storing them warm so the bases do not become damp.
tips: The mash should be smooth and cool so it blends without lumps.

title: Mamey and coconut muffins
description: Mamey-pulp muffins with fine shredded coconut and vanilla.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Line a muffin pan with 12 cavities, each holding 120 ml, with paper liners. Prepare all ingredients before mixing.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt. Break up lumps with a whisk to distribute the leavener evenly.
Whisk the eggs with the oil, mamey, coconut milk, and vanilla in another bowl until the mixture looks even.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and fold just until moistened. Fold in the shredded coconut gently at the end. Divide among the 12 liners, filling them no more than 3/4 full.
Bake for 24 to 30 minutes, until the domes are firm and a skewer inserted into the crumb comes out without raw batter.
Leave the muffins in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 25 minutes. Avoid storing them warm so the bases do not become damp.
tips: Weigh the mamey after removing skin and seed to preserve the formula’s moisture balance.

title: Banana and peanut muffins
description: Banana muffins with chopped roasted peanuts.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Line a muffin pan with 12 cavities, each holding 120 ml, with paper liners. Prepare all ingredients before mixing.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt. Break up lumps with a whisk to distribute the leavener evenly.
Whisk the eggs with the oil, banana, milk, and vanilla in another bowl until the mixture looks even.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and fold just until moistened. Fold in the chopped peanuts without beating the batter. Divide among the 12 liners, filling them no more than 3/4 full.
Bake for 22 to 28 minutes, until the domes are firm and a skewer inserted into the crumb comes out without raw batter.
Leave the muffins in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 25 minutes. Avoid storing them warm so the bases do not become damp.
tips: The peanuts should be cool before being added so they do not warm the batter.

title: Cocoa and beet muffins
description: Moist cocoa muffins made with cooked beet puree.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Line a muffin pan with 12 cavities, each holding 120 ml, with paper liners. Prepare all ingredients before mixing.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt, along with the cocoa. Break up lumps with a whisk to distribute the leavener evenly.
Whisk the eggs with the oil, beet puree, milk, and vanilla in another bowl until the mixture looks even.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and fold just until moistened. Scrape the sides to incorporate all the dark mixture. Divide among the 12 liners, filling them no more than 3/4 full.
Bake for 24 to 30 minutes, until the domes are firm and a skewer inserted into the crumb comes out without raw batter.
Leave the muffins in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 25 minutes. Avoid storing them warm so the bases do not become damp.
tips: Use cooked beets without vinegar or pickling liquid so the muffin flavor stays balanced.

title: Pineapple and yogurt muffins
description: Yogurt muffins with small well-drained pineapple pieces.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Line a muffin pan with 12 cavities, each holding 120 ml, with paper liners. Prepare all ingredients before mixing.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt. Break up lumps with a whisk to distribute the leavener evenly.
Whisk the eggs with the oil, yogurt and lime zest in another bowl until the mixture looks even.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and fold just until moistened. Fold in the drained pineapple just before dividing the batter. Divide among the 12 liners, filling them no more than 3/4 full.
Bake for 24 to 30 minutes, until the domes are firm and a skewer inserted into the crumb comes out without raw batter.
Leave the muffins in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 25 minutes. Avoid storing them warm so the bases do not become damp.
tips: Pat the pineapple cubes with paper towels if they still release a lot of juice.

title: Mango and cornmeal muffins
description: Fine-cornmeal muffins with ripe mango.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Line a muffin pan with 12 cavities, each holding 120 ml, with paper liners. Prepare all ingredients before mixing.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt, along with cornmeal. Break up lumps with a whisk to distribute the leavener evenly.
Whisk the eggs with the oil, milk and orange zest in another bowl until the mixture looks even.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and fold just until moistened. Fold in the mango gently to avoid crushing it. Divide among the 12 liners, filling them no more than 3/4 full.
Bake for 24 to 30 minutes, until the domes are firm and a skewer inserted into the crumb comes out without raw batter.
Leave the muffins in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 25 minutes. Avoid storing them warm so the bases do not become damp.
tips: The mango should be ripe but firm so some pieces remain in the crumb.

title: Coffee and cinnamon muffins
description: Soft muffins flavored with strong coffee, milk, and cinnamon.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Line a muffin pan with 12 cavities, each holding 120 ml, with paper liners. Prepare all ingredients before mixing.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt, along with cinnamon. Break up lumps with a whisk to distribute the leavener evenly.
Whisk the eggs with the oil, coffee, milk, and vanilla in another bowl until the mixture looks even.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and fold just until moistened. Stir only as much as needed to distribute the coffee. Divide among the 12 liners, filling them no more than 3/4 full.
Bake for 22 to 28 minutes, until the domes are firm and a skewer inserted into the crumb comes out without raw batter.
Leave the muffins in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 25 minutes. Avoid storing them warm so the bases do not become damp.
tips: Strong cooled coffee adds aroma without adding liquid beyond the formula.

title: Carrot and raisin muffins
description: Muffins with grated carrot, yogurt, and raisins.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Line a muffin pan with 12 cavities, each holding 120 ml, with paper liners. Prepare all ingredients before mixing.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt, along with cinnamon. Break up lumps with a whisk to distribute the leavener evenly.
Whisk the eggs with the oil and yogurt in another bowl until the mixture looks even.

Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and fold just until moistened. Fold in carrots and raisins until evenly distributed through the batter. Divide among the 12 liners, filling them no more than 3/4 full.
Bake for 25 to 32 minutes, until the domes are firm and a skewer inserted into the crumb comes out without raw batter.
Leave the muffins in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 25 minutes. Avoid storing them warm so the bases do not become damp.
tips: Grate the carrot finely so it softens during the short baking time.

title: Guava and white cheese muffins
description: Muffins with cubes of guava paste and firm white cheese.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Line a muffin pan with 12 cavities, each holding 120 ml, with paper liners. Prepare all ingredients before mixing.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt. Break up lumps with a whisk to distribute the leavener evenly.
Whisk the eggs with the oil, milk and vanilla in another bowl until the mixture looks even.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and fold just until moistened. Add guava and cheese, keeping them mostly covered with batter. Divide among the 12 liners, filling them no more than 3/4 full.
Bake for 24 to 30 minutes, until the domes are firm and a skewer inserted into the crumb comes out without raw batter.
Leave the muffins in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 25 minutes. Avoid storing them warm so the bases do not become damp.
tips: Use firm well-drained cheese; very moist cheese can leave pockets of liquid.

title: Savory corn and sweet pepper muffins
description: Savory muffins for serving with meals, made with corn, sweet peppers, and grated cheese.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Line a muffin pan with 12 cavities, each holding 120 ml, with paper liners. Prepare all ingredients before mixing.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt, along with cumin. Break up lumps with a whisk to distribute the leavener evenly.
Whisk the eggs with the oil and milk in another bowl until the mixture looks even.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and fold just until moistened. Fold in the corn, sweet peppers, and cheese evenly. Divide among the 12 liners, filling them no more than 3/4 full.
Bake for 25 to 32 minutes, until the domes are firm and a skewer inserted into the crumb comes out without raw batter.
Leave the muffins in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack for 25 minutes. Avoid storing them warm so the bases do not become damp.
tips: Finely chop the peppers and remove seeds and ribs to distribute their flavor throughout each muffin.

title: Sweet potato and walnut quick bread
description: A loaf made without baker’s yeast, with cooked sweet potato and walnuts.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line a loaf pan measuring 25 × 11 cm and 7 cm deep with parchment, leaving overhanging ends for lifting out.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt, along with cinnamon. This loaf uses baking powder and does not need fermentation.
Whisk the eggs with the oil, sweet potato and milk in a separate bowl until evenly combined.
Fold the wet ingredients into the dry with a spatula, without kneading. Add the walnuts and distribute throughout the batter. Pour into the pan and smooth without compressing the batter.
Bake for 55 to 68 minutes, until the center is firm and a long skewer comes out without raw batter. If it browns too soon, cover loosely with foil.
Rest in the pan for 15 minutes; unmold and cool on a rack for 60 minutes before cutting into 12 slices.
tips: Slice when cool so the moisture from the sweet potato does not make the slices crumble.

title: Banana and sesame quick bread
description: Quick bread with ripe banana and toasted sesame seeds.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line a loaf pan measuring 25 × 11 cm and 7 cm deep with parchment, leaving overhanging ends for lifting out.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt. This loaf uses baking powder and does not need fermentation.
Whisk the eggs with the oil, banana, milk, and vanilla in a separate bowl until evenly combined.
Fold the wet ingredients into the dry with a spatula, without kneading. Fold in the toasted sesame without beating the mixture. Pour into the pan and smooth without compressing the batter.
Bake for 55 to 68 minutes, until the center is firm and a long skewer comes out without raw batter. If it browns too soon, cover loosely with foil.
Rest in the pan for 15 minutes; unmold and cool on a rack for 60 minutes before cutting into 12 slices.
tips: Weigh the peeled banana to maintain the fruit-to-flour ratio.

title: Pumpkin and orange quick bread
description: Quick bread with cooked pumpkin, orange, and gentle spices.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line a loaf pan measuring 25 × 11 cm and 7 cm deep with parchment, leaving overhanging ends for lifting out.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt, along with cinnamon and nutmeg. This loaf uses baking powder and does not need fermentation.
Whisk the eggs with the oil, pumpkin, orange juice, and zest in a separate bowl until evenly combined.
Fold the wet ingredients into the dry with a spatula, without kneading. Scrape the bottom to make sure no dry flour remains. Pour into the pan and smooth without compressing the batter.
Bake for 55 to 70 minutes, until the center is firm and a long skewer comes out without raw batter. If it browns too soon, cover loosely with foil.
Rest in the pan for 15 minutes; unmold and cool on a rack for 60 minutes before cutting into 12 slices.
tips: Drain an overly watery puree before weighing it to avoid a wet underbaked center.

title: Mamey and cocoa quick bread
description: Dark quick bread made with ripe mamey and unsweetened cocoa.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line a loaf pan measuring 25 × 11 cm and 7 cm deep with parchment, leaving overhanging ends for lifting out.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt, along with cocoa. This loaf uses baking powder and does not need fermentation.
Whisk the eggs with the oil, mamey, milk, and vanilla in a separate bowl until evenly combined.
Fold the wet ingredients into the dry with a spatula, without kneading. Combine light and dark streaks with gentle folds. Pour into the pan and smooth without compressing the batter.
Bake for 55 to 68 minutes, until the center is firm and a long skewer comes out without raw batter. If it browns too soon, cover loosely with foil.
Rest in the pan for 15 minutes; unmold and cool on a rack for 60 minutes before cutting into 12 slices.
tips: Test the center with a long skewer; the dark color makes surface browning an unreliable guide.

title: Coconut and pineapple quick bread
description: Tropical quick bread with drained pineapple and shredded coconut.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line a loaf pan measuring 25 × 11 cm and 7 cm deep with parchment, leaving overhanging ends for lifting out.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt. This loaf uses baking powder and does not need fermentation.
Whisk the eggs with the oil, coconut milk and lime zest in a separate bowl until evenly combined.
Fold the wet ingredients into the dry with a spatula, without kneading. Fold in the drained pineapple and coconut at the end. Pour into the pan and smooth without compressing the batter.
Bake for 55 to 70 minutes, until the center is firm and a long skewer comes out without raw batter. If it browns too soon, cover loosely with foil.
Rest in the pan for 15 minutes; unmold and cool on a rack for 60 minutes before cutting into 12 slices.
tips: Do not pour the drained pineapple juice into the batter; it would change the intended moisture balance.

title: Cornmeal and white cheese quick bread
description: Savory quick bread with cornmeal, sweet corn kernels, and white cheese.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line a loaf pan measuring 25 × 11 cm and 7 cm deep with parchment, leaving overhanging ends for lifting out.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt, along with cornmeal and oregano. This loaf uses baking powder and does not need fermentation.
Whisk the eggs with the oil and milk in a separate bowl until evenly combined.
Fold the wet ingredients into the dry with a spatula, without kneading. Fold in corn and cheese, distributing them without overworking. Pour into the pan and smooth without compressing the batter.
Bake for 50 to 63 minutes, until the center is firm and a long skewer comes out without raw batter. If it browns too soon, cover loosely with foil.
Rest in the pan for 15 minutes; unmold and cool on a rack for 60 minutes before cutting into 12 slices.
tips: The cheese should be well drained so the savory crumb holds its structure.

title: Whole-wheat papaya and raisin quick bread
description: Mixed-flour quick bread with ripe papaya and raisins.

ingredients.name: pureed ripe papaya without skin or seeds

steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line a loaf pan measuring 25 × 11 cm and 7 cm deep with parchment, leaving overhanging ends for lifting out.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt, along with whole-wheat flour and ginger. This loaf uses baking powder and does not need fermentation.
Whisk the eggs with the oil, papaya and yogurt in a separate bowl until evenly combined.
Fold the wet ingredients into the dry with a spatula, without kneading. Add the raisins and distribute without kneading. Pour into the pan and smooth without compressing the batter.
Bake for 60 to 75 minutes, until the center is firm and a long skewer comes out without raw batter. If it browns too soon, cover loosely with foil.
Rest in the pan for 15 minutes; unmold and cool on a rack for 60 minutes before cutting into 12 slices.
tips: Whole-wheat flour absorbs more liquid; do not add extra flour just because the batter feels moist.

title: Malanga and scallion quick bread
description: Savory quick bread with cooked malanga, cheese, and scallions.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Line a loaf pan measuring 25 × 11 cm and 7 cm deep with parchment, leaving overhanging ends for lifting out.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt, along with black pepper. This loaf uses baking powder and does not need fermentation.
Whisk the eggs with the oil, malanga and milk in a separate bowl until evenly combined.
Fold the wet ingredients into the dry with a spatula, without kneading. Fold in cheese and scallions, distributing them evenly. Pour into the pan and smooth without compressing the batter.
Bake for 55 to 70 minutes, until the center is firm and a long skewer comes out without raw batter. If it browns too soon, cover loosely with foil.
Rest in the pan for 15 minutes; unmold and cool on a rack for 60 minutes before cutting into 12 slices.
tips: Use fully cooked, cooled malanga; the mash should contain no hard pieces.

title: Orange and honey braided bread
description: An enriched braided sweet bread scented with orange and sweetened with honey.
steps: Combine the flour, yeast, sugar, and salt with the milk, eggs, honey, and zest. Mix until no dry flour remains; liquids should be lukewarm, not hot.
Work in the softened butter in several additions. Knead for 10 to 12 minutes, until elastic and slightly tacky.
Place in a bowl, cover, and let rise for 60 to 90 minutes, until nearly doubled. Timing depends on the kitchen temperature.
Gently deflate and divide into 3 portions. Make 35 cm ropes, braid, and place on a parchment-lined baking sheet, tucking the ends under.
Cover loosely and let rise for 40 to 60 minutes, until puffy and a fingertip impression springs back slowly.
Heat the oven to 175 °C. Bake for 30 to 38 minutes, until the surface is golden and the center crumb is baked; cover with foil if it browns too soon.
Transfer to a rack and cool for at least 45 minutes before slicing. Do not seal still-warm bread in a bag.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Guava and peanut rolls
description: Soft bread spirals filled with guava paste and chopped roasted peanuts.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, milk, and eggs; reserve the guava paste and peanuts for filling. Mix until no dry flour remains; liquids should be lukewarm, not hot.
Gradually add the softened butter. Knead for 10 to 12 minutes, until elastic and slightly tacky.
Place in a bowl, cover, and let rise for 60 to 90 minutes, until nearly doubled. Timing depends on the kitchen temperature.
Roll into a 30 × 40 cm rectangle, distribute thin guava slices and chopped peanuts, and roll up from the long side. Cut into 12 rolls and place in a lined 23 × 33 cm pan.
Cover loosely and let rise for 40 to 60 minutes, until puffy and a fingertip impression springs back slowly.
Heat the oven to 180 °C. Bake for 25 to 32 minutes, until the surface is golden and the center crumb is baked; cover with foil if it browns too soon.
Transfer to a rack and cool for at least 45 minutes before slicing. Do not seal still-warm bread in a bag.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Coconut and condensed milk bread
description: A sweet loaf with shredded coconut and a crumb enriched with condensed milk.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, and salt with the milk, condensed milk, and egg. Mix until no dry flour remains; liquids should be lukewarm, not hot.
Work in the butter and shredded coconut. Knead for 10 to 12 minutes, until elastic and slightly tacky.
Place in a bowl, cover, and let rise for 60 to 90 minutes, until nearly doubled. Timing depends on the kitchen temperature.
Deflate and shape into a broad rectangle. Roll tightly and place seam-side down in a lined 25 × 11 cm loaf pan.
