Cover loosely and let rise for 40 to 60 minutes, until puffy and a fingertip impression springs back slowly.
Heat the oven to 175 °C. Bake for 35 to 45 minutes, until the surface is golden and the center crumb is baked; cover with foil if it browns too soon.
Transfer to a rack and cool for at least 45 minutes before slicing. Do not seal still-warm bread in a bag.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Caramelized pineapple buns
description: Enclosed soft buns filled with pineapple cooked into a thick filling.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt, and dough sugar with the milk and eggs. Reserve the pineapple, filling sugar, and lime juice. Mix until no dry flour remains; liquids should be lukewarm, not hot.
Add the dough butter. Knead for 10 to 12 minutes, until elastic and slightly tacky.
Place in a bowl, cover, and let rise for 60 to 90 minutes, until nearly doubled. Timing depends on the kitchen temperature.

During the first rise, cook the pineapple, filling sugar, and lime juice for 15 to 20 minutes until thick; cool. Divide the dough into 12 discs, fill and seal, and place seam-side down on a lined sheet.
Cover loosely and let rise for 40 to 60 minutes, until puffy and a fingertip impression springs back slowly.
Heat the oven to 180 °C. Bake for 22 to 28 minutes, until the surface is golden and the center crumb is baked; cover with foil if it browns too soon.
Transfer to a rack and cool for at least 45 minutes before slicing. Do not seal still-warm bread in a bag.
tips: The filling must be cool and have no free liquid before enclosing it.

title: Coffee and dulce de leche spirals
description: Coffee-flavored dough with thick dulce de leche filling, baked as individual rolls.
steps: Dissolve the coffee in the lukewarm milk and mix with the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, and eggs. Reserve the dulce de leche. Mix until no dry flour remains; liquids should be lukewarm, not hot.
Work in the butter in small cubes. Knead for 10 to 12 minutes, until elastic and slightly tacky.
Place in a bowl, cover, and let rise for 60 to 90 minutes, until nearly doubled. Timing depends on the kitchen temperature.
Roll into a 30 × 40 cm rectangle and spread with dulce de leche, leaving an uncovered edge. Roll up, cut into 12 spirals, and arrange with space between them in a lined 23 × 33 cm pan.
Cover loosely and let rise for 40 to 60 minutes, until puffy and a fingertip impression springs back slowly.
Heat the oven to 180 °C. Bake for 25 to 32 minutes, until the surface is golden and the center crumb is baked; cover with foil if it browns too soon.
Transfer to a rack and cool for at least 45 minutes before slicing. Do not seal still-warm bread in a bag.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Mamey and vanilla yeast loaf
description: A soft-crumb yeast loaf made with mamey pulp and vanilla.
steps: Blend the mamey with the milk, egg, and vanilla. Add the flour, yeast, sugar, and salt. Mix until no dry flour remains; liquids should be lukewarm, not hot.
Gradually work in the softened butter. Knead for 10 to 12 minutes, until elastic and slightly tacky.
Place in a bowl, cover, and let rise for 60 to 90 minutes, until nearly doubled. Timing depends on the kitchen temperature.
Deflate and shape into a compact cylinder. Place seam-side down in a 25 × 11 cm loaf pan lined with parchment.
Cover loosely and let rise for 40 to 60 minutes, until puffy and a fingertip impression springs back slowly.
Heat the oven to 175 °C. Bake for 40 to 50 minutes, until the surface is golden and the center crumb is baked; cover with foil if it browns too soon.
Transfer to a rack and cool for at least 45 minutes before slicing. Do not seal still-warm bread in a bag.
tips: Use thick mamey pulp without adding water when blending.

title: Fresh corn yeast bread
description: A wheat and puréed fresh corn loaf with a fluffy texture and moderate sweetness.
steps: Blend the corn with the milk and egg into a paste. Mix with the flour, yeast, sugar, and salt. Mix until no dry flour remains; liquids should be lukewarm, not hot.
Add the softened butter in small portions. Knead for 10 to 12 minutes, until elastic and slightly tacky.
Place in a bowl, cover, and let rise for 60 to 90 minutes, until nearly doubled. Timing depends on the kitchen temperature.
Deflate, roll into a cylinder, and place in a lined 25 × 11 cm loaf pan. Smooth the top with slightly damp hands.
Cover loosely and let rise for 40 to 60 minutes, until puffy and a fingertip impression springs back slowly.
Heat the oven to 180 °C. Bake for 38 to 48 minutes, until the surface is golden and the center crumb is baked; cover with foil if it browns too soon.
Transfer to a rack and cool for at least 45 minutes before slicing. Do not seal still-warm bread in a bag.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Garlic and parsley bread knots
description: Knotted rolls baked with garlic-parsley butter on their surface.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, and salt with the water; reserve the butter, garlic, and parsley for the topping. Mix until no dry flour remains; liquids should be lukewarm, not hot.
Add the olive oil. Knead for 10 to 12 minutes, until elastic and slightly tacky.
Place in a bowl, cover, and let rise for 60 to 90 minutes, until nearly doubled. Timing depends on the kitchen temperature.
Divide into 12 portions, stretch into 20 cm ropes, and knot them on a lined sheet. Melt the butter, mix with the garlic and parsley, and brush over the knots before the second rise.
Cover loosely and let rise for 40 to 60 minutes, until puffy and a fingertip impression springs back slowly.
Heat the oven to 190 °C. Bake for 20 to 26 minutes, until the surface is golden and the center crumb is baked; cover with foil if it browns too soon.
Transfer to a rack and cool for at least 45 minutes before slicing. Do not seal still-warm bread in a bag.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Olive and oregano loaf
description: A wheat loaf with drained green olives and dried oregano.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, and salt with the water and oregano; drain and dry the olives separately. Mix until no dry flour remains; liquids should be lukewarm, not hot.
Add the oil and fold in the chopped olives toward the end of kneading. Knead for 10 to 12 minutes, until elastic and slightly tacky.
Place in a bowl, cover, and let rise for 60 to 90 minutes, until nearly doubled. Timing depends on the kitchen temperature.
Shape into an oval loaf and place on a lined sheet. Tighten the surface with your hands without leaving olives exposed where they might burn.
Cover loosely and let rise for 40 to 60 minutes, until puffy and a fingertip impression springs back slowly.
Heat the oven to 200 °C. Bake for 32 to 40 minutes, until the surface is golden and the center crumb is baked; cover with foil if it browns too soon.
Transfer to a rack and cool for at least 45 minutes before slicing. Do not seal still-warm bread in a bag.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Tomato and onion focaccia
description: A wet-dough yeast flatbread topped with tomato and thinly sliced onion.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, and salt with the water and 20 ml oil to make a wet dough. Rest covered for 20 minutes.
With damp hands, fold the dough from the edges toward the center. Repeat 3 times at 20-minute intervals; then let rise for 40 minutes.
Oil a 23 × 33 cm pan with 20 ml oil and gently stretch the dough to fit. Cover and let rise for another 40 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220 °C. Add the halved tomatoes, very thin onion, oregano, and remaining 20 ml oil; press your fingertips into the dough to make dimples.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the bread is golden and baked underneath too. Transfer to a rack and cool for 30 minutes before cutting into 12 portions.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Banana and cocoa yeast ring
description: A yeast dough ring with mashed ripe banana and unsweetened cocoa.
steps: Mash the banana and mix with the milk and egg. Add the flour, cocoa, yeast, sugar, and salt. Mix until no dry flour remains; liquids should be lukewarm, not hot.
Work in the butter in small portions. Knead for 10 to 12 minutes, until elastic and slightly tacky.
Place in a bowl, cover, and let rise for 60 to 90 minutes, until nearly doubled. Timing depends on the kitchen temperature.
Shape into a thick rope and join the ends inside a lined 26 cm ring pan. Seal the join and distribute the dough evenly.
Cover loosely and let rise for 40 to 60 minutes, until puffy and a fingertip impression springs back slowly.
Heat the oven to 175 °C. Bake for 35 to 45 minutes, until the surface is golden and the center crumb is baked; cover with foil if it browns too soon.
Transfer to a rack and cool for at least 45 minutes before slicing. Do not seal still-warm bread in a bag.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Oat and molasses yeast loaf
description: A sandwich loaf with hydrated oats, cane molasses, and a soft crust.
steps: Soak the oats in the lukewarm water for 15 minutes. Add the molasses, flour, yeast, and salt. Mix until no dry flour remains; liquids should be lukewarm, not hot.
Work in the oil gradually. Knead for 10 to 12 minutes, until elastic and slightly tacky.
Place in a bowl, cover, and let rise for 60 to 90 minutes, until nearly doubled. Timing depends on the kitchen temperature.
Deflate and shape into a cylinder. Place seam-side down in a lined 25 × 11 cm loaf pan, distributing the dough to the ends.
Cover loosely and let rise for 40 to 60 minutes, until puffy and a fingertip impression springs back slowly.
Heat the oven to 185 °C. Bake for 35 to 45 minutes, until the surface is golden and the center crumb is baked; cover with foil if it browns too soon.
Transfer to a rack and cool for at least 45 minutes before slicing. Do not seal still-warm bread in a bag.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: White cheese and sesame rolls
description: Small wheat rolls with crumbled white cheese and sesame seeds.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, and salt with the milk and egg; reserve the cheese and sesame seeds. Mix until no dry flour remains; liquids should be lukewarm, not hot.
Add the butter and, at the end, the crumbled cheese and sesame seeds. Knead for 10 to 12 minutes, until elastic and slightly tacky.
Place in a bowl, cover, and let rise for 60 to 90 minutes, until nearly doubled. Timing depends on the kitchen temperature.
Divide the dough into 12 portions and shape into taut balls. Place with space between them on a lined baking sheet to allow for rising.
Cover loosely and let rise for 40 to 60 minutes, until puffy and a fingertip impression springs back slowly.
Heat the oven to 185 °C. Bake for 22 to 28 minutes, until the surface is golden and the center crumb is baked; cover with foil if it browns too soon.
Transfer to a rack and cool for at least 45 minutes before slicing. Do not seal still-warm bread in a bag.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Pumpkin and guava swirl bread
description: Pumpkin yeast bread with a guava paste swirl inside.
steps: Mix the pumpkin, milk, and egg; add the flour, yeast, sugar, and salt. Reserve the guava paste for filling. Mix until no dry flour remains; liquids should be lukewarm, not hot.
Work in the softened butter in several additions. Knead for 10 to 12 minutes, until elastic and slightly tacky.
Place in a bowl, cover, and let rise for 60 to 90 minutes, until nearly doubled. Timing depends on the kitchen temperature.
Roll into a 25 × 35 cm rectangle and cover with thin guava slices. Roll up from a short side and place seam-side down in a lined 25 × 11 cm loaf pan.
Cover loosely and let rise for 40 to 60 minutes, until puffy and a fingertip impression springs back slowly.
Heat the oven to 175 °C. Bake for 40 to 50 minutes, until the surface is golden and the center crumb is baked; cover with foil if it browns too soon.
Transfer to a rack and cool for at least 45 minutes before slicing. Do not seal still-warm bread in a bag.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Yogurt and raisin buns with a sugar crust
description: Yeasted plain-yogurt and raisin buns with a crisp sugar topping.
steps: Mix the yogurt, milk, and egg with the flour, yeast, salt, and dough sugar. Reserve the raisins and topping sugar. Mix until no dry flour remains; liquids should be lukewarm, not hot.
Work in the butter and then the raisins. Knead for 10 to 12 minutes, until elastic and slightly tacky.
Place in a bowl, cover, and let rise for 60 to 90 minutes, until nearly doubled. Timing depends on the kitchen temperature.
Shape into 12 balls and place in a lined 23 × 33 cm pan. Moisten the tops with the measured water and scatter the reserved sugar over them.
Cover loosely and let rise for 40 to 60 minutes, until puffy and a fingertip impression springs back slowly.
Heat the oven to 180 °C. Bake for 25 to 32 minutes, until the surface is golden and the center crumb is baked; cover with foil if it browns too soon.
Transfer to a rack and cool for at least 45 minutes before slicing. Do not seal still-warm bread in a bag.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Pineapple and ginger puff pastries
description: Puff pastry triangles filled with cooked pineapple, ginger, and lime.
steps: Keep the puff pastry cold and work on parchment. If frozen, thaw it beforehand in the refrigerator according to its package.
Cook the pineapple, sugar, ginger, and lime juice for 15 minutes. Dissolve the cornstarch in the measured cold water, add it, and boil for 1 minute; cool to a thick filling.
Roll the puff pastry to 3 mm and cut 8 squares measuring 12 cm. Divide the cold filling among them, fold into triangles, and seal with a fork; place on a lined sheet.
Beat the egg and brush only the tops, avoiding the cut edges so the layers can rise. Refrigerate the shaped pastries for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200 °C and bake for 22 to 28 minutes, until the pastry is deeply golden, crisp, and baked underneath too.
Transfer the pastries to a rack and cool for 20 minutes before serving. Refrigerate leftovers containing cheese filling once no longer hot.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Mamey and cheese puff pastry braid
description: A puff pastry braid filled with reduced mamey pulp and cream cheese.
steps: Keep the puff pastry cold and work on parchment. If frozen, thaw it beforehand in the refrigerator according to its package.
Cook the mamey with half the sugar for 8 minutes, stirring, and cool. Mix the cream cheese with the remaining sugar and vanilla until smooth.
Roll into a 30 × 40 cm rectangle. Place the cheese and mamey down the center; cut the sides into 2 cm strips and cross them over the filling. Place the braid on a lined sheet.
Beat the egg and brush only the tops, avoiding the cut edges so the layers can rise. Refrigerate the shaped pastries for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200 °C and bake for 30 to 38 minutes, until the pastry is deeply golden, crisp, and baked underneath too.
Transfer the pastries to a rack and cool for 20 minutes before serving. Refrigerate leftovers containing cheese filling once no longer hot.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Guava and coconut pinwheels
description: Open pinwheel-shaped puff pastries with guava and coconut centers.
steps: Keep the puff pastry cold and work on parchment. If frozen, thaw it beforehand in the refrigerator according to its package.
Cut the guava paste into small cubes and mix the cream cheese with the coconut. Keep both fillings chilled until shaping.

Cut 8 puff pastry squares measuring 12 cm. Cut diagonally inward from each corner without reaching the center; add cheese and guava in the middle and fold in alternating corner tips to form pinwheels.
Beat the egg and brush only the tops, avoiding the cut edges so the layers can rise. Refrigerate the shaped pastries for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200 °C and bake for 22 to 28 minutes, until the pastry is deeply golden, crisp, and baked underneath too.
Transfer the pastries to a rack and cool for 20 minutes before serving. Refrigerate leftovers containing cheese filling once no longer hot.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Apple and molasses puff pastries
description: Puff pastry parcels with sautéed apple and a touch of cane molasses.
steps: Keep the puff pastry cold and work on parchment. If frozen, thaw it beforehand in the refrigerator according to its package.
Sauté the apple in the butter for 8 minutes. Add the molasses, cinnamon, and cornstarch, stir for 2 minutes, and cool completely; the filling should have no free liquid.
Roll out the puff pastry and cut 16 rectangles measuring 8 × 10 cm. Fill 8, top with the remaining rectangles, and seal with a fork; cut a small vent in each top.
Beat the egg and brush only the tops, avoiding the cut edges so the layers can rise. Refrigerate the shaped pastries for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200 °C and bake for 22 to 28 minutes, until the pastry is deeply golden, crisp, and baked underneath too.
Transfer the pastries to a rack and cool for 20 minutes before serving. Refrigerate leftovers containing cheese filling once no longer hot.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Thin mango and almond puff tarts
description: Individual puff pastry bases with baked almond cream and mango slices.
steps: Keep the puff pastry cold and work on parchment. If frozen, thaw it beforehand in the refrigerator according to its package.
Beat the filling butter and sugar; add its egg and the ground almonds. Peel and thinly slice the mango; keep the uncooked almond cream refrigerated until assembly.
Cut 8 puff pastry rectangles measuring 10 × 15 cm and score a 1 cm border without cutting through. Spread almond cream in the centers and top with mango, leaving the borders clear.
Beat the egg and brush only the tops, avoiding the cut edges so the layers can rise. Refrigerate the shaped pastries for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200 °C and bake for 25 to 32 minutes, until the pastry is deeply golden, crisp, and baked underneath too.
Transfer the pastries to a rack and cool for 20 minutes before serving. Refrigerate leftovers containing cheese filling once no longer hot.
tips: The almond cream contains egg and nut flour: the filling must set and reach at least 71 °C.

title: Sweet potato and orange puff pastry spirals
description: Crisp spirals filled with thick sweet potato purée and orange zest.
steps: Keep the puff pastry cold and work on parchment. If frozen, thaw it beforehand in the refrigerator according to its package.
Mix the cooked sweet potato with the sugar, filling butter, zest, and cinnamon. Make sure the paste is cold and thick enough to spread.
Roll the pastry into a 30 × 40 cm rectangle and spread with the filling. Roll up from the long side, cut into 12 spirals, and space them on a lined sheet.
Beat the egg and brush only the tops, avoiding the cut edges so the layers can rise. Refrigerate the shaped pastries for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200 °C and bake for 25 to 32 minutes, until the pastry is deeply golden, crisp, and baked underneath too.
Transfer the pastries to a rack and cool for 20 minutes before serving. Refrigerate leftovers containing cheese filling once no longer hot.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Ricotta and raisin puff pastry envelopes
description: Envelope-shaped puff pastries with drained ricotta and raisins.
steps: Keep the puff pastry cold and work on parchment. If frozen, thaw it beforehand in the refrigerator according to its package.
Mix the ricotta with the raisins, sugar, zest, and cornstarch. If visible whey remains, drain the ricotta before weighing and mixing.
Cut 8 puff pastry squares measuring 12 cm. Place filling in the centers, bring the corners to the middle, and press to close; place seam-side up on a lined sheet.
Beat the egg and brush only the tops, avoiding the cut edges so the layers can rise. Refrigerate the shaped pastries for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200 °C and bake for 25 to 32 minutes, until the pastry is deeply golden, crisp, and baked underneath too.
Transfer the pastries to a rack and cool for 20 minutes before serving. Refrigerate leftovers containing cheese filling once no longer hot.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Cheese and sesame puff pastry sticks
description: Twisted puff pastry strips with grated cheese and oven-toasted sesame seeds.
steps: Keep the puff pastry cold and work on parchment. If frozen, thaw it beforehand in the refrigerator according to its package.
Mix the grated cheese with the sesame seeds and paprika. Work with cold cheese so it distributes without turning into a paste.
Roll into a 30 × 40 cm rectangle, cover half with the mixture, and fold the other half over. Press, cut into 16 strips, and twist them before placing on lined sheets.
Beat the egg and brush only the tops, avoiding the cut edges so the layers can rise. Refrigerate the shaped pastries for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200 °C and bake for 18 to 24 minutes, until the pastry is deeply golden, crisp, and baked underneath too.
Transfer the pastries to a rack and cool for 20 minutes before serving. Refrigerate leftovers containing cheese filling once no longer hot.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Pumpkin and white cheese puff pastries
description: Puff pastry half-moons with roasted pumpkin and crumbled white cheese.
steps: Keep the puff pastry cold and work on parchment. If frozen, thaw it beforehand in the refrigerator according to its package.
Lightly mash the pumpkin and mix with the crumbled cheese, scallions, and cumin. Drain any roasting liquid before making the filling.
Cut 10 puff pastry discs measuring 12 cm, stacking scraps without kneading them. Add the filling, fold into half-moons, and seal with a fork; place on a lined sheet.
Beat the egg and brush only the tops, avoiding the cut edges so the layers can rise. Refrigerate the shaped pastries for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200 °C and bake for 25 to 32 minutes, until the pastry is deeply golden, crisp, and baked underneath too.
Transfer the pastries to a rack and cool for 20 minutes before serving. Refrigerate leftovers containing cheese filling once no longer hot.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Mamey and almond tart
description: A shortcrust tart with a baked mamey and ground almond filling.
steps: Rub the crust flour with its cold butter, sugar, and salt into crumbs. Add the crust egg and bring together without kneading; form a disc and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Roll to 3 mm and line a 24 cm loose-bottomed tart pan; trim the rim and gently prick the base. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180 °C. Line the pastry with paper and baking weights; bake for 15 minutes, remove paper and weights, and bake for 5 more minutes.
Beat the filling butter with its sugar. Add its eggs, mamey pulp, ground almonds, and filling flour until evenly combined.
Spread the filling over the prebaked pastry and smooth without filling above the rim. Place the pan on a baking sheet for easy handling.
Bake at 175 °C for 32 to 40 minutes, until the filling is set and reaches at least 71 °C in the center; do not leave a liquid layer beneath the surface.
Cool on a rack for 45 minutes and refrigerate for at least 2 hours before unmolding and slicing. Keep the tart covered and chilled.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Banana and cocoa tartlets
description: Individual tartlets with ripe banana and a baked cocoa filling.
steps: Rub the crust flour with its cold butter, sugar, and salt into crumbs. Add the crust egg and bring together without kneading; form a disc and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Roll to 3 mm and line 12 tartlet molds measuring 8 cm; trim the rims and gently prick the bases. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180 °C. Line the pastry with paper and baking weights; bake for 15 minutes, remove paper and weights, and bake for 5 more minutes.
Blend the banana with the filling eggs, cream, and filling sugar. Add the sifted cocoa and cornstarch and mix until smooth.
Spread the filling over the prebaked pastry and smooth without filling above the rim. Place the pan on a baking sheet for easy handling.
Bake at 175 °C for 22 to 28 minutes, until the filling is set and reaches at least 71 °C in the center; do not leave a liquid layer beneath the surface.
Cool on a rack for 45 minutes and refrigerate for at least 2 hours before unmolding and slicing. Keep the tart covered and chilled.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Orange and almond tart
description: An orange tart with baked almond cream and a crisp crust.
steps: Rub the crust flour with its cold butter, sugar, and salt into crumbs. Add the crust egg and bring together without kneading; form a disc and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Roll to 3 mm and line a 24 cm loose-bottomed tart pan; trim the rim and gently prick the base. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180 °C. Line the pastry with paper and baking weights; bake for 15 minutes, remove paper and weights, and bake for 5 more minutes.
Mix the filling sugar with the cornstarch and almonds. Add the filling eggs, cream, orange juice, and zest; whisk by hand without incorporating too much air.
Spread the filling over the prebaked pastry and smooth without filling above the rim. Place the pan on a baking sheet for easy handling.
Bake at 175 °C for 32 to 40 minutes, until the filling is set and reaches at least 71 °C in the center; do not leave a liquid layer beneath the surface.
Cool on a rack for 45 minutes and refrigerate for at least 2 hours before unmolding and slicing. Keep the tart covered and chilled.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Coffee and walnut tart
description: A tart with chopped walnuts and a coffee custard set in the oven.
steps: Rub the crust flour with its cold butter, sugar, and salt into crumbs. Add the crust egg and bring together without kneading; form a disc and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Roll to 3 mm and line a 24 cm loose-bottomed tart pan; trim the rim and gently prick the base. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180 °C. Line the pastry with paper and baking weights; bake for 15 minutes, remove paper and weights, and bake for 5 more minutes.
Dissolve the coffee in lukewarm milk and let cool slightly. Beat the filling butter with its sugar; add the filling eggs, cornstarch, coffee milk, and chopped walnuts.
Spread the filling over the prebaked pastry and smooth without filling above the rim. Place the pan on a baking sheet for easy handling.
Bake at 175 °C for 32 to 40 minutes, until the filling is set and reaches at least 71 °C in the center; do not leave a liquid layer beneath the surface.
Cool on a rack for 45 minutes and refrigerate for at least 2 hours before unmolding and slicing. Keep the tart covered and chilled.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Mango and vanilla cream tartlets
description: Crisp shortcrust shells with cooked pastry cream and fresh mango.
steps: Rub the crust flour with its cold butter, sugar, and salt into crumbs. Add the crust egg and bring together without kneading; form a disc and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Roll to 3 mm and line 12 tartlet molds measuring 8 cm; trim the rims and gently prick the bases. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180 °C. Line the pastry with paper and baking weights; bake for 15 minutes, remove paper and weights, and bake for 5 more minutes.
For the cream, whisk its eggs with the sugar and cornstarch; gradually add the hot milk and return to the saucepan. Stir until bubbling in the center and maintain a gentle boil for 1 minute.
Add the vanilla, spread the cream in a shallow container, and cover its surface. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours until completely cold.
Finish baking the empty shells at 180 °C for 8 to 10 minutes, until golden; cool them on a rack for 30 minutes.
Briefly whisk the cold cream and divide among the shells. Slice the mango, arrange it on top, and keep the tartlets refrigerated until serving.
tips: Assemble the tartlets shortly before serving to keep the shells crisp.

title: Soursop and cream cheese tart
description: A baked tart with seedless soursop pulp and cream cheese.
steps: Rub the crust flour with its cold butter, sugar, and salt into crumbs. Add the crust egg and bring together without kneading; form a disc and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Roll to 3 mm and line a 24 cm loose-bottomed tart pan; trim the rim and gently prick the base. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180 °C. Line the pastry with paper and baking weights; bake for 15 minutes, remove paper and weights, and bake for 5 more minutes.
Check the soursop carefully and remove every seed. Mix the cream cheese and filling sugar; add its eggs, cornstarch, and pulp without overbeating.
Spread the filling over the prebaked pastry and smooth without filling above the rim. Place the pan on a baking sheet for easy handling.
Bake at 175 °C for 40 to 50 minutes, until the filling is set and reaches at least 71 °C in the center; do not leave a liquid layer beneath the surface.
Cool on a rack for 45 minutes and refrigerate for at least 2 hours before unmolding and slicing. Keep the tart covered and chilled.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Chocolate and sesame tartlets
description: Crisp tartlets filled with chocolate ganache and toasted sesame seeds.
steps: Rub the crust flour with its cold butter, sugar, and salt into crumbs. Add the crust egg and bring together without kneading; form a disc and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Roll to 3 mm and line 12 tartlet molds measuring 8 cm; trim the rims and gently prick the bases. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180 °C. Line the pastry with paper and baking weights; bake for 15 minutes, remove paper and weights, and bake for 5 more minutes.
Continue baking the empty shells at 180 °C for 8 to 10 minutes until fully golden. Cool on a rack for 30 minutes.
Chop the chocolate into a bowl. Heat the cream until it begins to boil, pour over the chocolate, wait 2 minutes, and stir; add the filling butter.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry skillet for 2 minutes, moving them around. Divide the ganache among the cold shells and scatter the seeds on top.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours until the filling firms up. Keep chilled and take out shortly before serving so the chocolate regains a creamy texture.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Pumpkin and coconut tart
description: A cooked pumpkin and coconut milk tart with cinnamon, chilled before serving.
steps: Rub the crust flour with its cold butter, sugar, and salt into crumbs. Add the crust egg and bring together without kneading; form a disc and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Roll to 3 mm and line a 24 cm loose-bottomed tart pan; trim the rim and gently prick the base. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180 °C. Line the pastry with paper and baking weights; bake for 15 minutes, remove paper and weights, and bake for 5 more minutes.
Mix the cold pumpkin purée with the coconut milk, filling eggs, filling sugar, cornstarch, and cinnamon. Blend if necessary to remove coarse fibers.
Spread the filling over the prebaked pastry and smooth without filling above the rim. Place the pan on a baking sheet for easy handling.
Bake at 175 °C for 40 to 50 minutes, until the filling is set and reaches at least 71 °C in the center; do not leave a liquid layer beneath the surface.
Cool on a rack for 45 minutes and refrigerate for at least 2 hours before unmolding and slicing. Keep the tart covered and chilled.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Apple and peanut galette
description: A rustic apple tart with roasted peanuts and juices thickened during baking.
steps: Rub the flour, cold butter, dough sugar, and salt into crumbs. Gradually add the water, bring together without kneading, and refrigerate the dough disc for 30 minutes.
Thinly slice the apples and chop the peanuts. Toss the fruit, peanuts, filling sugar, cornstarch, and lime juice immediately before assembling.
Roll the dough on parchment into a 35 cm circle. Spread the filling in the center, leaving a 4 cm border, and fold that border over the fruit.
Brush the edges with the beaten egg and refrigerate for 20 minutes. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 190 °C.
Bake for 35 to 45 minutes, until the base is golden and the filling bubbles. If the rim browns too soon, cover it with strips of foil.
Cool on a rack for 45 minutes so the juices thicken before cutting into 8 servings.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Guava cream choux buns
description: Dry, hollow choux pastries filled with guava pastry cream.

ingredients.name: beaten egg for the pastry
ingredients.note: Weight without shells; add gradually to obtain a glossy paste.

steps: Heat the milk with the guava until dissolved. Whisk the cream eggs, cream sugar, and cornstarch; add the milk, return to the heat, and boil gently for 1 minute, stirring. Spread in a shallow container, cover the surface, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Bring the pastry water, butter, salt, and pastry sugar to a boil. Remove from the heat, add all the pastry flour, and stir; return to the heat and dry the paste for 2 minutes.
Let the paste cool for 10 minutes until below 50 °C. Gradually beat in the beaten egg until smooth and falling from a spoon in a thick ribbon.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Using a piping bag or spoons, make 12 mounds about 5 cm across on a lined sheet, leaving room between them. Smooth the peaks with a slightly damp fingertip.
Bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes, lower to 180 °C, and continue for 20 to 25 minutes without opening early. Once deeply golden, make small slits and dry for 5 more minutes at 160 °C.
Cool the pastries completely on a rack for 30 minutes. Open with a serrated knife and fill only with completely cold cream.
Keep the filled pastries refrigerated and serve the same day to preserve the contrast between pastry and cream.
tips: Do not open the oven during the first part of baking: the pastries must set before releasing steam.

title: Lime cream éclairs
description: Choux éclairs filled with cooked lime cream and fresh zest.

ingredients.name: beaten egg for the pastry
ingredients.note: Weight without shells; add gradually to obtain a glossy paste.

steps: Whisk the cream eggs with the cream sugar and cornstarch. Add the hot milk with zest, return to the saucepan, and boil for 1 minute, stirring. Remove and add the lime juice; spread out, cover the surface, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Bring the pastry water, butter, salt, and pastry sugar to a boil. Remove from the heat, add all the pastry flour, and stir; return to the heat and dry the paste for 2 minutes.
Let the paste cool for 10 minutes until below 50 °C. Gradually beat in the beaten egg until smooth and falling from a spoon in a thick ribbon.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Pipe 12 strips measuring 10 cm onto a lined sheet, leaving room between them. Keep the thickness even and smooth any peaks with a slightly damp fingertip.
Bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes, lower to 180 °C, and continue for 20 to 25 minutes without opening early. Once deeply golden, make small slits and dry for 5 more minutes at 160 °C.
Cool the pastries completely on a rack for 30 minutes. Open with a serrated knife and fill only with completely cold cream.
Keep the filled pastries refrigerated and serve the same day to preserve the contrast between pastry and cream.
tips: Do not open the oven during the first part of baking: the pastries must set before releasing steam.

title: Chocolate and peanut choux ring
description: A choux pastry ring filled with creamy chocolate and roasted peanuts.

ingredients.name: beaten egg for the pastry
ingredients.note: Weight without shells; add gradually to obtain a glossy paste.

steps: Heat the cream until it begins to boil and pour over the chopped chocolate. Wait 2 minutes, stir, and add 80 g ground peanuts; cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours. Reserve the remaining peanuts for finishing.
Bring the pastry water, butter, salt, and pastry sugar to a boil. Remove from the heat, add all the pastry flour, and stir; return to the heat and dry the paste for 2 minutes.
Let the paste cool for 10 minutes until below 50 °C. Gradually beat in the beaten egg until smooth and falling from a spoon in a thick ribbon.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Draw a 22 cm circle on parchment and turn it over. Pipe a ring along the outline, another inside it, and a third on top between them to use all the pastry.
Bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes, lower to 180 °C, and continue for 30 to 35 minutes without opening early. Once deeply golden, make small slits and dry for 5 more minutes at 160 °C.
Cool the pastries completely on a rack for 30 minutes. Open with a serrated knife and fill only with completely cold cream.
Scatter the remaining chopped peanuts over the cream filling. Replace the top, refrigerate the ring, and cut into 12 servings with a serrated knife.
tips: Do not open the oven during the first part of baking: the pastries must set before releasing steam.

title: Banana cream choux buns
description: Choux pastries filled with cooked ripe banana and vanilla cream.

ingredients.name: beaten egg for the pastry
ingredients.note: Weight without shells; add gradually to obtain a glossy paste.

steps: Blend the banana with the milk and heat. Whisk the cream eggs, cream sugar, and cornstarch; add the banana milk and boil for 1 minute, stirring. Add the vanilla, spread in a shallow container, cover the surface, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Bring the pastry water, butter, salt, and pastry sugar to a boil. Remove from the heat, add all the pastry flour, and stir; return to the heat and dry the paste for 2 minutes.
Let the paste cool for 10 minutes until below 50 °C. Gradually beat in the beaten egg until smooth and falling from a spoon in a thick ribbon.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Using a piping bag or spoons, make 12 mounds about 5 cm across on a lined sheet, leaving room between them. Smooth the peaks with a slightly damp fingertip.
Bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes, lower to 180 °C, and continue for 20 to 25 minutes without opening early. Once deeply golden, make small slits and dry for 5 more minutes at 160 °C.
Cool the pastries completely on a rack for 30 minutes. Open with a serrated knife and fill only with completely cold cream.

title: Savory cheese and scallion choux puffs
description: Small choux puffs with grated cheese and scallions mixed into the pastry.

ingredients.name: beaten egg for the pastry
ingredients.note: Weight without shells; add gradually to obtain a glossy paste.

steps: Bring the water, butter, and salt to a boil. Remove from the heat and add all the flour, stirring with a sturdy spoon.
Return to medium heat and stir for 2 minutes, until the paste pulls away from the sides and a thin film forms on the bottom.
Cool for 10 minutes until below 50 °C. Gradually add the beaten egg, mixing until the paste is smooth and glossy.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Fold in the cheese and scallions and make 24 mounds about 3 cm across on lined sheets. Leave space between them because they will expand.
Bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes; lower to 180 °C and continue for 18 to 22 minutes, until the puffs are golden and firm with no wet pastry inside.
Make a small slit in each puff and dry for 5 minutes at 160 °C. Cool on a rack for 15 minutes before serving.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Coffee craquelin choux buns
description: Choux buns with a thin crisp topping and coffee pastry cream.

ingredients.name: beaten egg for the pastry
ingredients.note: Weight without shells; add gradually to obtain a glossy paste.

steps: Dissolve the coffee in hot milk. Whisk the cream eggs with the cream sugar and cornstarch; add the milk, return to the heat, and boil for 1 minute, stirring. Spread out, cover the surface, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Bring the pastry water, butter, salt, and pastry sugar to a boil. Remove from the heat, add all the pastry flour, and stir; return to the heat and dry the paste for 2 minutes.
Let the paste cool for 10 minutes until below 50 °C. Gradually beat in the beaten egg until smooth and falling from a spoon in a thick ribbon.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Using a piping bag or spoons, make 12 mounds about 5 cm across on a lined sheet, leaving room between them. Smooth the peaks with a slightly damp fingertip.
Mix the craquelin butter, sugar, and flour. Divide into 12 balls and flatten between papers into 5 cm discs; refrigerate for 20 minutes and place a disc on each choux mound.
Bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes, lower to 180 °C, and continue for 20 to 25 minutes without opening early. Once deeply golden, make small slits and dry for 5 more minutes at 160 °C.
Cool the pastries completely on a rack for 30 minutes. Open with a serrated knife and fill only with completely cold cream.
Keep the filled pastries refrigerated and serve the same day to preserve the contrast between pastry and cream.
tips: Do not open the oven during the first part of baking: the pastries must set before releasing steam.

title: Orange and chocolate éclairs
description: Éclairs with orange cream and a dark chocolate topping.

ingredients.name: beaten egg for the pastry
ingredients.note: Weight without shells; add gradually to obtain a glossy paste.

steps: Heat the milk with the zest. Whisk the cream eggs with the cream sugar and cornstarch; add the milk and cook until bubbling, maintaining a gentle boil for 1 minute. Spread out, cover the surface, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Bring the pastry water, butter, salt, and pastry sugar to a boil. Remove from the heat, add all the pastry flour, and stir; return to the heat and dry the paste for 2 minutes.
Let the paste cool for 10 minutes until below 50 °C. Gradually beat in the beaten egg until smooth and falling from a spoon in a thick ribbon.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Pipe 12 strips measuring 10 cm onto a lined sheet and smooth the tips. Leave at least 4 cm between the pastries so they can expand.
Bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes, lower to 180 °C, and continue for 20 to 25 minutes without opening early. Once deeply golden, make small slits and dry for 5 more minutes at 160 °C.
Cool the pastries completely on a rack for 30 minutes. Open with a serrated knife and fill only with completely cold cream.
Heat the topping cream and pour it over the chopped chocolate; stir until smooth. Spread a thin layer over the tops, replace them, and refrigerate the filled éclairs until serving.
tips: Do not open the oven during the first part of baking: the pastries must set before releasing steam.

title: Sweet potato and cinnamon cream choux buns
description: Choux buns filled with thick cooked sweet potato cream scented with cinnamon.

ingredients.name: beaten egg for the pastry
ingredients.note: Weight without shells; add gradually to obtain a glossy paste.

steps: Blend the sweet potato with the milk and heat. Whisk the cream eggs with the cream sugar, cornstarch, and cinnamon; add the milk and boil for 1 minute, stirring. Spread in a shallow container, cover the surface, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Bring the pastry water, butter, salt, and pastry sugar to a boil. Remove from the heat, add all the pastry flour, and stir; return to the heat and dry the paste for 2 minutes.
Let the paste cool for 10 minutes until below 50 °C. Gradually beat in the beaten egg until smooth and falling from a spoon in a thick ribbon.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Using a piping bag or spoons, make 12 mounds about 5 cm across on a lined sheet, leaving room between them. Smooth the peaks with a slightly damp fingertip.
Bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes, lower to 180 °C, and continue for 20 to 25 minutes without opening early. Once deeply golden, make small slits and dry for 5 more minutes at 160 °C.

title: Guava and cheese filo triangles
description: Crisp thin-layered triangles filled with guava paste and cream cheese.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a baking sheet. Unroll the filo and cover with a barely damp cloth to keep it from drying out.
Dice the guava paste and mix the cheese with the zest. Divide both fillings into 12 portions for even distribution.
Brush the sheets lightly with butter and stack in pairs of 2. Cut into strips about 10 cm wide; place filling at one end of each strip.
Fold repeatedly into triangles along each strip, enclosing the filling. Make 12 pieces, brush with the remaining butter, and place on the sheet.
Bake for 22 to 28 minutes, until golden and crisp underneath. Cool on a rack for 20 minutes and refrigerate leftovers because of their cheese filling.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Filo baskets with mango and coconut cream
description: Crisp baskets filled with cooked coconut cream and fresh mango.
steps: Whisk the eggs, sugar, and cornstarch. Gradually add the hot coconut milk; return to the heat and stir until bubbling, maintaining a gentle boil for 1 minute.
Spread the cream in a shallow container, cover its surface, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours. Do not fill the baskets with warm cream.
Heat the oven to 180 °C. Cut the filo into 12 cm squares, brush with butter, and overlap 4 crossed layers in each cup of a 12-cup muffin pan.
Bake for 12 to 16 minutes, until the baskets are golden. Toast the coconut on another tray for 3 minutes, watching closely; cool both preparations for 30 minutes.
Divide the cold cream among the 12 baskets and top with diced mango and toasted coconut. Assemble shortly before serving and keep the filled pastries refrigerated.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Pumpkin and walnut filo spiral
description: A baked filo spiral filled with roasted pumpkin, walnuts, and cinnamon.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C and line a 24 cm round pan. Keep the filo covered with a barely damp cloth while working.
Mix the cold pumpkin with the walnuts, sugar, cornstarch, and cinnamon. Check that the purée is thick and does not release liquid.
Brush the sheets with butter and make groups of 2 layers. Distribute the filling in lines along the long edges and roll without wrapping too tightly.
Arrange the rolls in a spiral in the pan, starting at the center and joining the ends. Brush with the remaining butter.
Bake for 35 to 45 minutes, until the filo is golden and the filling thick and hot. Cool on a rack for 40 minutes before cutting into 10 servings.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Banana and peanut filo parcels
description: Small filo parcels with ripe banana, peanuts, and cinnamon.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a baking sheet. Keep the filo sheets covered so they do not crack when folded.
Finely dice the banana and mix with the chopped peanuts, sugar, cinnamon, and lime juice. Prepare the filling just before using it.
Cut filo rectangles measuring about 15 × 20 cm. Brush with butter and stack 2 layers per pastry; divide the filling to make 12 parcels.
Fold the short sides over the filling and roll from a long side. Place seam-side down and brush with the remaining butter.
Bake for 22 to 28 minutes, until the layers are golden and crisp. Cool on a rack for 20 minutes before eating because the banana retains heat.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Coconut and almond baklava with lime
description: A home-style layered filo, coconut, and almond pastry with light lime syrup.
steps: Boil the sugar, water, and lime juice for 6 minutes to make a syrup. Remove from the heat and cool while preparing the layers.
Heat the oven to 170 °C and brush a 20 × 20 cm pan with butter. Mix the almonds, coconut, and cinnamon.
Trim the filo to fit the pan. Layer half the sheets on the bottom, brushing each with butter; spread the nut mixture over them.
Cover with the remaining sheets, brushing each layer. Cut into 12 portions with a sharp knife before baking so the layers can be separated without breaking later.
Bake for 35 to 45 minutes, until the edges are golden too. Gradually pour the cold syrup over the hot pastry, distributing it along the cuts.
Let stand for at least 2 hours so the syrup absorbs before lifting out the portions. Store the pieces protected from moisture.
tips: Pour the syrup gradually so it enters between the layers without pooling on one side.

title: Mango and raisin filo strudel
description: Filo rolls with firm mango and raisins, with crumbs to absorb the fruit juices.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a baking sheet. Cut the mango into 1 cm cubes and mix with the raisins, sugar, cornstarch, and cinnamon.
Divide the filo sheets into 2 groups and keep unused sheets covered. Stack each group, brushing butter between the layers to form a sturdy rectangle.
Sprinkle the breadcrumbs over both rectangles and distribute the filling near a long edge, leaving room at the ends.
Fold the ends inward and roll up using the paper to help. Place the 2 rolls seam-side down and brush with the remaining butter.
Bake for 30 to 38 minutes, until the filo is golden and the filling juices bubble. Cool on a rack for 30 minutes and cut each roll into 6 servings.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Cheese and quince filo tartlets
description: Filo tartlets with ricotta, quince paste, and a baked filling.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C and prepare a 12-cup muffin pan. Keep the filo covered while cutting squares about 12 cm across.
Brush the squares with butter and overlap 4 crossed layers in each pan cup. Press gently to form the shells without tearing them.
Mix the ricotta, egg, sugar, and zest until combined. Finely dice the quince paste and divide it among the shells.
Spoon the ricotta mixture over the quince without filling to the brim. Brush the exposed filo edges with the remaining butter.
Bake for 22 to 28 minutes, until the layers are golden and the filling reaches 71 °C. Cool for 20 minutes, unmold, and refrigerate for storage.
tips: Cool as directed before cutting or filling to preserve the texture.

title: Guava flan
description: Milk custard blended with guava paste and topped with a thin layer of caramel.

ingredients.name: hot water for the water bath
ingredients.note: Approximate quantity; the water should reach halfway up the mold.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: For the custard mixture, separate from the caramel sugar.

steps: Heat the oven to 160 °C and prepare a 1.2-liter metal mold and a deep pan for the water bath.
Heat the caramel sugar with the measured water until amber; pour into the mold and use oven gloves to tilt it and coat the bottom.
Blend the guava paste cut into small cubes with the specified milk, eggs and the custard sugar until combined; let the foam settle before pouring over the caramel.
Place the mold in the pan and add hot water halfway up its sides; bake for 55 to 75 minutes, until the center reaches 82 °C and jiggles slightly.
Remove the mold from the water, let it cool for 20 minutes, and refrigerate covered for at least 6 hours before unmolding.
Run a thin knife around the edge and invert onto a rimmed plate to catch the caramel; keep refrigerated until serving.
tips: Cut the paste into small pieces so it blends without lumps.

title: Cocoa flan
description: A milk and unsweetened cocoa custard gently baked in a water bath.

ingredients.name: hot water for the water bath
ingredients.note: Approximate quantity; the water should reach halfway up the mold.

Run a thin knife around the edge and invert onto a rimmed plate to catch the caramel; keep refrigerated until serving.
tips: Sift the cocoa before blending to avoid small dry lumps.

description: Creamy custard made with already cooked sweet potato and a touch of cinnamon.

ingredients.name: cooked sweet potato purée
ingredients.note: Weight of the cooked, peeled, cooled sweet potato before starting.

title: Dulce de leche flan
description: Custard sweetened with dulce de leche and finished with amber caramel.

steps: Heat the oven to 160 °C and prepare a 1.2-liter metal mold and a deep pan for the water bath.
Heat the caramel sugar with the measured water until amber; pour into the mold and use oven gloves to tilt it and coat the bottom.
Blend the dulce de leche with the specified milk, eggs until combined; let the foam settle before pouring over the caramel.
Place the mold in the pan and add hot water halfway up its sides; bake for 55 to 75 minutes, until the center reaches 82 °C and jiggles slightly.
Remove the mold from the water, let it cool for 20 minutes, and refrigerate covered for at least 6 hours before unmolding.
Run a thin knife around the edge and invert onto a rimmed plate to catch the caramel; keep refrigerated until serving.
tips: The dulce de leche supplies the sweetness in the custard mixture, so no extra sugar is needed.

title: Orange and vanilla flan
description: A mild custard made with orange juice, milk, and vanilla.

ingredients.name: hot water for the water bath
ingredients.note: Approximate quantity; the water should reach halfway up the mold.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: For the custard mixture, separate from the caramel sugar.

steps: Heat the oven to 160 °C and prepare a 1.2-liter metal mold and a deep pan for the water bath.
Heat the caramel sugar with the measured water until amber; pour into the mold and use oven gloves to tilt it and coat the bottom.
Blend the orange juice, orange zest, and vanilla with the specified milk, eggs and the custard sugar until combined; let the foam settle before pouring over the caramel.
Place the mold in the pan and add hot water halfway up its sides; bake for 55 to 75 minutes, until the center reaches 82 °C and jiggles slightly.
Remove the mold from the water, let it cool for 20 minutes, and refrigerate covered for at least 6 hours before unmolding.
Run a thin knife around the edge and invert onto a rimmed plate to catch the caramel; keep refrigerated until serving.
tips: Grate only the colored layer of the washed peel to avoid bitterness.

title: Mango and coconut milk flan
description: Mango custard made with coconut milk and whole milk.

ingredients.name: hot water for the water bath
ingredients.note: Approximate quantity; the water should reach halfway up the mold.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: For the custard mixture, separate from the caramel sugar.

steps: Heat the oven to 160 °C and prepare a 1.2-liter metal mold and a deep pan for the water bath.
Heat the caramel sugar with the measured water until amber; pour into the mold and use oven gloves to tilt it and coat the bottom.
Blend the fiber-free mango flesh with the specified milk, eggs and the custard sugar until combined; let the foam settle before pouring over the caramel.
Place the mold in the pan and add hot water halfway up its sides; bake for 55 to 75 minutes, until the center reaches 82 °C and jiggles slightly.
Remove the mold from the water, let it cool for 20 minutes, and refrigerate covered for at least 6 hours before unmolding.
Run a thin knife around the edge and invert onto a rimmed plate to catch the caramel; keep refrigerated until serving.
tips: Strain the mango if the variety has coarse fibers.

title: Egg-free guava custard
description: Milk and guava paste custard thickened with cornstarch.
steps: Set aside some of the cold milk and stir the cornstarch into it until no lumps remain.
Blend the diced guava paste with the remaining specified liquids and sweetener until smooth.
Pour into a saucepan and heat over medium heat, stirring; add the cornstarch mixture just before boiling.
Cook at a gentle bubble for 2 minutes, whisking constantly, until thick and free of raw starch flavor.
Divide among small cups, cool for 20 minutes, and refrigerate covered for 3 hours; serve cold without leaving at room temperature.
tips: Guava paste is already sweet; taste your chosen brand before adding more sugar.

title: Coconut and lime zest custard
description: Egg-free coconut milk custard with finely grated lime zest.
steps: Set aside some of the cold milk and stir the cornstarch into it until no lumps remain.
Blend the coconut milk and lime zest with the remaining specified liquids and sweetener until smooth.
Pour into a saucepan and heat over medium heat, stirring; add the cornstarch mixture just before boiling.
Cook at a gentle bubble for 2 minutes, whisking constantly, until thick and free of raw starch flavor.
Divide among small cups, cool for 20 minutes, and refrigerate covered for 3 hours; serve cold without leaving at room temperature.
tips: Use finely grated zest from washed fruit and avoid the white pith.

title: Mamey custard
description: Creamy custard made with ripe mamey flesh and milk.
steps: Set aside some of the cold milk and stir the cornstarch into it until no lumps remain.
Blend the mamey and vanilla with the remaining specified liquids and sweetener until smooth.
Pour into a saucepan and heat over medium heat, stirring; add the cornstarch mixture just before boiling.
Cook at a gentle bubble for 2 minutes, whisking constantly, until thick and free of raw starch flavor.
Divide among small cups, cool for 20 minutes, and refrigerate covered for 3 hours; serve cold without leaving at room temperature.
tips: Remove all skin and the pit from the mamey before weighing the flesh.

title: Peanut and honey custard
description: Milk custard thickened with cornstarch and enriched with peanut butter and honey.
steps: Set aside some of the cold milk and stir the cornstarch into it until no lumps remain.
Blend the peanut butter with the remaining specified liquids and sweetener until smooth.
Pour into a saucepan and heat over medium heat, stirring; add the cornstarch mixture just before boiling.
Cook at a gentle bubble for 2 minutes, whisking constantly, until thick and free of raw starch flavor.
Divide among small cups, cool for 20 minutes, and refrigerate covered for 3 hours; serve cold without leaving at room temperature.
tips: Stir along the bottom while cooking to prevent the peanut butter from sticking.

title: Semolina cream with raisins
description: Sweet wheat semolina and milk cream with tender raisins.
steps: Check the raisins and place them in a saucepan with the milk, cinnamon stick, sugar, and salt.
Heat over medium heat until the milk steams; stir to dissolve the sugar without sticking.
Sprinkle in the semolina while whisking; reduce the heat when the mixture starts to thicken.
Cook gently for 8 minutes, stirring, until the semolina is tender and the raisins have plumped.
Remove the cinnamon and divide among bowls; serve warm, or cool and refrigerate if preparing ahead.
tips: Semolina thickens as it stands; remove it from the heat while it still falls slowly from the spoon.

title: Sweet rice pudding with cooked pineapple
description: Creamy rice pudding with separately cooked pineapple and cinnamon.

ingredients.name: peeled pineapple with the tough core removed

steps: Rinse the rice and place it in a pot with most of the water, the salt, and cinnamon; reserve a little water for the pineapple.
Simmer for 15 minutes; add the milk and two thirds of the sugar and cook for 25 minutes, stirring.
Dice the pineapple and cook with the reserved sugar and water for 15 minutes, until soft and its juice has reduced.
Check that the rice is tender and the milk is creamy; remove the cinnamon and divide among shallow containers.
Spoon the cooked pineapple on top, cool for 20 minutes, and refrigerate for 2 hours; serve cold.
tips: Cook the pineapple separately to control its liquid before serving it with the rice.

title: Coffee and cocoa rice pudding
description: Rice pudding with a bold coffee and unsweetened cocoa flavor.
steps: Rinse the rice and simmer with the water and salt for 15 minutes until it starts to soften.
Whisk the cocoa with a little cold milk until no lumps remain; set the mixture aside.
Add the remaining milk, coffee, and sugar to the rice; simmer for 20 minutes, stirring along the bottom.
Add the cocoa mixture and cook for 8 more minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is creamy.
Divide among bowls, cool for 20 minutes, and refrigerate for 2 hours; serve with a dessert spoon.
tips: Brew the coffee before adding it; do not put ground coffee beans directly into the pudding.

title: Pumpkin and white cheese pudding
description: Baked pudding made with cooked pumpkin and crumbled white cheese.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C and grease a deep 20 cm square baking dish with the specified butter.
Mix the cooled pumpkin purée with the milk and crumbled cheese, making sure no coarse fibers remain.
Beat the eggs and fold them into the lukewarm mixture with the specified sugar and flavorings until combined.
Pour into the dish and bake for 45 to 55 minutes, until the center reaches 80 °C and is no longer liquid when gently moved.
Cool for 20 minutes, refrigerate for 2 hours, and cut into portions; keep the remainder covered in the refrigerator.
tips: Drain the purée before weighing so the pudding does not turn watery.

title: Cooked cassava and coconut milk pudding
description: Previously cooked sweet cassava in a firm pudding with coconut milk and vanilla.

ingredients.name: cooked and drained commercial sweet cassava
ingredients.note: Use commercial sweet cassava already peeled, fully cooked, and with the central fiber removed; discard its previous cooking water.

steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C and grease a deep 20 cm square baking dish with the specified butter.
Blend the cooked, cooled cassava with the coconut milk until smooth and free of hard fibers.
Beat the eggs and fold them into the lukewarm mixture with the specified sugar and flavorings until combined.
Pour into the dish and bake for 45 to 55 minutes, until the center reaches 80 °C and is no longer liquid when gently moved.
Cool for 20 minutes, refrigerate for 2 hours, and cut into portions; keep the remainder covered in the refrigerator.
tips: This formula starts with fully cooked cassava; baking it here does not replace that earlier preparation.

title: Oat and banana pudding
description: Pudding made with milk-soaked oats, ripe bananas, and cinnamon.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C and grease a deep 20 cm square baking dish with the specified butter.
Mix the oats and milk and soak for 15 minutes; fold in the banana mashed with a fork.
Beat the eggs and fold them into the lukewarm mixture with the specified sugar and flavorings until combined.
Pour into the dish and bake for 45 to 55 minutes, until the center reaches 80 °C and is no longer liquid when gently moved.
Cool for 20 minutes, refrigerate for 2 hours, and cut into portions; keep the remainder covered in the refrigerator.
tips: Use dessert bananas, not raw cooking plantains, for a soft mixture.

title: Sweet pumpkin in cane molasses
description: Tender pumpkin pieces in a dark cane molasses and cinnamon syrup.
steps: Cut the peeled pumpkin into evenly sized 4 cm pieces so they cook at the same rate.
Mix the water, sugar, molasses, and cinnamon in a wide saucepan; simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Add the pumpkin in one layer and cook covered for 20 minutes, until easily pierced.
Uncover and reduce for 10 minutes, spooning syrup over the pumpkin without breaking it; add the lime juice.
Remove the cinnamon and serve warm; to serve cold, let cool briefly and keep in the refrigerator.
tips: Choose firm-fleshed pumpkin so it holds its shape in the syrup.

title: Creamy pineapple coconut sweet
description: A sweet of shredded coconut and cooked pineapple with a little milk.

ingredients.name: peeled pineapple with the tough core removed

steps: Grate or finely chop the pineapple and place in a saucepan with the water and half the sugar.
Simmer gently for 15 minutes, stirring, until the fruit is tender and its juice has reduced.
Add the coconut, milk, and remaining sugar; cook over low heat for 20 minutes, stirring along the bottom.
Add the vanilla and cook for 3 more minutes; remove when thick but still moist and creamy.
Divide among small containers, cool for 20 minutes, and refrigerate for 2 hours before serving.
tips: Use a spatula that reaches the corners of the saucepan well to prevent sticking.

title: Mango and passion fruit compote
description: Ripe mango cooked with passion fruit pulp for a sweet and tangy compote.
steps: Dice the mango and check that the passion fruit pulp is strained, without peel fragments or hard seeds.
Place the prepared fruit in a saucepan with the specified water and sugar; stir without crushing the pieces.
Simmer gently for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the fruit softens and the liquid reduces slightly.
Mash just a few cubes with the back of a spoon to thicken the compote, leaving the rest whole.
Divide among small containers, cool for 20 minutes, and refrigerate for 2 hours; serve cold with its own juices.
tips: Use ripe but firm mango so some pieces remain intact after cooking.

title: Papaya and orange compote
description: Papaya gently cooked with orange juice and sugar.
steps: Dice the papaya and mix the orange juice with the water; remove any remaining seeds.
Place the prepared fruit in a saucepan with the water and orange juice mixture and the sugar; stir without crushing the pieces.
Simmer gently for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the fruit softens and the liquid reduces slightly.
Stir carefully to keep the pieces intact and check that the fruit is tender before removing from the heat.
Divide among small containers, cool for 20 minutes, and refrigerate for 2 hours; serve cold with its own juices.
tips: Choose ripe, firm-fleshed papaya to avoid a completely broken-down compote.

title: Banana and cocoa compote
description: Cooked, mashed bananas with unsweetened cocoa and a little vanilla.
steps: Slice the bananas and whisk the cocoa into the cold water until no lumps remain.
Place the prepared fruit in a saucepan with the specified water and sugar; stir without crushing the pieces.
Simmer gently for 12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the fruit softens and the liquid reduces slightly.
Add the vanilla and mash the fruit with a fork into a thick cream with small pieces.
Divide among small containers, cool for 20 minutes, and refrigerate for 2 hours; serve cold with its own juices.
tips: This recipe uses dessert bananas; raw cooking plantains need different cooking times.

title: Apple and guava compote
description: Tender apples in a light sauce made with guava paste.
steps: Dice the apples and cut the guava paste into small pieces so it dissolves during cooking.
Place the prepared fruit in a saucepan with the specified water and sugar; stir without crushing the pieces.
Simmer gently for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the fruit softens and the liquid reduces slightly.
Mash any remaining guava paste against the side of the pot and stir until the sauce becomes smooth.
Divide among small containers, cool for 20 minutes, and refrigerate for 2 hours; serve cold with its own juices.
tips: Use apples that retain some firmness when cooked to contrast with the sauce.

title: Cheese-filled guavas with orange syrup
description: Guava halves cooked in orange syrup and filled with white cheese.
steps: Wash and peel the guavas; halve them and scoop out the seeds without breaking the walls of the halves.
Boil the water, orange juice, sugar, and cinnamon for 5 minutes in a wide saucepan.
Add the guava halves and simmer gently for 20 minutes, until tender but still holding their shape.
Remove the cinnamon, cool for 20 minutes, and refrigerate the guavas with their syrup for 2 hours.
Drain the halves lightly, fill with crumbled cheese, and serve with a little cold syrup.
tips: Medium, firm guavas are easier to hollow out than very ripe ones.

title: Oranges in cinnamon syrup
description: Peeled orange segments coated in a light cinnamon syrup.
steps: Separate the orange segments and remove thick membranes and seeds; work over a bowl to catch the juice.
Mix the water, sugar, cinnamon, and collected juice in a small saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook the syrup for 10 minutes to dissolve the sugar and infuse it with cinnamon.
Add the segments, cook for 2 minutes without stirring vigorously, and remove the cinnamon stick.
Cool for 20 minutes and refrigerate for 2 hours; serve the segments with a small amount of syrup.
tips: Remove thick white pith so it does not make the syrup bitter.

title: Grated pineapple sweet
description: Grated pineapple slowly cooked into a moist, finely textured sweet.

ingredients.name: peeled pineapple with the tough core removed

steps: Coarsely grate the pineapple over a bowl and keep all the juice it releases.
Place the flesh and juice in a saucepan with the water and sugar; stir and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered for 30 minutes, stirring frequently, until the pineapple is tender and the liquid has reduced.
Add the lime juice and cook for 5 more minutes; remove when moist but no longer surrounded by a pool of syrup.
Transfer to small containers, cool for 20 minutes, and refrigerate for 2 hours before serving.
tips: Stir especially often as the liquid reduces, because sugary fruit sticks easily.

title: Green mango in syrup
description: Green mango slices softened and cooked in lime syrup.
steps: Cut the peeled mango into thick slices; check for hard fragments from the pit.
Place in a saucepan with the water and simmer gently for 20 minutes until it starts to soften.
Add the sugar and stir gently to dissolve it without breaking the slices.
Cook uncovered for 20 more minutes, until the fruit is tender and the syrup is light; add the lime juice.
Cool for 20 minutes and refrigerate for 3 hours; serve small portions with some of the syrup.
tips: Green mango varies in tartness and firmness; cook longer if it still resists a fork.

title: Roasted sweet potato with coconut cream
description: Tender oven-roasted sweet potato served with a thick, sweet coconut cream.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C; wash and pierce the sweet potatoes and place them on a baking tray.
Roast for 45 to 60 minutes, until a knife enters without resistance; timing depends on thickness.
Dissolve the cornstarch in the cold water and heat the coconut milk with the sugar and cinnamon in a saucepan.
Add the dissolved cornstarch and simmer gently for 2 minutes, whisking, until a thick cream forms.
Split the sweet potatoes, remove the skins if desired, and divide the flesh with the hot cream to serve.
tips: Choose similarly sized sweet potatoes so they finish roasting at the same time.

title: Ripe plantains in orange sauce with raisins
description: Ripe plantains browned and simmered in orange juice with raisins.
steps: Cut the peeled ripe plantains into thick diagonal slices so they retain their shape.
Melt the butter in a wide skillet and brown the plantain for 4 minutes on each side.
Mix the orange juice, sugar, and cinnamon and carefully pour into the skillet; add the raisins.
Cover and cook over low heat for 18 minutes, until the plantain is completely tender.
Uncover and reduce for 4 minutes, spooning sauce over the slices; serve warm with the plumped raisins.
tips: The plantain should have very yellow skin with dark patches before peeling.

title: No-machine coffee and milk ice cream
description: Egg-free ice cream made with whipped cream, condensed milk, and cold coffee.

ingredients.name: pasteurized heavy whipping cream
ingredients.note: At least 35% fat; keep very cold.

steps: Chill the cream and a large bowl; prepare a lidded 1.5-liter freezer-safe container.
Mix the condensed milk with the cold coffee and vanilla until no dark streaks remain.
Whip the cold cream to soft peaks; fold in the sweet mixture in several additions.
Pour into the container, smooth, and cover; freeze for at least 6 hours until firm. This method requires no machine.
Let soften for 5 minutes before scooping; immediately return the remainder to the freezer.
tips: Add the coffee completely cold to preserve the air in the whipped cream.

title: No-machine chocolate and peanut ice cream
description: Cream and cocoa ice cream blended with peanut butter, without raw egg.

ingredients.name: pasteurized heavy whipping cream
ingredients.note: At least 35% fat; keep very cold.

steps: Chill the cream and a large bowl; prepare a lidded 1.5-liter freezer-safe container.
Whisk the cocoa into the cold milk and mix with the condensed milk and peanut butter until smooth.
Whip the cold cream to soft peaks; fold in the sweet mixture in several additions.
Pour into the container, smooth, and cover; freeze for at least 6 hours until firm. This method requires no machine.
Let soften for 5 minutes before scooping; immediately return the remainder to the freezer.
tips: Mix the cocoa with the liquid first to avoid pockets of dry powder.

title: No-machine mango and yogurt ice cream
description: Ripe mango, yogurt, and cream frozen with periodic stirring to reduce ice crystals.
steps: Chill the mango, yogurt, and cream; cut the mango into pieces and remove coarse fibers before blending.
Blend the prepared fruit with the remaining ingredients until smooth; keep the mixture cold before beginning to freeze.
Pour into a shallow lidded metal container and freeze; an ice-cream machine is not needed.
During the first 3 hours, stir and whisk vigorously every 45 minutes, scraping the edges and bottom to break up crystals.
Freeze for 3 more hours until firm; let soften for 5 minutes to serve and keep the remainder frozen.
tips: Use thick yogurt and cold cream to give body to the fruit mixture.

title: No-machine mamey and vanilla ice cream
description: Ripe mamey flesh blended with milk, cream, and vanilla, without egg.
steps: Remove all skin and the pit from the mamey, weigh the flesh, and chill it with the milk and cream before mixing.
Blend the prepared fruit with the remaining ingredients until smooth; keep the mixture cold before beginning to freeze.
Pour into a shallow lidded metal container and freeze; an ice-cream machine is not needed.
During the first 3 hours, stir and whisk vigorously every 45 minutes, scraping the edges and bottom to break up crystals.
Freeze for 3 more hours until firm; let soften for 5 minutes to serve and keep the remainder frozen.
tips: Scrape frozen edges thoroughly during each stirring session for a more even texture.

title: No-machine cooked pineapple and coconut ice cream
description: Pineapple first cooked with sugar, then blended with coconut milk and cream.

ingredients.name: peeled pineapple with the tough core removed

steps: Chop the pineapple and cook with the sugar and water for 15 minutes; cool for 20 minutes and refrigerate for 1 hour before combining with the remaining ingredients.
Blend the prepared fruit with the remaining ingredients until smooth; keep the mixture cold before beginning to freeze.
Pour into a shallow lidded metal container and freeze; an ice-cream machine is not needed.
During the first 3 hours, stir and whisk vigorously every 45 minutes, scraping the edges and bottom to break up crystals.
Freeze for 3 more hours until firm; let soften for 5 minutes to serve and keep the remainder frozen.
tips: The pineapple base must be cold before adding the cream.

title: No-machine guava sorbet
description: Sorbet made with seedless guava pulp and a touch of lime.
steps: Heat the water with the sugar and simmer gently for 3 minutes until fully dissolved.
Cool the syrup for 20 minutes and refrigerate for 1 hour before combining it with the fruit.
Mix the guava pulp and lime juice with the cold syrup until evenly blended; transfer to a shallow container.
Freeze for 3 hours, stirring every 45 minutes and scraping the edges; when slushy, blend briefly to smooth it.
Freeze covered for another 3 hours; let soften for 5 minutes before serving. No ice-cream machine is needed.
tips: Strain the pulp before measuring to keep hard seeds out of the sorbet.

title: No-machine passion fruit sorbet
description: A boldly flavored sorbet of strained passion fruit, water, and light syrup.
steps: Heat the water with the sugar and simmer gently for 3 minutes until fully dissolved.
Cool the syrup for 20 minutes and refrigerate for 1 hour before combining it with the fruit.
Mix the strained passion fruit pulp with the cold syrup until evenly blended; transfer to a shallow container.
Freeze for 3 hours, stirring every 45 minutes and scraping the edges; when slushy, blend briefly to smooth it.
Freeze covered for another 3 hours; let soften for 5 minutes before serving. No ice-cream machine is needed.
tips: Check the pulp before starting: some brands contain added sugar and need a different formulation.

title: No-machine pink grapefruit sorbet
description: A pink grapefruit juice sorbet without peel or membranes.
steps: Heat the water with the sugar and simmer gently for 3 minutes until fully dissolved.
Cool the syrup for 20 minutes and refrigerate for 1 hour before combining it with the fruit.
Mix the strained grapefruit juice with the cold syrup until evenly blended; transfer to a shallow container.
Freeze for 3 hours, stirring every 45 minutes and scraping the edges; when slushy, blend briefly to smooth it.
Freeze covered for another 3 hours; let soften for 5 minutes before serving. No ice-cream machine is needed.
tips: Avoid pressing the peel excessively so the sorbet does not become too bitter.

title: Banana and peanut ice pops
description: Ice pops made with ripe bananas, milk, and peanut butter, sweetened with honey.
steps: Peel and weigh the bananas and slice them; stir the peanut butter to incorporate any separated oil.
Blend the prepared base with the remaining ingredients until smooth, without large pieces that would make filling the molds difficult.
Divide among 12 ice-pop molds of 100 ml each, leaving a little room at the top for expansion.
Insert the sticks and freeze for at least 6 hours until the ice pops are completely firm.
Briefly run warm water over the outside of the molds and unmold; keep the remaining ice pops well wrapped in the freezer.
tips: Use ripe bananas so they blend easily and provide a creamier texture.

title: Yogurt and guava ice pops
description: Creamy yogurt ice pops with guava paste dissolved in milk.
steps: Heat the milk with the chopped guava paste for 5 minutes, stirring; cool for 20 minutes and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Blend the prepared base with the remaining ingredients until smooth, without large pieces that would make filling the molds difficult.
Divide among 12 ice-pop molds of 100 ml each, leaving a little room at the top for expansion.
Insert the sticks and freeze for at least 6 hours until the ice pops are completely firm.
