Briefly run warm water over the outside of the molds and unmold; keep the remaining ice pops well wrapped in the freezer.
tips: The guava base should be cold before adding the yogurt.

title: Coffee and milk ice pops
description: Milk and brewed coffee ice pops sweetened with sugar.
steps: Dissolve the sugar in the hot coffee, add the vanilla, and cool for 20 minutes; refrigerate for 1 hour before combining with the milk.
Blend the prepared base with the remaining ingredients until smooth, without large pieces that would make filling the molds difficult.
Divide among 12 ice-pop molds of 100 ml each, leaving a little room at the top for expansion.
Insert the sticks and freeze for at least 6 hours until the ice pops are completely firm.
Briefly run warm water over the outside of the molds and unmold; keep the remaining ice pops well wrapped in the freezer.
tips: Brew the coffee before measuring and keep the grounds out of the ice pops.

title: Watermelon and mint ice pops
description: Seedless watermelon ice pops with lime juice and fresh mint.
steps: Wash and dry the mint; cut the chilled watermelon and remove all hard seeds before weighing the flesh.
Blend the prepared base with the remaining ingredients until smooth, without large pieces that would make filling the molds difficult.
Divide among 12 ice-pop molds of 100 ml each, leaving a little room at the top for expansion.
Insert the sticks and freeze for at least 6 hours until the ice pops are completely firm.
Briefly run warm water over the outside of the molds and unmold; keep the remaining ice pops well wrapped in the freezer.
tips: Use tender mint leaves and discard thick stems before blending.

title: Mango and yogurt gelatin
description: A chilled mango and yogurt dessert set with unflavored powdered gelatin.

ingredients.name: unflavored powdered gelatin
ingredients.note: Unflavored powdered animal gelatin; weigh it in grams, not a sweetened gelatin mix or agar.

steps: Sprinkle the gelatin over 100 ml of the cold water and let bloom for 5 minutes without excessive stirring.
Heat the remaining water with the sugar until dissolved; remove from the heat and add the bloomed gelatin.
Stir for 2 minutes until no gelatin granules remain; do not bring the mixture back to a boil.
Blend the mango and yogurt; mix a portion with the lukewarm gelatin, then gradually add the rest to avoid lumps.
Divide among 8 small glasses of 150 ml, refrigerate for at least 6 hours, and serve when the center is set.
tips: Avoid mixing hot gelatin directly into a large quantity of very cold yogurt.

title: Guava and milk gelatin
description: Guava paste dissolved in milk and set as a chilled dessert.

ingredients.name: unflavored powdered gelatin
ingredients.note: Unflavored powdered animal gelatin; weigh it in grams, not a sweetened gelatin mix or agar.

steps: Sprinkle the gelatin over 100 ml of the cold water and let bloom for 5 minutes in a small bowl.
Chop the guava paste and heat with the milk and remaining water for 6 minutes, stirring until the pieces dissolve.
Remove from the heat and add the bloomed gelatin; stir for 2 minutes until no visible granules remain.
Pour into a 1.5-liter mold and cool for 20 minutes before covering and refrigerating.
Refrigerate for at least 6 hours; unmold carefully or serve portions directly from the container.
tips: The guava paste provides sweetness, so a commercially sweetened gelatin mix is not needed.

title: Orange and carrot gelatin
description: Orange and carrot juice gelatin with a firm texture for serving in small glasses.

ingredients.name: unflavored powdered gelatin
ingredients.note: Unflavored powdered animal gelatin; weigh it in grams, not a sweetened gelatin mix or agar.

steps: Sprinkle the gelatin over 100 ml of the cold water and let bloom for 5 minutes; strain the orange juice.
Heat the remaining water with the sugar until dissolved; remove from the heat before adding the gelatin.
Add the bloomed gelatin and stir for 2 minutes until the liquid is free of granules.
Gradually mix with the orange and carrot juices, stirring to distribute the color and gelatin evenly.
Divide among 8 small glasses of 150 ml and refrigerate for at least 6 hours, until set in the center.
tips: Use juices without large pieces for an evenly textured gelatin dessert.

title: Cooked papaya gelatin
description: A papaya dessert in which the fruit is boiled first so the gelatin can set.

ingredients.name: unflavored powdered gelatin
ingredients.note: Unflavored powdered animal gelatin; weigh it in grams, not a sweetened gelatin mix or agar.

steps: Reserve 120 ml of the cold water to bloom the gelatin for 5 minutes; dice the papaya finely.
Boil the fruit with the remaining water and sugar for 10 minutes; this preliminary step prevents its enzymes from stopping the set.
Blend the cooked fruit and remove from the heat; once bubbling stops, add the bloomed gelatin and stir until dissolved.
Add the lime juice and divide among 8 glasses of 180 ml; cool for 20 minutes before covering.
Refrigerate for at least 6 hours and serve cold, checking that the center is set before bringing to the table.
tips: Do not add raw papaya to this mixture after cooking.

title: No-bake coconut and guava balls
description: Chilled bites of guava paste, coconut, and cream cheese, rolled in shredded coconut.
steps: Dice the guava paste finely and process with the cream cheese and milk until smooth.
Reserve some coconut for coating; mix the remainder with the powdered milk and guava mixture.
Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour so the coconut absorbs moisture and the mixture becomes workable.
Divide into 24 portions, shape into balls with clean hands, and roll in the reserved coconut.
Refrigerate for 30 more minutes before serving; keep covered and chilled because they contain dairy.
tips: If the mixture is sticky, chill it longer before shaping instead of adding unmeasured ingredients.

title: Cocoa, peanut, and date truffles
description: No-bake bites made with soft dates, roasted peanuts, and cocoa.
steps: Pour the hot water over the dates and soften for 10 minutes; check that no pits remain.
Process the peanuts into fine crumbs without going so far that they turn into butter.
Add the dates with their water, vanilla, and half the cocoa; process until the mixture holds together when pressed.
Divide into 20 portions and shape into balls; lightly coat with the remaining cocoa.
Refrigerate covered for 1 hour before serving to firm them up; keep the remainder in the refrigerator.
tips: The peanuts should be roasted and cool before processing for better texture control.

title: Cheese cups with mango and honey
description: Chilled white cheese and yogurt cream with diced mango and honey.
steps: Drain and crumble the white cheese; check that the mango is peeled and free of hard pit fragments.
Blend the cheese, yogurt, honey, and lime juice until smooth, scraping the sides of the container.
Dice the mango finely and divide half among 6 glasses of 200 ml.
Add the cheese cream and finish with the remaining mango; cover each glass without crushing the fruit.
Refrigerate for 2 hours and serve cold; keep the glasses refrigerated until ready to eat.
tips: A mild, lightly salted cheese lets the mango and honey stand out.

title: Fruit cup with vanilla custard
description: Mango, papaya, and pineapple with cooked, chilled vanilla custard.

ingredients.name: peeled pineapple with the tough core removed

steps: Whisk the yolks, cornstarch, sugar, and 100 ml of the cold milk until smooth.
Heat the remaining milk with the vanilla; gradually whisk into the yolks and return everything to the saucepan.
Cook while stirring until thick and above 82 °C; maintain a very gentle bubble for 1 minute to cook the starch.
Transfer the custard to a shallow container, cool for 20 minutes, and refrigerate for 2 hours; dice the cleaned fruit.
Divide the fruit and cold custard among 6 glasses of 300 ml and serve immediately, keeping any remainder refrigerated.
tips: Assemble the cups shortly before serving so the fruit does not release too much liquid onto the custard.

title: Mango with Whipped Cream
description: Ripe mango chunks with lightly whipped cream: a fresh, simple, no-bake dessert.

ingredients.name: powdered sugar
ingredients.note: Optional; adjust to the sweetness of the mango.

steps: Chill the bowl and beaters in the refrigerator for 10 minutes while preparing the mango. Keep the whipping cream very cold.
Wash and peel the mangoes and remove their pits. Weigh 600 g of flesh and cut it into chunks measuring 1 to 2 cm.
Pour the cold cream into the chilled bowl and add the sugar if desired. Whip until thickened to soft peaks; it should stay light and creamy.
Divide the mango among 4 glasses or bowls. Spoon the whipped cream on top and finish each serving with a few reserved mango chunks.
Cover and refrigerate the glasses for 20 minutes, then serve the dessert well chilled. Keep any unserved portions in the refrigerator.
tips: Use ripe but firm mango so the chunks keep their shape.
Stop whipping as soon as soft peaks form: the cream should stay fluffy and never become grainy.

title: Cuban hallacas (hayacas) in banana leaves
description: Fresh-corn parcels with sofrito and pork cracklings, wrapped in banana leaves and simmered until firm.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 200 ml for the corn and 4000 ml for cooking; add more hot water as needed.

steps: Wash the leaves, remove tough stems and soften the leaves in hot water. Drain them and prepare kitchen string to secure the parcels.
Grind the corn with 200 ml of water to a thick paste. Finely chop the pork cracklings and set them aside.
Cook the chopped onion, bell pepper and garlic in the lard for 6 minutes. Add the tomatoes and cracklings and cook for another 3 minutes.
Combine the ground corn, sofrito, cornmeal and salt. Rest for 10 minutes; the mixture should be thick and moist, without separated liquid.
Divide the mixture into 12 portions on the leaves. Fold the sides and ends into closed parcels and tie them without tightening too much.
Cover the parcels with the remaining 4000 ml of water and simmer gently for 60 to 75 minutes. Add hot water whenever the level drops.
Open a hayaca and check that the dough is firm and pulls away from the leaf. Rest for 10 minutes and serve 2 per portion, removing leaves and string.
tips: The leaves are wrappers only and must be removed before eating.
You can also find this recipe under hayacas, hallacas, ayacas or tamales; this home-style version uses pork cracklings.

title: Cassava Croquettes
description: Oblong cooked-cassava croquettes with garlic and parsley, soft inside with a crisp golden coating.

ingredients.name: frying oil
ingredients.note: Working quantity; reserve 30 ml for the sofrito.

steps: Remove any remaining peel from the cassava and cut it into chunks. Boil in the water for 25 to 35 minutes until very tender; discard the water and remove the fibrous core.
Finely chop the onion and garlic and cook them in the reserved 30 ml of oil for 6 minutes. Mash the hot cassava until no hard pieces remain.
Mix the mash with the sofrito, parsley, salt and pepper. Cool for 10 minutes, then mix in 1 egg to make a uniform dough.
Shape 16 oblong croquettes and place them apart on a tray. Refrigerate for 30 minutes so the mixture firms up.
Beat the remaining egg in a shallow dish. Coat each croquette lightly in flour, then dip in egg and cover completely with breadcrumbs.
Heat the remaining oil to 175 °C and fry in small batches for 4 to 5 minutes until golden and 71 °C in the center. Drain on a rack and serve 4 croquettes per portion.
tips: Drain the cassava thoroughly before mashing so the dough can be shaped.
Keep the croquettes refrigerated until frying and avoid crowding the pan.

title: Snapper Fish Soup
description: Tender snapper pieces with potatoes and carrots in a light fish broth with tomato and sofrito, finished with parsley.

ingredients.name: boneless snapper fillets
ingredients.note: Skin on or off; any retained skin must be thoroughly scaled.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: Adjust for the saltiness of the stock.

steps: If the snapper is frozen, thaw it in the refrigerator beforehand. Check the fillets, remove any bones, pat dry with paper towels and cut into pieces measuring 3 to 4 cm; keep refrigerated.
Cut the potatoes into 2 cm cubes and the carrots into thin rounds. Finely chop the onion, bell pepper and garlic.
Heat the oil over medium heat and cook the onion and bell pepper for 6 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute; add the tomatoes and cook for another 5 minutes.
Add the stock, potatoes, carrots, salt and pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 15 to 18 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Add the snapper and simmer very gently for 6 to 8 minutes, until the center of the thickest pieces reaches 63 °C and the flesh flakes easily. Gently move the pan to avoid breaking up the fish.
Add the parsley, taste the broth and adjust the salt. Divide the fish, vegetables and broth among 4 bowls and serve hot.
tips: Add the fish once the potatoes and carrots are tender so the pieces hold their shape.
The broth should stay light with a gentle tomato color; avoid a vigorous boil after adding the snapper.

title: Mullet Fish Soup
description: Mullet pieces with potatoes and pumpkin in a golden fish broth with sofrito, cilantro and a touch of lemon.

ingredients.name: boneless mullet fillets
ingredients.note: Known as lisa, liza or mújol in Spanish; skin on or off, with any retained skin thoroughly scaled.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: Adjust for the saltiness of the stock.

steps: If the mullet is frozen, thaw it in the refrigerator beforehand. Check the fillets and remove any bones; if retaining the skin, make sure it is free of scales. Pat dry and cut into pieces measuring 3 to 4 cm; keep refrigerated.
Cut the potatoes and pumpkin into 2 cm cubes. Finely chop the onion, bell pepper and garlic.
Heat the oil over medium heat and cook the onion and bell pepper for 6 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 more minute without browning it too much.
Pour in the stock and add the potatoes, pumpkin, salt and pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 15 to 18 minutes, until both vegetables are tender and the broth turns golden.
Add the mullet and simmer very gently for 6 to 8 minutes, until the center of the thickest pieces reaches 63 °C and the flesh flakes easily. Avoid vigorous stirring.
Remove from the heat, add the cilantro and the 30 ml of lemon juice, and check the salt. Divide among 4 bowls and serve hot with plenty of broth.
tips: The pumpkin adds color and softness to the broth; cut evenly sized pieces so they cook at the same time as the potatoes.
You can also find this preparation as lisa, liza or mújol soup; use clean fillets and check for bones before cooking.

title: Breaded Shrimp with Garlic, Onion and Lemon
description: Large shrimp briefly marinated with garlic, onion and lemon, then breaded and fried until golden and crisp.

ingredients.name: large raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
ingredients.note: Clean weight, with shells and digestive tracts removed.

ingredients.name: frying oil
ingredients.note: Working quantity; not all of it is consumed.

steps: If the shrimp are frozen, thaw them in the refrigerator beforehand. Check that they are peeled and deveined, pat dry with paper towels and keep refrigerated.
Grate the onion and crush the garlic. Mix them with the 30 ml of lemon juice and the salt; add the shrimp, cover and marinate for 15 minutes in the refrigerator.

Lift the shrimp out of the marinade, drain thoroughly and remove large pieces of garlic and onion and excess liquid. Gently pat the surface dry with paper towels and discard the marinade that contacted the raw shrimp.
Prepare 3 shallow dishes: one with flour, one with beaten eggs and one with breadcrumbs.
Coat each shrimp in flour and shake off the excess, then dip in egg and cover with breadcrumbs, pressing gently. Place on a tray and refrigerate for 10 minutes to set the coating.
Heat the oil to 175 °C. Fry a small batch for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until golden and 63 °C in the center. The flesh must be firm, pearly and completely opaque.
Repeat for about 3 batches, approximately 12 minutes of frying in total, letting the oil return to 175 °C between batches. Keep the unfried shrimp refrigerated.
Drain on a rack and serve immediately to preserve the crisp coating.
tips: Remove excess liquid and large pieces of marinade before breading so the coating sticks and browns evenly.
The brief marinade adds flavor; complete cooking during frying and check the centers of the largest shrimp.

title: Cuban caldosa with corn
description: A thick chicken, corn and root vegetable stew, with some vegetables mashed to give the broth body.

ingredients.name: peeled commercially sold sweet cassava
ingredients.note: Boil separately and discard the cooking water.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 1800 ml for the caldosa and 1800 ml to boil the cassava separately; add more hot water if needed.

steps: Boil the peeled, washed and cut cassava in a separate pot with 1800 ml of water for 30 to 40 minutes, until tender. Drain, discard the cooking water and remove the fibrous core.
Meanwhile, sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the tomatoes, cumin and oregano; stir for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken, salt, pepper and the other 1800 ml of water. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook with the lid partly open for 20 minutes.
Add the peeled, diced malanga and plantain, along with the corn cob cut into 4 rounds. Cook for 20 minutes without letting the broth dry out.
Add the pumpkin and cook for 15 to 20 minutes, until all the root vegetables are very tender. Check that the center of the chicken reaches at least 74 °C.
Remove the chicken and shred it. Mash some malanga and pumpkin into the broth; add the cooked cassava and shredded chicken, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the lime juice, adjust the consistency with hot water and rest for 5 minutes. Serve in deep bowls, dividing the corn so that each serving has a round.
tips: This version thickens by mashing some vegetables; family caldosa recipes can vary in meat, vegetables and texture.
Cook the cassava separately; use only commercially sold sweet cassava and do not add its cooking water to the broth.

title: Savory cornmeal soup with pork
description: A savory, spoonable cornmeal soup with pork, sofrito and lime, cooked to a thick soup consistency.

ingredients.name: fine yellow cornmeal
ingredients.note: Uncooked; not cornstarch or nixtamalized masa harina.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 300 ml for the pork, 300 ml cold to mix with the cornmeal and 900 ml to complete the soup; add more if needed.

steps: Cut the pork loin into 1 cm cubes and season with the salt, pepper and cumin. Chop the onion, bell pepper and garlic.
Heat the oil in a heavy-bottomed pot and brown the pork for 5 minutes. Add the onion and bell pepper and cook for another 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, oregano and tomato sauce; stir for 2 minutes. Add 300 ml of water and cook, covered, over low heat for 15 minutes.
In a bowl, mix the cornmeal with 300 ml of cold water until smooth. Add the remaining 900 ml of water to the pot and bring to a gentle simmer.
Pour in the cornmeal mixture slowly while stirring. Cook over low heat for 25 to 35 minutes, stirring frequently and scraping the bottom to prevent sticking.
Check that the cornmeal is soft with no gritty texture and the pork reaches at least 63 °C. Add hot water gradually if it becomes too thick; it should remain spoonable.
Remove from the heat, add the lime juice and rest for 5 minutes before serving. Stir again and divide among deep bowls while it retains its soupy consistency.
tips: This home-style adaptation echoes the idea of a corn soup such as pozole, but uses fine cornmeal and has a different texture; it is not presented as traditional pozole.
Cornmeal thickens as it rests. Add hot water and stir to restore the soup consistency.
Coarsely ground cornmeal may need more time and liquid; this recipe is calculated for uncooked fine cornmeal.

title: Mixed lettuce, radish and egg salad
description: Crisp lettuce with radishes, cucumber and hard-boiled eggs, dressed with lime and mustard.
steps: Rinse the lettuce, radishes and cucumber under running water; dry the lettuce thoroughly so the dressing clings.
Tear the lettuce by hand and cut the cucumber into half-moons; slice the radishes as thinly as possible.
Cut each hard-boiled egg into quarters with a clean knife and set them aside while preparing the vegetables.
Whisk the oil with the lime juice, mustard and salt until the dressing is smooth and slightly thickened.
Toss the lettuce, cucumber and radishes with the dressing; divide among plates and arrange the egg quarters on top.
tips: Add the eggs last to keep the yolks intact and the lettuce crisp.

title: Cabbage, apple and celery salad
description: Finely sliced cabbage with red apple and celery in a creamy yogurt and lime dressing.
steps: Remove any damaged outer cabbage leaves; rinse the remaining cabbage, apple and celery stalks.
Slice the cabbage into very fine shreds and the celery into small slices; place them in a large bowl.
Cut the unpeeled apple into thin matchsticks and immediately toss it with the lime juice.
Whisk the yogurt with the oil and salt; stir it through the cabbage and add the apple with its juice.
Mix gently, cover and refrigerate for 15 minutes; stir again before dividing the salad into servings.
tips: Use a firm apple so it retains its texture after chilling.

title: Shrimp, avocado and grapefruit salad
description: Cooked shrimp with fresh grapefruit, avocado and lettuce leaves in a gentle citrus dressing.
steps: Keep the cooked shrimp refrigerated while preparing the vegetables and drain any accumulated liquid.
Rinse and dry the lettuce; slice the onion very thinly and arrange both on a wide serving platter.
Separate the grapefruit segments without membranes or seeds; collect any juice released while cutting in a small bowl.
Whisk the oil, lime juice and salt with the collected grapefruit juice; cut the avocado into large cubes.
Arrange the shrimp, grapefruit and avocado over the leaves; drizzle with the dressing and serve immediately.
tips: Use ready-to-eat shrimp and firm grapefruit so the salad does not become watery.

title: Chicken, pineapple and bell pepper salad
description: Cooked chicken strips with pineapple, colorful bell peppers and lettuce in an orange vinaigrette.
steps: Rinse the bell peppers and lettuce; dry the leaves thoroughly and remove the seeds and white ribs from the peppers.
Cut the peppers into thin strips and the pineapple into small cubes, removing any remaining fibrous core.
Cut the cooked chilled chicken into strips; combine it in a bowl with the pineapple and peppers.
Whisk the orange juice with the lime juice, oil and salt; pour over the mixture and toss gently.
Divide the torn lettuce among plates and spoon the chicken mixture on top; serve without letting it stand.
tips: Chilled boneless roast chicken works well; weigh only the ready-to-eat meat.

title: Roasted eggplant, tomato and chickpea salad
description: Oven-roasted eggplant with chickpeas, fresh tomato and parsley in a warm salad.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C; rinse the eggplant and cut it into cubes about 2 cm wide, keeping the skin.
Toss the eggplant with 2 tablespoons of the oil and half the salt; spread it in a single layer on a baking tray.
Roast for 30 minutes, turning halfway through, until browned and tender; allow to cool slightly for 10 minutes.
Rinse and dice the tomato; chop the onion and parsley and mix them with the well-drained chickpeas.
Whisk the remaining oil with lime juice, cumin and remaining salt; toss with the chickpeas and warm eggplant.
tips: Leave space between the cubes on the tray so the eggplant browns and retains its shape.

title: Quinoa, cucumber and orange salad
description: Fluffy quinoa with cucumber, orange and sweet pepper, dressed with lime and cilantro.
steps: Rinse the quinoa in a fine sieve until the water runs clear; drain it and place it in a saucepan.
Add the water and half the salt; bring to a boil, cover and cook over low heat for 18 minutes or until the liquid is absorbed.
Fluff the grains with a fork and spread them in a wide dish; allow to cool slightly for 20 minutes.
Rinse the cucumber, sweet pepper and cilantro; dice the cucumber and pepper finely and cut up the orange segments.
Whisk the oil, lime juice and remaining salt; toss with the quinoa, vegetables and cilantro, then gently fold in the orange.
tips: This is a contemporary home-style combination; the quinoa should be fluffy before adding the fruit.

title: Grilled zucchini, cheese and tomato salad
description: Golden grilled zucchini slices with tomato, white cheese and fresh basil.
steps: Rinse the zucchini, tomatoes and basil; dry everything and cut the zucchini into evenly thick slices.
Brush the slices with 1 tablespoon of the oil and heat a griddle or wide frying pan over medium-high heat.
Brown the zucchini in batches for about 12 minutes in total, turning to mark both sides; allow to cool slightly for 10 minutes.
Halve the tomatoes and cut the cheese into cubes; mix the remaining oil with the vinegar, salt and pepper.
Arrange the zucchini with the tomatoes and cheese; add the dressing and finish with hand-torn basil.
tips: Allow the zucchini to cool slightly so the cheese keeps its shape when mixed in.

title: Pasta, broccoli and cooked ham salad
description: Short pasta with broccoli, cooked ham and carrot in a mild yogurt dressing.
steps: Rinse the broccoli florets and carrot; cut the broccoli into small bite-sized pieces and grate the carrot.
Bring the water to a boil with half the salt and cook the pasta according to its package; add the broccoli for the last 3 minutes.
Drain the pasta and broccoli, cool briefly under cold running water and drain thoroughly; dice the ham.
Whisk the yogurt with the oil, lime juice and remaining salt; mix with the pasta, broccoli, ham and grated carrot.
Cover the bowl and refrigerate for 20 minutes; stir before serving to distribute the dressing.
tips: Drain the pasta well before adding the yogurt so the dressing stays creamy.

title: Watermelon, cucumber and white cheese salad
description: Fresh watermelon with crisp cucumber, white cheese and mint, finished with lime.
steps: Rinse the cucumber and mint; dry both carefully and remove any remaining watermelon seeds.
Cut the watermelon into large cubes and drain briefly in a colander to remove loose juice.
Cut the cucumber into half-moons and the cheese into small cubes; strip the mint leaves from their stems.
Whisk the oil with the lime juice and pour it over the watermelon and cucumber; toss with a broad spoon.
Arrange on a platter, add the cheese and mint and serve immediately to keep the fruit firm.
tips: Taste the cheese before adding salt: many varieties already provide enough for the salad.

title: Sardine, potato and bell pepper salad
description: Boiled potatoes with canned sardines, roasted pepper and parsley in a lime dressing.
steps: Cut the peeled potatoes into medium cubes and place them in a saucepan with the water; bring to a gentle boil.
Cook the potatoes for about 20 minutes until easily pierced with a fork; drain and allow to cool slightly for 15 minutes.
Cut the roasted pepper into strips and thinly slice the onion; rinse and chop the fresh parsley.
Whisk the oil with the lime juice and salt; toss with the warm potatoes, pepper, onion and parsley.
Break the sardines into large pieces, remove any bones you prefer and arrange them on top without mashing them.
tips: Add the sardines last so their pieces remain recognizable and do not break into the dressing.

title: Coconut milkshake
description: Tender coconut flesh blended with cold milk and coconut water into a creamy white drink.
steps: Remove any brown skin left on the tender coconut flesh and cut the flesh into small pieces.
Place tender coconut flesh, cold pasteurized milk, pasteurized coconut water in the blender jar; work in batches if necessary.
Blend for 45 seconds, until the fruit and liquid are thoroughly combined and the mixture is smooth.
Pour the drink into a pitcher and stir with a spoon to check that no large pieces remain.
Divide the ice among 4 glasses, pour the drink over it and stir gently before bringing it to the table.
tips: Tender coconut blends more smoothly than dry, very hard flesh.
If fibers remain, strain before pouring the drink over the ice.

title: Chilled sugarcane juice
description: Unfermented sugarcane juice served chilled over ice, prepared at home with ready-extracted guarapo.
steps: Check that the sugarcane juice is a food-grade, unfermented beverage and read the storage instructions on the package.
Chill the guarapo in the refrigerator until serving; use ready-extracted juice, not pieces of sugarcane.
Gently shake the closed package or stir the juice in a clean pitcher to mix in any natural sediment.
Divide the ice among 4 clean glasses, leaving enough space to pour the drink without spilling.
Pour the guarapo over the ice and stir gently; immediately return any remaining packaged juice to the refrigerator.
tips: Sugarcane is pressed with a cane mill; do not put its fibrous stalks into a household blender.
This version contains no alcohol and does not require fermenting the juice.

title: Mango juice
description: Ripe mango blended with cold water for a smooth drink with the golden color of the fruit.
steps: Wash and peel the mangoes, remove the flesh from the pit and weigh the required amount before cutting it.
Place ripe mango flesh, cold water in the blender jar; work in batches if necessary.
Blend for 45 seconds, until the fruit and liquid are thoroughly combined and the mixture is smooth.
Pour the drink into a pitcher and stir with a spoon to check that no large pieces remain.
Divide the ice among 4 glasses, pour the drink over it and stir gently before bringing it to the table.
tips: Weigh the edible portion of the fruit and remove hard seeds as directed in the preparation steps.
Serve freshly prepared; if it stands for a few minutes, stir the pitcher before pouring.

title: Orange juice
description: Home-squeezed oranges served over ice, with a little water for a lighter drink.
steps: Wash the oranges under running water, dry them and cut them in half on a clean cutting board.
Squeeze the halves with a citrus juicer and collect the juice in a pitcher; discard the peels and seeds.
Pass the juice through a coarse strainer if you prefer less pulp, without pressing the white parts of the peel.
Add the cold water and stir; the yield may vary with the size and juiciness of the oranges.
Divide the ice among 4 glasses and pour equal amounts of juice; serve immediately after squeezing.
tips: Weigh the edible portion of the fruit and remove hard seeds as directed in the preparation steps.
Serve freshly prepared; if it stands for a few minutes, stir the pitcher before pouring.

title: Pineapple juice
description: Ripe pineapple and cold water, blended and strained into a yellow tropical juice.
steps: Peel the pineapple and remove the eyes and fibrous core; weigh the cleaned flesh and cut it into cubes.
Place ripe pineapple flesh, cold water in the blender jar; work in batches if necessary.
Blend for 45 seconds, until the fruit and liquid are thoroughly combined and the mixture is smooth.
Pass the mixture through a fine strainer, gently pressing the pulp; discard the trapped seeds and fibers.
Divide the ice among 4 glasses, pour the drink over it and stir gently before bringing it to the table.
tips: Weigh the edible portion of the fruit and remove hard seeds as directed in the preparation steps.
Serve freshly prepared; if it stands for a few minutes, stir the pitcher before pouring.

title: Níspero (sapodilla) milkshake
description: Ripe Cuban níspero or sapodilla, with seeds removed, blended with cold milk for a cinnamon-colored drink.
steps: Wash the ripe brown sapodilla, remove the peel and every hard seed and weigh only the flesh.
Place fully ripe brown sapodilla flesh, seeds removed, cold pasteurized milk in the blender jar; work in batches if necessary.
Blend for 45 seconds, until the fruit and liquid are thoroughly combined and the mixture is smooth.
Pour the drink into a pitcher and stir with a spoon to check that no large pieces remain.
Divide the ice among 4 glasses, pour the drink over it and stir gently before bringing it to the table.
tips: Use Cuban níspero or sapodilla (Manilkara zapota), a different fruit from red mamey and Japanese loquat.
Do not blend any seeds: carefully check the pulp before adding the milk.

title: Classic ham and cheese sandwich spread
description: A smooth spread of cooked ham, cream cheese and roasted red pepper, enough to fill 12 small sandwich rolls.

ingredients.name: commercial mayonnaise made with pasteurized egg

steps: Dice the ham finely and drain the roasted pepper thoroughly; pat it dry before adding it to the food processor.
Pulse the ham and pepper together until finely chopped, leaving no large pieces.
Add the cream cheese, mayonnaise and mustard; process again until the mixture forms a thick spreadable paste.
Transfer the spread to a clean container, cover and refrigerate for 20 minutes to let it firm up.
Split the 12 small rolls and divide the spread among them; serve 3 rolls per portion and keep the remainder refrigerated.
tips: Drain moist ingredients thoroughly and fill the rolls close to serving time so they do not become soggy.
Keep the spread covered and refrigerated, taking out only the amount you will serve.

title: Tuna and pickle sandwich spread
description: Flaked tuna with pickles and mayonnaise in a chilled spread for 12 small sandwich rolls.

ingredients.name: commercial mayonnaise made with pasteurized egg

steps: Drain the tuna and press it gently with a fork to remove excess liquid before flaking it.
Drain and finely chop the pickles; rinse the parsley and chop its leaves together with the red onion.
Mix the mayonnaise with the lime juice; fold in tuna, pickles, onion and parsley, mashing until evenly spreadable.
Cover the container and refrigerate for 20 minutes; stir afterward to redistribute the creamy dressing.
Fill the 12 small rolls with similar amounts of spread; serve 3 per portion and keep the others chilled.
tips: Drain moist ingredients thoroughly and fill the rolls close to serving time so they do not become soggy.
Keep the spread covered and refrigerated, taking out only the amount you will serve.

title: Sardine and tomato sandwich spread
description: Canned sardines blended with cream cheese and tomato paste to fill 12 small sandwich rolls.
steps: Drain the sardines and break them into pieces; remove any bones you prefer before blending the fish.
Peel and finely chop the onion; place it in the food processor with the sardines, tomato paste and lime juice.
Add the cream cheese and oil; pulse until the mixture forms a thick, smooth, evenly colored spread.
Transfer the spread to a covered container and refrigerate for 20 minutes before filling the small rolls.
Divide the spread among the 12 split rolls; serve 3 sandwiches per portion and keep the remainder refrigerated.
tips: Drain moist ingredients thoroughly and fill the rolls close to serving time so they do not become soggy.
Keep the spread covered and refrigerated, taking out only the amount you will serve.

title: Yellow cheese and carrot sandwich spread
description: Grated yellow cheese with finely shredded carrot and cream cheese in a creamy filling for 12 small rolls.
steps: Rinse and peel the carrot, grate it very finely and press lightly to remove any loose moisture.
Rinse and dry the chives before chopping; make sure the yellow cheese is grated into short shreds.
Beat the cream cheese with the yogurt until softened; add yellow cheese, carrot and chives and mix until combined.
Cover the spread and refrigerate for 20 minutes; stir to distribute the shreds and check that it spreads easily.
Spread the mixture over the 12 small rolls and close them gently; serve 3 per portion and keep the others chilled.
tips: Drain moist ingredients thoroughly and fill the rolls close to serving time so they do not become soggy.
Keep the spread covered and refrigerated, taking out only the amount you will serve.

title: Chicken and mustard sandwich spread
description: Finely chopped cooked chicken with pickles and mustard, bound with mayonnaise for 12 small sandwich rolls.

ingredients.name: commercial mayonnaise made with pasteurized egg

steps: Check that the cooked chicken has no bones or cartilage; chop it finely and keep it chilled while preparing the rest.
Drain and finely chop the pickles; pulse the chicken until finely chopped and easy to spread.
Whisk the mayonnaise, mustard, lime juice and pepper; mix with the chicken and pickles until the spread holds together.
Transfer the mixture to a clean covered container and refrigerate for 20 minutes to let the flavors combine.
Fill the 12 small rolls with the chilled spread and serve 3 per portion; refrigerate any not served immediately.
tips: Drain moist ingredients thoroughly and fill the rolls close to serving time so they do not become soggy.
Keep the spread covered and refrigerated, taking out only the amount you will serve.

title: Egg, ham and chive sandwich spread
description: Mashed hard-boiled eggs with finely chopped ham and chives in a soft spread for 12 small rolls.

ingredients.name: commercial mayonnaise made with pasteurized egg

steps: Chop the chilled hard-boiled eggs and mash them with a fork until the whites and yolks are finely combined.
Cut the ham into tiny cubes; rinse, dry and chop the chives so they distribute evenly throughout the spread.
Mix the mayonnaise with the lime juice and pepper; add egg, ham and chives and stir until creamy and spreadable.
Cover the spread and refrigerate for 20 minutes; use a clean spoon to stir before filling the bread.
Distribute the spread among the 12 small rolls and serve 3 per portion; keep chilled until bringing them to the table.
tips: Drain moist ingredients thoroughly and fill the rolls close to serving time so they do not become soggy.
Keep the spread covered and refrigerated, taking out only the amount you will serve.

title: Avocado and white bean sandwich spread
description: Ripe avocado with white beans and cilantro, blended into a vegetable spread for 12 small rolls.
steps: Drain the cooked chilled beans thoroughly; rinse and dry the cilantro and remove the leaves from the thick stems.
Cut the peeled avocado and immediately toss it with the lime juice to coat all the flesh.
Blend the avocado, beans, oil and salt into a thick spread; fold in the chopped cilantro at the end.
Place the spread in a small tightly covered container and refrigerate for 15 minutes while splitting the rolls.
Divide the spread among the 12 small rolls, serve 3 per portion and keep the remainder refrigerated until serving.
tips: Drain moist ingredients thoroughly and fill the rolls close to serving time so they do not become soggy.
Keep the spread covered and refrigerated, taking out only the amount you will serve.

title: Coconut bread pudding
description: A home-style bread pudding with coconut milk and shredded coconut, a moist, dense crumb and a caramel coating.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 90 g for the pudding and 80 g for the caramel

ingredients.name: Unsweetened shredded coconut
ingredients.note: 60 g for the mixture and 10 g to finish

steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Prepare a solid metal pan measuring 20 cm with a capacity of at least 2 liters, and a larger baking dish for the water bath.
Cut the bread into small pieces and cover with the milk and coconut milk. Soak for 15 minutes, stirring halfway through, then mash with a fork until no dry patches remain.

Put 80 g of sugar and the water in a saucepan. Heat over medium heat, without stirring with a spoon, for about 5 to 8 minutes, until amber. Pour into the pan and use oven mitts to tilt it and coat the base.
Beat the eggs with 90 g of sugar, the vanilla and salt just until combined. Add the soaked bread and 60 g of shredded coconut; mix until the coconut is evenly distributed.
Pour the mixture into the caramel-coated pan and smooth it without pressing down. Set the pan inside the larger dish and add hot water halfway up its sides, keeping water out of the pudding.

Bake for 55 to 70 minutes, until the edges are firm and the center is set, with a gentle wobble and no visible liquid. Check that the center reaches at least 71 °C; continue baking if it is still liquid. Cover loosely with foil if it browns too much.

Remove the pan from the water bath and let it cool on a rack for 30 minutes. Refrigerate for at least 3 hours. Run a thin spatula around the edge and turn out the cold pudding onto a rimmed plate to catch the caramel.
Scatter the reserved 10 g of coconut over the cold pudding. Slice with a clean knife and serve with the caramel collected on the plate.
tips: Use bread with no mold. Soak it until the crumb is fully softened and mash with a fork to retain the texture of bread pudding.
Stir the coconut milk before measuring to combine its thick and liquid parts. Unsweetened shredded coconut keeps the sweetness at the intended level.
Chilling helps the pudding hold together in slices. Keep it covered in the refrigerator and unmold only when fully cold.

title: Guava and cream cheese bread pudding
description: A home-style bread pudding with pieces of guava paste and cream cheese, coated in caramel and served cold in slices.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 50 g for the pudding and 80 g for the caramel

steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Prepare a solid metal pan measuring 20 cm with a capacity of at least 2 liters, and a larger baking dish for the water bath.
Tear up the bread, cover with the milk and soak for 15 minutes. Mash with a fork until all the crumb is moist; leave small pieces to give the pudding body.

Put 80 g of sugar and the water in a saucepan. Heat over medium heat, without stirring with a spoon, for about 5 to 8 minutes, until amber. Pour into the pan and use oven mitts to tilt it and coat the base.
Cut the guava paste and cold cream cheese into cubes measuring about 1 cm. Beat the eggs with 50 g of sugar, the vanilla and salt; fold in the soaked bread.
Fold in the guava and cheese with a spatula, keeping some cubes intact. Pour into the caramel-coated pan and spread the pieces evenly so they appear throughout the servings.

Set the pan in the larger dish and add hot water halfway up its sides. Bake for 60 to 75 minutes, until the center is set and reaches at least 71 °C. It may wobble gently, but should not look liquid; continue baking if needed.

Remove the pan from the water bath and let it cool on a rack for 30 minutes. Refrigerate for at least 3 hours. Run a thin spatula around the edge and turn out the cold pudding onto a rimmed plate to catch the caramel.
tips: Use bread with no mold. Soak it until the crumb is fully softened and mash with a fork to retain the texture of bread pudding.
Firm guava paste leaves small pockets of sweet fruit. Jam adds more water and can change the consistency of this version.
Cut the cheese while it is cold so it is easy to distribute. Avoid beating it completely into the mixture if you want to keep pale streaks.
Chilling helps the pudding hold together in slices. Keep it covered in the refrigerator and unmold only when fully cold.

title: Chocolate bread pudding
description: A home-style bread pudding with dark chocolate and cocoa, a dense, moist texture and a layer of caramel.

ingredients.name: Milk
ingredients.note: 350 ml to melt the chocolate and 300 ml to cool the mixture

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 90 g for the pudding and 80 g for the caramel

ingredients.name: Dark chocolate
ingredients.note: with 70% cocoa; check the label for allergens

steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Prepare a solid metal pan measuring 20 cm with a capacity of at least 2 liters, and a larger baking dish for the water bath.
Warm 350 ml of milk over low heat for 3 to 5 minutes, without boiling. Remove from the heat, add the chopped chocolate and sifted cocoa, and stir until smooth.
Add the remaining 300 ml of milk to cool the mixture. Add the torn bread and soak for 15 minutes, then mash with a fork. The mixture should be lukewarm before adding the eggs.

Put 80 g of sugar and the water in a saucepan. Heat over medium heat, without stirring with a spoon, for about 5 to 8 minutes, until amber. Pour into the pan and use oven mitts to tilt it and coat the base.
Beat the eggs with 90 g of sugar, the vanilla and salt. Fold into the chocolate-soaked bread and mix until no streaks of egg remain, then pour into the caramel-coated pan.

Set the pan in the larger dish and add hot water halfway up its sides. Bake for 55 to 70 minutes, until the edges are firm and the center is set; check for at least 71 °C in the center and continue baking if it still looks liquid.

Remove the pan from the water bath and let it cool on a rack for 30 minutes. Refrigerate for at least 3 hours. Run a thin spatula around the edge and turn out the cold pudding onto a rimmed plate to catch the caramel.
tips: Use bread with no mold. Soak it until the crumb is fully softened and mash with a fork to retain the texture of bread pudding.
Sift the cocoa and melt the chocolate thoroughly to prevent bitter lumps. If the chocolate contains soy or other allergens, account for them when serving.
Chocolate firms up as it cools. Check that the pudding is set during baking without expecting it to be as firm as it will be after refrigeration.
Chilling helps the pudding hold together in slices. Keep it covered in the refrigerator and unmold only when fully cold.

title: Ripe banana bread pudding
description: A home-style bread pudding with very ripe sweet bananas, vanilla and cinnamon, finished with caramel and small banana slices.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 70 g for the pudding and 80 g for the caramel

ingredients.name: Very ripe sweet banana
ingredients.note: peeled weight: 150 g to mash, 50 g to dice and 50 g to slice

steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Prepare a solid metal pan measuring 20 cm with a capacity of at least 2 liters, and a larger baking dish for the water bath.
Tear up the bread, cover with the milk and soak for 15 minutes. Stir and mash with a fork until no dry pieces remain, keeping some texture.

Put 80 g of sugar and the water in a saucepan. Heat over medium heat, without stirring with a spoon, for about 5 to 8 minutes, until amber. Pour into the pan and use oven mitts to tilt it and coat the base.
Mash 150 g of banana with a fork, dice 50 g into small pieces and cut the other 50 g into slices. Once the caramel in the pan has hardened, arrange the slices over the base.
Beat the eggs with 70 g of sugar, the vanilla, cinnamon and salt. Add the mashed banana and soaked bread, mix well, fold in the diced banana and pour carefully over the slices.

Set the pan inside the larger dish and add hot water halfway up its sides. Bake for 60 to 75 minutes, until the center is set, with no visible liquid, and reaches at least 71 °C. Continue baking if needed, and cover with foil if it browns too much.

Remove the pan from the water bath and let it cool on a rack for 30 minutes. Refrigerate for at least 3 hours. Run a thin spatula around the edge and turn out the cold pudding onto a rimmed plate to catch the caramel.
tips: Use bread with no mold. Soak it until the crumb is fully softened and mash with a fork to retain the texture of bread pudding.
This recipe uses sweet bananas with soft flesh. Cooking plantains require different preparation and a different liquid ratio.
Weigh the flesh after peeling the fruit. Very ripe bananas add sweetness and moisture, so this version uses less milk than others in the collection.
Chilling helps the pudding hold together in slices. Keep it covered in the refrigerator and unmold only when fully cold.

title: Coffee bread pudding
description: A home-style bread pudding with strong coffee and milk, a roasted aroma and dense texture, served with its caramel.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 100 g for the pudding and 80 g for the caramel

steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Prepare a solid metal pan measuring 20 cm with a capacity of at least 2 liters, and a larger baking dish for the water bath.
Mix the milk with the cold coffee. Add the bread, cut into pieces, and soak for 15 minutes, then stir and mash with a fork until all the crumb is moist.

Put 80 g of sugar and the water in a saucepan. Heat over medium heat, without stirring with a spoon, for about 5 to 8 minutes, until amber. Pour into the pan and use oven mitts to tilt it and coat the base.
Beat the eggs with 100 g of sugar, the vanilla and salt. Fold in the soaked bread and mix gently, without adding much foam, until the coffee is distributed throughout.
Pour the mixture into the caramel-coated pan and smooth it without pressing down. Set the pan inside the larger dish and add hot water halfway up its sides, keeping water out of the pudding.

Bake for 55 to 70 minutes, until the center is set and only gently wobbles when the pan is moved. Check that it reaches at least 71 °C and has no visible liquid; continue baking if needed. Cover with foil if the surface browns too much.

Remove the pan from the water bath and let it cool on a rack for 30 minutes. Refrigerate for at least 3 hours. Run a thin spatula around the edge and turn out the cold pudding onto a rimmed plate to catch the caramel.
tips: Use bread with no mold. Soak it until the crumb is fully softened and mash with a fork to retain the texture of bread pudding.
The coffee is part of the soaking liquid: measure it after brewing. You can use decaffeinated coffee at the same volume and strength.
Coffee that tastes pleasant to drink gives a more balanced aroma. Avoid making the caramel too dark so it does not add excess bitterness.
Chilling helps the pudding hold together in slices. Keep it covered in the refrigerator and unmold only when fully cold.

title: Orange bread pudding
description: A home-style bread pudding with orange juice and zest, a moist, dense crumb, caramel and a citrus aroma.

ingredients.name: Orange zest
ingredients.note: 3 g for the mixture and 1 g to finish; orange part only

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 90 g for the pudding and 80 g for the caramel

steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Prepare a solid metal pan measuring 20 cm with a capacity of at least 2 liters, and a larger baking dish for the water bath.
Cut the bread into small pieces, cover with the milk and soak for 15 minutes. Mash with a fork until all the crumb is soft, without turning it into a completely smooth purée.

Put 80 g of sugar and the water in a saucepan. Heat over medium heat, without stirring with a spoon, for about 5 to 8 minutes, until amber. Pour into the pan and use oven mitts to tilt it and coat the base.
Beat the eggs with 90 g of sugar, the vanilla, salt and 3 g of zest. Add the cold juice, followed by the soaked bread. Mix gently to distribute the flavor throughout.
Pour the mixture into the caramel-coated pan and smooth it without pressing down. Set the pan inside the larger dish and add hot water halfway up its sides, keeping water out of the pudding.

Bake for 55 to 70 minutes, until the edges are firm and the center is set, with a gentle wobble. Check for at least 71 °C in the center and continue baking if any liquid remains visible. Cover loosely with foil if it browns too much.

Remove the pan from the water bath and let it cool on a rack for 30 minutes. Refrigerate for at least 3 hours. Run a thin spatula around the edge and turn out the cold pudding onto a rimmed plate to catch the caramel.
Sprinkle the reserved 1 g of zest over the cold pudding just before serving. Cut into slices and serve with the caramel collected on the plate.
tips: Use bread with no mold. Soak it until the crumb is fully softened and mash with a fork to retain the texture of bread pudding.
Wash and dry the orange before zesting. Remove only the orange layer because the white pith adds bitterness.
Add the cold juice to the eggs, then combine with the soaked bread. Heating the juice together with the milk can separate the mixture before baking.
Chilling helps the pudding hold together in slices. Keep it covered in the refrigerator and unmold only when fully cold.

title: Cuban garapiña (pineapple peel drink)
description: A home-style boiled pineapple peel drink, strained and chilled; this version is not fermented.

ingredients.name: peel from one sound ripe pineapple, thoroughly washed

steps: Wash the whole pineapple under running water and scrub the skin well before peeling. Use sound fruit and discard the crown and any damaged areas.
Cut the clean peel into pieces and place in a saucepan with the 1500 ml of drinking water.
Bring to a boil, reduce to a gentle simmer and cook covered for 15 minutes to extract the flavor from the peel.
Turn off the heat, add the sugar and stir until dissolved. Strain through a fine sieve into a clean container and discard the peels.
Cool the container in an ice-water bath and refrigerate immediately for at least 2 hours. Serve in 4 glasses with the measured ice.
tips: This version is served without fermentation: do not leave the drink standing at room temperature.
Keep covered in the refrigerator and consume within 2 days.

title: Yellow mamey milkshake (mammee apple)
description: Ripe yellow mamey or Santo Domingo mammee apple blended with cold milk in a creamy home-style drink.

ingredients.name: clean ripe yellow mamey (Mammea americana) pulp

steps: Wash the yellow mamey, peel off the skin and remove all the bitter white membrane and large seeds; weigh 400 g of clean pulp.
Cut the ripe pulp into small pieces and place it in a blender with the 600 ml of cold milk.
Add the 30 g of sugar and blend for 60 seconds, until the fruit pulp is fully combined with the milk.
Add the 120 g of ice and blend again for 20 seconds; work in batches if the blender jar is small.
Divide the milkshake among 4 glasses and serve immediately. If fibers remain, strain before serving.
tips: Yellow mamey or Santo Domingo mammee apple is Mammea americana, a different fruit from red mamey sapote and canistel.
Use only ripe pulp: discard the skin, bitter membrane and seeds before blending.

title: Plain corn tamal with salt
description: A simple tamal of ground fresh corn and salt, wrapped in corn husks, without filling or other seasonings.

ingredients.name: fresh corn kernels, mature and starchy
sound fresh corn husks, for wrapping

steps: Wash the fresh corn husks and drain. Check the kernels; use mature, starchy fresh corn that produces a thick paste when ground.
Grind the 1000 g of corn in a mill or food processor in batches, without adding water, until a fine paste forms that holds its shape on a spoon.
Mix only the 5 g of salt into the ground corn. If the paste is runny, drain it in a clean cloth before wrapping; do not add flour or other ingredients.
Overlap two husks, divide the paste into 8 portions, wrap each portion and tie with strips cut from the same husks, leaving some room for expansion.
Bring the 3000 ml of water to a boil in a large pot. Add the sealed tamales and simmer gently for 60 minutes, keeping them covered with hot water.
Open one to check that the paste is firm and cooked in the center. If it is still raw, cook for another 10 minutes; drain and rest for 10 minutes before unwrapping.
tips: The paste contains only corn and salt; the husks and water are used for wrapping and cooking.
Very milky or insufficiently starchy corn may not set firmly without additions; choose ears with full kernels.
